      '<table class="tb"><thead><tr><th>Connection</th><th>Direction</th><th>Linked to the city</th></tr></thead><tbody>' +
      c.conexoes.map((k, i) => `<tr class="cl" data-con="${i}"><td>${nomes[k[0]] || esc(k[0])}</td><td>${k[3] && k[4] ? 'in and out' : k[3] ? 'in' : 'out'}</td><td>${k[5] === 1 ? 'yes' : k[5] === 0 ? '<b style="color:#b02a2a">no</b>' : 'depends on a station'}</td></tr>`).join('') + '</tbody></table>' +
      sugestoesDe('conexoes') + '<h2>Imports per week</h2>' + barras(prod.map(p => ({ r: p[1], v: Cx.importa[p[0]] })).filter(p => p.v > 0), { cor: '#eb6834', fmt: curto }) +
      '<h2>Exports per week</h2>' + (prod.some(p => Cx.exporta[p[0]] > 0) ? barras(prod.map(p => ({ r: p[1], v: Cx.exporta[p[0]] })).filter(p => p.v > 0), { cor: '#2a78d6', fmt: curto }) : '<p class="nota">The city exports nothing at the moment.</p>');
  },
  terreno(c) {
    return ln('Average land value', '₡' + c.ambiente.valorTerreno + '/m²') + (c.distritos.length ? '<h2>By district</h2>' + barras(c.distritos.map(d => ({ r: d[1], v: d[3] })).sort((a, b) => b.v - a.v), { cor: '#a9841c', fmt: v => '₡' + v }) : '') +
      '<p class="nota">It rises with parks, schools, healthcare, police, fire stations and transport nearby. It falls with pollution, noise, crime and garbage.</p>' + sugestoesDe('terreno') + grafHist('gvt', 'Land value over time', [['valorTerreno', 'Value']], { zero: true, fmt: v => '₡' + fmt(v) });
  },
  recursos(c) {
    const R = c.ambiente.recursos, I = c.industria, n = [['soloFertil', 'Fertile land', '#a9841c'], ['floresta', 'Forest', '#1f6b22'], ['minerio', 'Ore', '#2f55a4'], ['petroleo', 'Oil', '#1d1d1d']];
    return '<p>Switch the layer in the map legend to see where each resource sits inside and around your tiles.</p><h2>Usage in the purchased tiles</h2>' +
      n.map(k => R[k[0]][1] > 0 ? medidorNeutro(k[1], R[k[0]][0], R[k[0]][1], k[2]) : ln(k[1], 'none in your tiles')).join('') +
      '<h2>Industry by type</h2>' + barras([['generica', 'Generic'], ['agricola', 'Agricultural'], ['florestal', 'Forestry'], ['minerio', 'Mining'], ['petroleo', 'Oil']].map(k => ({ r: k[1], v: I[k[0]][0], extra: I[k[0]][0] ? 'productivity ' + I[k[0]][1] + '%' : '' })), { fmt: v => fmt(v) + ' cells' }) + sugestoesDe('recursos');
  },
  distritos(c) {
    const pol = c.dinheiro.politicas;
    return ln('Districts created', fmt(c.distritos.length)) + ln('Park, industry or campus areas', fmt(c.parques)) + sugestoesDe('distritos') +
      (c.distritos.length ? '<h2>Districts</h2><table class="tb"><thead><tr><th>District</th><th class="n">Pop.</th><th class="n">Land</th><th class="n">Happy</th><th class="n">Crime</th></tr></thead><tbody>' +
        c.distritos.map(d => `<tr class="cl" data-dist="${d[7]},${d[8]}"><td><b>${esc(d[1])}</b>${d[6] && d[6] !== 'None' ? '<small>' + esc(d[6]) + '</small>' : ''}</td><td class="n">${fmt(d[2])}</td><td class="n">₡${d[3]}</td><td class="n">${d[4]}%</td><td class="n">${d[5]}%</td></tr>`).join('') + '</tbody></table>' : '') +
      '<h2>City-wide policies</h2>' + (pol.length ? '<p>' + pol.map(esc).join(', ') + '</p>' : '<p class="nota">No active policy.</p>');
  },
  lazer(c) {
    return cobLinha('Homes with leisure nearby', 'lazer', true) + ln('Parks and plazas', fmt(c.predios.porServico.Beautification || 0)) + ln('Unique buildings', fmt(c.predios.porServico.Monument || 0)) + ln('Spent on parks', din((c.dinheiro.porServico.Beautification || [0, 0])[1]) + ' per week') +
      sugestoesDe('lazer') + tabelaServicos(['Beautification'], 'Parks and plazas');
  },
  turismo(c) {
    const P = c.populacao, t = P.turistas, vis = P.visitasTuristas;
    return ln('Tourists in the city', fmt(t[0] + t[1] + t[2])) + ln('Visits this week', fmt(vis[0] + vis[1] + vis[2])) + ln('Tourism income', din((c.dinheiro.porServico.Tourism || [0, 0])[0]) + ' per week') +
      '<h2>Tourists by wealth</h2>' + barras([{ r: 'Low wealth', v: t[0] }, { r: 'Medium wealth', v: t[1] }, { r: 'High wealth', v: t[2] }], { cor: '#e87ba4' }) + sugestoesDe('turismo') + tabelaServicos(['Monument'], 'Unique buildings') + tabelaServicos(['Beautification'], 'Parks and plazas');
  },
  emprego(c) {
    const P = c.populacao, S = c.setores, D = c.demanda, niv = [['semEstudo', 'Uneducated'], ['fundamental', 'Elementary'], ['medio', 'High school'], ['superior', 'University degree']];
    const set = [['comercial', 'Commercial', 'ca'], ['industrial', 'Industry', 'in'], ['escritorios', 'Offices', 'es'], ['publico', 'Public service', 'sv']];
    return ln('Unemployment', P.desempregoPct + '%') + ln('Unemployed', fmt(D.desempregados)) + ln('Open jobs', fmt(D.vagasLivres)) + ln('Total jobs', fmt(D.empregos)) +
      '<h2>Unemployed by education level</h2>' + barras(niv.map(n => ({ r: n[1], v: P[n[0]].desempregados, extra: 'of ' + fmt(P[n[0]].aptos) + ' eligible' })), { cor: '#d03b3b' }) +
      '<h2>Jobs by sector</h2>' + empilhada(set.map(s => ({ r: s[1], v: S[s[0]].total, cor: ZONAS[s[2]].cor }))) +
      '<h2>Open jobs by sector</h2>' + barras(set.map(s => ({ r: s[1], v: S[s[0]].vazios, cor: ZONAS[s[2]].cor }))) + sugestoesDe('emprego') +
      grafHist('gdes', 'Unemployment over time', [['desemprego', 'Unemployment']], { zero: true, fmt: v => fmt(v) + '%' });
  },
  industria(c) {
    const Cx = c.comercioExterior, S = c.setores, P = c.predios.problemas, k = n => fmt((P[n] || [0])[0]);
    return ln('Commercial jobs', fmt(S.comercial.total)) + ln('Industrial jobs', fmt(S.industrial.total)) + ln('Office jobs', fmt(S.escritorios.total)) + ln('Goods imported', curto(Cx.importa.mercadorias) + ' per week') +
      '<h2>Supply warnings</h2>' + ln('Shops with no goods', k('NoGoods')) + ln('Shops with no customers', k('NoCustomers')) + ln('Factories with no raw materials', k('NoResources')) + ln('Factories with full storage', k('NoPlaceforGoods')) +
      sugestoesDe('industria') + '<h2>Imports per week</h2>' + barras([['mercadorias', 'Goods'], ['agricola', 'Agricultural'], ['madeira', 'Lumber'], ['minerio', 'Ore'], ['petroleo', 'Oil']].map(p => ({ r: p[1], v: Cx.importa[p[0]] })), { cor: '#eb6834', fmt: curto });
  },
  dinheiro(c) {
    const D = c.dinheiro, saldo = D.receita - D.despesa, e = Object.entries(D.porServico);
    const rec = e.filter(x => x[1][0] > 0).sort((a, b) => b[1][0] - a[1][0]).map(x => ({ r: SERVICO[x[0]] || x[0], v: x[1][0], extra: pct(x[1][0], D.receita) }));
    const des = e.filter(x => x[1][1] > 0).sort((a, b) => b[1][1] - a[1][1]).map(x => ({ r: SERVICO[x[0]] || x[0], v: x[1][1], extra: pct(x[1][1], D.despesa) }));
    const imp = { ResidencialBaixa: 'Low-density residential', ResidencialAlta: 'High-density residential', ComercialBaixa: 'Low-density commercial', ComercialAlta: 'High-density commercial', Industria: 'Industry', Escritorios: 'Offices' };
    return ln('Cash', din(D.caixa)) + ln('Income per week', din(D.receita)) + ln('Expenses per week', din(D.despesa)) + ln('Weekly balance', (saldo >= 0 ? '+' : '−') + din(Math.abs(saldo))) + sugestoesDe('dinheiro') +
      '<h2>Where the income comes from</h2>' + barras(rec, { cor: '#1baf7a', fmt: din }) + '<h2>Where the expenses go</h2>' + barras(des, { cor: '#eb6834', fmt: din }) +
      '<h2>Taxes</h2>' + Object.keys(imp).map(k => ln(imp[k], D.impostos[k] + '%')).join('') + '<h2>Service budgets (day and night)</h2><button class="lk" data-ir="dianoite">Compare day and night usage</button>' + Object.entries(D.orcamento).map(o => ln(SERVICO[o[0]] || o[0], o[1][0] + '%' + (o[1][1] !== o[1][0] ? ' and ' + o[1][1] + '%' : ''))).join('') +
      grafHist('gcx', 'Cash over time', [['caixa', 'Cash']], { fmt: v => '₡' + curto(v) }) + grafHist('grd', 'Income and expenses per week', [['receita', 'Income', '#1baf7a'], ['despesa', 'Expenses', '#eb6834']], { zero: true, fmt: v => '₡' + curto(v) });
  },
  demanda(c) {
    const D = c.demanda, z = c.zonas;
    return '<h2>Demand right now</h2>' + barras([{ r: 'Residential', v: D.r, cor: '#5fbf3a' }, { r: 'Commercial', v: D.c, cor: '#4aa3e8' }, { r: 'Industry and offices', v: D.w, cor: '#f0a71e' }], { max: 100, fmt: v => v + '%' }) +
      ln('Unemployed', fmt(D.desempregados)) + ln('Open jobs', fmt(D.vagasLivres)) + ln('Empty homes', fmt(c.setores.residencial.vazios)) + ln('Tax effect (R, C, I)', [D.ajusteImpostoR, D.ajusteImpostoC, D.ajusteImpostoW].join(', ')) +
      '<p class="nota">Residential rises when there are open jobs and not enough homes. Industry and offices rise when people are out of work. Commercial follows residents, tourists and the goods available.</p>' + sugestoesDe('demanda') +
      '<h2>Zoned cells</h2><table class="tb"><thead><tr><th>Zone</th><th class="n">Total</th><th class="n">Empty</th></tr></thead><tbody>' + Object.keys(ZCEL).filter(k => z[k]).map(k => `<tr><td>${ZONAS[ZCEL[k]].nome}</td><td class="n">${fmt(z[k][0])}</td><td class="n">${fmt(z[k][1])}</td></tr>`).join('') + '</tbody></table>' +
      grafHist('gdem', 'Demand over time', [['demR', 'Residential', '#5fbf3a'], ['demC', 'Commercial', '#4aa3e8'], ['demW', 'Industry and offices', '#f0a71e']], { min: 0, max: 100, fmt: v => fmt(v) + '%' });
  },
  historico(c) {
    const n = E.h && E.h.linhas ? E.h.linhas.length : 0;
    return `<p class="nota">${n} sample(s) recorded, one per in-game week while the game runs with the mod enabled. They live in one CSV file per city, in the CityDashboard folder of the game's data directory.</p>` +
      grafHist('h1', 'Population', [['pop', 'Inhabitants']], { zero: true }) + grafHist('h2', 'Cash', [['caixa', 'Cash']], { fmt: v => '₡' + curto(v) }) +
      grafHist('h3', 'Income and expenses per week', [['receita', 'Income', '#1baf7a'], ['despesa', 'Expenses', '#eb6834']], { zero: true, fmt: v => '₡' + curto(v) }) +
      grafHist('h4', 'Demand', [['demR', 'Residential', '#5fbf3a'], ['demC', 'Commercial', '#4aa3e8'], ['demW', 'Industry and offices', '#f0a71e']], { min: 0, max: 100, fmt: v => fmt(v) + '%' }) +
      grafHist('h5', 'Homes and jobs', [['moradias', 'Homes'], ['empregos', 'Jobs']], { zero: true }) + grafHist('h6', 'Unemployment', [['desemprego', 'Unemployment']], { zero: true, fmt: v => fmt(v) + '%' }) +
      grafHist('h7', 'Happiness', [['felicidade', 'Happiness']], { min: 0, max: 100, fmt: v => fmt(v) + '%' }) + grafHist('h8', 'Land value', [['valorTerreno', 'Value']], { zero: true, fmt: v => '₡' + fmt(v) }) + grafHist('h9', 'Crime rate', [['crime', 'Crime']], { zero: true, fmt: v => fmt(v) + '%' });
  },
  motor(c) {
    const nomes = { predios: 'Buildings', trechosDeRede: 'Road, rail and pipe segments', nos: 'Network nodes', blocosDeZona: 'Zone blocks', veiculos: 'Vehicles on the road', estacionados: 'Parked cars', cidadaos: 'Citizens', pedestresAtivos: 'People on the move', arvores: 'Trees', linhas: 'Transport lines', distritos: 'Districts' };
    const G = c.geral;
    return ln('Simulation', G.pausado ? 'paused' : 'speed ' + G.velocidade) + ln('Measured pace', G.diasPorSegundo > 0 ? dec(G.diasPorSegundo, 2) + ' in-game day per second' : 'measuring') +
      '<h2>Internal game limits</h2><p class="nota">The game has a fixed ceiling for each kind of object. Near the ceiling, things stop appearing without warning.</p>' +
      Object.entries(c.limites).map(e => medidor(nomes[e[0]] || e[0], e[1][0], e[1][1], '')).join('') + sugestoesDe('motor') +
      '<h2>Cost of this panel</h2>' + ['cidade', 'mapa', 'servicos'].map(k => ln({ cidade: 'City numbers', mapa: 'Map', servicos: 'Service buildings' }[k], (E.ms[k] != null ? fmt(E.ms[k]) + ' ms of collection' : 'collection not measured') + (E.ritmo[k] ? ', every ' + dec(E.ritmo[k], 1) + ' s' : ''))).join('') +
      '<p class="nota">The collection runs on the simulation thread, not the render thread: it causes no stutter on screen. If it gets expensive, the page spaces the requests out by itself.</p>' +
      '<h2>About this panel</h2><p class="nota">The mod only reads. It builds nothing, does not touch the money and does not change the simulation. Data is collected when this page asks for it; with the tab closed, the cost is zero.</p>';
  }
};
let GRUPOS_PROB = [], GRUPOS_VIA = [], GRUPOS_CON = [];
function medidorNeutro(rotulo, uso, cap, cor) {
  const p = pc(uso, cap);
  return `<div class="med"><div class="tp"><b>${rotulo}</b><span>${fmt(p)}% used</span></div><div class="tr" role="img" aria-label="${rotulo}: ${fmt(p)}% used"><i style="width:${lim(p, 0, 100)}%;background:${cor}"></i></div></div>`;
}

function cartaoSel() {
  const o = E.sel, m = E.m; if (!o || !m) return '';
  let h;
  if (o.s) {
    const t = m.tipos[o.s[6]], n = o.s[9] != null && o.s[9] >= 0 ? m.ruas[o.s[9]] : '';
    h = `<h3><span>${esc(n || redePT(t.nome))}</span><button data-fechar aria-label="Close">×</button></h3>` + ln('Type', esc(redePT(t.nome))) + (t.serv === 'Road' ? ln('Road occupancy', o.s[7] + '%') : '');
  } else {
    const b = o.b, c = m.cls[b[F.classe]], sv = E.sv ? E.sv.predios.find(p => p[0] === b[F.id]) : null;
    h = `<h3><span>${esc(c.zoneado ? ZONAS[c.z].nome + ', level ' + b[F.nivel] : m.nomes[b[F.nome]] || SERVICO[c.s] || c.s)}</span><button data-fechar aria-label="Close">×</button></h3>`;
    const ps = traduzProblemas(m.problemas[b[F.problema]]);
    if (ps.length) h += `<p style="color:#b02a2a;font-weight:700;margin:0 0 4px">${esc(ps.join(', '))}</p>`;
    if (sv) h += `<pre>${esc(sv[6])}</pre>` + ln('Upkeep', '≈ ' + din(sv[7]) + ' per week') + (sv[8] ? ln('Jobs', fmt(sv[8])) : '') + (sv[9] ? '' : ln('State', 'turned off'));
    if (c.zoneado) h += ln(c.s === 'Residential' ? 'Residents' : 'Workers', b[F.moradores]) + ln('Happiness', b[F.felicidade] + '%') + ln('Healthcare', b[F.saude] + '%');
    h += ln('Land value', '₡' + b[F.valorTerreno]) + ln('Ground pollution', fmt(b[F.poluicao] / 2.55) + '%') + ln('Noise', b[F.ruido]) + ln('Garbage piling up', fmt(b[F.lixo]));
    const dist = b[F.distrito] ? (m.distritos.find(d => d[3] === b[F.distrito]) || [])[0] : null;
    if (dist) h += ln('District', esc(dist));
    h += '<h2 style="margin-top:10px">What reaches this building</h2>' + COBERTURAS.map(k => ln(rotuloCampo(k), b[F[k]] > 0 ? fmt(b[F[k]]) : '<span style="color:#b02a2a">out of reach</span>')).join('');
  }
  return `<div id="sel">${h}</div>`;
}

let ultimoHTML = '';
$('painel').addEventListener('pointerdown', () => { E.segura = true; });
window.addEventListener('pointerup', () => { if (E.segura) { E.segura = false; setTimeout(pintarPainel, 0); } });
window.addEventListener('pointercancel', () => { E.segura = false; });
function pintarPainel(topo) {
  const v = V(), corpo = $('corpo');
  if (v.tela) return pintarTela(topo);
  $('pTitulo').textContent = v.nome; $('pSub').textContent = v.sub || '';
  let h;
  if (!E.c) h = `<p class="nota">${E.noMenu ? 'The game is at the menu. Load or create a city and this page fills itself in.' : 'Waiting for the game to answer at 127.0.0.1:19680.'}</p>`;
  else { GRUPOS = []; h = cartaoSel() + PAINEIS[v.id](E.c); }
  if (h === ultimoHTML && !topo) return;
  if (!topo && (E.segura || document.querySelector('.graf:hover'))) return;   // does not replace the content in the middle of a click or while a chart is being read
  const pos = corpo.scrollTop; ultimoHTML = h; corpo.innerHTML = h; corpo.scrollTop = topo ? 0 : pos;
}
function focar(pts) {
  E.focos = pts || []; if (!E.focos.length) return pedir();
  const xs = E.focos.map(p => p[0]), zs = E.focos.map(p => p[1]), x1 = Math.min(...xs), x2 = Math.max(...xs), z1 = Math.min(...zs), z2 = Math.max(...zs);
  const mg = Math.max(350, (x2 - x1) * 0.15, (z2 - z1) * 0.15); ajustar([x1 - mg, z1 - mg, x2 + mg, z2 + mg]);
}
document.addEventListener('click', ev => {
  const t = ev.target, q = s => t.closest && t.closest(s);
  let el;
  if ((el = q('.visao'))) return trocarVisao(el.dataset.v);
  if ((el = q('[data-ir]'))) return trocarVisao(el.dataset.ir);
  if ((el = q('[data-sub]'))) { E.sub[E.visao] = el.dataset.sub; reconstruir(false); pintarLegenda(); return; }
  if ((el = q('[data-foco]'))) { const s = E.sug[+el.dataset.foco]; if (s && s.area !== E.visao && s.area !== 'cidade' && E.visao !== 'assessor') trocarVisao(s.area); return focar(s && s.foco); }
  if ((el = q('[data-grupo]'))) return focar(GRUPOS[+el.dataset.grupo]);
  if ((el = q('[data-prob]'))) return focar(ondeProb(GRUPOS_PROB[+el.dataset.prob]));
  if ((el = q('[data-via]'))) { const p = GRUPOS_VIA[+el.dataset.via]; E.focos = [p]; return irPara(p[0], p[1], 1.1); }
  if ((el = q('[data-con]'))) { E.focos = [GRUPOS_CON[+el.dataset.con]]; return pedir(); }
  if ((el = q('[data-dist]'))) { const p = el.dataset.dist.split(',').map(Number); return irPara(p[0], p[1], 0.5); }
  if (q('[data-fechar]')) { E.sel = null; pedir(); pintarPainel(); }
  if ((el = q('[data-faixa]'))) { E.faixa = el.dataset.faixa; cacheTela.telaEvo = ''; return pintarTela(); }
  if (q('[data-todos]')) { E.grafFoco = null; cacheTela.telaEvo = ''; return pintarTela(true); }
  if ((el = q('#telaEvo [data-cartao]'))) { E.grafFoco = E.grafFoco ? null : el.dataset.cartao; cacheTela.telaEvo = ''; return pintarTela(true); }
});

// ---------- bottom bar ----------
function pintarBarra() {
  const c = E.c, el = $('barra');
  const vivo = `<div class="fim"><small><span id="vivo" class="${E.vivo ? 'on' : ''}"></span>${E.vivo ? (E.noMenu ? 'game at the menu' : 'live' + (E.ritmo.mapa ? ', map every ' + dec(E.ritmo.mapa, E.ritmo.mapa < 10 ? 1 : 0) + ' s' : '')) : 'no connection to the game'}</small></div>`;
  if (!c) { el.innerHTML = '<div class="cid"><b>City Dashboard</b><span>Cities: Skylines</span></div>' + vivo; return; }
  const D = c.dinheiro, saldo = D.receita - D.despesa, dm = c.demanda, G = c.geral;
  const b = (v, cor, r) => `<div title="${r}: ${v}%"><i style="height:${lim(v, 0, 100)}%;background:${cor}"></i></div>`;
  el.innerHTML = `<div class="cid"><b>${esc(G.cidade)}</b><span>${dataBR(G.data)}, ${G.pausado ? 'paused' : 'speed ' + G.velocidade}</span></div>
    <div class="rci" role="img" aria-label="Demand: residential ${dm.r}%, commercial ${dm.c}%, industry and offices ${dm.w}%">${b(dm.r, 'var(--res)', 'Residential')}${b(dm.c, 'var(--com)', 'Commercial')}${b(dm.w, 'var(--ind)', 'Industry and offices')}<span>R ${dm.r}<br>C ${dm.c}<br>I ${dm.w}</span></div>
    <div class="bl"><b>${din(D.caixa)}</b><small class="${saldo >= 0 ? 'pos' : 'neg'}">${saldo >= 0 ? '+' : '−'}${din(Math.abs(saldo))} per week</small></div>
    <div class="bl"><b>${fmt(c.populacao.total)}</b><small>inhabitants</small></div>
    <div class="bl"><b>${c.populacao.felicidade}%</b><small>happiness</small></div>
    <div class="bl"><b>${c.populacao.desempregoPct}%</b><small>unemployment</small></div>` + vivo;
}

// ---------- refresh cycle ----------
function aviso(t, s) { const a = $('aviso'); if (!t) { a.hidden = true; return; } a.hidden = false; a.innerHTML = `<b>${t}</b>${s || ''}`; }
async function cicloCidade() {
  try {
    const c = JSON.parse(await pegaTexto('cidade')); E.vivo = true;
    if (c.erro) { $('erro').hidden = false; $('erro').textContent = 'The mod answered with an error: ' + c.erro; }
    else if (!c.carregado) { E.noMenu = true; E.c = null; aviso('The game is at the menu', 'Load or create a city. This page fills itself in.'); }
    else { E.noMenu = false; E.c = c; E.sug = regras(c); aviso(null); $('erro').hidden = true; document.title = c.geral.cidade + ' – City Dashboard'; }
  } catch (e) { E.vivo = false; if (!E.c) aviso('No connection to the game', 'Open Cities: Skylines. With the City Dashboard mod enabled, this page comes back by itself.'); }
  pintarBarra(); pintarMarcas(); pintarPainel();
}
let textoMapa = '';
async function cicloMapa() {
  if (V().tela && E.m) return;   // full-screen view open: the map is not visible
  try {
    const txt = await pegaTexto('mapa');
    if (txt === textoMapa) return;            // nothing changed in the game: redo nothing
    const m = JSON.parse(txt); if (!m.carregado || m.erro) return;
    textoMapa = txt;
    const sel = E.sel ? (E.sel.b ? ['b', E.sel.b[F.id]] : ['s', E.sel.s[8]]) : null;
    E.m = prepararMapa(m); reconstruir(true);
    if (sel) { if (sel[0] === 'b') { const b = m.predios.find(p => p[F.id] === sel[1]); E.sel = b ? { b } : null; } else { const s = m.redes.find(p => p[8] === sel[1]); E.sel = s ? { s } : null; } }
    if (!M.ajustado || M.cidade !== (E.c && E.c.geral.cidade)) {
      M.ajustado = true; M.cidade = E.c && E.c.geral.cidade;
      if (E.visao === 'conexoes') ajustar([-8900, -8900, 8900, 8900]); else ajustar();
      // optional URL shortcuts: ?x=...&z=...&zoom=2 opens the map at a point; ?sub=funeraria picks the layer
      const q = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
      if (q.get('zoom')) irPara(+q.get('x') || M.cx, +q.get('z') || M.cz, 0), M.k = +q.get('zoom');
      if (q.get('sub')) { E.sub[E.visao] = q.get('sub'); reconstruir(false); }
    }
    if (E.c) { E.sug = regras(E.c); pintarMarcas(); pintarPainel(); }
    pintarLegenda();
  } catch (e) { if (E.vivo) { $('erro').hidden = false; $('erro').textContent = 'Error while building the map: ' + e.message; console.error(e); } }
}
async function cicloServicos() { try { const s = JSON.parse(await pegaTexto('servicos')); if (s.carregado && !s.erro) E.sv = s; } catch (e) { } pintarPainel(); }
async function cicloHistorico() { try { E.h = await pega('historico'); } catch (e) { } pintarPainel(); }
async function cicloDN() {
  try {
    const r = await fetch('/api/dianoite', { cache: 'no-store' });
    if (r.status === 404) E.dn = { semRota: true };          // old mod still in the game's memory
    else { const j = await r.json(); E.dn = j.carregado ? j : null; }
  } catch (e) { }
  if (V().tela === 'dianoite') pintarTela();
}

// Each loop waits for the previous request to finish before scheduling the next. The interval grows by itself if the
// collection gets expensive: at most ~5% of the game's time goes to the panel, even in a huge city. A hidden tab asks for nothing.
async function laco(nome, fn, base) {
  let ultimo = 0;
  for (;;) {
    if (document.visibilityState === 'visible' || !ultimo) {
      const t0 = performance.now();
      await fn();
      const gasto = performance.now() - t0;
      if (ultimo) E.ritmo[nome] = (t0 - ultimo) / 1000;
      ultimo = t0;
      const intervalo = Math.max(base, gasto * 3, (E.ms[nome] || 0) * 20);   // from the start of one request to the start of the next
      await espera(Math.max(0, intervalo - gasto));
    } else await espera(500);
  }
}
montarTrilho();
E.visao = VISOES.some(v => v.id === location.hash.slice(1)) ? location.hash.slice(1) : 'cidade';
$('app').classList.toggle('modo-tela', !!V().tela);
pintarLegenda(); pintarBarra(); pintarMarcas(); pintarPainel(true);
window.addEventListener('hashchange', () => trocarVisao(location.hash.slice(1), true));
(async function () {
  await cicloCidade(); await cicloMapa(); await cicloServicos(); await cicloHistorico(); await cicloDN();
  await espera(1000);
  laco('cidade', cicloCidade, 2000); laco('mapa', cicloMapa, 2000); laco('servicos', cicloServicos, 6000); laco('historico', cicloHistorico, 5000); laco('dianoite', cicloDN, 4000);
})();

`examples/mindustry-homing/README.md`:

```md
# Mindustry: a free single-player homing lab

An original MIT-licensed JSON/JavaScript example for **Mindustry 160.7**. Two copper-fed turrets fire at
identically scripted moving targets with fixed aim. The bullet definitions use `MissileBulletType` and
change `homingPower` from **0** to **0.08**; colours identify the lanes. This is a controlled steering
demonstration, not a normal-play damage benchmark.

## Tested setup and cost

- Mindustry 160.7, official [author's itch.io distribution](https://anuke.itch.io/mindustry), which offers a
  free download. Steam, an external mod loader, paid assets and a fal API key are not required.
- macOS 15.7, Apple M1 Max, official x86_64 app under Rosetta, bundled Java 25.0.1.
- Original case built with Codex (GPT-6) and Universal Modder 0.2.0, revision `8370faa`.
  Knowledge search, scan, backup and publication checks were used. Mac window control used desktop
  automation, not the Windows-only `um win` commands.
- Running the finished mod needs no coding-agent account. Editing with a hosted agent may incur usage
  fees. Other systems and multiplayer have not been tested.

## Package and run

From this repository's root on the tested Mac:

```sh
cd examples/mindustry-homing
python3 -m zipfile -c /tmp/modlab-homing-lab.zip mod.json content scripts sprites README.md LICENSE
```

1. Back up existing game data and use a separate lab profile. Save and exit any other active world.
2. In Mindustry, choose **Mods → Open Folder**, quit, copy the ZIP into that folder, keep it zipped, and
   restart. `mod.json` must be at the archive root. The Mac **Import File** picker did not open during
   testing; that alternative remains unverified.
3. Choose **ModLab Homing Lab [F8]** from the main menu or press F8 (some Macs need Fn+F8). Wait for the
   30-second simulation-time comparison. The helper reads turret `totalShots` and counts real target
   `UnitDamageEvent` events; it writes `modlab-last-run.json` in the game-data folder.
4. F8 restarts this temporary arena; F9 exits. The helper rejects network connections and other active
   worlds. It does not save a campaign.
5. Exit with F9, disable the mod in Mods and restart to remove the lab menu entry. Restore a pre-install
   backup for any existing world that used the new blocks.

## Read the saved run

The helper writes `modlab-last-run.json` to the game-data folder, the parent of the folder that
**Mods → Open Folder** opens. It is plain JSON, written when the 30 seconds are up and again when F9 exits the lab:

- `shots` and `hits` have two entries. Index 0 is the straight baseline lane and index 1 is the homing lane.
  Shots are each turret's `totalShots`; hits are `UnitDamageEvent`s on a lane's target from bullets its own
  turret fired.
- `simulationTicks` and `durationSeconds` (ticks / 60) are simulation time, which stops while the game is
  paused.
- `finished` is `false` if F9 ended the run before 30 seconds. Those counts are not a finished comparison.

A lane with zero shots has no hit percentage. The counts describe this scripted arena only: they don't prove
where a log came from, and they are not a normal-play benchmark.

Optional: ModLab's [run log viewer](https://github.com/liubrain39/universal-modder-run-log-viewer) (MIT, by
this example's author) is a static page that shows both lanes, checks the counts and timing, and previews or
downloads the selected run as CSV. Served locally with `python3 -m http.server`, it reads the file in the
browser and sends it nowhere.

## Recorded verification

The [existing field note](../../knowledge/games/mindustry/mindustry-160-7-a-reproducible-json-and-javascript-homing-la.md)
documents both the original run and a clean-profile installation of the released 0.1.0 ZIP. Each recorded
**25 launches** per lane: **1 target-damage event** for straight bullets and **24** for guided bullets.
The six engine-loaded files here are copied unchanged from that tested mod; this example's README and
packaging are separate from the historical ZIP checksum in [the saved record](evidence/mindustry-verification.json).

Targets have scripted movement and extra health. Engine timing can change the counts. The suggested
`homingPower: 0.02` edit is an unmeasured learner experiment; keep the baseline unchanged and edit one
value before repackaging. Independent learner acceptance and normal automatic-targeting balance remain
unverified. The recorded clip is a montage of actual game-window screenshots, not continuous 24-fps video.

[Recorded workshop, complete installation and recovery](https://modlabguides.online/workshop/mindustry-homing).
The source and geometric turret sprites are original ModLab work under the included MIT license; no
game files or extracted assets are included. ModLab is independent of Mindustry and Universal Modder.

```

`examples/mindustry-homing/scripts/main.js`:

```js
// ModLab: a deliberately controlled SINGLE-PLAYER laboratory.
// The two lanes use the real Mindustry turret / bullet / collision engine.
// The moving target is scripted, and both turrets aim at a fixed marker.
// This demonstrates steering; it is not a normal-play DPS benchmark.
var active = false;
var clock = 0;
var targets = [];
var turrets = [];
var shots = [0, 0];
var hits = [0, 0];
var centers = [176, 464];
var hud = null;
var statusLabel = null;
var limit = 60 * 30;
var done = false;
var modId = 'modlab-homing';
var previousMinZoom = null;
var previousScale = null;

function laneFor(bullet){
  if(!bullet || !bullet.owner) return -1;
  for(var i = 0; i < turrets.length; i++) if(bullet.owner.id === turrets[i].id) return i;
  return -1;
}

function spawnTarget(i){
  var u = UnitTypes.flare.create(Team.crux);
  u.set(centers[i], 304);
  u.health = 10000;
  u.add();
  u.controller(extend(AIController, { updateUnit: function(){} }));
  targets[i] = u;
}

function recordResult(){
  var result = {
    game: 'Mindustry', build: String(Version.build) + '.' + String(Version.revision), modVersion: '0.1.0',
    simulationTicks: clock, durationSeconds: clock / 60,
    method: 'real desktop engine; scripted identical targets; fixed aim; no splash; steering demonstration, not a normal-play benchmark',
    shots: shots, hits: hits, finished: done,
    observer: String(Vars.player.unit().type), observerDead: Vars.player.dead()
  };
  Vars.dataDirectory.child('modlab-last-run.json').writeString(JSON.stringify(result, null, 2));
}

function startLab(){
  if(Vars.net.active()){
    Vars.ui.showInfo('This lab is single-player only. Disconnect first.');
    return;
  }
  if(!Vars.state.isMenu() && !active){
    Vars.ui.showInfo('Return to the main menu before opening the lab. Save your current game first.');
    return;
  }
  if(hud !== null){hud.remove(); hud = null;}
  active = false;
  Vars.logic.reset();
  var rules = new Rules();
  rules.infiniteResources = true;
  rules.teams.get(Team.sharded).cheat = true;
  rules.waves = false;
  rules.canGameOver = false;
  rules.enemyCoreBuildRadius = 0;
  rules.unitCap = 30;
  Vars.state.rules = rules;
  Vars.world.loadGenerator(80, 62, cons(function(tiles){
    tiles.fill();
    for(var x = 0; x < 80; x++){
      for(var y = 0; y < 62; y++){
        var tile = tiles.getn(x,y);
        tile.setFloor((x === 40 || y === 8 || y === 49) ? Blocks.darkPanel3 : Blocks.stone);
      }
    }
    tiles.getn(5,5).setBlock(Blocks.coreShard, Team.sharded, 0);
    tiles.getn(22,14).setBlock(Vars.content.block(modId + '-baseline'), Team.sharded, 0);
    tiles.getn(58,14).setBlock(Vars.content.block(modId + '-homing'), Team.sharded, 0);
  }));
  Vars.player.team(Team.sharded);
  Vars.logic.play();
  Vars.player.set(320, 248);
  var observer = UnitTypes.alpha.create(Team.sharded);
  observer.set(320, 248);
  observer.add();
  Vars.player.unit(observer);
  if(previousMinZoom === null){
    previousMinZoom = Vars.renderer.minZoom;
    previousScale = Vars.renderer.getScale();
  }
  Vars.renderer.minZoom = 0.5;
  Vars.renderer.minZoomInGame = 0.5;
  Vars.renderer.setScale(Math.min(Core.graphics.getWidth()/720, Core.graphics.getHeight()/600));
  Core.camera.position.set(320,248);
  turrets = [Vars.world.build(22,14), Vars.world.build(58,14)];
  targets = [];
  shots = [0,0]; hits = [0,0]; clock = 0; done = false;
  spawnTarget(0); spawnTarget(1);
  active = true;
  hud = new Table();
  hud.setFillParent(true);
  hud.top().marginTop(8);
  hud.table(Styles.black6, cons(function(t){
    t.defaults().pad(5);
    t.add('[accent]MODLAB / HOMING LAB[]').colspan(3).get().setFontScale(0.8); t.row();
    t.add('LEFT: straight     |     RIGHT: homing').colspan(3).get().setFontScale(0.7); t.row();
    statusLabel = t.add('Running a 30-second steering comparison...').colspan(3).get();
    statusLabel.setFontScale(0.7);
    t.row();
    t.button('Restart [F8]', run(startLab)).width(160);
    t.button('Exit lab [F9]', run(exitLab)).width(160);
    t.row();
    t.add('[lightgray]Identical targets / Fixed aim / Real engine[]').colspan(3).get().setFontScale(0.65);
  }));
  Core.scene.add(hud);
  print('LAB_START: desktop steering comparison');
}

function exitLab(){
  if(!active) return;
  recordResult();
  active = false;
  if(hud !== null){hud.remove();hud = null;}
  if(previousMinZoom !== null){
    Vars.renderer.minZoom = previousMinZoom;
    Vars.renderer.setScale(previousScale);
    previousMinZoom = null;
  }
  Vars.state.set(GameState.State.menu);
  Vars.logic.reset();
}

Events.on(ClientLoadEvent, cons(function(){
  Vars.ui.menufrag.addButton('ModLab Homing Lab [F8]', run(startLab));
  Events.fire(new ResizeEvent());
  print('READY: ModLab Homing Lab 0.1.0. F8 opens a local laboratory from the main menu.');
}));

Events.on(UnitDamageEvent, cons(function(e){
  if(!active || done) return;
  var i = laneFor(e.bullet);
  if(i >= 0 && e.unit.id === targets[i].id) hits[i]++;
}));
Events.run(Trigger.update, run(function(){
  if(Vars.headless) return;
  if(Core.input.keyTap(KeyCode.f8)) startLab();
  if(Core.input.keyTap(KeyCode.f9)) exitLab();
  if(!active) return;
  if(Vars.net.active() || Vars.state.isMenu()){
    active = false;
    if(hud !== null){hud.remove();hud = null;}
    return;
  }
  if(Vars.state.isPaused()) return;
  if(!done) clock += Time.delta;
  var motion = clock / 68;
  for(var i=0;i<2;i++){
    if(!targets[i].isAdded()) spawnTarget(i);
    targets[i].set(centers[i] + 72 * Math.sin(motion), 304 + 18 * Math.cos(motion));
    targets[i].rotation = Math.cos(motion) >= 0 ? 0 : 180;
    targets[i].health = 10000;
    targets[i].isShooting = false;
    for(var m=0;m<targets[i].mounts.length;m++) targets[i].mounts[m].shoot = false;
    shots[i] = turrets[i].totalShots;
    if(turrets[i].totalAmmo < 4) turrets[i].handleStack(Items.copper, 10, null);
    turrets[i].control(LAccess.shoot, centers[i]/8, 304/8, done ? 0 : 1, 0);
  }
  if(!done && clock >= limit){done = true;recordResult();print('LAB_FINISH: ' + JSON.stringify({shots:shots,hits:hits}));}
  statusLabel.setText((done ? '[accent]Finished[]' : (clock/60).toFixed(1) + ' / 30s') + '  |  straight ' + hits[0] + '/' + shots[0] + ' hits  |  homing ' + hits[1] + '/' + shots[1] + ' hits');
}));

```

`examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough/README.md`:

```md
# Minecraft x GTA V: a passthrough mod

Real Minecraft Java 26.3 running next to GTA V (story mode) and drawn into it. GTA's camera drives Minecraft's,
GTA's ground becomes invisible collision in Minecraft, Minecraft's picture (colour + depth, plus the hand/HUD) is
composited into GTA's frame against GTA's depth buffer, and what happens in Minecraft happens in GTA too.

- **Build** with Minecraft blocks in Los Santos. Placed blocks become invisible GTA props, so people and cars stop
  at your walls.
- **TNT and creepers** blow up in both games: each Minecraft explosion is also a GTA explosion.
- **Minecraft weapons with GTA effects.** Crossbow fireworks burst as GTA rockets where they hit, arrows that hit
  a person or a car land as GTA bullets, a sword swing sends people flying and shoves cars, and an ender pearl
  moves GTA's player.
- **Elytra flight.** Minecraft's physics fly Steve and GTA follows with a chase camera. Once flight is armed,
  Space or a fall from anything tall takes off, the mouse steers, fireworks boost, and touching down lands you
  back on foot.
- **Mobs vs police.** Minecraft's hostile mobs hunt GTA's people, GTA's police shoot back, and damage crosses over
  both ways.
- **The Nether.** Walk through a lit nether portal and the ground around it turns into the Nether, nether mobs
  pour out, GTA's sky goes red while the clock races to midnight, and people and cars on lava or fire burn.

It was built and tested in GTA V Legacy (Steam, game build 3889) with ScriptHookV 3889.0 and ReShade 6.8.0 in
September 2026. This folder is that code with its paths made configurable. A few shot configs from the demo
videos are included.

## How it works

```
GTA V (story mode)                                    Minecraft 26.3 + Fabric (mc/)
  MCPassthrough.asi (gta/src)                           dev.rehan.passthrough
    script.cpp  -- WebSocket 127.0.0.1:25599 ------->     HostLink: cam / ground / key / slot / cmd
                <------------------------------------     explosion events
    compositor.cpp (ReShade add-on)  <-- shared memory --  FrameExporter: world RGBA + depth, overlay RGBA
    MCPassthrough.fx: depth test + overlay                 "Local\MCPassthroughFrame"
```

Coordinates: 1 GTA metre = 1 block; GTA (x, y, z) -> Minecraft (x, z + yOffset, -y); Minecraft yaw = 180 - heading,
pitch = -pitch. The script picks yOffset so the ground where the player stands lands on a whole block (F8 re-levels).

- **Every GTA frame**, the ScriptHookV script (`gta/src/script.cpp`) sends the camera GTA rendered with and the
  player's feet and heading (`cam`). Minecraft renders from that camera with no sky, fog or clouds, and Steve
  stands where GTA's player (hidden) stands.
- **Ground.** The script probes GTA's ground in the columns around the player (40 blocks out, 160 probes a
  frame) and sends them as `ground`. The mod fills them with barrier blocks, so blocks, mobs and items rest on
  GTA's world. Each block you place or break comes back as a GTA prop (at most 400 of them; GTA crashes at
  around 1500 script objects).
- **Frames.** The mod copies Minecraft's world colour and depth just before the hand is drawn, then the hand,
  HUD and screens as a separate overlay, into a named shared-memory mapping (three slots, asynchronous GPU
  readback). The ReShade add-on (`compositor.cpp`) uploads the newest frame into textures. `MCPassthrough.fx`
  then draws Minecraft wherever it is nearer than GTA's depth buffer and puts the overlay on top. Before that,
  the effect re-projects Minecraft's frame from the pose it was rendered with to GTA's current camera,
  which hides the link's latency. It also relights the frame from GTA's blurred picture, gives it GTA's colour
  grade and haze, and softens the edges.
- **Events back.** Explosions, projectiles in flight (traced through GTA's world), sword swings, ender pearls,
  mobs and the Nether's hot blocks go to the plugin, which acts them out in GTA.
- **Input.** GTA has the focus, so the plugin forwards the mouse buttons, the wheel and the number keys to
  Minecraft and keeps GTA from acting on them.

## Files

| path | what it is |
|---|---|
| `mc/` | the Fabric mod (Java 25, Loom): `HostLink` (WebSocket server), `FrameExporter` + `SharedMemory` (the frames), `PlayerSync`, `WorldBridge` (barriers, block sync, explosions, projectiles), `MobWar`, `Nether`, and the mixins |
| `gta/src/script.cpp` | the ScriptHookV script: camera, ground, input, explosions, director ops, flight, mobs vs police, the Nether |
| `gta/src/compositor.cpp` | the ReShade add-on: uploads Minecraft's frame and sets the effect's uniforms |
| `gta/src/natives.h` | the GTA natives the script calls, by hash |
| `gta/src/ws.cpp` | a small WebSocket client |
| `gta/shaders/MCPassthrough.fx` | the ReShade effect: depth test, re-projection, relighting, haze, edges, glow, overlay |
| `gta/fetch_deps.sh`, `build.sh`, `build.bat`, `install.sh` | fetch ScriptHookV and ReShade, build with MSVC, install into the game folder |
| `gta/tests/` | `fakegta.cpp` (a GTA stand-in) and `ws_test.cpp` (the WebSocket client against the running mod) |
| `host/` | tests without GTA (`fakehost.py`, `place_test.py`, `tnt_test.py`), `mcframe.py` (reads the shared memory), `cmd.py` (runs Minecraft commands) |
| `video/` | the director (scripted shots) and the recording and cutting scripts, plus shot configs |
| `gradle.sh` | runs Gradle on Windows from WSL |

## Requirements

- **Windows 10/11 with WSL.** The scripts are bash (run them in WSL) and batch.
- **Minecraft Java Edition 26.3**, Fabric Loader 0.19.5 or newer, and Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3.
- **GTA V Legacy** on Steam, story mode. It must be the Legacy edition (`GTA5.exe`); the Enhanced edition isn't
  supported here.
- **ScriptHookV** and its ASI loader (`dinput8.dll`), by Alexander Blade. ScriptHookV only runs on the game
  builds it supports, so after a GTA update, wait for a new ScriptHookV and run `fetch_deps.sh` again.
- **ReShade 6.8.0 with add-on support.** Both ReShade and ScriptHookV are downloaded by `gta/fetch_deps.sh`.
- **MSVC**: Visual Studio 2022 or newer with the C++ desktop tools (x64).
- **JDK 25**, for example Temurin 25. `gradle.sh` wants a Windows one; `./gradlew` on its own takes any.
- **Python 3.12 for the host tools.**
  - Windows Python with `websockets` runs the director and the host tools; `fakehost.py` also needs `numpy`
    and `Pillow`.
  - WSL Python with `Pillow` and a Linux `ffmpeg` cut the videos.
  - Recording needs a Windows ffmpeg with gfxcapture: `um win setup` downloads one.

Paths come from environment variables, with these defaults:

| variable | default | used by |
|---|---|---|
| `PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR` | `C:\dev\passthrough` | everything: the Windows working folder with the `mc\` and `gta\` build mirrors, `gradle-home\`, `jdk25\`, `pyenv\`, `mcgame\`, `takes\`, `shots\`, `gta_save\` |
| `PASSTHROUGH_JDK` | `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\jdk25` | `gradle.sh` |
| `PASSTHROUGH_MC_DIR` | `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\mcgame` | `gradle.sh install`: the game dir of your Minecraft launcher profile |
| `GTA_DIR` | GTA V Legacy (Steam app 271590), found in your Steam libraries | `gta/install.sh` |
| `RUNTIME`, `BUILD` | `gta/third_party/runtime`, `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\gta\build` | `gta/install.sh` |
| `VCVARS` | the newest Visual Studio with C++ tools (vswhere) | `gta/build.bat`, `gta/tests/build_fakegta.bat` |
| `PASSTHROUGH_PY` | `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\pyenv\Scripts\python.exe` | `video/take.py`, `video/go.py`: the Windows Python the director runs with |
| `UM_FFMPEG_WIN` | um's download, or `ffmpeg` on PATH | `video/record.py`, `video/director.py scout` |
| `MC_CLIENT_JAR` | the client jar Loom cached when `mc/` was built | `video/titles.py` (the Minecraft font) |
| `GTA_SAVE_DIR` | `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\gta_save` | `video/go.py save` |

## Build, install, run

1. **The mod.** From WSL, `./gradle.sh build` mirrors `mc/` to `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\mc` and builds it there
   with the Windows JDK. Anywhere with JDK 25, `cd mc && ./gradlew build` builds the same jar, at
   `mc/build/libs/passthrough-0.1.0.jar`.
2. **A Minecraft launcher profile with its own game dir.** The mod changes options: no clouds, no view bobbing,
   a 120 fps cap, and it keeps running unfocused. It also creates a void creative world called `passthrough` and
   opens it by itself. So give it a game dir apart from your own worlds.
   - Install Fabric Loader for 26.3 with the Fabric installer.
   - In the launcher, add an installation with the `fabric-loader-0.19.5-26.3` version and a game directory of
     its own, for example `C:\dev\passthrough\mcgame`. If the installer can't add the profile itself (it failed
     with the Microsoft Store launcher), add it by hand.
   - Put Fabric API in `<game dir>\mods`. `./gradle.sh install` builds the mod and copies it there too
     (`PASSTHROUGH_MC_DIR`).

   For development, `./gradle.sh runClient` starts a dev client instead (game dir `mc\run` in the mirror, offline
   account).
3. **The GTA side**, from WSL:
   ```bash
   gta/fetch_deps.sh   # ScriptHookV SDK + ReShade headers into gta/third_party/, the runtime DLLs into third_party/runtime/
   gta/build.sh        # mirrors gta/ to <PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\gta and builds build\MCPassthrough.asi with MSVC
   gta/install.sh      # copies it all into the GTA V folder
   ```
   `install.sh` adds `ScriptHookV.dll`, `dinput8.dll` (the ASI loader), `MCPassthrough.asi`, `args.txt`
   (`-nobattleye -noBE`) and ReShade. ReShade goes in as `ReShade64.asi`, so the ASI loader loads it: GTA
   loads the system `dxgi.dll` ahead of a proxy in its folder, so the usual `dxgi.dll` install never runs. It
   also writes `ReShade.ini` (if there is none), `ReShadePreset.ini`, and the effect in
   `reshade-shaders\Shaders\`.
   - It stops rather than replaces a `dinput8.dll`, `ReShade64.asi` or `args.txt` that isn't its own
     (`FORCE=1` overrides).
   - `install.sh --remove` deletes the files it adds. It deletes `ReShade.ini` only if install wrote it, which
     install records in a `.mcpassthrough_reshade_ini` marker (an install from before the marker keeps its
     `ReShade.ini`; delete that by hand). `ReShadePreset.ini` is always written and removed, so back up your own.
   - `build.bat` also works from a Windows prompt, in a copy of `gta/` with `third_party/` fetched.
4. **GTA settings.** The demo ran GTA windowed at 1920x1080, with "Pause game on focus loss" off, depth of field
   off, and post FX lowered. Minecraft's window is resized to GTA's picture, up to 1080p worth of pixels. Depth
   of field and heavy post effects blur GTA's picture but not Minecraft's.
5. **Run.**
   - Start Minecraft with that profile. Leave its window open: it renders slowly when minimized.
   - Start GTA V from Steam with BattlEye off. The `-nobattleye` in `args.txt` does it, or the BattlEye toggle
     in the Rockstar Games Launcher settings. That also keeps GTA Online out.
   - Pick Story Mode on the landing page yourself.
   - In story mode the plugin connects ("Minecraft passthrough connected"), sizes Minecraft's window to GTA's
     picture and starts sending the ground. The two can start in either order, because the plugin keeps
     reconnecting.

## Controls

| key | what it does |
|---|---|
| F7 | turns the passthrough off and on |
| F8 | re-levels Minecraft's ground to where you stand (it also happens by itself when nothing is built nearby) |
| left mouse | Minecraft's attack: break blocks, swing the sword |
| right mouse | Minecraft's use: place blocks, light TNT, shoot, throw pearls, boost with fireworks |
| mouse wheel, 1-9 | Minecraft's hotbar |
| Tab | gun mode (experimental): GTA's carbine rifle, minigun and RPG in Steve's hands, then back to Minecraft |
| Space | while flight is armed: take off with the elytra |

Everything else (walking, driving, the camera, the view key) is GTA's own, and Minecraft follows. GTA's own
attack, aim, weapon wheel and weapon keys are disabled while Minecraft has the mouse.

The mod sets up the hotbar when you join:

1. ender pearls
2. a diamond sword
3. a crossbow (multishot, quick charge)
4. a bow (power, infinity)
5. TNT
6. flint and steel
7. creeper eggs
8. grass blocks
9. fireworks

Your off hand holds explosive fireworks for the crossbow, and you get 64 arrows.

- **Elytra flight.** Flight is armed from the director: `python video\director.py op armdrive "{\"user\":1}"`.
  Then Space, or a fall from anything tall, opens the elytra.
- **The Nether.** Get obsidian (`python host\cmd.py "give @a minecraft:obsidian 64"`), build a portal, light it
  and walk through it. The director's `portal` step builds and lights one 10 m in front of you
  (`video/nether_cfg.json`).
- **Mobs vs police.** Hatch creepers, or spawn waves with `spawnmobs`. The director's `cops` op brings a
  police squad; `video/mobwar_live.py` keeps both coming while you play.

## Tests without GTA

- **`host/fakehost.py`** runs with Windows Python while Minecraft runs:
  `python host\fakehost.py [seconds] [outdir] [fp|tp]`. It flies Minecraft's camera round a few test blocks
  and gives it a flat ground. It then composites the exported frames over a synthetic scene rendered for the
  same pose, a checkerboard and a red pillar that only the "host" has. The PNGs it writes (default
  `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\fakehost_out`) show whether alignment and occlusion are right. `tp` tests third
  person.
- **`gta/tests/fakegta.cpp`** is the whole GTA half except GTA's natives. It is a D3D11 window with a
  reversed-Z depth buffer and GTA's camera conventions, with the compositor and WebSocket client compiled in.
  - Build it with `gta/build.sh tests` (`tests\fakegta.exe`).
  - To run it, put ReShade next to it as `dxgi.dll`. For a normal program the folder's `dxgi.dll` does load.
    Copy `third_party/runtime/ReShade64.dll`, and add a `ReShade.ini`, `ReShadePreset.ini` and the three
    shader files the way `install.sh` writes them.
  - `fakegta.exe [seconds] [1]` orbits the test blocks (the `1` swings the camera fast to show latency).
  - While it runs, `python video\director.py shoot video\fake_steps.json` (or `fake_cfg.json`) drives its
    stand-in player like the real plugin.
- **`gta/tests/ws_test.cpp`** checks the plugin's WebSocket client against the running mod: the handshake, a
  60 Hz camera, ground columns, a TNT command, and the explosion event coming back.
- **`host/tnt_test.py`, `host/place_test.py`** are the same kind of check from Python.

## Director and video pipeline

- **The director.** `video/director.py` (Windows Python, because Minecraft's link is on Windows' 127.0.0.1)
  scripts shots through Minecraft's link.
  - GTA ops (`{"t":"gta","op":...}`) are relayed by the mod to the plugin: teleport, walk, face, view, look,
    time, weather, ped (with a scenario or a looped animation), car, explode, drive/armdrive/flylook (flight),
    cops/mobfit (mobs vs police), and more (see `handle_director` in `script.cpp`).
  - Minecraft input (hotbar, clicks) and commands go to the mod.
  - Shot lists are JSON: `elytra_cfg.json`, `mobwar_cfg.json`, `nether_cfg.json`, and the fakegta dry runs.
    Positions are GTA coordinates, or relative to an origin and heading.
  - `director.py scout [x y z]` takes screenshots in four directions.
  - `director.py op <op> '{json}'` sends one op and prints GTA's state.
- **Takes.** From WSL, `python3 video/take.py <name> video/mobwar_cfg.json` records GTA's window while the
  director runs the shot list.
  - Audio comes from GTA and Minecraft separately, each from its own process (the repo's
    `um/ps1/ProcLoopback`).
  - It writes `<PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\takes\<name>.*` with an event log.
- **Cuts.** `video/cut.py <name> out.mp4 [head] [length] [title]` and `video/cut_segments.py` cut a take to
  1080p with one-line titles in Minecraft's font. The font sheet is Mojang's, so `titles.py` reads it from
  your own Minecraft jar.
- **Helpers.**
  - `video/go.py` waits for GTA and the link, installs a save, backing the old one up, and scouts.
  - `video/backup_rec.py` records until a `STOP` file appears.
  - `video/mobwar_live.py` keeps mob waves and police coming while you play.

## Safety

- **Story mode only; never GTA Online.** BattlEye protects GTA Online. This runs with BattlEye off, which also
  keeps Online from starting, and ScriptHookV closes the game if it goes online anyway. Don't try to get a
  modded game near Online.
- **Never automate clicks on GTA's landing page while someone is at the keyboard.** During development a script
  focused GTA and clicked Story Mode while the user was typing in another window. Their keystrokes landed in
  GTA, which showed "attempting to access GTA Online servers with an altered version". ScriptHookV blocked it,
  but don't risk it. Pick Story Mode by hand. `go.py` never clicks.
- **The game folder.** `install.sh` lists what it adds, won't replace another mod's loader or ReShade, and
  `--remove` takes it all out again.
- **Saves.** `go.py save` keeps your save files as `.bak` before it replaces them.
- **Processes.** Scripts stop GTA by its exact PID, never by name pattern.
- **The link.** It listens on 127.0.0.1:25599 only, with no token, so any program on the machine can send it
  commands. Close Minecraft when you're done.
- **Redistribution.** ScriptHookV and ReShade are fetched from their own sites and aren't redistributed here,
  and neither is anything from Minecraft or GTA.

`examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough/gradle.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# From WSL: sync the Fabric project to the Windows working folder and run a Gradle task there with a Windows JDK
# (Minecraft has to run on Windows, next to GTA).
#   ./gradle.sh build | runClient | genSources
#   ./gradle.sh install      build, then copy the jar into the launcher profile's game dir (<game dir>\mods)
# PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR  the Windows working folder (default C:\dev\passthrough); the project is mirrored to its mc\,
#                      and Gradle's cache is its gradle-home\
# PASSTHROUGH_JDK      a Windows JDK 25 (default <PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\jdk25)
# PASSTHROUGH_MC_DIR   the game dir of the launcher profile you play with (default <PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\mcgame)
# On Linux or macOS, `cd mc && ./gradlew build` with JDK 25 builds the same jar.
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
WIN=${PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR:-'C:\dev\passthrough'}
DST=$(wslpath -u "$WIN\\mc")
if [ "$1" = install ]; then
	"$0" build
	MODS=$(wslpath -u "${PASSTHROUGH_MC_DIR:-$WIN\\mcgame}")/mods
	mkdir -p "$MODS"
	cp -v "$DST/build/libs/passthrough-$(sed -n 's/^version=//p' "$HERE/mc/gradle.properties").jar" "$MODS/"
	exit 0
fi
mkdir -p "$DST"
rsync -a --delete --exclude build --exclude .gradle --exclude run --exclude '*.log' "$HERE/mc/" "$DST/"
# cmd.exe starts in the mirror (a Windows folder, not \\wsl$); .\ because cmd may not look in the current folder
# (NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath). The JDK and Gradle home go over as environment.
cd "$DST"
export JAVA_HOME=${PASSTHROUGH_JDK:-"$WIN\\jdk25"} GRADLE_USER_HOME="$WIN\\gradle-home"
export WSLENV=${WSLENV:+$WSLENV:}JAVA_HOME:GRADLE_USER_HOME
cmd.exe /c ".\\gradlew.bat --console=plain $*" 2>&1 | grep -v "UNC paths\|CMD.EXE was started\|Defaulting to Windows"
exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}

```

`examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough/gta/build.bat`:

```bat
@echo off
rem Builds MCPassthrough.asi (ScriptHookV script + ReShade add-on) with MSVC into build\. Run fetch_deps.sh first.
rem Uses the newest Visual Studio with the C++ x64 tools; set VCVARS to another vcvars64.bat to pick one.
setlocal
set HERE=%~dp0
if not defined VCVARS for /f "usebackq delims=" %%i in (`"%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe" -latest -products * -requires Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 -property installationPath`) do set "VCVARS=%%i\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat"
if not exist "%VCVARS%" (echo No Visual Studio with the C++ x64 tools was found. Install "Desktop development with C++" ^(Visual Studio 2022 or its Build Tools^), or set VCVARS to your vcvars64.bat& exit /b 1)
if not exist "%HERE%third_party\shv\ScriptHookV.lib" (echo third_party is missing: run fetch_deps.sh first& exit /b 1)
call "%VCVARS%" >nul || exit /b 1
if not exist "%HERE%build" mkdir "%HERE%build"
cl /nologo /LD /O2 /EHsc /std:c++20 /MT /W3 /DWIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN /DNOMINMAX ^
  /I "%HERE%third_party\shv" /I "%HERE%third_party\reshade" ^
  "%HERE%src\script.cpp" "%HERE%src\compositor.cpp" "%HERE%src\ws.cpp" ^
  /Fo"%HERE%build\\" /Fe"%HERE%build\MCPassthrough.asi" ^
  /link "%HERE%third_party\shv\ScriptHookV.lib" ws2_32.lib user32.lib

```

`examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough/gta/build.sh`:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
# Build from WSL: mirror gta/ to <PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR>\gta (default C:\dev\passthrough\gta) and run MSVC there.
#   ./build.sh          build\MCPassthrough.asi (build.bat); run fetch_deps.sh first
#   ./build.sh tests    that, then tests\fakegta.exe and tests\ws_test.exe (tests\build_fakegta.bat)
set -e
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
WIN=${PASSTHROUGH_WIN_DIR:-'C:\dev\passthrough'}
DST=$(wslpath -u "$WIN\\gta")
mkdir -p "$DST"
rsync -a --delete --exclude build --exclude 'tests/*.exe' --exclude 'tests/*.obj' "$HERE/" "$DST/"
# cmd.exe starts in the mirror; .\ because cmd may not look in the current folder (NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath)
cd "$DST"
BATS='.\build.bat'
[ "$1" = tests ] && BATS='.\build.bat && .\tests\build_fakegta.bat'
cmd.exe /c "$BATS" 2>&1 | grep -v "UNC paths\|CMD.EXE was started\|Defaulting to Windows"
exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}
