# An external game master for Caves of Qud: a scripting-mod bridge, save identity and native effects

> A C# scripting mod connects Caves of Qud to an external Python program (an AI game master called Randur)
> over a loopback socket, without ever touching game objects off the game thread. In real runs it survived
> reconnects and a save/reload, created NPCs, items, effects, reputation changes and an owned side quest
> through the game's own systems, and didn't repeat any of them when the same command was replayed. The
> bridge itself is private; this note records what the game does and the traps, so you can build your own.

## Setup
- Caves of Qud on Steam (Windows). The runs were on 2026-08-29 to 2026-08-31; the exact game and Unity build
  wasn't recorded, so don't read this as "works on the latest build".
- The mod is a Qud C# scripting mod. Its project targets `netstandard2.1` / C# 9 and references the installed
  `Assembly-CSharp.dll` and `Newtonsoft.Json.dll`. Mono.Cecil was used to read the installed method signatures
  and bodies (nothing decompiled is published).
- Test in a copied profile with a disposable save. Credit: Freehold Games, and the Qud wiki's
  [modding overview](https://wiki.cavesofqud.com/wiki/Modding:Overview) for the scripting route. The wiki's
  Modding pages cover `[HasCallAfterGameLoaded]`/`[CallAfterGameLoaded]`, `StatShifter`, quests and
  conversations.

## Route and why
Qud compiles and loads C# scripting mods itself, so no external loader is needed. The external program only
ever sees plain data objects:
- In a `[CallAfterGameLoaded]` method (on a class marked `[HasCallAfterGameLoaded]`), capture the game thread's
  `SynchronizationContext` and post every game
  access to it. A worker thread does the socket I/O and never dereferences a Qud `GameObject`. Thread-safe JSON
  serialisation doesn't make game access thread-safe.
- The bridge took a snapshot about every 500 ms and ran at most one queued action per snapshot.
- Actions are a fixed list of narrow, typed capabilities with allowlists (no arbitrary blueprints, reflection,
  console passthrough or generated C#). The game checks legality, runs the effect on the game thread and then
  re-reads the game state to report what actually happened.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Which identity survives what
| Identity | What it is | Don't use it as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `XRLGame.GameID` | The save/world. A normal reload keeps it | The player's name or the bridge connection |
| Bridge session | One connection between the mod and the external program | The world, or proof of save lineage |
| Timeline generation | A counter the mod bumps on a rewind (below) | A durable save-lineage proof |
| Game object ID | An object seen in the current scope | A permanent identity, or anything matched by display name |

The mod treats it as a rewind when the `XRLGame` object is replaced but `GameID` stays the same, or when
`Turns` goes down. On a rewind it bumps the generation and drops queued actions. The external side keeps its raw
history but stops using facts from the abandoned branch, keyed by `(Turns, TimeTicks)`. One case can't be told
apart: restoring a save at exactly the last recorded position in a new process looks like a normal restart.

### Effects through the game's own systems
These were the mechanisms behind each action in the tested run. The capability names are the bridge's own,
not a Qud API.

| Action | Game mechanism | Checked after the action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Introduce an NPC with its own dialogue | A serialisable `IPart` handling `BeginConversationEvent` | One non-hostile NPC with the authored dialogue; same NPC after reload |
| Unique reward item | A precompiled `IPart`, equip/unequip events, `StatShifter` | One item; exactly +1 while equipped, removed on unequip; same after reload |
| Temporary stat effect | A serialisable `Effect`, `ApplyEffect`, duration, `StatShifter` | One +1 defensive modifier; duration left after reload; expired later |
| Permanent stat change | `Statistic.AddShift`, keeping the `Guid` it returns as the shift's identity | Exactly +1 base attribute; persisted; a replay didn't reapply it |
| Faction reputation | `Factions` lookup, `The.Game.PlayerReputation.Get`/`Modify` (the lowercase forms are obsolete) | One +25 change to an existing faction; persisted; not reapplied |
| Owned side quest | A fully initialised `Quest`/`QuestStep` in the quest registry | Exactly one optional one-step quest; same quest after reload |
| Advance that quest | The owned quest's objective state | Only that objective finished; visible in the journal; not repeated |
| Local encounter | Allowlisted blueprints, `Brain` and faction disposition | Two neutral creatures at a safe distance |

- `GameObjectFactory.Factory.CreateObject` plus `Cell.AddObject` create and place objects, but safe placement
  and ownership are yours to handle. A created object's name is presentation; store the owner and action ID as
  serialised properties on your part.
- **No duplicates on replay.** Each action has a stable ID and a fingerprint of its arguments, and the success is
  recorded in the game state itself (a serialised part property, the stored stat shift, or quest properties),
  not only in the external program. A replay finds the existing result instead of creating another. Reusing an ID
  with different arguments is a conflict. If the recorded object is gone, that needs a decision, not a silent
  re-creation.
- **Saves hold your types.** Parts and effects serialise their data only; sockets and request objects stay
  transient. Keeping the mod enabled with the external program offline works. Removing the mod that defines a
  saved part or effect type was not tested and shouldn't be assumed safe.
- **Readable clues:** a created book or note doesn't make its text known to the player. Treat it as known only
  once its Read action has run.
- **Autoexplore:** a mod can interrupt the player's autoexplore when a chosen object first becomes visible, but
  only if the decision is already made in the game. The bridge "arms" the exact target in advance and interrupts
  at the first visibility check (`arm_until_visible`). Waiting for the external program took about four seconds,
  by which time the player had walked past.

## Build steps
1. Copy the profile and save. Reference the installed assemblies; record their versions and hashes. Don't publish
   the assemblies or a decompiler dump.
2. In `[CallAfterGameLoaded]`, capture the game thread's `SynchronizationContext`. Snapshot on the game thread,
   pass immutable data to a loopback socket worker.
3. Require a loaded game (GameID, player, zone) before accepting actions. Tag every request with GameID, bridge
   session and timeline generation, and drop queued work when any of them changes.
4. Implement one narrow action at a time: validate on the game thread, apply the one effect, re-read the game
   state, and report "accepted", "performed" and each check separately.
5. Save and reload, reconnect, then replay the same action ID: expect the existing result and no new object or
   modifier. Also test a changed payload under the same ID, and a recorded object that has gone missing.

## Verification
- **In the real game (Steam, August 2026):** a save/reload kept `GameID`, opened a new bridge session and
  needed an explicit re-arm; owned content survived it, and an earlier restart rebuilt the same content without
  duplicates. The eight actions in the table above worked with the checks listed, including one save/reload and
  replay suppression. Strong attention interrupted autoexplore, and the weakest level didn't. An owned NPC
  survived a restart and was seen and talked to.
- **Offline tests (mocked game side):** stale connections and old sequences can't overwrite state, pending
  commands for another world are cancelled, and a lower-turn rewind excludes the abandoned branch.
- **Not verified:** the exact game build; current builds (nothing was re-run for this note); other mod
  combinations; removing the mod from a save that uses its types; multi-step quests and dialogue trees.

## Gotchas
1. **The quest is created, but the external program times out.** **Cause:** `The.Game.StartQuest` and
   `FinishQuestStep` call `PopupStartQuest`/`PopupFinishQuestStep`, UI that waits for the player after the
   state has already changed. **Fix:** register a fully initialised
   owned quest and raise the normal events without the blocking popup. A timeout doesn't mean nothing happened;
   read the game state before retrying.
2. **A new NPC speaks unrelated merchant dialogue.** **Cause:** its blueprint inherits a vanilla
   `ConversationScript`. **Fix:** remove the inherited conversation part from your NPC and handle
   `BeginConversationEvent` in your own serialised part.
3. **A replay still changes the attribute.** **Cause:** the dedup record lived only in the external program, and
   some reconnect/reload paths lost it. **Fix:** record the action in the game state and check the exact stored
   stat shift or object before changing anything.
4. **Paused menus look like a dropped connection.** **Cause:** capture pauses on the game thread while the
   transport keeps resending the last snapshot. **Fix:** accept a repeated sequence number only when the snapshot
   is identical, and don't count it as new data.
5. **Old knowledge survives a rewind.** **Cause:** `GameID` identifies the save, not the timeline. **Fix:** watch
   for a replaced `XRLGame` or falling `Turns`, drop queued work, and stop using facts from the abandoned branch.
6. **Autoexplore isn't interrupted.** **Cause:** the external round trip (about 4 s) missed the moment the
   object became visible. **Fix:** arm the exact target in advance and interrupt inside the game at first
   visibility.
7. **Reading a book the game master planted triggers yet another story beat.** **Cause:** the pickup and
   read events came from the mod's own delivery and were taken as the player's interest. **Fix:** keep the
   authored origin on later events, count a passive pickup or read as attention only, and wait for a deliberate
   act (talking, fighting) before planning more.

## Assets
None. No game binaries, saves or decompiled code are included.

## Open questions
- Which Qud build this was, and whether the same calls work on the current one.
- Whether a save that contains the mod's parts and effects loads cleanly after the mod is removed.
- A public minimal bridge would let others re-run these checks.

# Cities: Skylines 1 and 2 modding: official APIs, editors, and the .crp/.locale containers

Both Cities: Skylines games are Unity titles that ship a **supported** modding route, so nothing here
touches anti-cheat or ownership checks. This note is the map of that route for an agent: which API to
write against, which editor produces which asset, and the two container formats that keep coming up
(`.crp`, `.locale`). Format knowledge is from the community/XeNTaX side; API knowledge is from the
official Paradox wikis. I have **not** built or loaded a mod.

## Setup
- **CS1** — Unity 5-era, Steam app **255710**. Mods are C# assemblies against the game's **Modding API**,
  plus assets/maps made in the in-game editors. Distribute/install through the Content Manager / Workshop.
- **CS2** — Unity DOTS/ECS. Code mods are C# built with the **Modding Toolchain**; content is made in the
  all-in-one Editor and shared on **Paradox Mods**. The CS2 modding docs are explicitly marked
  **Beta Documentation** and are version-badged per page — check the badge before trusting a page.
- CS2 supports building mods **on Linux via Proton** (see the wiki "Modding Toolchain on Linux" page).

## Route and why
Route: **loader-api** — use the shipped API rather than hooking the engine. The APIs are the sanctioned
path and survive patches far better than memory patches. Asset work uses the **asset-only** route through
the in-game editors. A native-hook route is neither needed nor supported here.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
### CS1
- Two in-game editors: **Map Editor** and **Asset Editor** (plus **Road Editor** and **Theme Editor**).
  The **Content Manager** installs/manages/shared content; custom **color correction** is supported.
- The **Modding API** is a C# surface allowing a mod to read, override, add or modify game features.
- Containers and formats the community hit:
  - **`.crp`** — a saved map is a single `.crp`, and it is the *same container used for any in-game asset*.
    It carries the mesh/data **and** a `.bin` portion holding object **coordinates/placement**.
  - **`.locale`** — localized text lives under `Cities Skylines/Files/Locale`, one file per language, and is
    a **compiled/proprietary binary, not plain text**; the practical editing route was a Steam Community guide.
  - Also documented on the wiki: **CRAP file format**, **Data types**, **Heightmap**, **terrain/theme** pages.
- Editing is done against a per-user **user path** (the wiki "User path" page); assets land in the user's
  content folders and are loaded as loose content, not by rewriting game files.

### CS2
- **ECS/DOTS**: gameplay is systems over components. Modding guides document **Systems** and a
  **Systems and Components catalog**, and the **PrefabSystem** (values such as capacities, rates, workers).
- Code-mod surface: **UI Modding**, **Mod Key Binding**, **Options UI**, settings files, logging, debugging
  (devUI / developer mode), localization, custom **Tools**, and an **extra assets importer**.
- Asset pipelines (buildings, props, decals, aging trees, surfaces) plus texture sharing, color variations
  and emissive setup; package and upload to Paradox Mods.

## Build steps
- **CS1:** install content via the in-game **Content Manager** (Workshop); author a map in the Map Editor or
  an asset in the Asset Editor; drop loose content in the user-path folders; write C# against the Modding API.
- **CS2:** install the **Modding Toolchain**, create a code-mod assembly, iterate with the in-game editor /
  developer mode, then publish to **Paradox Mods**. On Linux, set the toolchain up through Proton.
- To move a CS1 map between players, ship the `.crp`; do not expect a third-party 3D layout to round-trip
  (see Gotcha 2).

## Verification
- API/editor/pipeline facts: the official Paradox wikis, *Cities: Skylines* → `Modding` (page id 17140,
  last edited 2024-01-19) and *Cities: Skylines II* → `Modding` (page id 6681, last edited 2026-06-25),
  plus the CS1 sub-pages `Modding_API`, `CRAP_File_Format`, `User_path`, `Heightmap`, `Data_types`.
- `.crp`/`.locale` format facts: community XeNTaX reverse-engineering threads
  (t=12681, t=12761, t=18672, t=25039), the usual starting point for the community's
  container documentation.
- **Not verified:** I did not open the game, extract a `.crp`, or build a mod. CS2 pages are beta and may be stale.

## Gotchas
1. **Editing `.locale` as text corrupts it.** **Cause:** `.locale` is a compiled binary, not plaintext.
   **Fix:** use the documented edit tool/method rather than a text editor; back up first.
2. **Extracted map meshes won't rebuild the map.** **Cause:** `.crp` meshes can be extracted with
   in-game **modTools**, but the object **coordinates live in the `.bin`** portion and are not extracted by
   the known preview tool. **Fix:** treat `.crp` as the only faithful carrier of layout; don't expect a
   third-party scene to match.
3. **A CS1 mod does nothing in CS2 (and vice-versa).** **Cause:** different runtimes and APIs (Mono C# API vs
   DOTS/Toolchain). **Fix:** target the game explicitly; keep separate projects.
4. **A CS2 code mod fails to load after a patch.** **Cause:** CS2 mod docs are version-badged and the toolchain
   tracks the game build. **Fix:** match the toolchain/game version the guide's badge states.
5. **Modding "on Linux" fails out of the box.** **Cause:** the CS2 toolchain assumes Windows. **Fix:** follow
   the wiki's Proton setup (`Modding_Toolchain_on_Linux`).
6. **Building a `.crp` asset by hand doesn't load.** **Cause:** the wiki's "CRAP File Format"
   page documents the `.crp` header, but the `.bin` placement/coordinate portion is not covered;
   a 2022 thread asking for a full spec got no answer. **Fix:** create assets through the in-game
   editors, which write the container correctly.

## Assets
CS1: Asset Editor (buildings/props), Road Editor, Theme Editor, color correction. CS2: first-party asset
pipelines for buildings/props/decals/trees/surfaces, texture sharing, color variations and emissive. Both are
node/tool-driven — no hand-authored container required.

## Cost and time
Small: the official Paradox wikis plus community XeNTaX threads. No in-game session, no build.

## Open questions
- `.crp` `.bin` placement/coordinate binary layout — not publicly documented; only the mesh side is extracted.
- `.locale` binary format spec, and the game **font** location for non-Latin scripts — both still open.
- Whether the CS2 `.crp`/asset container is the same family as CS1's, and whether any of it is documented
  outside Paradox's own tools.
- The wiki's **CRAP file format** page documents the `.crp` header; it was not read here (the
  raw/`action=raw` endpoint returned a bot challenge), so the exact header fields are a follow-up.

# Read-only live city dashboard for Cities: Skylines 1: an HTTP server inside a C# mod, built on Linux with mcs

> A C# mod that opens `http://127.0.0.1:19680` from inside the running game and serves a browser dashboard:
> all the city statistics, a vector map drawn from the game's own data, rule-based advice, charts and a
> day/night budget comparison. Route: the supported `IUserMod` API, compiled on Linux with plain `mcs` against
> the game's assemblies. It runs in the real game (a 128,000-inhabitant city, loading, playing, saving). One
> abort on save happened on the owner's machine with the mod installed and was never reproduced or explained,
> which is why the status is `in-progress`. Code: `examples/cities-skylines-city-dashboard`.

## Setup
- Cities: Skylines **1.21.1-f9**, Steam build 22724702, **native Linux** binary (`Cities.x64`), Unity 5.6.7f1
  with its bundled old Mono (C# 6 at most, .NET 3.5 profile: no tuples, no `out var`).
- Arch Linux, kernel 7.2. Compiler: Mono `mcs` 6.12.0. No Unity editor, no Visual Studio, no MSBuild.
- Other mods present in the player's game: 81 Tiles 2, TM:PE, Intersection Marking Tool, Harmony.
- Paths on Linux:
  - local mods: `~/.local/share/Colossal Order/Cities_Skylines/Addons/Mods/<ModName>/` (one folder per mod);
  - saves: `.../Cities_Skylines/Saves/` (Steam Cloud saves live under Steam's `userdata/<id>/255710/remote/`);
  - game log: `~/.config/unity3d/Colossal Order/Cities_ Skylines/Player.log` (note the space in the folder name).

## Route and why
**loader-api.** A CS1 mod is any class library with a class implementing `ICities.IUserMod`; the game loads
every DLL in a mod folder. Nothing else is needed for a read-only tool: every manager is a public singleton.
- Not a save-file reader: the `.crp` container is only partly documented, and the point was live data.
- Not memory reading or a native hook: the managed API already exposes everything.
- Not Harmony: nothing is patched. The mod only reads.
- The browser is the UI on purpose. In-game UI means the game's own UI framework; a web page can be built and
  tested with no game running (see Verification).
- The editors, the `.crp`/`.locale` containers and CS2 are covered in
  [the API and containers note](cities-skylines-modding-api-and-container-formats.md).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
### Mod loading
- `IUserMod` needs `Name` and `Description`. `OnEnabled()` and `OnDisabled()` are optional and found by reflection.
- **The mod class is instantiated even when the mod is disabled** (the plugin manager needs the name). A constructor
  can therefore bootstrap: create a `GameObject` with a `MonoBehaviour`, mark it `DontDestroyOnLoad`, and on the
  first `Update` set its own `PluginInfo.isEnabled = true`. That value is persisted by the game.
- `PluginManager.FindPluginInfo(assembly)` only returns **enabled** plugins. To find yourself while disabled,
  walk `GetPluginsInfo()` and test `ContainsAssembly`. `PluginInfo.modPath` is the mod's folder.
- Assemblies are loaded from bytes, not mapped from the file. Overwriting the DLL in place while the game ran
  changed nothing every time it was tried here (no reload, no log line); the new code ran only after a restart.
  The game does reload mods while running in other setups: see Gotcha 4.

### Threads
- The **main thread** renders and runs `MonoBehaviour.Update`. The **simulation thread** owns the city data.
  There are also water, path-finding and audio threads.
- `SimulationManager.AddAction(Action)` queues work for the simulation thread. Queued actions run at the top of
  every simulation step **even while the game is paused**. The official `ICities` equivalent is
  `IThreading.QueueSimulationThread(Action)` (and `QueueMainThread` for the other direction).
- Reading managers from the main thread works but costs frames. Collecting a 9,600-building, 4,300-segment map
  into 1.6 MB of JSON took about 80 ms on the simulation thread; on the main thread that is a visible hitch
  every refresh.
- Saving is itself a queued simulation task: the save panel starts a coroutine, which queues a task that
  serializes everything into `Saves/Temp/<guid>.ccs`; only afterwards is that file packed into the `.crp`.
  The log line `Saved simulation data to: ...` is written only on success. A 0-byte `.ccs` left behind means
  the process died before the first flush.

### Where the numbers are
- `DistrictManager.m_districts.m_buffer[0]` is **the whole city**; index 1 and up are painted districts with
  the same fields. It has population by age and education level (with eligible workers and unemployed per
  level), per-sector blocks (homes or jobs, empty, building count, abandoned, happiness, level shares),
  imports and exports by product, and getter methods for every utility and service capacity and load.
- Units: electricity values are kW (divide by 1000 for the MW the game shows); water and sewage are m³/week;
  garbage is the game's raw unit. Money values are in hundredths.
- `EconomyManager`: cash, income and expenses per service, tax rates, and `GetBudget(service, subService, night)`.
- `ZoneManager`: the three demand bars. Zone blocks are 4 cells deep and up to 8 wide, 8 m per cell, with bit
  masks for valid, shared and occupied cells and a block angle; cell centres follow from position and angle.
- `ImmaterialResourceManager.CheckLocalResource(resource, position, out value)` gives service **coverage at a
  point** (fire, police, healthcare, deathcare, the three school tiers, public transport, entertainment) plus
  land value, noise and crime. Zero means out of reach. This is what makes "which buildings no hearse can
  reach" a one-line query.
- `NaturalResourceManager` holds a 512×512 grid of 33.75 m cells: ore, oil, fertility, forest, tree density
  and ground pollution, one byte each.
- Buildings: position, angle, and `Width`/`Length` in 8 m cells give the footprint. `m_problems.ToString()`
  lists the problem names (`Garbage`, `Death`, `NoGoods`, …) plus `MajorProblem`/`FatalProblem`.
  `BuildingAI.GetLocalizedStats` returns the same text the building's info panel shows ("Students: 232 / 910").
- Roads: a segment has two nodes and `m_middlePosition`, a point **on** the curve. The dashboard draws each
  segment as the quadratic Bézier through that point, whose control point is `2·M − (A+B)/2`. That's an
  approximation: the game's own curve is a cubic `Bezier3` from the node positions, whose inner points
  `NetSegment.CalculateMiddlePoints` derives from the segment's `m_startDirection`/`m_endDirection` (TM:PE's
  `GeometryUtil` does exactly this). `m_trafficDensity` is 0–100. `NetInfo.m_halfWidth` gives the width.
- Service vehicles: each building keeps a linked list of its own vehicles; the AI class has a count field
  (ambulances, hearses, fire trucks, police cars, garbage trucks, maintenance trucks). Available vehicles are
  that count scaled by the building's production rate.
- Budget to capacity is not linear: below 100% the production rate is the budget squared over 100 (80% → 64%),
  from 100 to 150% the gain tapers (150% → 125%), and upkeep follows the budget linearly. Inverting this turns
  "peak usage was 71%" into "this budget can drop to 95%".
- Day and night: `SimulationManager.m_isNightTime`, `m_currentDayTimeHour`, `m_enableDayNight`. Night is before
  05:00 and after 20:00, so 9 of 24 hours. Every service has a day budget and a night budget. Those hours come
  from the static `SimulationManager.SUNRISE_HOUR` / `SUNSET_HOUR`, which time mods such as Real Time and Rush
  Hour change; read them (or `m_isNightTime`) rather than hard-coding the hours.
- Map geometry: 17.28 km across, 9×9 tiles of 1,920 m. The base game lets the player buy 9 of them (the
  official wiki's Tiles page); tile borders are drawn for the middle 5×5, and mods raise the limit to 25 or 81
  (81 Tiles 2 was installed here). `GameAreaManager.MaxAreaCount` gives the current limit.
- Engine limits are plain buffer sizes: 49,152 buildings, 36,864 net segments, 32,768 nodes, 16,384 active
  vehicles, 65,536 citizen instances, 262,144 trees, 256 transport lines, 128 districts. Each manager exposes
  the current count next to the buffer.

### Gameplay facts the advisor rules encode
These came from a 128,000-inhabitant city played the same day, then confirmed in the dashboard:
- A full landfill stops sending trucks, so its area goes uncollected even with spare incinerator capacity.
- Bodies pile up for lack of reach, not of crematoriums: about 75 crematoriums clustered together still left
  roughly a fifth of the buildings uncovered.
- Unemployment concentrates among university graduates when schools outgrow office zoning.
- Outside highway connections can belong to a road system the city never touches. A union-find over road
  nodes finds them; until they are linked, imports starve.
- A water tower on polluted ground contaminates the whole network.

## Build steps
1. Reference the game's `Cities_Data/Managed` assemblies; copy nothing:
   `mcs -target:library -nostdlib -noconfig -langversion:6 -r:mscorlib.dll -r:System.dll -r:System.Core.dll
   -r:Assembly-CSharp.dll -r:ColossalManaged.dll -r:ICities.dll -r:UnityEngine.dll -out:Mod.dll Mod.cs`
   (each `-r:` with the full path into `Managed`). `-nostdlib -noconfig` makes `mcs` use the game's own
   `mscorlib` instead of the system one.
2. Copy the DLL and the page into `Addons/Mods/<ModName>/`. Start the game.
3. In the example: `./build.sh` does both; `./build.sh --page` updates only the page, which the mod re-reads
   from disk on every request, so page work needs no game restart.
4. No game at hand: `python3 tools/mock_game.py` serves the page against a synthetic city in the same wire format.

## Verification
- **In the real game:** every route returned valid JSON for a loaded 128k city, paused and at speed 3; the
  day/night sampler crossed a dusk and filled both buckets; a brand-new empty map returned sane values.
- **Saving with the mod installed** worked in three scripted runs (loaded city, new city, and after swapping
  the DLL on disk), each with a client polling all routes every 2 s. Those runs started the game binary
  directly (`SteamAppId=255710 ./Cities.x64`), not through the launcher.
- **The page:** driven in headless Chromium over the DevTools Protocol (clicks, hover, console errors,
  screenshots) against the game and against the mock, in both languages, at 420, 1680 and 2560 px wide.
- **Not verified:** Windows, macOS, the Epic build. Districts and transport lines with a real city that has
  them (only injected data and the mock). A session longer than a few minutes of polling in a test run. The
  abort on save described in Gotcha 1.

## Gotchas
1. **The game aborted one second into a save, with the mod installed, and a city was lost.** The process got
   SIGABRT, the temp `.ccs` stayed at 0 bytes, and the city had never been saved before. **Cause:** unknown.
   Three scripted save runs with the same DLL and a run of the newer build did not reproduce it; those ran the
   binary directly while the crash happened in a session started through the Paradox launcher, so the mod is
   not cleared. The evidence was lost because the player reopened the game, which truncates `Player.log`.
   **Fix (what to do instead):** before installing any mod for someone, back up their saves and make them save
   the current city; test load, play, **save** and quit yourself, started the same way the player starts the
   game; and when a crash is reported, first run `coredumpctl list` and copy `Player.log` before anything
   relaunches the game.
2. **Starting a second city in the same session breaks the game.** Loading or creating another city without
   quitting threw `Argument is out of range` while deserializing game-area data, then the simulation logged a
   null-reference on every step, and quitting hung at `Waiting for simulation to quit...`. **Cause:** not this
   mod: it reproduces with this mod removed. Most likely stale state in other mods' patches across loads (81
   Tiles 2, which changes the game-area data, and TM:PE were loaded); a run without them wasn't tried.
   **Fix:** one city per process. When scripting tests, restart the game for every load.
3. **The mod's server never started on a fresh install.** **Cause:** the mod was disabled, and the self-enable
   code looked itself up with `FindPluginInfo`, which skips disabled plugins. **Fix:** iterate `GetPluginsInfo()`
   and match with `ContainsAssembly`.
4. **Overwriting the DLL in place while the game ran did nothing, silently.** **Cause:** not established. The
   game can reload mods while running: the official Modding API page says extensions' `OnCreated`/`OnReleased`
   also run "when recompiling a mod while the game is running", and TM:PE handles an in-game hot reload. Other
   mods' build scripts trigger it by deleting the DLL and then copying the new one (NetworkAnarchy's `.csproj`,
   "trigger hot reload"), and many give every build a new version (`[assembly: AssemblyVersion("1.0.*")]`).
   Here the DLL was overwritten in place, and with no `AssemblyVersion` every build is 0.0.0.0; whether either
   change makes the reload work wasn't tested. **Fix:** restart to test C# changes (given Gotcha 1, the safer
   choice anyway); keep anything you iterate on (here, the whole page) in files the mod reads at request time.
5. **Polling the map made the game stutter.** **Cause:** collection ran on the main thread through a
   `MonoBehaviour` queue. **Fix:** queue it with `SimulationManager.AddAction`, keep the main-thread queue only
   as a fallback after a timeout, and let the client stretch its interval to a multiple of the measured cost.
6. **`Player.log` from the crash was gone.** **Cause:** Unity truncates it on every start. **Fix:** copy it
   first. The example's author now keeps a watcher that copies the log every 15 s while the game runs.
7. **A custom window-close shortcut did not close the frozen game.** **Cause:** most likely the process had
   already aborted and systemd-coredump was writing a multi-gigabyte dump (about a minute, by its own log); the
   window stays on screen meanwhile. **Fix:** wait for the dump, then read `coredumpctl info <pid>`.
8. **Core dumps of the game were useless for a stack.** **Cause:** the game runs inside Steam's runtime
   container, so the library paths recorded in the dump do not exist on the host and gdb could not unwind it.
   **Fix:** rely on `Player.log`, which gets the managed stack when the runtime dies in the open.
9. **Translating the UI broke the script.** **Cause:** English text with apostrophes (`residents' health`) went
   into single-quoted strings. **Fix:** escape the quote character of the literal when substituting text.
10. **A word was both a JSON key and on-screen text**, so translating by text would have renamed the key.
    **Fix:** translate only whole string literals from an explicit table, and special-case the few literals
    where one word plays both roles.
11. **Headless screenshots of the canvas map came out blank.** **Cause:** `--screenshot` with a virtual time
    budget captures before the last animation frame. **Fix:** drive the browser over the DevTools Protocol and
    capture in real time.
12. **A shell `pkill -f <pattern>` killed the agent's own shell**, twice. **Cause:** the pattern text is part
    of the shell's own command line. **Fix:** kill by PID read from `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`.

## Assets
None from the game and none generated. The map is drawn in a `<canvas>` from numbers; icons are small inline
SVG paths written by hand; screenshots in the example come from the synthetic city.

## Cost and time
One long session (about 3 hours of work on the dashboard, after a day of agents playing the same game through
another mod). Roughly 15 game restarts for C# changes; page changes needed none.

## Open questions
- What aborted the game on save (Gotcha 1)? Is it reproducible when the game is started through the launcher,
  with a browser tab polling for an hour?
- Does a long session of large JSON strings (a megabyte every 2 s) fragment the old Boehm heap enough to matter?
  Streaming the response or reusing buffers would remove the question.
- A history with more than 14 columns (utilities, traffic, sick, dead) needs a CSV format that tolerates old rows.
- Windows and macOS: the code uses nothing Linux-specific, but nobody has run it there.
- Does deleting the DLL and copying the new one, or a new `AssemblyVersion` per build, make this build reload
  the mod while running (Gotcha 4)?

# Total conversion (Middle-earth): trees, civs, 2D leaders, custom 3D wonders, victory reskin

> "Ages of Arda" turns Civ VI (Gathering Storm) into Middle-earth with a plain `.modinfo` data mod:
> - nine eras, restructured tech and civic trees;
> - 8 civilizations with 14 leaders, shown as painted 2D portraits;
> - gunpowder and air units locked;
> - city-states, Great People, governors, religion, Eurekas and victories reskinned;
> - 52 of 53 world wonders with their own 3D models.
>
> The wonder models went concept image → image-to-3D → Blender, then into Firaxis' Granny `.fgx` format with no
> GUI, by calling the SDK's FBX importer DLL directly.
>
> All of it was checked in the running game, using real mouse input, screenshots, `Lua.log` and `Modding.log`, a
> 100-turn AI autoplay, and scripted test scenes that place wonders and force a victory.

## Setup
- **Game:** Windows 11, Civ VI 1.0.12.68 (Steam), Base + Rise and Fall + Gathering Storm, played on the GS ruleset.
  - Windowed at a 1920x1080 client size; every click coordinate below assumes it.
- **SDK:** Civilization VI Development Tools from Steam (Library → Tools).
  - "Sid Meier's Civilization VI SDK" holds `Civ6AssetCooker_FinalRelease.exe` and the Asset Editor.
  - "...SDK Assets" holds the pantries. The real pantry is `SDK Assets\Civ6\pantry`; DLC pantries are under
    `Civ6\DLC\*\pantry`.
- **Art and checks:**
  - Blender 5.2 (headless, `--background --python`).
  - ffmpeg for image work.
  - `sqlite3` for offline database checks.
- **Mod location:** `Documents\My Games\Sid Meier's Civilization VI\Mods\<Mod>\`. The game picks it up from there;
  enable it under Additional Content.
- **Logs:** `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Firaxis Games\Sid Meier's Civilization VI\Logs\`, mainly `Modding.log`, `Database.log`
  and `Lua.log`.
- **Debug database:** after a game starts, `...\Cache\DebugGameplay.sqlite` holds the merged gameplay database.
  Query it to confirm what really loaded.

## Route and why
- **The route:** an official data mod.
  - A `.modinfo` whose actions are UpdateDatabase (SQL/XML), UpdateText, UpdateIcons, UpdateColors and UpdateArt
    (a cooked `.dep`).
  - Plus ImportFiles and AddGameplayScripts for Lua.
- **Proxy-DLL hooks: no.** `um scan` reports "unknown native" and suggests them; that's wrong for this game,
  because data and Lua reach every system needed here.
- **ModBuddy: no.** The cooker is a command-line tool, so the whole pipeline is scripts. A generated modinfo
  (`dev/gen_modinfo.sh` from a manifest) avoids hand edits.
- **Custom 3D wonders:** the documented path is the Asset Editor importing from 3ds Max/Maya. The community's
  is Deliverator's CivNexus6 (`.fgx` import/export, Blender scripts, and FBX → `.fgx`). Both are GUI tools; the
  headless DLL route below replaces them.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
**Databases and load order**
- There are two SQLite databases.
  - **Configuration** (FrontEnd) drives game setup. The civ and leader picker reads `Players` rows in the domains
    `Players:StandardPlayers`, `Players:Expansion1_Players` and `Players:Expansion2_Players`, with Portrait and
    PortraitBackground columns for the 2D art.
  - **Gameplay** (InGame) holds rules and text.
- Each action has a LoadOrder, and later wins. Text is one `LocalizedText` table keyed by (Language, Tag).
  `<Replace Tag Language>` rows override base text.

**Tech and civic trees**
- Layout is derived, not stored: the column is the node's cost rank within its era, and the row is `UITreeRow`.
- Prerequisites must cost less than the node that needs them.
- **Never delete base TECH_/CIVIC_ rows.** Boosts, AI and modifiers reference them. Re-link the prerequisites and
  rename the text instead.

**Units**
- Gunpowder and air units can be locked by giving them a `TraitType` that no civ has (e.g. `TRAIT_ARDA_DISABLED`).
  Then fix `ObsoleteTech` / `MandatoryObsoleteTech` on the units left playable, so nothing upgrades into a locked
  unit.
- New units: `INSERT ... SELECT` from a base unit, and clone its `Units.artdef` entry for the art.

**Civs and leaders**
- New civs and leaders can reuse existing trait kits.
- To have only your own civs in setup, delete the other `Players` rows in all three domains. The game then offers
  only yours.
- Civs need citizen names (male and female, classic and modern; base civs have 10 of each). See Gotcha 6.

**2D leaders (no 3D)**
- An entry in `ArtDefs/FallbackLeaders.artdef` per leader points at a BLP texture.
- The diplomacy screen draws it with an `Image` control (`FallbackLeaderImage`), centred at 3/4 of screen width and
  scaled to screen height.
- The 3D leader scene is absent, so anything the image doesn't cover is **black** (Gotcha 9).
- Loading screen and setup use `LoadingInfo.ForegroundImage` / `BackgroundImage` and `Players.Portrait` /
  `PortraitBackground` (UI textures by name).

**Cooking 2D art without ModBuddy**
- PNG → DDS (a small C# writer: uncompressed RGBA plus mips) → `.tex` / `.xlp` / `.artdef` / `.Art.xml`.
- Then `Civ6AssetCooker_FinalRelease.exe` in its three modes: `XLP` → BLP, `ArtDef`, `Dependency` → one generated
  `<Mod>.dep`, listed under UpdateArt.
- The cooker accepts several `--pantry`; pass the SDK Assets pantries so cloned base assets resolve.

**Wonder models**
- A wonder model is a `WonderMovie` asset: `.geo` (XML mesh list) + `.fgx` geometry, and `.anm` + `.fgx`
  animation (the build-up, 500 frames at 30 fps), plus `.ast`, `.mtl` and textures.
- The element is keyed by `BUILDING_*` in `WonderMovie.artdef`. Overriding that element in your own artdef/package
  swaps the model for the map, the build-up and the completion cinematic.
- `.fgx` is binary **Granny 3D** (GR2: Oodle-compressed sections, Firaxis string remapping). Blender can't write it
  directly. CivNexus6 converts between `.fgx` and its own `.cn6`, which its Blender scripts read and write, but it
  runs as a GUI and isn't part of this pipeline.

**The headless .fgx route**
- The Asset Editor's managed `Firaxis.CivTech.Impl.dll` has an FBX interface whose export only P/Invokes
  `FbxImporter_Release.dll!ExportFBXScene(fbx, node, out.fgx, ShowInterface, ShowProgress, hWnd)`.
- Call it directly with `ShowInterface=false`, `ShowProgress=false`, `hWnd=0` and it converts an FBX scene to
  `.fgx` with no window.
- Defaults omit tangents: you get `Position3 Normal3 TextureCoordinates0x2`. The shipped layout is
  `Position3 Normal3 Tangent3 Binormal3 TextureCoordinates0x3`. Patch the vertex data afterwards: the SDK's own
  Granny wrapper can load and save the file.
- Missing tangents cook to zeros (black/flat shading); see Gotcha 11.
- **Expansion/DLC wonders** (Etemenanki, Statue of Zeus, Angkor Wat, Torre de Belém, Bolshoi, Venetian Arsenal...)
  have **no SDK pantry asset**. Clone the `.ast`, camera, sounds and footprint from a similar base-game pantry wonder,
  and keep the artdef element from the DLC.
- **Coastal wonders** (Colossus, Great Lighthouse, Torre de Belém, Venetian Arsenal, Sydney Opera House) sit on a
  `TERRAIN_COAST` water tile next to land, not on coastal land. A self-contained diorama model makes the facing
  irrelevant.

**End-game screen**
- The base `UI/EndGame/EndGameMenu.lua` ends with `include("EndGameMenu_", true)` (a wildcard include).
- So an ImportFiles Lua named `EndGameMenu_<yours>.lua` loads inside that context and can patch the global
  `Styles` table:
  - `Background` (a UI texture name);
  - `Movie` (set it to nil to drop the base cinematic; the replay button hides itself);
  - ribbons.
- No Firaxis file is replaced. Expansion files can add styles after yours, so patch again in a wrapper around the
  global `View(data)`.
- Several other base screens end with the same kind of wildcard include. Grep for `include(".*_", true)` before
  reaching for ReplaceUIScript.

**Testing hooks (Lua)**
- In gameplay scripts (AddGameplayScripts):
  - `cities:Create(x, y)`, `UnitManager.Kill(unit)`;
  - `capital:GetBuildQueue():CreateIncompleteBuilding(buildingIndex, plotIndex, 100)` places a finished wonder
    and plays its completion view;
  - `WorldBuilder.CityManager():SetPlotOwner(plot, city)` claims tiles;
  - `PlayersVisibility[0]:ChangeVisibilityCount(plotIndex, 1)` reveals them.
- In a UI script: `UI.LookAtPlot`, `UI.SetMapZoom`, and
  `UI.RequestAction(ActionTypes.ACTION_ENDTURN, { REASON = "UserForced" })`. The last one is what shift-clicking
  End Turn does, and it ignores the "choose production / research / unit needs orders" blockers.
- `AutoplayManager` (`SetTurns`, `SetReturnAsPlayer`, `SetObserveAsPlayer(PlayerTypes.OBSERVER)`, `SetActive`)
  runs AI-only turns for soak tests.
- `UserConfiguration.TutorialLevel(-1)` plus `LuaEvents.TutorialUIRoot_AdvisorLower()` on
  `LuaEvents.TutorialUIRoot_AdvisorRaise` silences advisor popups for the session.

## Build steps
1. **Back up.** Back up `Documents\My Games\Sid Meier's Civilization VI` (`um backup create`). Make a copy of the
   stock gameplay database for offline checks: let a game start, then copy `Cache\DebugGameplay.sqlite`.
2. **Write the data.** One SQL file per era for the trees; units, civs (gameplay) and civs (configuration) SQL.
   Text as `TAG|Text` lists turned into `<Replace>` XML by a script.
3. **Generate the `.modinfo`** from a manifest:
   - FrontEnd: configuration SQL, text, icons, colours, art.
   - InGame: gameplay SQL, text, icons, colours, art, ImportFiles.
   - Text at LoadOrder 5000 (Gotcha 7).
4. **Check offline before every launch.** Apply the gameplay SQL in manifest order to a copy of the stock database
   with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` and check for:
   - foreign-key violations;
   - unreachable tree nodes;
   - prerequisites that cost more than their dependants;
   - XML that doesn't parse;
   - text tags that don't exist in the game;
   - a modinfo that doesn't match the manifest.

   This catches most mistakes in seconds; a game launch takes minutes.
5. **2D art.** Leader cut-outs and civ landscapes → PNG inputs (ffmpeg) → DDS → cook (XLP, ArtDef, Dependency) →
   install BLPs under `Platforms/Windows/BLPs/` plus the `.dep` and artdefs; list them under `<Files>`.
6. **Wonders**, one at a time:
   - concept image → image-to-3D GLB;
   - Blender: clean up, decimate to about 25k tris, bake one texture set, level the albedo to the base wonders'
     brightness, cut into height bands and keyframe a rise-up build animation;
   - FBX → `ExportFBXScene` → `.fgx` → patch tangents → `.geo` → clone `.ast`/camera from the base wonder;
   - write the WonderMovie artdef → cook all wonders into one package.
7. **Victories.** Text, plus `UI/EndGameMenu_<Mod>.lua` (ImportFiles) and UI textures for the end-game backgrounds.

## Verification
- **The game is the oracle.** Each step was launched for real.
- **Tech and civic trees:** opened and screenshotted (gfxcapture).
- **New games:** started as several leaders; checked setup, the loading screen and the diplomacy view.
- **Logs:** `Modding.log` for "Error Loading" lines (anything not ours was already there before the mod).
  `Lua.log` for runtime errors and the harness `print`s.
- **Soak test:** 100 turns of AI autoplay as several civs. 0 Lua errors; the Database.log error count stayed at
  the pre-mod baseline.
- **Wonders:** a test scene places them at 100% next to the capital and frames the camera; each screenshot was
  reviewed. In game, I checked the Argonath, Orthanc, the Tower of Ecthelion and five coastal wonders. The other 44
  were only reviewed from Blender renders taken from the game's camera angle. Loads of a game with all 52 models
  were fine; low-memory machines were not tested.
- **Victory screen:** a harness removes the rival civs' units on turn 1 and force-ends the turn. Victory of Arms
  showed with the new background, no movie and the new ranking list. The other victory types were not triggered,
  but they share the patched code path.
- **Not verified:** multiplayer, Steam Workshop upload, non-English languages (English only), other rulesets
  (vanilla / Rise and Fall).

## Gotchas
1. **`um win drive click` is ignored by Civ VI.**
   - **Cause:** it sets the cursor position and sends button down/up with no move events; Civ needs real moves.
     Two bugs in my own replacement followed: an x64 `INPUT` struct padded to 48 bytes (SendInput returns 0,
     error 87; it must be 40), and a PowerShell `-File` script with `param([int[]]$a)` that bound only the first
     number.
   - **Fix:** SendInput with ABSOLUTE|VIRTUALDESK moves, gliding about 25 steps to the target, a 300 ms dwell,
     then down/up, with separate int parameters.
2. **Autoplay or tests hang on "the AI's turn".**
   - **Cause:** an advisor popup is waiting (first wonder, volcano, historic moment...).
   - **Fix:** in a dev UI script, `UserConfiguration.TutorialLevel(-1)` and lower or clear raised advisors.
     Do this in every harness, before anything else.
3. **The new civ or leader is missing from setup, or setup shows base civs only.**
   - **Cause:** the Configuration database is a separate FrontEnd action.
   - **Fix:** put `Players` rows in all three domains, in a FrontEnd UpdateDatabase.
4. **Removing a tech/civic crashes or breaks boosts and the AI.**
   - **Cause:** many tables reference the base IDs.
   - **Fix:** keep every ID, re-link prerequisites, rename by text only.
5. **Tree columns come out wrong.**
   - **Cause:** the column is the cost rank within the era.
   - **Fix:** costs must rise along each prerequisite chain. Check this offline against the stock database.
6. **The game freezes for good after a particular AI's turn** (turns 25 and 49 in two runs).
   - **Cause:** a male leader reused Catherine de Medici's ability. Its modifier `UNIQUE_LEADER_ADD_VISIBILITY`
     uses `SourceType = DIPLO_SOURCE_FEMALE_ONLY`, and the custom civ had **no female citizen names**, so the
     engine looped forever looking for one.
   - **Fix:** set that modifier argument to `DIPLO_SOURCE_ALL_NAMES` and give every civ full citizen-name lists
     (male and female, classic and modern).
   - **Method:** bisect abilities with **new** games. A loaded save keeps the modifiers attached at game start.
7. **Some of your text reverts to base names in game** (e.g. city-states, other `LOC_CITY_NAME_*`).
   - **Cause:** another enabled mod sets the same tags later. Yet (not) Another Maps Pack sets about 11k
     `LOC_CITY_NAME_*` at LoadOrder 2000.
   - **Fix:** load your text at a higher LoadOrder (5000). Check with `Locale.Lookup` in a test script.
8. **A cook step "succeeded" but the art never changed.**
   - **Cause:** the cooker's error was swallowed by `| tail` in a script.
   - **Fix:** check each mode's exit status and log. Also:
     - pass every needed `--pantry`;
     - don't put commas in PowerShell `-File` arguments;
     - PowerShell variables are case-insensitive, so a local `$extraArtDefs` overwrote the `-ExtraArtDefs`
       parameter.
9. **2D leaders stand on a black screen in diplomacy.**
   - **Cause:** there is no 3D scene; the fallback image is only as wide as the portrait.
   - **Fix:** a **2048x1024** fallback with the portrait centred on a dimmed civ landscape. The game centres it at
     3/4 screen width and scales it to screen height, so it reaches under the left panel.
   - **Cost:** 2.5x the texture memory when the DDS is uncompressed (14 leaders: 63 → 157 MB). Use BC compression
     if you can.
10. **Custom wonders render nearly black in game** while the Blender preview looks fine.
    - **Cause:** the AI textures' mean linear albedo was about 0.03–0.07. Base wonder textures are 0.15–0.33, and
      UV padding was black.
    - **Fix:** fill the padding, then level the albedo towards about 0.18 (capped gain).
    - **Check:** compare against the base wonder's own textures before cooking. Very dark sources (a black cliff)
      stay dark by design.
11. **Custom geometry cooks with flat/odd shading.**
    - **Cause:** the headless Granny export has no tangents, and the cooker copies the zeros.
    - **Fix:** add tangents and binormals (and a third UV set) to the `.fgx` vertex data after export.
12. **`ArtDef` element not found / "not in any pantry" for an expansion wonder.**
    - **Cause:** expansion/DLC wonders have no SDK asset.
    - **Fix:** stand in a base wonder's asset (Colosseum; Great Lighthouse for coastal ones) and keep the DLC
      artdef element.
13. **A coastal test wonder found "no valid plot".**
    - **Cause:** these wonders go on coast **water** tiles next to land, and a new city owns only one ring.
    - **Fix:** claim tiles in the test with `WorldBuilder.CityManager():SetPlotOwner`, and reveal them, or the
      camera looks at unexplored parchment.
14. **The end-game screen never opens during autoplay.**
    - **Cause:** the victory fires (`Events.TeamVictory`), but the menu does not show while the AI drives player 0.
    - **Fix:** in a test, force-end the local player's turn with `REASON = "UserForced"` instead.
15. **A text file stops parsing after a harmless edit.**
    - **Cause 1:** `--` inside an XML comment (generated from `# --- heading`).
    - **Cause 2:** writing `&lt;&lt;` into a source that is escaped again on generation; grammar markers like
      `{LOC_GRAMMAR_CIVNAME << {1_CivName}}` must end up as a single `&lt;&lt;`.
    - **Also:** some tags really have no `LOC_` prefix (e.g. `ADVISOR_LINE_LISTENER_*`).
16. **The paid asset budget burned on failures.**
    - **Cause:** several parallel agents shared one scratch folder and overwrote each other's batch scripts. About
      20 image-to-3D calls failed with HTTP 422 `file_download_error` on bad input URLs, and others were
      duplicated.
    - **Fix:** a single serial generator. At most one paid call per item, and only if its output is missing.
      Stop at the first API error. Price the batch and ask before spending. After that, 39 image-to-3D runs in a
      row had 0 failures.

## Assets
- **Leaders:** 14 leader portraits (painted, original designs) from `fal-ai/nano-banana-2`, cut out with
  `fal-ai/birefnet/v2`.
  - Head crops for circular icons.
  - Leader-select 748x1024 foregrounds.
  - 2048x1024 diplomacy images.
- **Civs:** 8 civ symbols, generated white-on-black, with alpha taken from luminance (gpt-image-2 refused a
  transparent background in the size needed). 8 civ landscapes (16:9) serve as loading, diplomacy and end-game
  backgrounds.
- **Wonders:**
  - 53 concept images (nano-banana-2): one isometric diorama per wonder on a round or hex plinth, neutral grey
    background, no text.
  - 52 GLBs from `fal-ai/trellis-2`, processed in Blender as in Build steps 6.
  - Weak results came from busy concepts (big trees, thin spires); one clear silhouette per concept works best.
- **Movies:** none are generated. The base victory movies are simply not played.
- **Records:** prompts and request ids are kept in each folder's `fal_manifest.jsonl`. The README discloses that
  the art is AI-generated.

## Cost and time
- About two long days of agent time across several context compactions.
- Each wonder takes about 2–4 minutes of Blender and cooker time, run one at a time because of memory use.
- **fal:**
  - Image-to-3D was the main spend: about 39 good runs plus the wasted ones in Gotcha 16.
  - 2D art was a few dozen image calls.
  - Check prices with `um fal price` before a batch.
- **Size:** the cooked mod is about 500 MB (wonder package ~225 MB, uncompressed leader images ~157 MB).

## Open questions
- **Leader portraits:** a few look too much like the film actors. Regenerate them for a public release, with
  prompts that steer away from actor likeness.
- **Texture size:** add BC1/BC3/BC7 compression to the DDS writer to shrink the BLPs.
- **Units:** still use base-game 3D models. The same headless `.fgx` route should work for units, but unit assets
  need rigs and an animation state graph; not tried.
- **Rulesets and languages:** only English and Gathering Storm were tested.
