```md
# CS2 conversion of Elden Ring offline: native Rust DLL via me3 (fall death, spirit springs, 3D inspect, params)

> A "play Elden Ring as Counter-Strike 2" conversion: CS2 guns with their real handling, CS2 movement
> (bhop), the CS2 agent in third person, grenades, HUD, buy menu, inventory, cases with Valve's odds, skins
> composited from CS2's own paint kits, a 3D item inspect, the CS2 death screen, and spirit springs on foot.
> It is a native Rust DLL loaded by me3 plus rebuilt regulation params; every CS2 asset is converted from the
> user's own CS2 install at build time and stays local. The user played every feature in the real game; the
> agent read the DLL's own log after each run and used offline D3D12 / ImGui renders under Wine as oracles.

## Setup
- Elden Ring 1.17.1 (exe ProductVersion 2.7.1.0 = fromsoftware-rs's `Ww2710` RVA table), Steam, CachyOS Linux,
  Proton. `um scan` mislabels the game as Unity (an `ERD_ArtbookOST` folder): it is Dantelion native.
- me3 0.13.0 profile: natives = our DLL, package = our `regulation.bin`, `savefile = ER0000.cs2er.sl2`.
  A wrapper launcher renames the user's existing `dinput8.dll` mod loader aside for the session and back after.
- Rust 1.98 + cargo-xwin, MSVC target, static CRT. fromsoftware-rs 0.14 and hudhook 0.9.3 vendored (patched).
- WitchyBND 3.0.1.0 (linux build) for params; it insists on a TTY: run it as `script -qec "WitchyBND --passive <path>" /dev/null`.
- Source2Viewer-CLI (VRF) reads CS2's VPKs: models/clips to glTF, `.vpcf` particles, `.vtex`, `.vsndevts`, panorama.

## Route and why
`native-hook`. Elden Ring has no scripting API; params alone cannot add guns, a movement controller or a UI.
Considered and rejected: a passthrough (running CS2 alongside: impossible offline with VAC, and pointless
since CS2's data can be converted), Elden Mod Loader DLL (fine, but me3 gives a profile, a separate save and
offline launch in one place). The DLL draws CS2 models with its own D3D12 renderer injected into the game's
frame (a pre-ImGui hook in hudhook), the UI with ImGui, and changes behaviour through the `eldenring` crate
plus regulation rows built from the user's vanilla `regulation.bin`.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Boot order:** don't resolve fromsoftware-rs singletons from `DllMain`'s thread before the game window
  exists. The crate's singleton map caches the first reflection scan forever; an early scan lacks later
  singletons (`InvalidRva`). Gate on: window visible, then a fresh scan finds the reflection name. Use the
  singleton attribute name (`CSTask`), not the Rust type name (`CSTaskImp`).
- **Input:** the game reads mouse and keyboard with DirectInput `GetDeviceState` only (never `GetDeviceData`).
  Hooking it lets you blank keys/buttons for the game while your own UI or controller uses them.
- **Movement:** `CSChrPhysicsModule` has no usable velocity: motion is root-motion driven. A kinematic
  controller (CS2's movement constants read from the user's `libserver.so`) moves the character with Havok
  ray casts (`CSPhysWorld::cast_ray`, filter 0x2000058 hits map collision) and writes `physics.position` +
  `chr_proxy_pos_update_requested` + orientation every frame after physics. Hand control back for ladders,
  mounting, throws, death and interactions; resync when the game warps the character (map re-basing moves the
  Havok coordinates by tens of metres while the character stays put).
- **Fall death under a position-writing controller (the hard one):** the game keeps applying its *own* gravity
  to the physics body while you write positions. The body's velocity builds up a hidden falling speed the
  whole time the character is airborne; at touchdown the behaviour script plays a scripted fall death, which
  is not damage. What does **not** stop it: zeroing `CSChrFallModule.fall_timer`,
  `CSChrMaterialModule.disable_fall_damage`, clearing `physics.is_falling`, SpEffects with `fallDamageRate 0`,
  `noDead`, or the spirit-spring immunities (184 / 185, stateInfo 420 / 464). What stops it: while your
  controller drives, set `CSChrPhysicsModule.gravity_multiplier = 0` and `gravity_disabled = true` (your
  controller does gravity), restore the saved multiplier whenever the game drives again. Then apply your own
  fall damage on landing (CS2: (speed - 580) / (1024 - 580) of max HP, in u/s).
- **Spirit springs:** they are MSB regions of type MountJump (46) with a jump height in the type data. Only a
  mount gets SpEffect 183 "In Range", so the character on foot never knows it stands in one. The loaded MSB
  files are reachable at runtime: `MsbRepository` → its `res_cap_holder.entries()` (named `m60_XX_YY_00`);
  the file image is found by scanning the file cap's pointers for the `MSB ` header. Check every read with
  `VirtualQuery` first. Parse the region param list per SoulsFormats' MSBE layout: positions are block-local
  and match `PlayerIns.block_position` / `current_block_id`. Verified in game: heights 24 / 26 / 45 m read
  correctly, and on-foot launches work.
- **Level-ups:** `PlayerGameData` holds level, the eight attributes, runes and HP/FP/stamina maxima. Comparing
  them each tick lets a mod undo a level-up and refund its exact rune cost (no ESD editing needed). The talk
  menu types (`MenuType::Soul` = level up) exist in the crate but the live `CSNpcTalkIns` is not easy to reach.
- **ER UI elements:** `CSMenuManImp.ui_states[0x46]` (created/visible bits) gives a cheap "which ER menu is
  open" signal. Log transitions to map ids to screens.
- **"YOU DIED":** FeTextEffectParam rows 5 and 50. Blank them (`resId 0`, `textId -1`, `seId -1`) and the
  banner and its sound disappear while the death flow continues. `CSFeManImp.full_screen_message_request_id`
  is the runtime request.
- **Killer / last hit:** `ChrIns.last_hit_by` is a field-ins handle. Resolve it through
  `WorldChrMan.chr_inses_by_distance` (that list's `distance` is a relative metric, not metres).
- **Gear neutralised by params:** EquipParamProtector (cut rates, resistances, poise, weight, resident
  SpEffects) and EquipParamAccessory (`refId`, resident SpEffects); WitchyBND omits default values in XML,
  so an unset field means default.
- **Rendering into the game:** capture the scene depth (main DSV `D32_FLOAT_S8X24_UINT`, reversed Z; copy at
  the first `ClearDepthStencilView` of that DSV each frame) to occlude your 3D draws. If the copy is a frame
  stale (alt-tab, resize), use the last one instead of skipping the draw. Otherwise the hidden ER character
  "reappears" in place of your model.
- **Bullets:** spawn real engine bullets (`CSBulletManager::spawn_bullet`, Throwing-Dagger-like rows) so the
  game does the hits. Give each gun row `HitBulletID` = an inert marker bullet: its spawn is an
  engine-confirmed impact point.

## Build steps
1. Unpack the user's vanilla `regulation.bin` once with WitchyBND; a Python script copies it, appends rows
   (bullets, attacks, SpEffects, AI sounds) and edits rows (FeTextEffectParam, armour/talismans), writes only the
   edited `.param.xml` files back and repacks. Rows must stay sorted by id.
2. Pipelines (Python + VRF) convert CS2 content from the user's install into a local `cs2assets/out/`
   (gitignored): viewmodels with clips and sound events, the agent with world clips, glove/agent/charm meshes,
   paint-kit inputs for runtime skin compositing, case catalogue, panorama UI art, particle systems.
3. `cargo xwin build --release` the DLL into the me3 profile's `natives/`; launch via the me3 profile.
4. Offline oracles before every in-game test: `vmtest.exe` (the real D3D12 renderer offscreen under Wine)
   and `uitest.exe` (the real ImGui frame, rasterised from its draw lists).

## Verification
- In game by the user, every feature, with the DLL's own log as the oracle. It logs HP drops as
  `HIT c#### npc=… hp a->b`, boot state, menu transitions, spring regions read, landings with which immunities
  were on, case rolls, and render errors.
- Offline: the renderer and UI harnesses above (screens compared against the user's own CS2 screenshots),
  native harnesses for movement and recoil (Rust vs a Python reference), a 2M-roll simulation of the case odds,
  and a round trip of every rebuilt param (unpack the built regulation and compare).
- Not verified: other game versions, Windows (built and run only via Proton), co-op of any kind (offline only).

## Gotchas
1. **Boot: `InvalidRva` 7 ms after load.** **Cause:** the crate's singleton cache was built before reflection
   finished. **Fix:** wait for the game window plus a fresh reflection scan; never call crate singletons from
   `DllMain`'s thread early.
2. **Boot gate never passes.** **Cause:** searched the Rust type name instead of the reflection name
   (`CSTaskImp` vs `CSTask`). **Fix:** take names from `<T as FromStatic>::name()`.
3. **Dying after dropping onto a spirit spring (or anywhere) despite every fall-immunity effect.**
   **Cause:** the game's own gravity keeps accumulating velocity on the physics body under a position-writing
   controller; touchdown at that speed plays the scripted fall death. Fall timer, material flag, `is_falling`,
   `fallDamageRate 0`, `noDead`, SpEffects 184 / 185 and stateInfo 420 all did not help (each was verified to be
   on in the log). **Fix:** `gravity_multiplier = 0` + `gravity_disabled = true` while your controller drives,
   and your own fall damage. It took six test rounds; log the state at landing from the start.
4. **On-foot spirit springs do nothing.** **Cause:** SpEffect 183 "In Range" is only given to a mount.
   **Fix:** read MountJump (46) regions from the loaded MSBs in memory and test the player's block position.
5. **WitchyBND refuses to repack "regulation version exceeds latest known".** **Cause:** its Paramdex lagged
   the game patch. **Fix:** compare the defs you touch with a current Smithbox; if identical, bump the
   Paramdex upgrader version (keep the original) and round-trip check. Re-check whenever you add a param
   (EquipParamProtector's def did change in 1.17).
6. **Unpacking one `.param` outside its folder fails ("Could not determine PARAM type").** **Cause:**
   WitchyBND needs the regulation folder's context file. **Fix:** unpack in place in the unpacked regulation
   folder.
7. **Melee / short-range bullets never hit.** **Cause:** a row with life = range / speed under one frame
   (Zeus: 3 m at 2000 m/s = 1.5 ms) dies before the engine collides it; a melee row shorter than your target
   acceptance falls short. **Fix:** speed so life spans about two frames; reach past the accepted target.
8. **Bullet holes in the air / on enemies.** **Cause:** decals were placed at the marker even with no map
   surface there, and the character-hit report can arrive after the impact marker. **Fix:** require a map ray
   hit within 25 cm along the shot, and skip any impact within a character capsule + 25 cm.
9. **The ER character reappears in third person after alt-tab.** **Cause:** the replacement model only drew
   with a depth copy from this or the last frame. **Fix:** fall back to the last copy.
10. **3D models either hidden under the ImGui menus or drawn over the HUD.** **Cause:** hudhook 0.9.3's DX12
    backend has no hook around its ImGui pass. **Fix:** patch in a pre-ImGui hook (world-space draws, under
    the HUD) and a post-ImGui hook (a 3D model inside a menu, e.g. the item inspect); both get the command
    list, RTV and frame slot.
11. **VRF-exported clips double the root transform.** **Cause:** a standalone clip export keeps glTF's
    Z-up → Y-up turn on `root_motion`, while a model export with `--gltf_animation_list` bakes it into the
    root's children. **Fix:** convert (root r·R0⁻¹, children R0·t / R0·r). Clips outside the agent's animation
    graph (CS2's death clips) are not exported with the model; export them on their own.
12. **Additive world clips used as poses give A-pose arms.** VRF composes additive clips over the bind pose
    (`--gltf_compose_additive`); apply them relative to their first frame, never as a full pose.
13. **Particles with tinted sprites look dark.** **Cause:** the additive pass multiplies colour by alpha, so
    textures baked premultiplied lose it twice. **Fix:** bake RGB without alpha for additive sprites.
14. **A small screen texture (Zeus charge digits) blurs.** **Cause:** a 7-segment display draws every segment
    from one texture column with its own row; mips merge the rows. **Fix:** one mip level for that texture.
15. **Case odds felt rigged.** **Cause:** the RNG was seeded from `Instant::now().elapsed()` (≈ 0, same seed
    every time). **Fix:** seed from the performance counter, time and pid; verify by simulation.
16. **The death screen named a long-dead enemy after a fall.** **Cause:** `last_hit_by` keeps the last
    attacker forever. **Fix:** treat a death right after a hard landing as a fall.
17. **The level-up undo looks like it might fight the game.** It doesn't, if you restore the previous tick's
    level, attributes, both PlayerGameData maxima and the ChrIns data-module maxima, and refund the rune
    delta of that same tick.

## Assets
None generated: everything is converted from the user's own CS2 install by pipelines (VRF + Python + Pillow)
into a gitignored folder, never committed or redistributed. Skins are composited at runtime from CS2's paint
kit inputs (wear and pattern seed per item).

## Cost and time
About three days of agent sessions (several usage-limit resumes); the user ran every in-game test.

## Open questions
- What exactly the scripted fall death reads (velocity on the Havok character proxy is the working
  hypothesis; the fix is consistent with it).
- Blocking the Equipment tab and the grace Level Up screen outright: `ui_states` ids are being logged to map
  them.
- CS2's lid animation and 3D warehouse scene for case opening (a 2D case image zooms instead).
```

```md
# Porting a Dark Souls Remastered enemy into Elden Ring as a new character (Hollow c2500 -> c7250)

> The basic DS1 Hollow (sword variant) now exists in Elden Ring as its own character ID c7250: its own DSR
> skeleton, model, textures and animations, its own stats, hitboxes, AI (DS1's AI script ported), hit reactions,
> parry/riposte/backstab reactions and its own DS1 sounds. Only the ragdoll bodies are borrowed (Wandering Noble
> c4300, resized). Everything is built from the user's own DSR and ER installs by local scripts and loaded with
> ModEngine 2; the user tested every step in game (about 30 tests for the body and behaviour, 16 for sound).

## Setup
- Elden Ring 1.17.1 / exe 2.7.1.0, regulation from that build. DSR from Steam with loose files (`chr\c2500.*`,
  `param\GameParam\GameParam.parambnd.dcx`, `script\m10_01_00_00.luabnd.dcx`, `sound\frpg_c2500.fsb/.fev`).
  The DSR enemy randomizer had edited the live luabnds/params: use its `.bak` files as vanilla.
- ER archives read with the BinderKeys RSA keys + name lists (Data0-3, DLC, and `sd\sd.bhd`/`sd_dlc02.bhd` for
  sound; sound paths are relative to `sd\`).
- ModEngine 2: one profile per experiment (`config_*.toml` + `.bat`), mod folder with `chr\`, `action\script\`,
  `map\mapstudio\`, `script\`, `sd\`, `regulation.bin`. **Use a 2024 development build** (see Gotcha 1).
  ModEngine 2 is discontinued; its README points to me3, its successor (see Gotcha 1).
- Saves: ModEngine 2 has no save-file option, so it loads the normal `ER0000.sl2`. Back it up (`um backup`)
  before the first modded launch, and don't take a save used with these files online. me3's `savefile` option
  keeps a separate save.
- Wwise 2019.2.15 Authoring installed through the Audiokinetic Launcher (Authoring + Windows platform, no
  plug-ins); only `WwiseConsole.exe` is used, headless.

## Route and why
`data`: every change is a file the game already knows how to load (chr binders, TAE, behaviour, params, MSB, AI
Lua, sound bank). A first pass replaced the Wandering Noble's files (retargeting the Hollow onto the Noble
skeleton) to learn each format; the real port then gave the Hollow its own chr ID so it can coexist with every
vanilla enemy (goal: placing DS1 enemies with an Elden Ring enemy randomizer). No DLL needed.

ID scheme used: ER chr = 7000 + DS1 chr / 10 (c2500 -> c7250, Black Knight c2790 -> c7279), NpcParam/think
72500000, behaviour variation 72500, AtkParam_Npc 7250000 + judge, AI battle goal 725000, sound IDs 7250xxxxx.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
**Character files for a new ID** (`chr\c7250.*`): chrbnd (FLVER + ragdoll HKX), anibnd (skeleton + TAE),
div00-02 anibnds (spline-compressed animations referencing the div's `.compendium`), behbnd (shared c9997
graph + character data), `_h`/`_l` texbnds, `action\script\c7250.hks`. Every string inside the behbnd that names
the old ID (project, character, skeleton path, hks name, clip paths) must be renamed. No ChrModelParam row is
needed.

**Skeleton and animations.** DSR uses Havok 2015, ER Havok 2018. A DSR skeleton can be used natively if the 6 ER
foot-IK target bones (`L/R_Foot_Target2/1/Target`, indices 1-6) are added and every animation moves that chain
onto the feet each frame (ER's leg IK pulls the feet to them). Animations: degree-1 splines, one control point
per frame, TCRF-referenced to the div's compendium; the slot list is the template enemy's (animation IDs come
from the shared behaviour graph's `CustomManualSelectorGenerator.animId`, e.g. 8030-8057 damage, 10000/10001
death/death idle, 11000/11001/11002 thrown, 5000-5003 battle turns, 2100 run).

**Matching DS1 clips to ER slots without names.** Profile each clip (duration, root motion incl. yaw, pelvis/head
height start->end) and read the DS1 TAE: DS1 JumpTable IDs and ER FlagTypes are the same numbers (5 hit, 23 AI
combo window, 78/79/86 cancel windows), and DS1 TAE spEffects name states (DSR SpEffectParam 30 "parry-broken
(throwable)" marks the parried clip, 35 "throws disabled" marks knock-downs). ER's ThrowDef 11000/11010 have
exactly DS1 2500/2510's durations, so backstab/riposte sync carries over.

**TAE.** For each slot that now plays a DS1 clip, the template's events are time-scaled by
DS1-duration / template-duration; attack slots get DS1's hit windows (type 1, behaviour judge = DS1 judge), and
DS1's own 23/78/79/86 windows replace the template's (combos chain at DS1 timing).

**Params** (regulation.bin): NpcParam (HP, poise = `superArmorDurability`, runes, capsule, behaviourVariationId,
model masks, `SoundBankId`/`SoundAddBankId`), BehaviorParam `(200000 + variation) * 1000 + judge` -> AtkParam_Npc
(DS1 damage, `dmgLevel` = DS1 ImpactLevel, hit capsules on DS1 dummy IDs, which the native FLVER keeps),
NpcThinkParam (`battleGoalID`), ThrowParam (rows keyed by **DefChrId** = the defender's model ID).
Paramdex defs work if you take the latest layout (skip `RemovedVersion` fields) and let bitfields share a unit
across same-size types (u8 and dummy8).

**AI.** ER AI scripts are Lua 5.0 bytecode in luabnds, but ER also loads plain-text Lua there. DS1 AI scripts are
Lua 5.0 too and keep local names, so the DS1 Hollow script disassembles readably. ER still has the same helpers
and goals (`Approach_Act`, `GOAL_COMMON_Attack/ComboAttack/ComboRepeat/ComboFinal`, `Damaged_Step`,
`MissSwing_Attack`, `DIST_Middle`, SpinStep 701/702). The port is a hand-written table goal in ER style with
DS1's odds/distances, the goal ID constant defined in the file itself, packed as `script\725000_battle.luabnd.dcx`
(the vanilla luabnd layout; `.luagnl` = u64 offsets, 0, UTF-16 global names, 16-byte padding). The template's
logic script reads `battleGoalID` from NpcThinkParam, so only the battle script is new.

**Ragdoll.** Borrowing another enemy's hknp ragdoll works if the anim<->ragdoll mappers and the anim skeleton in
the ragdoll file are rewritten **in place in FromSoft's bytes** (Gotcha 2), and the bodies are refitted
(Gotcha 6).

**Sound (Wwise 2019.2, bank v135).** A character's TAE sound event (SoundType 1, ID n) posts the Wwise event
`Play_c<n>` (FNV-1 32-bit of the lower-case name; names are not stored in banks). Chain: Event -> Play action
(0x0403, target + bank ID = FNV of the bank name) -> random container -> Sounds -> embedded WEMs (DIDX/DATA,
16-byte aligned), under an actor-mixer whose top ancestor routes to a bus in `Init.bnk`. Each character loads
`sd\cs_c<SoundBankId>.bnk` (+ an additional `sd\enus\cs_c<SoundAddBankId>.bnk`). Every shipped ER WEM sampled
(520) is Wwise Vorbis. We cloned the template enemy's own chain (event/action/container/sounds), re-parented it
to a clone of its *top-level* mixer, and added the Hollow's sounds to a loose copy of that enemy's bank.

## Build steps
1. Extract the needed ER files (chr, behbnd, MSB tile, regulation, the template's luabnds and sound bank) and the
   DSR files; keep vanilla copies for round-trip checks.
2. Skeleton: DSR skeleton + 6 ER foot-IK target bones. Animations: decode each DSR clip, add the target chain,
   encode as degree-1 splines with TCRF to the template div compendium, one file per template slot.
3. FLVER: DSR meshes on DSR bones + target bones + one root "part" bone the meshes anchor to; write per-bone AABBs
   and the oriented mesh boxes yourself (Gotcha 3); add the template's dummy points the DS1 model lacks
   (sound/ground/trace points) re-placed on matching bones.
4. Ragdoll: copy the template's physics HKX bytes, patch the anim skeleton and both mappers in place, resize
   joint pivots and capsules (Gotchas 2, 6).
5. TAE (WitchyBND XML): re-time the template's events per slot, insert DS1 hits/windows/sounds; repack.
6. Package: rename every internal ID string (behbnd, binder names); repack with WitchyBND.
7. Params: add rows (NpcParam, BehaviorParam, AtkParam_Npc, NpcThinkParam, ThrowParam) with a byte-exact PARAM
   writer, then replace only those entries inside regulation.bin (decrypt, ZSTD, patch BND4 headers, re-encrypt;
   check the other entries stay byte-identical).
8. AI: plain-text battle Lua packed as a luabnd; NpcThinkParam row pointing at its goal ID.
9. Map: patch one MSB enemy part in place (model name/sib, NpcParam, think) to place the enemy.
10. Sound: vgmstream decodes the DSR FSB4 to WAV; WwiseConsole `convert-external-source` (minimal new project,
    ShareSet "Vorbis Auto Detect High") makes WEMs; append Event/Action/Container/Sound objects + WEMs to a loose
    copy of the template's bank; set the new containers' props to neutral (Gotcha 15); NpcParam SoundBankId/
    SoundAddBankId = the template's existing banks.

## Verification
- Byte-level oracles before every in-game test: PARAM writer and Wwise bank parser reproduce the vanilla files
  byte for byte; regulation rebuild keeps all untouched entries identical; HKLib reads the raw-patched ragdoll and
  every patched value equals the intended one (joint pivot gap 0.000 mm at rest); animations decode back to the
  input within tolerance; TAE repack re-unpacked and compared; vgmstream decodes every new WEM from the bank.
- In game (the human played each build): spawn without crash, LOD/visibility at all angles, walk/run/turn, all
  DS1 attacks incl. leaps from range and the flurry, hits landing with DS1 damage, distinct light/heavy staggers,
  parry -> riposte, backstab, guard bounce (DS1 a00_3500), death, and every DS1 sound at DS1 volume/pitch.
- Not verified: other DS1 Hollow variants (torch, bow), the dying ragdoll's looks (still stretches on the floor;
  accepted for now), multiplayer (never used), whether a character's *own* new bank (`cs_c7250.bnk`) loads with
  the newer ModEngine (see Open questions).

## Gotchas
1. **Custom sounds silent for 15 tests, whatever we changed.** **Cause:** the ModEngine 2 release (2.1.0.0,
   modengine2.dll of 2023-08-31) does not load loose sound banks; the game kept using its own banks. Found via the
   soulsmodding.com "Elden Ring Soundbank Editing" guide, which requires a "Mod Engine 2 artifact" build. The
   Wwise hook that serves loose `.bnk` files arrived later (ModEngine2 PR #166, merged 2024-01-13), and no
   release followed it. **Fix:** a 2024 ModEngine 2 development build (we used the one shipped with the
   Convergence mod, dll dated 2024-10-18). me3, ModEngine 2's successor, has had Wwise overrides for ER since
   mid-2025 (me3 PR #128; `sd`, `sd/enus` and `sd/ja` paths); this port wasn't tested with it. A test that posts
   a *stock* event from the vanilla bank cannot tell you whether your bank loaded.
2. **Any HKX physics file re-serialised by HKLib crashes ER** (even an unmodified round trip, with type hashes
   restored). Behaviour HKX round-trips fine. **Fix:** edit FromSoft's original physics bytes in place: in a
   2018 tagfile, arrays and strings are a u32 item index in the owner and the ITEM table holds (type|flags, DATA
   offset, count), so arrays can be shrunk (overwrite + lower the count) and names written into existing string
   items. Keep the file size identical.
3. **New model invisible at some angles / stuck on low LOD.** **Cause:** the FLVER writer we used wrote empty
   per-bone bounding boxes; ER also wants the mesh box as an oriented box (half extents, XYZ rotation, centre) and
   each mesh anchored to a "part" bone (usage flag 4). **Fix:** write per-bone AABBs in bone bind space (all
   weight slots) and the oriented mesh boxes; anchor meshes to a root part bone; low-res textures named `<name>_l`.
4. **Crash when approaching the new character.** **Cause:** strings inside the behbnd still named the template
   ID. **Fix:** rename every internal reference (the Convergence mod's new enemies were the reference).
5. **Stiff, straight legs.** **Cause:** ER's leg IK pulls the feet to the Foot_Target chain, which the DS1 clips
   don't animate. **Fix:** move the target chain onto the feet every frame when building each clip.
6. **Dead body's limbs stretch apart.** **Cause:** the borrowed ragdoll's joint pivots are spaced for a larger body
   (forearm 0.39 m vs 0.26 m); once limp, the constraints pull the Hollow's bones to those spacings. **Fix:** move
   each parent-side pivot to where the child pivot sits on the new body; scale capsules per axis. (It still
   stretches somewhat once fully collapsed; deferred.)
7. **No hit reactions / stands still before dying.** **Cause:** damage and death slots still held a placeholder.
   **Fix:** map DS1 damage/death clips into the 8030-8191, 8500, 10000+ slots; a death idle = the clip's last
   pose held.
8. **No leaps or flurry, stops at mid range.** **Cause:** the template enemy's AI only requests its own few
   attacks; turn slots were placeholders. **Fix:** port the DS1 AI (above) and map DS1 turns/run/steps.
9. **Parry played a knock-down.** **Fix:** use the clip whose DS1 TAE applies spEffect 30 (DS1 Hollow: 2100).
10. **No backstab or riposte possible.** **Cause:** ThrowParam rows are keyed by DefChrId (defender model).
    **Fix:** copy the template's rows with DefChrId = the new model ID.
11. **Guard bounce turned the enemy 90 degrees.** **Cause:** DS1 2050/2051 rotate the root. **Fix:** the
    Hollow's real bounce clip is a00_3500 (found by the user in DS Anim Studio).
12. **regulation.bin repack fails silently with WitchyBND; soulstruct's binder doesn't round-trip it.** **Fix:**
    surgical BND4 edit: append the new .param, repoint its file header, recompress with the original DCX header.
13. **PARAM writer output differs from the game's.** **Cause:** rows with identical names share one string.
    **Fix:** de-duplicate names on write.
14. **We guessed what template sound IDs were and were wrong** (430001000 is a 0.15 s clank, not a swing). **Fix:**
    decode every WEM of the bank and hash candidate names `Play_c<chr><xx><yyy>` to list each event's clips,
    length and loudness before using one as a test sound.
15. **Ported sounds far too quiet and pitched down.** **Cause:** the cloned container carried the template's props
    (Volume -21 dB, Pitch -280 cents, random pitch +-100). **Fix:** after the parent id, the container holds a
    u8 bit vector, a prop bundle (u8 n, ids, f32 values; 0 Volume, 2 Pitch) and a ranged bundle; set them neutral.
16. **Cloned actor-mixer pointed at a parent that only exists in the template's bank.** **Fix:** clone the
    template's *top-level* mixer (parent 0, its output bus lives in Init.bnk). (Found while the bank wasn't loading
    at all; correct by Wwise's hierarchy rules but not isolated in game.)
17. **Wwise 2026 vs 2019.** Same Vorbis audio for every file; 2022+ adds a 16-byte `hash` RIFF chunk (we strip
    it). The u32 at fmt+0x3C varies with sample rate/setup; it is not an encoder version. "Auto Detect" lowers
    sample rates and trims silent tails.

## Assets
All art, animation and audio come from the user's own DSR install, converted at build time and kept local:
DDS textures via texconv (BC7 albedo/normal + quarter-size `_l` copies), sounds via vgmstream + WwiseConsole. No
generated assets.

## Cost and time
Four days (2026-10-08 to 10-11); about 30 in-game tests for the body, behaviour and params, 16 for sound (most
of the sound tests were spent on Gotcha 1).

## Credits
Built on community tools and knowledge: WitchyBND and its Paramdex / TAE templates (params, binders, TAE XML),
HKLib (Havok 2018 tagfiles), soulstruct (FLVER / HKX / DSR params), BinderKeys (ER archive keys and names),

## Open questions
- With the 2024 ModEngine build (or me3), does a new character's *own* bank (`sd\cs_c7250.bnk`, SoundBankId
  -1) load? If so, each ported enemy can ship its own bank instead of editing a template's. Our earlier
  conclusions that "missing banks silence a character" and "ER won't play PCM WEMs" were made with the old
  ModEngine and are unproven.
- Port DS1's common swing sound (it lives in DSR's shared bank, not the enemy's).
- Torch/bow Hollow variants (separate animation sets and AI), the dying ragdoll, then randomizer integration
  and more DS1 enemies (Black Knight c2790 -> c7279).
```

```md
# Sunless (Shadow Slave) in Elden Ring: params, native DLL, retextures and a shade army

A playable Sunless from *Shadow Slave*: an aimed shadow teleport costed in FP, a
shapeshifting mirror sword that learns elements from greases, a near-death
damage blade, and an army of black silhouettes raised from whatever you have
killed. Three new weapon rows with their own models and textures, a rebuilt
`regulation.bin`, and a native Rust DLL loaded by me3. It runs in the real game;
the Verification section separates what was observed from what was only reasoned.

The parts worth stealing regardless of what you are building: a **scriptable
param pipeline with a round-trip proof**, a way to **read the game archives
without touching RSA keys**, the **FLVER → MATBIN → TPF** chain that decides
whether your model renders at all, and a full account of Elden Ring's
**spirit-summon system as a general-purpose "spawn an ally" mechanism**.

## Setup

| | |
|---|---|
| Game | Elden Ring 1.17.1, exe ProductVersion **2.7.1.0**, Steam appid 1245620, SOTE installed |
| Loader | [me3](https://github.com/garyttierney/me3) 0.13.0 |
| Bindings | [fromsoftware-rs](https://github.com/vswarte/fromsoftware-rs), pinned by git **rev**, not branch |
| Params/archives | WitchyBND 3.0.1.0 |
| Textures | `texconv.exe` from DirectXTex |
| Overlay | hudhook 0.9.3, DX12 backend, imgui 0.12 |
| DLL | Rust `cdylib`, `panic = "unwind"` (see gotcha 1) |

me3 starts `eldenring.exe` directly instead of going through
`start_protected_game.exe`, so EAC never loads and the game runs offline, with a
separate savefile. Nothing here requires defeating anti-cheat, and the modded
client must never go online.

**Pin the bindings by revision.** crates.io `eldenring` 0.14.0 only carries RVA
tables for 2.6.2.0/2.6.2.1 and panics on anything else. Upstream main had added
the 2.7.1.0 table; a `rev = "..."` pin gets it without a branch moving under you.

## Route and why

**Params + a native DLL + asset replacement, all delivered by me3.** Params for
anything the game already models (weapons, effects, shop entries, summon rows);
the DLL for behaviour the game has no concept of (an aimed teleport, a radial
menu, binding a creature's shade on death).

Rejected: **UXM**. It unpacks the game and patches the exe, which is heavier and
harder to undo than me3's load-order overlay. Its *dictionary* of archive paths
is still useful — see Archives.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Params

`regulation.bin` is a **DCX_ZSTD-compressed BND4** holding ~194 param tables,
AES-encrypted on disk with a key that is public in SoulsFormats. WitchyBND
decrypts and unpacks it to `.param` files, each of which unpacks again to XML.

**A field absent from a row's XML is that field at its paramdef default, not
zero.** This is the most dangerous thing about scripting param edits: a row that
looks empty is inheriting dozens of values. Resolve defaults before reading
anything, and write a field only when it differs from its default.

Upgrade paths: `reinforceTypeId` / `materialSetId` **2200** is the standard
somber path (+0..+10). **`isEnhance` means "can change affinity", not "can be
upgraded"** — a weapon with `materialSetId = -1` cannot be reinforced at all,
which presents as a weapon permanently stuck at +0.

Cloning must rewrite self-references. A weapon row carries 26 `originEquipWep*`
fields describing its own upgrade chain; miss one and the tree walks back into
the original weapon.

### Text

Item names live in `msg/engus/item.msgbnd.dcx` — **and in `item_dlc01.msgbnd.dcx`
and `item_dlc02.msgbnd.dcx`, which are complete replacements, not patches.** With
SOTE installed the DLC archive wins and the base file is ignored entirely. Edit
and ship all three or your names silently do not change.

### Archives

Game data lives in `Data*.bhd` (index) + `Data*.bdt` (payload). The index is
RSA-encrypted, each file inside is AES-128-ECB with a per-file key, and paths are
located by a **64-bit hash: iteratively `hash * 133 + byte` over the lowercased
path**.

You do not need the RSA keys. **me3 leaves a decrypted copy of each BHD in its
cache** (with `boot_boost` on: `<xxh3 hash>.bhd.zz`, a u32 decrypted length and
then raw Deflate), so a reader can parse those and pull single files out of the
BDTs. Ours is ~400 lines of Python with a pure-Python AES checked against the
FIPS-197 test vector on every run, so a decryption bug cannot masquerade as a
corrupt file. The UXM dictionary is a good source for the path list.

For shared installs: filter the BHD indexes by game codename — Nightreign's
(`CL_*`) sit alongside Elden Ring's and match nothing.

### Models, materials and textures

The chain is **FLVER → MATBIN → TPF**, and the middle link is the one that bites.

A FLVER mesh does **not** reference textures directly; it names a **material**,
and the material (a MATBIN inside `allmaterial.matbinbnd.dcx`) names the textures
and the shader. So renaming a weapon's textures and byte-patching the FLVER to
match yields a **white, untextured mesh** — the FLVER now points at a material
that does not exist. You must also create the MATBIN.

MATBIN v2 layout: magic `MAB\0`, version, two `i64` offsets to shader and source
paths, counts, then a param table (0x28 per entry) and a sampler table (0x30 per
entry), with strings UTF-16LE elsewhere in the file.

**DDS header style is load-bearing.** Elden Ring ships `_m` metallic maps as
legacy `ATI1`; `texconv -dx10` writes a DX10 header for the same data and the
model renders white. The fix that works regardless of format: re-encode, then
**copy the original file's DDS header back onto the new pixel data**.

Channel meanings, established by experiment: on the normal map, **B is shininess,
not roughness** — higher is shinier. Setting it low on the theory that "blurry =
rough" produced a completely flat blade.

### Weapons cannot reflect, and this is settled

Several rounds went into a mirror-finish sword. The answer is in the game's own
data and takes one query: of **707 distinct shaders across 15,089 materials**,
screen-space reflection is enabled on **110**, and **every one is static map
geometry** on an `M[...]`-family shader. All **559 weapon materials** are on
`C[...]` character shaders, which carry the SSR parameter *name* as shared
boilerplate but never feed the SSR pass. The only true reflection shader in the
game is a cutscene ocean plane.

Metallic, shininess and the shader's colour parameters buy an environment sheen
and nothing more. If you need a mirror on a weapon, **bake it into the albedo** —
paint a horizon, because a hard edge is what reads as reflective and a smooth
brightness ramp never will, however bright you make it.

### Spirit summons as a general "spawn an ally" mechanism

The most reusable finding here. Elden Ring's spirit-ash system will summon **any
creature in the game** as a working ally, driven entirely by params plus one
integer written at runtime.

- A **`BuddyParam`** row is `{ triggerSpEffectId, npcParamId, npcThinkParamId }`
  plus an x/z spawn offset.
- `SummonBuddyManager` holds `trigger_speffect_to_buddy_map`, a **chaining** map:
  **many BuddyParam rows may share one trigger SpEffect** and are summoned
  together. That is how vanilla's group ashes work — 36 of 94 vanilla triggers
  drive more than one row.
- Writing **`request_summon_speffect_id`** asks for a summon. The binding notes
  it is "written by TAE goods consume" — the animation event fired when you use
  an ash — so writing it directly does what the game does, one step earlier.
- **The id encodes the chr model.** BuddyParam never names a model and
  NpcParam has no model field. For ordinary eight-digit enemy rows the 4-digit
  chr id is `npcParamId / 10000`: Torrent's row 80000000 is c8000, and
  `ChrIns.character_id` holds the same 8000. Dividing by 100000 drops the last
  digit and merges models: Juvenile Scholar (20400000) and Kindred of Rot Larva
  (20410000) both become 204. The purpose-built `[Spirit Summon]` rows have nine
  digits and don't follow this pattern. One integer read off a corpse therefore
  carries the entire creature.
- Rows can be rewritten **in live memory** through the param repository, so the
  roster need not be fixed at build time.

Four things the system will not do for you:

1. **Team.** A real enemy's NpcParam is on the hostile team; only the ~115
   purpose-built `[Spirit Summon]` rows carry team **47**. Force `team_type` on
   the spawned character — every frame, since the engine builds it from that row
   after you act.
2. **Appearance.** Use **`PhantomParam`** via `ChrIns.phantom_param_override`,
   the layer that makes every ash look spectral. The field that matters is
   **`diffMulColorA`**: at 0 the creature's own texture is deleted and you get a
   silhouette; vanilla's spirit row leaves it at 0.9, which is why ashes look
   like blue-tinted versions of themselves rather than shadows.
3. **Placement.** Offsets are relative to **`spawn_origin` AND `spawn_rotation`**;
   setting only the origin anchors the formation to a fixed world bearing.
   Creatures also need room — a Troll's `hitRadius` is 1.8 m, so spawn points
   1.4 m apart simply fail to place it, silently.
4. **Count.** Vanilla's largest group is 5. The practical ceiling measured here
   is **10 rows per trigger**: asking for 12 reliably lost the last two, and the
   proof it is a slot limit rather than size or placement is that a creature
   *identical in size* to ten that spawned failed purely by being in slot 10.
   Note `summon_buddy_chr_set.capacity` reports 80 — that is the ChrSet array,
   not what one trigger can drive.

**Torrent lives in the summon ChrSet too.** Anything iterating it and writing to
what it finds will modify the player's horse.

Power scaling is the doping ladder `290000..290010`, the game's own ash upgrade
levels: `290000` applies **no** HP or attack multiplier at all (so a summon keeps
the creature's native stats), while `290010` is ×7.4 HP and ×3.8 attack.

### Effects, and an inheritance trap

`spCategory` is the axis the engine uses to decide which effects **displace**
which, and a cloned SpEffect inherits it. Two of our abilities cloned from
unrelated sources that both sat in category 20 and silently fought; our
weapon-enchant effects inherited the greases' category and were displaced by real
greases while the mod still believed them active. Give mod-owned effects private
categories (the game's highest is 10010).

### Input and the camera

Elden Ring reads **DirectInput only**; nothing reaches an ImGui overlay through
raw input, so an overlay-driven radial menu gets no mouse state.

Reading `MouseDevice` works for *getting* movement, and zeroing it does **not**
stop the camera: `CSPad::poll_analog_input` reads an aggregate assembled during
`PadStep`, earlier in the frame than any mod task. The lever that works is
**`FD4BasePad.allow_polling`**, which the poll functions check first — clear it
and the camera holds perfectly still. Do it before `CameraStep`;
`ChrIns_PrePhysics` is early enough.

### Singletons exist before they are populated

`WorldChrMan::instance()` succeeding means the object exists, **not** that the
engine has filled it in. On the first frame it succeeds, its summon manager
pointer is **null** and its character counts are zero. Reading a pointer typed
non-null there and dereferencing it is a hard fault, not a Rust panic, so
`catch_unwind` will not save you.

### Bonfire (resting) state

`CSLuaEventProxy.control_flags` carries four bits: the sit-down request, the
sitting loop, the stand-up, and a pending end. **Only `bonfire_stand_up_in_progress`
is documented as being cleared when a rest ends**; the sit-down bit is only
cleared when the next rest begins. Treating "any bit set" as "is resting" reads
true forever after the first rest. What does work is edge-triggering on the
four-bit pattern *changing*, since the one bit that does clear keeps it moving.

## Build steps

1. Install me3. Unpack **your own** `regulation.bin` once with WitchyBND as the
   build's pristine input. Nothing from the game is redistributed.
2. `python params/build_regulation.py --verify` — applies a declarative row spec
   (clone-from-vanilla, or blank-from-defaults, plus field overrides), repacks,
   then re-unpacks and proves only the intended params differ.
3. `python params/build_text.py` — patches all three `item*.msgbnd.dcx`.
4. `python tools/retexture.py --all` — pulls the vanilla weapon part files,
   recolours albedo/metallic/normal, re-encodes, renames every reference (TPF
   entries, BND manifest, FLVER strings), and builds the new MATBINs.
5. `cargo build --release` in the DLL crate.
6. `python stage.py` — assembles the me3 profile: the DLL in `natives/`, and
   `regulation.bin`, `msg/`, `parts/`, `material/` in the package.
7. `me3 launch -p <profile>.me3 -g eldenring`.

## Verification

**The DLL's own log is the primary oracle.** It prints a line per ability event
carrying the numbers that decided it, plus a periodic state line. Several bugs
here sat visible in it for multiple sessions before anyone read the field that
mattered — including a count that was *one too high* printed directly beside the
count that was one too low, which turned out to be the same bug.

Also used, all repeatable without launching the game:

- **Param round-trip:** 194 params in, 194 out, only the intended ones differ by
  hash, plus a read-back of every added row and edited field.
- **A constants check** asserting the ids shared between the param script and the
  Rust, wired into staging so a drift cannot ship. Nothing else would catch it:
  the symptom is summons silently not appearing.
- **Pixel measurement of the shipped textures** — unpack from the staged build,
  convert, assert contrast and saturation. This caught a debug "probe" texture
  nearly shipping, and a blade whose bands had landed on the wooden hilt.
- **Screenshots of the running game**, then cropping and sampling pixels rather
  than eyeballing.

**Not verified:** the i-frame and stealth windows are never logged and were only
confirmed by feel; the near-death damage bonus was never observed firing; and the
mod has only ever run on this machine and game version.

## Gotchas

1. **The game dies instantly, exit code 0xC0000409, no log.** *Cause:* a panic on
   the mod's boot thread with `panic = "abort"` in the release profile. *Fix:*
   never use `panic = "abort"` in a game mod. Unwind, log from a panic hook, and
   wrap every engine entry point in `catch_unwind`.
2. **A crash with an empty log is not a panic.** *Cause:* a bad memory access,
   which `catch_unwind` cannot contain. *Fix:* use the log's last line to date
   the fault, then look for a pointer dereference in whatever ran next. "Dies on
   the first frame the world exists" is a diagnosis, not an absence of one.
3. **Dereferencing a singleton's sub-pointer on the first frame it is available
   crashes.** *Cause:* the object is published before it is populated. *Fix:*
   read the pointer as an **integer** and test it before forming a reference —
   `&*p` is undefined behaviour when `p` is null, before any read. Re-check every
   frame; a one-shot readiness test latches the wrong answer if it samples the
   empty frame.
4. **Reading an engine enum out of memory is undefined behaviour.** *Cause:* a
   `#[repr(u8)]` enum valid for 0..=5 does not tolerate a 6, and walking
   uninitialised container slots guarantees you meet one. *Fix:* read the byte,
   compare the number.
5. **Retextured weapons render pure white.** *Cause (a):* texconv wrote a DX10
   DDS header where the game ships legacy `ATI1`. *Cause (b), the real one:* the
   FLVER references a **material**, so renaming textures left it pointing at a
   MATBIN that does not exist. *Fix:* adopt the original DDS header, and create
   the MATBIN.
6. **Weapon names do not change despite editing `item.msgbnd.dcx`.** *Cause:*
   with SOTE installed, `item_dlc02.msgbnd.dcx` is a full replacement and wins.
   *Fix:* patch and ship all three.
7. **A cloned weapon is stuck at +0.** *Cause:* `materialSetId = -1`; `isEnhance`
   is about affinity, not upgrading. *Fix:* set a real reinforce path.
8. **A summoned ally is hostile.** *Cause:* you used the enemy's own NpcParam,
   which is on the enemy team. *Fix:* force `team_type` to 47, every frame.
9. **The summon appears, then vanishes seconds later.** *Cause:* vanilla ties
   summons to a buddy stone's activation range and despawns them outside it.
   *Fix:* assert the in-range flags **and their `prev_` partners**, or the
   in→out transition still fires.
10. **The summon formation faces the wrong way.** *Cause:* offsets are applied at
    `spawn_rotation`, which was never set, so the formation anchors to a fixed
    world bearing. *Fix:* set it from the player's facing — and note that
    **flipping the sign of an offset can never fix a rotation error**, it only
    changes which facing is broken.
11. **"Asked for 12, got 11", repeatedly.** *Cause — three separate ones:* a
    stale summon from the previous request holding a slot; **Torrent** occupying
    one; and a real ~10-row ceiling per trigger. *Fix:* sweep your own summons
    before requesting, exclude the horse, cap at ten.
12. **The player's horse turns into a black silhouette.** *Cause:* Torrent lives
    in the summon ChrSet and the grooming loop wrote to everything it found.
    *Fix:* exclude it. Its `character_id` is **8000** (model c8000, NpcParam
    80000000); 800 is what `npcParamId / 100000` gives, so compare like with
    like.
13. **An enable flag has no effect.** *Cause:* `g_GX_bEnableSSR` exists in every
    material's shared parameter block, weapon or not, but is only sampled for map
    geometry. *Fix:* check a parameter's *distribution* across the game before
    believing its name.
14. **Two unrelated abilities interfere.** *Cause:* both SpEffects were cloned
    from sources sharing an `spCategory`, the engine's overwrite axis. *Fix:*
    give mod-owned effects private categories.
15. **Keys fire twice or do something unintended.** *Cause:* Elden Ring binds
    most of the keyboard — `C` is Switch Item, `Space` is jump. *Fix:* use keys
    the game does not bind, and make them rebindable. Suppressing the game's own
    jump key through an input freeze is a far larger claim than not using it.
16. **A radial menu gets no mouse input.** *Cause:* the game is DirectInput-only.
    *Fix:* read `MouseDevice` directly and accumulate movement yourself.
17. **The camera keeps moving while a menu is open.** *Cause:* zeroing the mouse
    device is too late; the camera reads an aggregate built during `PadStep`.
    *Fix:* clear `FD4BasePad.allow_polling` in a pre-physics task.
18. **A modal UI's action key leaks into the game on close.** *Cause:* the input
    freeze lifts the instant the modal closes, while the key is still held. *Fix:*
    hold the freeze until the action keys are released too.
19. **A painted "mirror" reads as shiny metal, never as a mirror.** *Cause:* a
    smooth brightness ramp contains no edge anywhere, and an edge is what a mirror
    *is*. *Fix:* paint a hard horizon — and put it where the blade's UVs actually
    are; bands spread across a whole atlas gave the visible face about a third of
    one period, i.e. a gradient.
20. **Texture changes land on the wrong part of the model.** *Cause:* the UV
    layout is not inferable from the vanilla art — the smooth-looking half of one
    atlas was the crossguard, not the blade. *Fix:* ship a debug texture of
    saturated colour bands and read the answer off a screenshot. Better still,
    check the **metallic mask** first: it needs no launch, and if your pipeline
    only paints where the mask says metal, a span with no metal under it cannot
    produce anything.
21. **Param script and native code drift apart silently.** *Cause:* ids shared
    between a build script and the DLL, kept in step only by a comment. *Fix:* a
    check that asserts them, wired into the build.

## Assets

No generated art. Everything is a **recolour of the game's own textures**: the
vanilla weapon's albedo, metallic and normal maps are pulled out, worked in
perceptual space with the metallic mask separating metal from wood and leather,
and re-encoded in the original formats. Models are vanilla FLVERs copied to new
ids with their material references renamed — nothing from the game is
redistributed, and the pipeline runs against the user's own install.

## Cost and time

Several sessions across about four days. The dominant cost was not writing code
but **launch-and-look cycles** on things that cannot be previewed offline —
particle effects, shader appearance, UV layouts. Anything that reduces those paid
for itself many times over: a config file re-read once a second while the game
runs, and a debug texture that answers three questions in a single launch.

## Open questions

- **Why exactly ten summons per trigger?** Measured, not explained. The limit may
  be in the summon manager, in the chaining map, or elsewhere.
- **A genuine weapon reflection** is impossible by the route above. Borrowing a
  map shader onto a weapon mesh is the only untried idea, and the vertex layouts
  do not match, so the expected result is an invisible weapon.
- **Identifying a mesh's visible face offline.** Decoding FLVER UVs is easy;
  deciding which region the player actually *sees* is not. Vertex density is
  nearly the inverse of visible area — a flat blade is few vertices, a pommel is
  many — so it needs triangle areas. Until then the debug-texture probe wins.
- **`spCategory` semantics** are only partially understood here; we moved our
  effects out of the way rather than learning the full rule.

```

`knowledge/games/etrian-odyssey-2-hd/etria-inside-eo2-bepinex-protected-il2cpp.md`:

```md
---
kind: game
title: "Etrian Odyssey 1's labyrinth and battles running inside Etrian Odyssey 2 HD (BepInEx on a protected IL2CPP build)"
game: "Etrian Odyssey II HD"
games_also: ["Etrian Odyssey HD"]
game_version: "Steam builds of Oct 2026 (EO2 app 1868170, EO1 app 1868180), Unity 2020.3.1f1, IL2CPP"

anti_cheat: "none (single-player). Both games ship with Denuvo (Steam store DRM notice); it stays in place and is never unpacked or removed. The lab copy runs with steam_appid.txt through the owning Steam account"
status: in-progress
agents: ["Claude Code (Opus 5.5)"]
humans: []
date: 2026-10-12
links: []
tags: [bepinex, il2cpp, protected-gameassembly, denuvo, il2cppinterop, addressables, cross-game, mashup, harmony, save-redirect]
---

# Etrian Odyssey 1's labyrinth and battles running inside Etrian Odyssey 2 HD

> A BepInEx plugin in a lab copy of EO2 HD loads EO1 HD's Addressables content at runtime and swaps it into
> EO2's systems: EO1's floors, events, text, world state and enemies run inside EO2's engine. Verified in game
> by screenshots (walking EO1's first floor, EO1 town/quest events, a won battle against EO1 monsters). The
> hard parts were getting BepInEx to start at all on EO2's protected GameAssembly, and loading a second game's
> Addressables catalog without breaking the host. The protection stays in place throughout: the game unpacks its
> own code at run time, and the plugin side only follows the resulting jump stubs in the running process.

## Setup
- Windows 11, Steam installs of both games. Both are Unity 2020.3.1f1 IL2CPP, metadata v27, Addressables with
  JSON `catalog.json`.
- Lab copy of the game folder + `steam_appid.txt` (never the Steam install). Steam still has to be running and
  signed in to the account that owns both games: the file only lets the copy start outside the library, and
  changes nothing about ownership or DRM. BepInEx 6.0.0-be.788 Unity.IL2CPP win-x64 unzipped into it. .NET 8
  SDK (user-local `dotnet-install.ps1`). Il2CppDumper 6.7.46 (.NET Framework build) for reading types.

## Route and why
`managed-patch`: Harmony patches on existing game methods from a BepInEx plugin. Both games share ~8,466
script types, so the host engine already contains almost every code path the guest needs; the work is
feeding it the guest's data and assets. Full reimplementation would have been far larger.
- In the terms of [`choosing-a-mashup-route.md`](../../techniques/choosing-a-mashup-route.md), this is content
  ported into a sibling host, loaded from the user's own guest install at run time. The closest earlier case is
  [Pre-Sequel assets in Borderlands 2](../../techniques/loading-pre-sequel-assets-in-borderlands-2.md), also two
  games on one engine branch.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Protected GameAssembly.dll (EO2):** both games' Steam pages list Denuvo. EO2's GameAssembly has scrambled
  section names, a ~300 MB `.link` section, and every il2cpp export is a stub
  `call <spin-wait-until-unpacked>; jmp <thunk>` with `thunk: jmp <real body>`. Some exports have their callee
  inlined (`il2cpp_field_static_get_value` contains `Field::StaticGetValue`). Nothing in this note unpacks,
  dumps or removes the protection.
- **Interop namespaces** are real C# namespaces that Il2CppDumper's dump.cs doesn't show (`Master.MasterManager`,
  `MasterData.MasterDataTypes`, `Common.TextLabelDataManager`, `DungeonData.*`, `EventScript.EventObjCombine`).
  Obfuscated member names (BB obfuscator) differ between the two games' builds.
- **Master data:** `MasterManager` holds `MasterData.bin` + `MasterOffset.bin` (u32 offsets ÷ 4, indexed by a
  `DataEnum`) as byte[] fields; events actually run from a separate `EventObjCombine` ScriptableObject
  (per data file: index table + script bytes), so swapping the blob alone changes nothing.
- **Floors** are `DungeonDataScriptableObject` assets (35×30 cell grid, model layout, placed prefabs), kept in
  memory and selected by `DungeonDataManager.DgLoadFloor(int)` — overwriting the host asset's fields in a prefix
  swaps the floor.
- **Saves:** `SaveDataManager` is a `SingletonWithoutMonobehaviour<T>` (not a Unity object); the folder comes
  from `Environment.GetFolderPath(ApplicationData)`.
- **Per-frame hooks:** `InputManager.Update` runs in town/dungeon but not on the title screen; there is no
  patchable per-frame game code on the title screen at all (input goes through InControl).

## Build steps
1. Lab copy, BepInEx, first launch to generate `BepInEx/interop`.
2. Set `[Logging] UnityLogListening = false` in `BepInEx.cfg`.
3. Rebuild Il2CppInterop.Runtime at the exact commit of the bundled DLL (its file version contains the hash)
   with two changes in `InjectorHelpers`: `TryGetIl2CppExport` unthunks the protector's two shapes only
   (`E8 rel32 E9 rel32` → target; then `E9 rel32 CC` → target), and `Setup()` applies each injector hook in a
   try/catch that logs and continues. Copy over `BepInEx/core/Il2CppInterop.Runtime.dll`, keep the original.
4. Plugin csproj (net6.0) referencing `BepInEx/core/*` and `BepInEx/interop/*` with `Private=false`, output
   straight into `BepInEx/plugins/<name>/`. Close the game before building (the DLL is locked).
5. First patch: redirect `Il2CppSystem.Environment.GetFolderPath` (both overloads) so the lab copy saves into
   its own folder.
6. Cross-game assets: rewrite a copy of the guest's `catalog.json` (`{...RuntimePath}` → absolute guest
   `StreamingAssets/aa`, new `m_LocatorId`), load it with `Addressables.LoadContentCatalogAsync`, then
   immediately `Addressables.RemoveResourceLocator(locator)` and look up guest keys via that locator only.

## Verification
- Oracle: screenshots of the real game plus BepInEx and Unity `Player.log`. Verified: chainloader starts;
  Harmony postfix fires on `MasterManager.GetMasterDataSize` (in-memory MasterData size = file size);
  guest music plays; guest floor 1 renders and is walkable with the guest's automap; guest town menu and
  quest events run; a random battle shows the guest's monsters and is won; lab saves land in the lab folder
  and the real save folder stays untouched.
- Not verified: guest enemy AI (all guest enemies use one host script), FOEs, treasure, later floors.

## Gotchas
1. **`Sequence contains more than one element` in `GenericMethod_GetMethod_Hook`, chainloader dead.**
   **Cause:** the protector's export stubs break Il2CppInterop's xref scans (`JumpTargets(...).Single()`).
   **Fix:** `UnityLogListening = false` gets the chainloader up; for class injection, the unthunk + tolerant
   hooks patch above.
2. **Unthunk too eager → a different hook breaks.** Following every `jmp` also "unwraps" exports that are
   legitimately one-jump wrappers. **Fix:** match only the protector's exact byte shapes.
3. **Class injection still crashes (AccessViolation in `Class_FromName_Hook`).** **Cause:** with tolerant hooks a
   scan can "succeed" on the wrong function. **Fix:** no injected classes, no `DelegateSupport.ConvertDelegate`,
   no custom MonoBehaviours; patch existing methods only.
4. **AccessViolation a scene after writing ~1,700 entries into the host's native text-label dictionary.**
   **Cause:** managed-created strings stored in a native IL2CPP container. **Fix:** postfix `TextAsset.text` and
   serve merged CSVs so the host builds its own dictionary.
5. **Crash after hooking `TryGetTextLabelData` (a non-blittable struct `out` param).** Don't hook methods with
   non-blittable struct out/ref parameters.
6. **"An item with the same key has already been added" at boot after loading the guest catalog.**
   **Cause:** registered globally, the host's label-wide load (tutorial images) also returned the guest's
   same-named assets. **Fix:** remove the guest locator right after loading; query it directly.
7. **Guest enemy sprites "No Location found for Key".** The host loads them via generic
   `LoadAssetAsync<T>(object)`, which can't be patched. **Fix:** `Addressables.AddResourceLocator(guest)` only
   after the host's boot-time loads are done (on entering the labyrinth); host locators stay first for
   shared keys.
8. **Patched `TitleMenu.Open` never fires.** Small methods are inlined by IL2CPP. Poll state or use a
   background thread instead.
9. **`Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<SaveDataManager>` returns nothing.** It's a plain C# singleton; call
   `get_Instance` via reflection.
10. **Plugin build fails "file is locked by the game".** Close the game; MSBuild retries then fails.
11. **The first lab run rewrites the real settings save.** It happens before any plugin loads (BepInEx
    interop generation run). Back up the real save folder before the very first launch of the lab copy.

## Assets
None generated; all guest assets are loaded from the user's own installed copy of the guest game at runtime.

## Cost and time
Roughly two long sessions for M0–M4 (plugin running → guest floors, events, text, battles).

## Open questions
- Converting the guest's table-driven enemy AI to the host's flowscript AI.
- Whether the tolerant-hook Il2CppInterop patch generalises to other protectors; upstreaming a safer xref
  fallback.

```

```md
# Factorio 2.0 recon: official Lua mod API, info.json, mods under %APPDATA%

> Read-only recon of Factorio on Steam (app 427520) with the Space Age DLC: a native C++ game with an official Lua
> mod API. Mods are folders or zips in `%APPDATA%\Factorio\mods`, each with an `info.json`. `data.lua` defines
> prototypes and `control.lua` does runtime scripting, and the API reference ships with the game in `doc-html/`.
> Nothing was built or launched, and the version below comes from an old log, not from the install.

## Setup

- Steam, Windows x64. The game binary is `bin\x64\factorio.exe`, not in the install root.
- Version: the last launch was `2.0.72 (build 84292, win64, steam, space-age)`, from
  `%APPDATA%\Factorio\factorio-current.log` dated 2026-01-05. Steam has probably updated the game since. The
  installed version is in `data/base/info.json`, which wasn't read (Gotcha 1).
- The install's `data/` has `base/`, `core/` and the Space Age folders `elevated-rails/`, `quality/` and
  `space-age/`.
- User data: `%APPDATA%\Factorio` holds `mods/` (with `mod-list.json`), `saves/`, `player-data.json` and the logs.
  The log also prints the config, data and write-data paths the game uses.
- `doc-html/` in the install is the Lua API reference (classes, concepts, prototypes).
- Current releases (lua-api.factorio.com, 2026-10-08): stable 2.0.77, experimental 2.1.21.

## Route and why

The official Lua API: develop in `%APPDATA%\Factorio\mods` and publish on the Mod Portal. No loader, hooks or
patching. `um scan`'s known-game route says the same (`misc-engines.md`). Rejected: native hooks, which are
unsupported and unnecessary next to an official API.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

- `info.json` is the only mandatory file in a mod (Lua API docs, "Mod structure"). `name`, `version`, `title` and
  `author` are mandatory. `factorio_version` defaults to `"0.12"` when it's left out, so set it to `"2.0"`. A mod
  that uses Space Age content lists `space-age` in `dependencies`.
- Naming: an unzipped mod folder is `{name}_{version}` or just `{name}`. A zip must be `{name}_{version}.zip`, and
  the folder inside it can have any name.
- Stages: `data.lua` (with `data-updates.lua` and `data-final-fixes.lua`) defines prototypes. `control.lua` is
  runtime scripting.
- Mods are enabled in `mods/mod-list.json` or the in-game Mods menu, which also downloads from the Mod Portal and
  resolves dependencies.
- The base game and the DLC sit in the install's `data/` with their own `info.json`. Don't edit them in place;
  override from a mod.
- The online API docs are versioned (`lua-api.factorio.com/<version>/`), and `/latest/` is the newest stable.
  Read the tree for the installed version, or the `doc-html/` that ships with the install.

## Build steps

1. `um scan Factorio --json`: expect engine `native`, the known-game Lua API route, and the `%APPDATA%\Factorio`
   saves hint.
2. Read the installed version from `data/base/info.json` (`version`) and use the matching API docs.
3. Create `%APPDATA%\Factorio\mods\<name>\` with an `info.json` (`name`, `version`, `title`, `author`,
   `factorio_version: "2.0"`), then `data.lua` for prototypes and/or `control.lua` for runtime scripting.
4. Back up `%APPDATA%\Factorio\saves` (`um backup`), then enable the mod in `mod-list.json` or the in-game Mods
   menu.

## Verification

- Read directly on 2026-10-08: `um scan` output, the head of `factorio-current.log` (version, build, paths), the
  `%APPDATA%\Factorio` listing, the install's `data/` folders and `doc-html/`.
- From the docs: the `info.json` rules and folder naming (Lua API "Mod structure" page, checked 2026-10-09), and
  the current versions (2026-10-08).
- Not verified: the installed version, launching with a mod, Mod Portal downloads, Space Age prototype overrides,
  multiplayer mod sync.

## Gotchas

1. **The version in `factorio-current.log` can be months old.** The log read here said 2.0.72 and was dated
   2026-01-05. **Cause:** the game writes that log when it starts, and Steam updates the files without launching
   the game. **Fix:** read `version` from `data/base/info.json` in the install.

## Assets

None (recon only). Factorio mods are mostly prototypes and Lua. Art would follow the sprite specs in the
prototype docs.

## Open questions

- The installed version (read `data/base/info.json`).
- How mods sync to a headless server (there's no server on this machine).

## Sources and verification

- Local install and user data, read-only, 2026-10-08: the head of `factorio-current.log` (dated 2026-01-05), the
  `%APPDATA%\Factorio` listing, the `data/` folders, `doc-html/`, `bin\x64\factorio.exe`.
- lua-api.factorio.com (fetched 2026-10-08): versioned API trees, latest stable 2.0.77, experimental 2.1.21. The
  front page links the Mod Portal, the wiki and the forums.
- lua-api.factorio.com/latest/auxiliary/mod-structure.html (checked 2026-10-09): `info.json` is "the only
  mandatory file", its mandatory fields, the `factorio_version` default, folder and zip naming.
- `um scan Factorio --json`, run in-session.
```

```md
# Fallout 4 recon: F4SE for runtime 1.11.221 next to Address Library databases for 1.10.x only

> Read-only recon of a modded Steam install of Fallout 4 (app 377160): Creation engine, x64, F4SE and the
> Creation Kit installed, and Vortex deploying into `Data/`. The useful finding is a mismatch. The game root has
> `f4se_1_11_221.dll`, but `Data/F4SE/Plugins/` only had `version-1-10-*.bin` Address Library databases, so any
> F4SE plugin built on Address Library would fail on 1.11.221 until a matching database is installed. Nothing was
> built or launched, and the game exe's own version wasn't read.

## Setup

- Steam install (app 377160), Windows, x64. `um scan` reports engine `creation` from the DLC `.esm` masters in
  `Data/`, and the Script Extender loader from `f4se_loader.exe`.
- Root exes: `Fallout4.exe`, `Fallout4Launcher.exe`, `CreationKit.exe`, `f4se_loader.exe`.
- F4SE in the game root: `f4se_1_11_221.dll`, `f4se_loader.exe`, `f4se_readme.txt`, `f4se_whatsnew.txt`. The DLL's
  name is the game runtime that F4SE build targets.
- `Data/F4SE/Plugins/` held F4SE plugin DLLs, a Vortex marker (`__folder_managed_by_vortex`) and Address Library
  databases named `version-1-10-*.bin`, with none for 1.11.x.
- Game build: not established. See Gotcha 2 for how not to read it.
- Current F4SE builds (f4se.silverlock.org, 2026-10-08): 0.7.9 for runtime 1.11.240, 0.7.2 for 1.10.984, 0.6.23
  for 1.10.163. Steam and GOG are supported but are on different versions; the Windows Store version isn't.
- No anti-cheat.

## Route and why

Data plugins first: `.esp`/`.esl` made in FO4Edit or the Creation Kit for items, records and quests. F4SE plugin
DLLs (`Data/F4SE/Plugins/*.dll`) only when the change needs engine code. Most are built on CommonLibF4 and
Address Library, which ties them to the game's runtime version. Install both through the mod manager that owns the
install (Vortex here). This is the `bethesda.md` playbook's route. Rejected: native hooks outside F4SE, since the
extender already provides a loader and a plugin API.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

- Content is `.esm` masters plus `.ba2` archives. Mods add `.esp`/`.esl` plugins and loose files under `Data/`.
  Load order lives in `Plugins.txt` and the manager's profile, not in the game folder.
- Each F4SE build supports one game runtime, named in its DLL (`f4se_1_11_221.dll`). After a game update, F4SE
  needs the build for the new runtime.
- Address Library: CommonLibF4-based plugins don't hardcode addresses. They look up IDs in a per-runtime database.
  CommonLibF4's `IDDatabase::load` opens `Data/F4SE/Plugins/version-<runtime>.bin` (the runtime with dashes, e.g.
  `version-1-10-163-0.bin`) and fails hard if that file is missing. The databases present have to cover the
  runtime the game actually runs.
- `__folder_managed_by_vortex` in a folder means Vortex deploys into it. Add and remove mods through Vortex, not
  by hand, so its deployment stays consistent.

## Build steps

1. `um scan "Fallout 4" --json`: expect engine `creation` and the Script Extender loader flag.
2. Read the game's version: `(Get-Item "<install>\Fallout4.exe").VersionInfo.FileVersion` in PowerShell, or any
   other `GetFileVersionInfo` reader. Compare it with the `f4se_<runtime>.dll` in the game root.
3. Check `Data/F4SE/Plugins/` for `version-<that runtime>.bin`. If it's missing, install the Address Library
   release for that runtime through the manager before launching with F4SE plugins.
4. Data mods: `.esp`/`.esl` in FO4Edit or the Creation Kit. Engine mods: an F4SE plugin DLL against CommonLibF4.
   Install both through the manager.
5. Back up `Documents/My Games/Fallout4` (`um backup`) before the first modded launch.

## Verification

- Read directly on 2026-10-08: the root F4SE files, the `Data/F4SE/Plugins/` listing (plugin DLLs, Vortex marker,
  `version-1-10-*.bin`), `CreationKit.exe` in the root, and `um scan` output.
- The Address Library behaviour comes from CommonLibF4's `IDDatabase::load`, not from a launch on this install.
- Not verified: launching, F4SE loading, whether the installed plugins use Address Library, the game exe's
  FileVersion, load order.

## Gotchas

1. **Address Library databases for 1.10.x only, next to F4SE for 1.11.221.** `Data/F4SE/Plugins/` had
   `version-1-10-*.bin` files that look like leftovers from an older F4SE. **Cause:** they're Address Library
   databases, one per runtime. CommonLibF4-based plugins open `version-<runtime>.bin` for the running game and fail
   hard when it's missing, so on 1.11.221 they need `version-1-11-221-0.bin`. **Fix:** install the Address Library
   release that matches the game's runtime. Don't treat the 1.10.x files as junk from F4SE. Not reproduced here,
   since the game wasn't launched.
2. **No version string in the first 6 MB of `Fallout4.exe`.** A raw byte scan of the start of the exe found no
   version, so the game build was left unknown. **Cause:** the VERSIONINFO resource sits in the `.rsrc` section
   near the end of the file. **Fix:** read it through the Windows API, e.g.
   `(Get-Item Fallout4.exe).VersionInfo.FileVersion` in PowerShell. CommonLibF4 reads the same resource with
   `GetFileVersionInfo`. Not run on this install yet.

## Assets

None (recon only).

## Open questions

- The game's actual runtime (read `Fallout4.exe`'s FileVersion). If it's 1.11.240, the target of current F4SE
  0.7.9, the installed `f4se_1_11_221.dll` is out of date too. If it's 1.11.221, F4SE matches and only the Address
  Library database is missing.
- Which Address Library release covers 1.11.221 (not checked).
- Whether the installed F4SE plugins depend on Address Library (not checked).

## Sources and verification

- Local install, read-only, 2026-10-08: root F4SE files, `Data/F4SE/Plugins/` listing, `CreationKit.exe`,
  `um scan "Fallout 4" --json`.
- f4se.silverlock.org (fetched 2026-10-08): 0.7.9 for 1.11.240, 0.7.2 for 1.10.984, 0.6.23 for 1.10.163 (0.6.21 is
  VR only). Latest Steam and GOG supported, on different versions; no Windows Store support. Nexus mirror:
  nexusmods.com/fallout4/mods/42147.
- CommonLibF4 `IDDatabase::load`: opens `Data/F4SE/Plugins/version-<runtime>.bin` and fails if it's missing. Its
  runtime version comes from the exe's version resource via `GetFileVersionInfo`.
- creationkit.com (checked 2026-10-08): the official CK wiki served a backend-maintenance notice dated 2024-02-07.
  Until it's back, FO4Edit's docs and the installed Creation Kit's help are the working references.
```

`knowledge/games/far-cry-6/dunia-engine-modding-and-swf-format.md`:

```md
---
kind: game
title: "Far Cry 6 — Dunia engine modding and the SWF/FEU UI format"
game: "Far Cry 6"
```
