# Kenshi 1.0.65 recon: native OGRE engine, FCS data mods, and RE_Kenshi plugin route

> Full read-only reconnaissance of installed Kenshi 1.0.65 (Steam, Windows x64): the game process is native C++ on a custom OGRE 2.0.0unstable fork, not .NET; data mods are FCS-built `.mod` files plus asset overrides; advanced code mods go through RE_Kenshi (an OGRE plugin) and the KenshiLib C++ plugins it loads, not Harmony/BepInEx. Verified from PE headers, import lists, and the game's own logs; no game files were modified.

## Setup

- Game: Kenshi `1.0.65 - x64 (Newland)`, Steam AppID `233860` (from `currentVersion.txt` and `kenshi_info.log` `Version: 1.0.65 - x64 (Newland) (Steam)`).
- Install: `E:\Steam\steamapps\common\Kenshi\` (Steam). Workshop: `E:\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\233860\` (868 subscribed items, 18.3 GB at inspection; **835 active** in `data/mods.cfg` + `data/__mods.list`). Saves: `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Kenshi\` (contains `save/`).
- Workshop census (read-only walk): all 868 items carry `.mod` + XML `.info`. The `.info` schema (`ModData`: `id`, `mod`, `title`, `tags` (list of `string`), `visibility`, `lastUpdate`) is exemplified by Dust's: id `3703458265`, mod/title `Dust` / `Dust - A Kenshi Rendering Framework`, tags `[Graphical]`, `lastUpdate` 2026-04-10. 844 items also carry `.img` previews. 382 items ship asset overrides (`.mesh` 288, `.dds` 227, `.skeleton` 80, `.zone` 56, `.material` 29, ParticleUniverse `.pu` 20, HLSL `.hlsl` 5, MyGUI `.layout` files such as `Kenshi_InventoryCharacterWindow.layout`). Only 6 ship native `.dll`s — all RE_Kenshi-ecosystem plugins, all updated in 2026: BFrizz's Extra Extensions (by the RE_Kenshi author, tagged `RE_Kenshi`), KenshiExtensionPlugin (`kep-core-preload-x64.dll`, the preload pattern), Vital-Sense, KenshiRotate (Rotate Items), Freecam Rebuilt, and Dust (self-titled "A Kenshi Rendering Framework"; its folder ships files named `nvngx_dlss.dll`, `amd_fidelityfx_loader_dx12.dll`, `amd_fidelityfx_upscaler_dx12.dll` plus 16 `Dust<Effect>.dll` files — presence observed, behavior not tested). So: FCS data mods dominate, asset mirrors are common, UI-layout modding is practiced, and native plugins are rare but alive and current.
- Key binaries (sizes from read-only listing): `kenshi_x64.exe` 36,718,592 bytes; `forgotten construction set.exe` 1,035,776 bytes; `KenshiModTool.exe` 164,397,435 bytes; `KenshiLib.dll` 632,832 bytes; `RE_Kenshi.dll` 1,481,216 bytes; `OgreMain_x64.dll` 10,207,744 bytes.
- Toolchain evidence in install: `dependencies/` holds `dotnet4.0Client (needed for mod tools).exe`, `dx9/`, `vcredist_x64.exe`, `vcredist_x64_2012.exe`, `vcredist_x86.exe`. Game imports `MSVCP100.dll`/`MSVCR100.dll`/`mfc100u.dll` (Visual Studio 2010 runtime). Version resources (read-only): FCS `2.14.2` by LoFi Games (`forgotten construction set.exe`); KMM `2.7` (`KenshiModTool.exe`, which also contains Steam Client API version strings `05.25.65.21`); the native game/plugin binaries carry no version resource.
- Already installed at inspection: RE_Kenshi is active (`Plugins_x64.cfg` contains `Plugin=RE_Kenshi`; `RE_Kenshi.ini`, `RE_Kenshi/` folder, and `RE_Kenshi_log.txt` report `RE_Kenshi 0.3.1` + `KenshiLib 0.2.0`). Local `mods/` holds only `readme.txt`; the user runs Workshop mods. `KenshiModTool.exe` is the community Kenshi Mod Manager (KMM) by millerscout (strings: `Kenshi Mod Manager by millerscout`, `KMM-Tooling by millerscout`; `config.json` has `MasterlistVersion 1.2`, `MasterlistSource millerscout/kmm-masterlist`).
- OS/context: Windows, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, 2560x1440 windowed (from `kenshi.cfg` / `kenshi_info.log`). No anti-cheat found; single-player only, so no online/client protections apply.

## Route and why

Recommended stack, cheapest-first:

1. **Data route (FCS `.mod` files) for gameplay/data.** Official Forgotten Construction Set builds `.mod` patch files that override `gamedata.base` records. Use for items, weapons, armor, characters, races, factions, dialogue, towns, game starts, research, AI packages/tasks, and similar DB content (ranges per FCS schema + docs; dialogue records verified in the raw `.mod` files, the rest not exercised here).
2. **Asset-override route (`mods/<name>/` mirroring `data/`) for art/UI/audio-data.** Per `mods/readme.txt`: replicate the `data/` relative path inside your mod folder (e.g. `buildings/materials/construction.dds`). Covers DDS textures, OGRE `.mesh`/`.skeleton`, MyGUI layouts/skins under `data/gui`, materials/compositors, ParticleUniverse scripts, zone/level data. Wwise `.bnk` overrides are loaded through RE_Kenshi (`Queued soundbank` / `Mod bank load` in its log).
3. **OGRE-plugin native route (RE_Kenshi + KenshiLib) for code.** RE_Kenshi loads as an OGRE plugin (`Plugin=RE_Kenshi` in `Plugins_x64.cfg`) and hosts KenshiLib preload/post-load plugins. This is the community-standard equivalent of a loader API for Kenshi. Use it for runtime behavior, heightmap/fast-path hooks, shader/physx caches, custom game speeds, and file-override plumbing.
4. **Not recommended:** Harmony/MonoMod via BepInEx against `kenshi_x64.exe` (the target process has no CLR — see Verification); a from-scratch proxy-DLL injector when the OGRE `Plugin=` mechanism already exists; direct terrain/heightmap authoring as a first step (per developer forum posts, even internal terrain edits are hoop-jumping).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

- **Process architecture:** `kenshi_x64.exe` is native x64 `PE32+` with zero .NET markers (`mscoree`, `_CorExeMain`, `mscorlib`, `v4.0.30319` all absent; no Mono/Harmony/BepInEx strings). Raw import enumeration finds `OgreMain_x64.dll`, `MyGUIEngine_x64.dll`, `OIS64.dll`, `PhysXLoader64.dll`, `Plugin_ParticleUniverse_x64.dll`, `Plugin_Terrain_x64.dll`, `SkyX_x64.dll`, `steam_api64.dll`, plus Win32 (`KERNEL32`, `USER32`, `GDI32`, `SHELL32`, `WS2_32`, `ole32`) and `XAudio2_7`. String counts: ~4850 `Ogre` hits, ~1009 `MyGUI` hits, 26 `PhysX` hits in the game exe.
- **Rendering/UI/input/physics/audio:** `kenshi.log` shows OGRE plugin loads (`RenderSystem_Direct3D11_x64`, `Plugin_ParticleUniverse_x64`, `Plugin_Terrain_x64`, then `RE_Kenshi`) followed by `*-*-* OGRE Initialising` / `*-*-* Version 2.0.0unstable (Tindalos)` — a custom OGRE 2.0 dev-branch fork. `kenshi.cfg` pins `Render System=Direct3D11 Rendering Subsystem`. `MyGUI.log` reports `MyGUI version 3.2.3` with build paths under `C:\kenshi\kenshi-dependencies\mygui\`. Input is OIS (`OIS64.dll`); physics is PhysX plus `NxCharacter.dll`, `PhysXCooking64/PhysXCore64/PhysXDevice64/PhysXLoader64`, `physxcudart_20.dll`, `cudart64_30_9.dll`; sky is SkyX; images decode via FreeImage 3.13.1. Audio banks under `data/audio/*.bnk` carry Wwise `BKHD`/`DIDX`/`DATA` magic (verified header bytes), consistent with RE_Kenshi soundbank-override behavior.
- **Tools vs game:** `forgotten construction set.exe` is x86 `PE32` .NET (CLR markers present) — the official data editor. `KenshiModTool.exe` is the KMM mod manager (.NET self-contained bundle: `KenshiModTool.dll` / `KenshiModTool.Model` strings, 164 MB, no CLR header; runs on this machine's installed runtimes). Neither runs in the game process; scanning them as "the engine" misclassifies the game.
- **Data model:** `data/` core is `gamedata.base` (4,653,867 bytes), `Newwworld.mod` (2,016,808), `Dialogue.mod` (11,891,341), `rebirth.mod` (4,029,941). Partial header reading (first 256 bytes of each): two leading `u32` LE values, then one or more length-prefixed (`u32` LE) dependency strings naming the parent files — `Newwworld.mod` declares `gamedata.base` (`0x0D` = 13 chars), `Dialogue.mod` declares `gamedata.base,Newwworld.mod` (`0x1B` = 27) then `rebirth.mod` (`0x0B` = 11), `gamedata.base` declares `Newwworld.mod`. So the chain is `gamedata.base` <- `Newwworld.mod` <- `Dialogue` <- `rebirth`. Past the header come typed records (dialogue lines, foliage instances, signs); the full record layout was not reversed. Token census over the raw files: `Dialogue.mod` holds 17,105 `DIALOGUE_LINE` + 15,786 `DIALOG_ACTION` records; `gamedata.base` holds 1,244 `DIALOGUE_LINE` + 1,287 `DIALOG_ACTION`. Lines carry `conditions` fields referencing other records by `<numeric-id>-<source-file>` string IDs (e.g. `14168-Dialogue (4).mod`, `1292-gamedata.base`) plus chance/repetition fields — this is the override mechanism FCS edits and load order resolves. `data/mods.cfg` + `data/__mods.list` + launcher order define the override chain; KMM `masterlist.json` groups mods into ordered categories (UI/graphics first, then animations, races, etc.). Workshop items are typically `<workshop-id>/<ModName>.mod` + `_<ModName>.img` + `_<ModName>.info` (all 868 carry `.mod`+`.info`; 844 carry `.img`).
- **RE_Kenshi/KenshiLib model:** OGRE `Plugin=` loading (no injector needed) — the operative lines of `Plugins_x64.cfg` on this install are `PluginFolder=.\` followed by `Plugin=RenderSystem_Direct3D11_x64`, `Plugin=Plugin_ParticleUniverse_x64`, `Plugin=Plugin_Terrain_x64`, `Plugin=RE_Kenshi`. That RE_Kenshi-last order follows RE_Kenshi's old manual-install instructions; don't copy it. Its README (rewritten 2026-07-12) says to use the release installer, or, for a manual install on 1.0.65, to copy `RE_Kenshi.dll`, `KenshiLib.dll`, `CompressToolsLib.dll` and the whole `RE_Kenshi/` folder into the game root and add `Plugin=RE_Kenshi` as the **first** plugin, before `Plugin=RenderSystem_Direct3D11_x64`. RVA signature files per game build (`RE_Kenshi/RVAs/Steam_1.0.65.br`, `GOG_1.0.65.br`); `RE_Kenshi.ini` toggles (`HeightmapMode`, `AttackSlots*`, `MaxFactionSize*`, `MaxSquadSize*`, `MaxSquads*`, `FixRNG`, `FixModListScroll`, `CacheShaders`, `CachePhysXColliders`, `SkipUnusedMipReads`, `SkipSplashScreens`, `GameSpeeds`, etc.); preload vs post-load plugins (both phases appear in `RE_Kenshi_log.txt`); file-override and soundbank-override plumbing; shader cache (`RE_Kenshi/shader_cache.sc`, 2,113,400 bytes). KenshiLib exposes a version-independent API plus its own hooking layer; per its README it is built with the VS2010 (v100) x64 toolset, Boost 1.60.0, and the multihook MinHook branch, and plugins linking it fall under GPLv3. Relatives (per their project docs, not tested here): KenshiPy (embedded Python 3.4 via SWIG bindings over RE_Kenshi; Ogre/MyGUI/Boost parts unwrapped; hook-callback model) and KenshiCoop (experimental co-op as a KenshiLib plugin; AGPL/GPL interplay; ENet transport).
- **FCS schema:** `fcs.def` / `fcs_enums.def` / `fcs_layout.def` / `fcs_theme.def` define editable types (e.g. `AI_PACKAGE`, `AI_TASK`, `DIALOGUE` events). Official doc `Using the FCS.pdf` (1,956,867 bytes) plus the in-install `readme.txt` describe the new-mod/active-mod/dependency workflow and the asset-mirror rule.
- **Asset formats (header-verified):** stock textures are standard DDS (`data/buildings/ATLAS1.dds`: 4096x4096, DXT5, 16 MB) — the swappable unit. OGRE meshes carry serializer tag `[MeshSerializer_v1.100]` (verified in `data/meshes/arrow.mesh`). That is the default v1-mesh format OGRE 2.0 itself writes (`MESH_VERSION_1_10` in ogre-next `v2-0` `OgreMeshSerializer.cpp`), so the stock files match the game's own fork; converters from OGRE 1.9 or older only go up to v1.8 (consistent with community reports that other converter versions fail on Kenshi files).
- **Moddability map:** locally verified plus schema/docs-backed (items below marked): FCS reaches DB gameplay — items/weapons/armor, bodies/characters, factions, dialogue packages and conditions (verified in `.mod` token census), towns/spawns, AI packages/tasks (type names seen in `fcs.def`); game starts and research (per FCS docs/wiki, not exercised here). Asset mirrors reach textures/meshes/materials/particles/MyGUI/audio-data/zone files (override mechanism per `mods/readme.txt`; MyGUI layouts and mesh/DDS overrides observed in Workshop content). RE_Kenshi reaches the `RE_Kenshi.ini` runtime flags observed on disk, heightmap/fast paths, shader/physx caches, soundbank loading (all with log lines in `RE_Kenshi_log.txt`), and custom plugin logic (6 live Workshop plugins). Terrain authoring, engine multithreading/render-pipeline upgrades, hard-coded mechanics, and TES-style script extension are not reliably available (community + developer-forum statements + engine shape agree here; none tested firsthand).

## Build steps

Read-only recon path (nothing written to the game):

1. `um scan kenshi` and `--json`. Output with #150's original `um/scan.py` patch: `Unknown native engine [65%]` evidence `kenshi_x64.exe, ogremain_x64.dll`, loaders `RE_Kenshi (Kenshi OGRE plugin), Kenshi Mod Manager`, routes[0] the Kenshi known-game route. Baseline with `um` before #150: `.NET application [70%]` evidence `forgotten construction set.exe`, loaders `none installed`.
2. Inventory the install read-only: list root DLLs/EXEs/CFGs; read `currentVersion.txt`, `kenshi.cfg`, `settings.cfg`, `Plugins_x64.cfg`, `resources.cfg`, `config.json`, `masterlist.json`, `RE_Kenshi.ini`, `mods/readme.txt`, `Using the FCS.pdf` presence.
3. PE check each exe (MZ + `e_lfanew` + machine `0x14C` x86 / `0x8664` x64; `PE32` vs `PE32+`) and search first megabytes for `mscoree.dll`, `_CorExeMain`, `mscorlib`, `v4.0.30319`, `Mono`, `Harmony`, `BepInEx`.
4. Enumerate raw `*.dll` imports and `Ogre`/`MyGUI`/`PhysX` byte counts; confirm `kenshi_x64.exe` has OGRE/MyGUI/PhysX imports and no CLR markers while `forgotten construction set.exe` has CLR markers.
5. Read the oracles: `kenshi.log` (`Loading library`, `OGRE Initialising`, `Version 2.0.0unstable (Tindalos)`), `MyGUI.log` (`MyGUI version 3.2.3`), `kenshi_info.log` (`Version: 1.0.65`, `[Mods] Loaded core`, launcher mod list), `RE_Kenshi_log.txt` (`RE_Kenshi 0.3.1`, `KenshiLib 0.2.0`, `RVAs loaded`, `Loading preload plugins`, `Load mod hook`).
6. Map data flow: `data/gamedata.base` + `Newwworld.mod` + `Dialogue.mod` + `rebirth.mod` headers (dependency strings), `data/mods.cfg`, `data/__mods.list`, workshop `<id>/*.mod|*.img|*.info`, `data/audio/*.bnk` `BKHD` magic, `data/gui/*`.

To start a real mod after this recon (not done here): create a new mod in FCS (never edit `gamedata.base` directly), keep it after its dependencies in load order, mirror any asset under `mods/<YourMod>/` with the same relative path as `data/`, set the order in the launcher (KMM is an optional community tool for that), and only add RE_Kenshi plugin work (VS2010 v100 x64, KenshiLib includes + Boost 1.60.0, KenshiLib hooking layer, GPLv3) when FCS + assets cannot reach the idea. Per KenshiLib_Examples/HelloWorld, a plugin is a DLL that exports `startPlugin()`, sits in `mods/<Name>/` next to a `<Name>.mod`, is listed in that folder's `RE_Kenshi.json` as `{"Plugins": ["<Name>.dll"]}`, and is enabled in the game's Mods tab.

## Verification

- Reproduced `um scan kenshi` and `--json` with `um` before #150: engine `.NET application [70%]` evidence `forgotten construction set.exe`; exes `forgotten construction set.exe [x86, .NET]`, `kenshimodtool.exe [x64]`, `kenshi_x64.exe [x64]`; loaders `none installed`; workshop/saves paths correct. The JSON itself proves the flaw: `kenshi_x64.exe` is `managed: false` yet the game-level engine key is still `dotnet`.
- PE/marker matrix (read-only Python over the real files): `kenshi_x64.exe` native x64, no CLR markers; `forgotten construction set.exe` x86 with all four CLR markers; `KenshiModTool.exe` x64 with `mscorlib`/`v4.0.30319` strings and KMM identity strings (self-contained .NET bundle: no CLR header, hence scan reports it unmanaged); `KenshiLib.dll` and `RE_Kenshi.dll` native (MSVCP100/MSVCR100, no CLR). RE_Kenshi imports `OgreMain_x64`/`MyGUIEngine_x64`/`Plugin_Terrain_x64`.
- Log oracles looked at (not executed): OGRE version line, D3D11/ParticleUniverse/Terrain plugin sequence, MyGUI 3.2.3, Wwise `BKHD` bank headers, mod-load lines (`Loaded core gamedata.base`, `Loaded core mod: Newwworld/Dialogue/rebirth`, then Workshop mods), RE_Kenshi version/RVA/plugin/override lines.
- Follow-up probes (this session, still read-only, no launches): `.mod` token census and `conditions` context windows above; DDS header parse (`ATLAS1.dds` 4096x4096 DXT5) and `.mesh` serializer tag (`[MeshSerializer_v1.100]`); toolchain audit — this machine had **no C++ compiler** (`cl`/`msbuild` absent, no VS VC-tools install, no VS2010, no Boost, no MinHook; only CMake, git, and .NET 8/9/10 SDKs), so no KenshiLib plugin build was attempted.
- Scan-fix verification: with #150's original `um/scan.py` patch (tool-exe demotion + OGRE signal + RE_Kenshi/KMM loader entries + Kenshi known-game route), `um scan kenshi` reported `Unknown native engine [65%]` evidence `kenshi_x64.exe, ogremain_x64.dll`, loaders `RE_Kenshi (Kenshi OGRE plugin), Kenshi Mod Manager`, and routes[0] the Kenshi known-game route with `native.md`. Full UM suite: **78 passed, 2 skipped** (skips are pre-existing platform gates), including 3 new Kenshi regression tests. The review fixes made on merge (.NET apphost guard, no tool-like native exe as the game binary, `masterlist.json` dropped from KMM detection) pass the suite with fixtures shaped like this install, but were not re-run against the real install.
- NOT verified: launching the game, building/loading a new FCS mod, compiling or loading a new KenshiLib plugin, audio-bank override round-trip, mesh export/import round-trip, or any performance claim. Web findings (RE_Kenshi/KenshiLib READMEs, FCS wiki, OGRE-upgrade history) are reported as community sources, not local test results.

## Gotchas

1. **`um` before #150 said .NET because of the editor.** Symptom: engine `.NET application [70%]` with `dotnet-xna.md` playbook and Harmony/BepInEx route. Cause: the classifier scores `forgotten construction set.exe` (x86 .NET tool) as engine evidence and ignores that the shipped game exe is native. Note this is purely a weighting bug: the Forgotten Construction Set is Kenshi's official mod-creation tool (FCS 2.14.2 by LoFi Games, ships with the game) and remains the required route for all data mods — the fix only stops scan from mistaking this tool binary for the game engine. Fix (#150, `um/scan.py`): when every managed exe looks like a tool and a bigger non-tool native exe exists that isn't a .NET apphost (no sibling `<stem>.runtimeconfig.json` / `<stem>.deps.json`), report that native exe as the engine evidence instead of emitting `dotnet`, and route Kenshi to `native.md` + FCS docs.
2. **`um` before #150 reported no loaders while RE_Kenshi was installed.** Symptom: `loaders: none installed` despite `RE_Kenshi.dll` + `Plugin=RE_Kenshi` + `RE_Kenshi/` + `RE_Kenshi_log.txt`. Cause: loader detection knew no Kenshi markers. Fix (#150): `RE_Kenshi (Kenshi OGRE plugin)` detected from `re_kenshi.dll`/`kenshilib.dll` filenames, `Kenshi Mod Manager` from `kenshimodtool.exe`, plus a secondary native-engine signal from `OgreMain` DLLs.
3. **Harmony/BepInEx do not apply to the game process.** Symptom: following route 1 leads nowhere for `kenshi_x64.exe`. Cause: no CLR/Mono in that process (zero markers). Fix: use FCS/data + asset mirrors first, RE_Kenshi/KenshiLib for code.
4. **KMM vs FCS naming confusion.** Symptom: `kenshimodtool.exe` looks official. Cause: it is the community Kenshi Mod Manager (KMM), not Lo-Fi's tool. Fix: check strings (`Kenshi Mod Manager by millerscout`) and `config.json` before documenting it as stock.
5. **Workshop edits need a patch mod, not in-place edits.** Symptom (per community modding guides; not executed here): edited Workshop files get overwritten or gain phantom dependencies. Cause as documented: Steam owns `<workshop-id>/` folders; FCS records the active mod plus every checked dependency. Fix: copy the Workshop item into `mods/` renamed to its `.mod` basename for inspection, then make a new mod that loads after it and contains only the override.
6. **Load order is the mod.** Symptom: same mods, different behavior. Cause: `mods.cfg`/`__mods.list`/launcher order plus KMM masterlist categories decide which record wins. Fix: pin and document the full order (868 Workshop items here make this non-optional); use KMM categories.
7. **Native plugins are toolchain-pinned and license-viral.** Symptom (expected if attempted with the wrong toolchain, per project docs — no build attempted here): a modern MSVC build links but crashes or will not load. Cause: KenshiLib/RE_Kenshi require VS2010 (v100) x64, Boost 1.60.0, OgreMain lib pairing, KenshiLib's own hooking layer (no third-party detour libs side-by-side), and GPLv3 applies to linked plugins. Fix: use the KenshiLib example deps repo, release-mode builds, preload-plugin discipline, and no MyGUI calls off the UI thread.
8. **Version lock for native work.** Symptom (by design, not observed breaking here): hooks break after a game patch. Cause: addresses move; support is per-build via RVA files (`Steam_1.0.65.br` / `GOG_1.0.65.br` observed on disk). Every RE_Kenshi release since v0.3.1 lists Kenshi 1.0.65 + 1.0.68 on both Steam and GOG; RE_Kenshi is based on 1.0.65, and for 1.0.68 its installer creates a compatible exe in `RE_Kenshi/`. This install had RE_Kenshi 0.3.1 + KenshiLib 0.2.0; current upstream (October 2026) is RE_Kenshi v0.3.5 / KenshiLib v0.5.1. Fix: develop against a supported build, document which one (and the RE_Kenshi/KenshiLib versions), ship per-build RVA support, fail loudly when signatures miss.
9. **Mesh pipeline is version-sensitive.** Symptom: exported bodies have shading/seam errors or will not import. Cause (community-reported): wrong `OgreXMLConverter`/OgreMax/Blender-plugin pairing for Kenshi's `.mesh`/`.skeleton` serializer, plus dual-UV/normal handling differences between Blender and 3ds Max. Fix: treat the converter + exporter versions used as part of the build spec, round-trip one stock asset and view it before batch work, and expect iteration.
10. **Terrain is not a normal mod target.** Symptom: towns/objects are editable but land/heightmap work stalls. Cause: the engine's terrain path is bespoke and even internal edits are described as hoop-jumping; RE_Kenshi only exposes limited heightmap/fast-path modes. Fix: plan world mods around towns/spawns/instances and heightmap overrides where available, not a new terrain system.

## Assets

No new art or audio was produced for this recon (read-only investigation, no mod built). For future work: study stock sizes/palettes/camera handling first; generate with `um fal` (recorded in `fal_manifest.jsonl`); convert with `um sprite` / `um render3d`; override via `mods/<ModName>/` data-mirrors; Wwise bank overrides via the RE_Kenshi-tested soundbank path; MyGUI skin/layout overrides under `data/gui`.

## Cost and time

Single local session: read-only inspection plus community-doc cross-check, then the `um/scan.py` fix with tests. No game launches, no game-file writes, no external submissions.

## Open questions

- Re-run `um scan kenshi` on a real install with the merged `um/scan.py` (#150 with its review fixes, on top of #154's nested-exe fingerprinting) and confirm it still reports the native engine with `kenshi_x64.exe` as evidence and both loaders.
- Native plugin work on this machine needs the VS2010 v100 x64 toolchain, Boost 1.60.0 and the KenshiLib example deps, none of which was installed; until then, FCS + asset mods are the only buildable route here.

# Left 4 Dead's common infected (19 looks) and Tank as animated Minecraft mobs

> A Fabric mod that adds Left 4 Dead's common infected (13 male looks, 4 common female looks, a nurse and a
> rural woman) and the Tank to Minecraft Java 1.21.1, with the games' own meshes, textures, animation clips and
> sounds converted from the player's install into a private resource pack. All of it runs in the real game:
> the infected sprint at you, claw in a continuous rhythm, scream while chasing and fall over when killed, and
> the Tank charges, punches with a shove and lobs concrete.

## Setup
- Left 4 Dead 1 from Steam (about 6 GB). Minecraft Java 1.21.1 with the Fabric toolchain above, on Windows 11.
- The converters are plain Python reading the game folder; they write a resource pack (meshes as JSON, one PNG
  atlas per mesh, sounds as ogg). The mod itself contains no Valve data and renders a placeholder box if the
  pack is missing. **Never publish the generated pack.**
- Format details of the Source model, texture and animation reading are in the technique note
  "Reading Source engine (MDL v49) models, textures and animations in plain Python, no SDK".

## Route and why
A **content port**: reimplement the behaviour in Minecraft's own mob and projectile code and use the game's
art. Minecraft's mob and renderer API is open, so any behaviour is possible; the original Left 4 Dead 1 has no
code SDK, so the reverse (Minecraft into Left 4 Dead) means a re-skin and a map, or SourceMod plugins for new
mechanics on a server you run.
A passthrough design (running Left 4 Dead beside Minecraft) was rejected because the original game's AI and
rules were not needed, only its look and feel, and it would have meant touching a multiplayer-capable game.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Character data.** The common infected model has 40 bones; the female models share a 40-bone skeleton and one
  animation file; the Tank has 56. Each is split into body parts with several interchangeable models (the male
  has 5 heads, 8 upper bodies, 3 lower bodies) and 32 skin families.
- **Clips used.** Idle, a 3 by 3 blend run grid (use the cell straight ahead), a walk grid, a melee swing that is
  a layer overlaid on the run, a death clip, and for the Tank a rock-throw clip. Clip names differ slightly
  between the male and female sets (the female idle has a different name).
- **Sizes.** The mesh is baked at one block per 33 units for the infected (about 2 blocks tall) and about 25 units
  per block for the Tank (about 3 blocks tall), chosen by feel with the player.
- **Sounds.** The infected's voice lines are loose wav files in `sound/npc/infected/...` (idle moans, alert and
  "enraged" lines, rage screams at the victim, claw swish, scrape and punch hits, pain, death). The Tank's are in
  `sound/player/tank/...` (yell, growl, breathe, attack, pain, die, plus a rock rip, a thud and a rock hit).

## Build steps
1. Install the game and Minecraft; set up a Fabric 1.21.1 mod project.
2. Write the Source reader (see the technique note) and a pack builder that converts: each model with its
   chosen clips baked as per-frame vertex positions, and each sound group as ogg.
3. In the mod, add a `Monster` for each creature with goals for chase, attack and (Tank) rock throw; a
   renderer that draws the baked mesh and picks a clip from the entity's state; and, for the Tank's rock, a
   small projectile entity.
4. Build the pack, build the mod, launch the dev client, spawn with `/summon`.

Design choices worth copying:
- **Variants without the file size.** Skin variants of the same geometry write only new UVs and a new atlas
  (about 0.3 MB) and borrow the baked animations of a base mesh. A different model needs its own full bake
  (7 to 10 MB).
- **Chase, swing and animation.** Keep the chase goal running every tick whenever there is a target, so the mob
  never has to be restarted when the player moves. Make the claw a loop that chains swings on an exact rhythm
  with no gap, and stretch the baked clip over exactly one swing so the strike lands on the server's hit tick.
- **Stand-in for ragdoll.** The games hand dead characters to physics. With none available, play the stagger clip
  and tip the whole body over about its feet, backward or forward by entity id.
- **Tank numbers that felt right after tuning:** 400 HP, immune to knockback, punch 6 with a 1.5 block shove and
  hop, reach 4.2 blocks, rock 8 damage with a shove, a 7 to 26 block throw window and a random 4 to 8 second
  cooldown, about 3 blocks tall. The first version (2.2 blocks, 600 HP) was judged too small and too tanky.
- **The infected:** 50 HP, speed 0.27, claw 2 damage every 1.5 seconds, a scream every 2.5 to 4.5 seconds while it
  chases.

## Verification
- In the game, with screenshots: standing, sprinting, claw wind-up and strike, falling over; the Tank's charge,
  punch and rock. To make animation checkable without a human, freeze the game with `/tick freeze` and advance
  with `/tick step N`, screenshotting between steps.
- A log line printed whenever the renderer switched clips and whenever a swing started, run for ten seconds,
  gave the exact timeline that exposed the half-speed bug below.
- Not verified: sound levels (an agent cannot hear), long-run performance with large crowds, and the hitbox
  against every pose.

## Gotchas
1. **A mob's swing looks like it stutters and idles between hits.** Cause: Minecraft ticks a goal every other
   game tick unless `requiresUpdateEveryTick()` returns true, so a counter in a goal runs at half speed; the
   swing took twice as long as the animation. Fix: override it to return true for any goal that counts ticks.
2. **The player's hits are mostly ignored by a mob in melee with them.** Cause: vanilla's hurt-invulnerability
   after each hit. Fix: clear it before applying gun-style damage, and sum pellets per target.
3. **A walking mob flicks between walk and run poses.** Cause: one threshold on the movement value while the
   value hovers near it. Fix: hysteresis (on above 0.5, off below 0.3).
4. **The mob attacks with its back turned.** Cause: models are drawn along the body direction, which lags the
   head. Fix: snap the whole body to face the target while attacking.
5. **The "attack" animation is just running.** Cause: the clip is an empty stub; the swing is in the layer
   clip (see the technique note). Fix: bake the layer over the run.
6. **Missing hands.** Cause: alpha was a tint mask (see the technique note).
7. **The player dies in tests and the next commands do nothing.** Cause: the death screen swallows the typed
   commands. Fix: respawn first, give resistance during tests, and keep inventory on.
8. **The dead mob vanishes in a second with no fall.** Cause: Minecraft removes a dead mob after 20 ticks and a
   custom renderer gets no death tilt. Fix: tilt the body in the renderer and compress the death clip into 20
   ticks.

## Assets
All converted from the player's own install at build time, never committed. Pack size about 70 MB for 19
infected looks, the Tank, the rock and about 120 sounds.

## Open questions
- The remaining common-infected bodies (police, military, pilot, surgeon, baggage handler, suit, worker,
  patient, TSA agent) and the other special infected (Hunter, Smoker, Boomer, Witch) are not done.
- Hit reactions, footsteps and hordes are not done.

# In-game ImGui trainer and save-queue item delivery for LET IT DIE Offline Edition (UE3)

> A `dinput8.dll` proxy that hooks D3D9 `EndScene` and draws an ImGui mod menu inside LET IT DIE Offline Edition, the
> paid single-player release that replaced the online game (custom Unreal Engine 3, "BrgEngine"). It has infinite
> durability, ammo and stamina (done by skipping specific UnrealScript functions in `ProcessInternal`), currency
> buttons (calling script through `ProcessEvent`), an icon item picker, and permanent item and fighter-stat
> delivery. Delivery works through a save-edit queue that a helper process applies after the game exits. All of it
> is verified in the real game (play-tested 2026-10-11), except that one delivered part, Demon Gun 1, never shows
> up in the locker (Gotcha 17).

## Setup
- Game: LET IT DIE **Offline Edition 5.0.1**, Windows 11 x64.
  - **What "offline" means here.** GungHo ended LET IT DIE's online service on 2026-09-01 and released the Offline
    Edition the same day: the base game plus the $19.99 "Offline Key" DLC (Steam and PS4). It has no servers and no
    microtransactions. Death Metals (the paid currency) are gone, and Kill Coins, earned in game, replaced them.
  - That is why a trainer and save edits are fine here: they only touch your own local save and process. Nothing
    in this note touches the Offline Key ownership check; keep it that way. Don't carry this over to a game that
    still sells currency or items, or still talks to a server.
  - `BrgGame\Config\BrgEngine.ini` has `AllowD3D11=False`, so the live renderer is **D3D9**. Hook `EndScene` (vtable 42)
    and `Reset` (16).
- Toolchain:
  - **Build:** MSVC Build Tools (x64, `/MT`), MinHook and Dear ImGui 1.91.5.
  - **Static analysis:** Ghidra 12.1.4 running headless on JDK 21, with the scripts in Java. Ghidra 12 made PyGhidra
    the default Python; Jython scripts still run with a `# @runtime Jython` header.
  - **Save tools:** Python 3.14.
- **Ghidra import crash:** importing `BrgGame-Steam.exe` crashes in the exception-directory parser. Import a copy with
  PE data directory #3 zeroed instead.
- **Script dump:** UnrealScript bytecode came from `BrgGame.u` via UELib, after decompressing the package yourself (see
  Gotchas). The dump is kept outside the mod repo and is never shared.

## Route and why
- **Native hook (proxy DLL + MinHook)**, because there is no community loader.
  - UE4SS and similar tools don't apply: this is UE3, x64, with a heavily customised engine.
  - Cheat Engine tables don't cover item spawning or a menu.
- **Data-only first.** Editing `masters.db` (SQLite) and the save was tried first. It does change prices and the stats of
  *newly created* items. It cannot stop durability or ammo from draining, and owned items keep their saved values.
- **Live item spawning** through the game's debug exec `BrgGameInfo.DebugPartEquip` only works as a temporary preview
  (see Gotchas). Permanent items therefore go through **save editing with the game closed**, automated by a queue.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Offline edition = bundled backend.**
  - The save `Savedata\<steamid>.sav` is a JSON copy of what used to be server data.
  - Master data is a local SQLite file `BrgGame\Content\masters.db`. The exe opens it by bare name.
  - There is also a native in-memory save database that mirrors parts of the JSON.
- **Save format:**
  - Header: `"BRG\0"`, `u32 version` (2), `u32 total_uncompressed`, `"ZLIB"`.
  - Then chunks of `[u32 usize][u32 csize][zlib]`, which concatenate into UTF-8 JSON.
  - Then a 4-byte zero terminator.
  - **No checksum or signature.** It round-trips byte-exact apart from float formatting (`0.0000` vs `0.0`), which the
    game accepts.
- **Save JSON landmarks:**
  - `soul.free_money` / `soul.spirit`: Kill Coins in the Buffalo Bank and SPLithium in the SPLithium Tank. Their caps
    come from `master_safe_level.limit` / `master_spirit_tank_level.limit` for the current `soul.safe_level` /
    `spirit_tank_level` (500,000 at level 1). What a fighter carries is in `soul.chr.chrs[...].money/spirit`.
  - `soul.bloodnium_point` (account Bloodnium, max 999,999) and `soul.tdm_point` (TDM points).
  - `part.pts["1"]`: owned parts. Each record is
    `{uid, eid(GUID), gettime, owner USER|COIN_LOCKER, created, modified, ptid, rest, spare, grade, dur, lvl}`.
  - `item.items`: materials and consumables, `{eid, gettime, itemid, owner}`.
  - **Coin Locker = `soul.cl`:** 30 slots `{slot, type, eid}`, with type 0 = part, 3 = item, -1 = empty.
    `gameflg.cl` is unrelated.
  - Fighters: stat levels in `bodyuser["1"][i]` (`lvl, hp, str, dex, vit, stm, luk`). Level = 1 + stat points spent.
    XP pool and HP in `soul.chr.chrs["1"][i]` (`gain_exp, start_exp, total_exp, rest_exp, hp, type, grade, limit_break`).
- **masters.db:**
  - `master_part`: per-part `dur`, `dur_hit/shoot/rage` (drain), `capacity/spare` (ammo), and `lvllmttp/lvllmt`
    (equip requirement).
  - `master_item`: `itemtype ITTP_MATERIAL` covers the 106 R&D materials.
  - `master_body_detail.param_lv_max` is the per-stat cap (5 for grade-1 BAL fighters).
    `master_bodylvl_status_value` maps stat level to HP and other values.
  - `master_text (sct, id, lang, txt)` holds names. Join using the `sct.id` split of the `name` column, not the id alone.
- **Engine internals (RVAs, ASLR on):**
  - `UObject::ProcessEvent` 0x10E770, `UObject::ProcessInternal` 0x10EC70, `UObject::CallFunction` 0x103610,
    `FString::operator=` 0x19850.
  - `GNames` 0x2949C98. Entries hold the name at +0x14 and flags at +0x08 (bit 0 = wide).
  - `GObjects` is found at runtime by scanning writable sections for a `TArray` whose entries' `Index` (+0x38) equals
    their position.
- **Object layouts (x64):**
  - UObject: Index +0x38, Outer +0x40, Name +0x48, Class +0x50.
  - UField::Next +0x60, UStruct::Children +0x80.
  - UFunction: PropertiesSize +0x88, FunctionFlags +0xD0, iNative +0xD4, Func +0xF0.
  - UProperty: PropertyFlags +0x70, Offset +0x94.
  - FFrame: Node +0x14, Object +0x1C, Code +0x24, Locals +0x2C.
- **Script dispatch:** `CallFunction` calls `ProcessInternal` **directly** for script functions. Swapping
  `UFunction::Func` therefore misses script-to-script calls. Hooking `ProcessInternal` and comparing `FFrame.Node` catches
  every script function body.
- **Drain functions** (all void and decrement-only):
  - Durability: `BrgCommonPawn_CustomChara.WeaponDurabilityDown`, `WeaponShotDurabilityDown` and `ArmorDurabilityDown`.
    They run on the per-character helper object, so the owner is its `mPawn` property.
  - Ammo: `BrgWeapon_*.BulletConsumption` (9 overrides). The owner is `BrgWeapon_Base.mOwnerPawn`.
  - Stamina: `BrgPawn_CustomCharaPlayer.StaminaConsumption`.
  - Repairs use the separate `PartDurabilityRecovery*` functions.
- **Currency:** `BrgUserData` natives through ProcessEvent: `Get/AddMoney` and `Get/AddSpirit(..., cindex=-1)`
  (carried by the current fighter), `Get/SetSafeMoney` + `GetSafeLimit` (Bank), `Get/SetSafeSpirit` +
  `GetSpiritTankLimit` (Tank), `Get/SetUserBloodnium` + `GetBloodniumLimit`, `Get/SetTdmPoint`. Read, clamp to the
  game's limit (never lowering a balance already above it), then set. Bloodnium needs one more step (see Gotchas).
  The live objects are `PlayerController.WorldInfo.Game` (the GameInfo) and its `.mUserData`.
- **Icons:**
  - Every item has its own package `CookedPCConsole\UI_Icon_<id>_SF.upk`, holding one inline Texture2D (108x132, mostly
    A8R8G8B8).
  - The game has **no icon fallback**: a part without its own package has no icon in game.
- **Packages:** the cooked `.upk` files are fully LZO-compressed. Bulk-data headers use **64-bit size/offset** (24-byte
  header), which stock UE Viewer (umodel) can't read.

## Build steps
1. Build `dinput8.dll` with the exports `DirectInput8Create`, `DllCanUnloadNow`, `DllGetClassObject`, `DllRegisterServer`
   and `DllUnregisterServer`, each forwarding to `System32\dinput8.dll`. Place it next to `BrgGame-Steam.exe`
   (`Binaries\Win64`).
2. Worker thread:
   - Make a throwaway D3D9 device to read the vtable, then MinHook `EndScene`/`Reset`.
   - MinHook `ProcessEvent` and `ProcessInternal`.
   - Hook `IDirectInputDevice8::GetDeviceState`/`GetDeviceData` (vtable 9/10, both the A and W interfaces), so the game
     gets blank mouse/keyboard input while the menu is open.
3. Queue game-thread work, and run it from inside `ProcessEvent` only when the event is `PlayerTick`.
   - Resolve targets in one pass by FName index.
   - Read property offsets from the UProperty objects themselves (`Offset` at +0x94).
4. **Cheats:** in the `ProcessInternal` hook, compare `FFrame.Node` against the resolved drain functions. If the owner is
   the local `BrgPawn_CustomCharaPlayer`, return without running the body.
5. **Permanent items and stats:**
   - The overlay appends lines to `lid_mod\save_queue.txt`.
   - At launch the DLL starts a detached `pythonw` helper that waits on the game PID. After exit it takes a lock file,
     backs up the save and applies the queue (new locker records shaped exactly like the game's own, or a stat max).
   - It writes atomically (tmp → decode-verify → fsync → `os.replace`) and leaves a result file for the next launch.
6. **Item icons:** extract the `UI_Icon_*` textures with a custom UELib-based exporter (LZO + 64-bit bulk data + DXT
   decode). Then build a 64 px atlas plus a TSV index, which the overlay loads with WIC into a managed-pool D3D9 texture.

## Verification
- **Oracles used:**
  - Screenshots of the live overlay.
  - The game's own `BrgGame\Logs\Launch.log`. Engine asserts are logged there, e.g. `body_lvl distribute failed! ...`.
  - Windows Application event log entries 1000/1001 (exception code 0x1 in KERNELBASE = engine `appError`).
  - Decoding the save before and after each change.
  - A file-based RPC in the DLL (command/result text files) to drive scans and calls from the agent.
- **Verified in game:**
  - The overlay and Insert toggle.
  - Currency adds through the `BrgUserData` natives.
  - The live `DebugPartEquip` preview.
  - Locker delivery of six gear parts through the queue (shown in the locker after relaunch).
  - Fighter stat max (level 1 → 25).
  - Recovery from a launch crash caused by a stale RPC command.
  - Play-tested 2026-10-11: the `ProcessInternal` cheats in their final form (durability, ammo, stamina), input
    blocking while the menu is open, and R&D material delivery to the Coin Locker.
- **Also tested on a scratch copy of the save:** the queue helper, including the lock file, stale-lock takeover,
  structured retry, one bad entry not blocking the rest, and material (`item`) delivery.

## Gotchas
1. **Edited `masters.db` but nothing changed in game.** **Cause:** owned items keep the values stored in the save; the DB
   only seeds newly created items. Drain also has a flat `MaintenanceValue` term on top of `dur_hit`, and an exe check
   (`[cheat]part dur/rest/spare over!`) clamps saved values to the DB maximum on load. **Fix:** skip the drain script
   functions live instead; DB edits only for prices and new items.
2. **Live "add XP" crashed the stat screen** (`body_lvl distribute failed! ... exp=14, nec_exp=138`, then an assert).
   **Cause:** `AddExp` raised the script-side value only; the native stat-distribute check uses the saved XP pool. The GM
   tool natives (`DebugGmTool*_NT`) are compiled-out stubs in this build. **Fix:** edit stat levels in the save
   (`bodyuser`) with the game closed; level = 1 + points spent, capped by `param_lv_max`.
3. **Spawned item vanished on hand switch or reload.** **Cause:** `DebugPartEquip` mints a debug entity id (empty or
   leading `-`), which the save code skips. Forcing a real GUID made it persist briefly, but the game then crashed going up
   the tower: an integrity pass looks the part up in the native save DB and null-derefs because it was never registered.
   **Fix:** treat live spawn as a preview only; deliver permanent items by save injection.
4. **Item injected with `owner: COIN_LOCKER` didn't appear.** **Cause:** the locker also needs a `soul.cl` slot entry
   (type 0 part / 3 item) pointing at the `eid`. **Fix:** fill the first `type -1` slot.
5. **Hooking `UFunction::Func` didn't catch script calls.** **Cause:** `CallFunction` calls `ProcessInternal` directly
   for non-native functions. **Fix:** hook `ProcessInternal` and match `FFrame.Node`.
6. **Durability hook never fired** (caught in code review). **Cause:** the drain functions run on the
   `BrgCommonPawn_CustomChara` helper object, not the pawn, so a class check on `this` never matched the player. **Fix:**
   follow the helper's `mPawn` property; for weapons, `mOwnerPawn`.
7. **Game wouldn't launch after an update.** **Cause:** a leftover RPC command file was executed before the module base
   was known. **Fix:** ignore any command already present at startup, and initialise the base lazily.
8. **UELib saw 0 exports.** **Cause:** the cooked packages are LZO-compressed as a whole. **Fix:** decompress first,
   using the chunk table in the summary (this build reports engine version 9953, cooker version 135).
9. **umodel fails on every Texture2D ("Serializing behind stopper").** **Cause:** bulk-data headers are 24 bytes (flags,
   count, i64 size, i64 offset). **Fix:** a custom exporter.
10. **Mouse invisible in the overlay.** **Cause:** the game hides the OS cursor, and `SetCursor` from the render thread
    doesn't apply. **Fix:** `io.MouseDrawCursor = true` plus `ImGuiConfigFlags_NoMouseCursorChange`.
11. **Mouse still turned the camera with the menu open.** **Cause:** the game reads input through DirectInput, not
    window messages. Counters in the hooks showed it uses **buffered** `GetDeviceData` only (about 100k calls, zero
    `GetDeviceState`, zero `SetCursorPos`). A first filter that kept "releases" by offset (`dwOfs >= DIMOFS_BUTTON0`)
    let mouse motion through, because UE3 sets its own mouse data format whose axis offsets are not the standard
    `DIMOFS_*`. **Fix:** classify each device once with `GetDeviceInfo` (vtable 15; mouse/keyboard only, never
    joysticks, whose zeroed axes read as full deflection). While the menu is open, keep only buffered events whose
    value says "released": `dwData == 0` for the mouse, `(dwData & 0x80) == 0` for the keyboard. Nothing stays stuck
    down after the menu closes.
12. **Threading hazards** (code review). `EndScene` runs on UE3's render thread, not the window thread:
    - ImGui input must be queued from the WndProc. Capture Ctrl/Shift/Alt there, because `GetKeyState` is per-thread.
    - `SetWindowPos` for borderless must run on a separate worker thread; on the render thread it can deadlock against
      the game thread's `WM_SIZE` handler.
13. **Script-call parameter buffers.** `ProcessEvent` copies `ParmsSize` bytes in *and back out*, so use generous zeroed
    buffers. String parameters must be engine-allocated (`FString::operator=`), because script may reassign them
    (`DebugPartEquip` does) and would then free a caller-owned buffer.
14. **`DebugPartEquip` side effects.** It sets `GameInfo.mbDeadInfoOutputCancel` (a debug flag affecting death
    bookkeeping), adds to the Death Bag, and treats unknown slot names as Head ("All" wipes the inventory). **Fix:**
    whitelist the slot names and restore the flag's DWORD after the call.
15. **Adding Bloodnium, then levelling up, crashed** (`body_lvl distribute failed! ... bloodnium=0,
    nec_bloodnium=13`). **Cause:** the stat screen shows `GetUserBloodnium() + GetBloodnium()` from `BrgUserData`, but
    the native stat-distribute check (`FUN_141366480` → `FUN_14133f7c0`) takes its pool from the native save-store soul
    record (static object at `DAT_14f89ef80`, Bloodnium at +0xB4) plus the current chara record (+0x5C), and spends
    from those. `SetUserBloodnium` updates only the script-side copy, so the UI allowed an upgrade the native check
    rejected with an assert. Adding to the per-fighter pool through `AddBloodnium(cindex)` has the same problem.
    **Fix:** after the `BrgUserData` add, also write the new total into soul+0xB4. Verify first: the right exe build
    (PE timestamp), the field equal to what the game reports, and the neighbouring replica cap (+0xB8) being -1 or not
    below it. Undo the UI-side add if the native write fails. Same lesson as Gotcha 2: anything spent through a native
    check must be written to the native store.
16. **Death Metals.** The Offline Edition replaced them with Kill Coins, so `Get/SetMedal` still exists but does nothing
    useful; leave it out.
17. **Demon Gun 1 (`PT_ARM_WP017_0A1`) injected into the locker never showed** while GLIDER 2 (`PT_ARM_WP025_0K3`) did.
    Both have no icon package. Unresolved; see Open questions.

## Assets
None generated. Item icons are extracted at build time from the user's own install into a local atlas (64 px cells,
40 per row) and a TSV index. They are never committed or redistributed.

## Cost and time
One long session (about a day of wall-clock), including Ghidra/UELib tooling setup and two automated code-review passes
(30 findings, all addressed).

## Open questions
- Why some injected locker parts (`PT_ARM_WP017_0A1`) don't display. Candidates: no `UI_Icon_` package, or a native
  filter on `master_part.platform`.
- Where the native save-DB insert for parts lives. Finding it would make live spawning permanent.
- Whether `BeginGunBulletConsumptionDisable` (a native flag) is a cleaner infinite-ammo route.
- R&D blueprints (`ITTP_RMAP`, about 1,900 entries) are not in the picker yet.

# Limbo A8L8 texture format, standalone sprites, live-verified menu-title mod

> Limbo stores sprite art as A8L8 (16-bit luminance+alpha) textures. Two layouts:
> **standalone sprite files** (`data/sprites/**/*.png`, `.png_a`, `.pngblur`) carry
> their own **render dims and a full mip chain**, and **atlases**
> (`data/texture/atlas/*.pngatlas`) **are themselves 6-level mip chains** (base
> 4096-wide level 0, then five halvings; confirmed by decoding level 1 as a
> 4096/2=2048-wide image). Runtime semantics (user-verified in the live game):
> the **L (luma, low byte) channel drives visibility** on the darkness/blur pass
> (L=0 → invisible), the **A channel is read by the shipped pixel shaders** (it feeds
> the output alpha, see Channel semantics below) though a live whole-sheet A=255 atlas
> edit looked ≈ vanilla; the **UI/menu is drawn
> from the standalone sprite files, not the atlas**; the atlas blob IS consumed
> (whole-sheet edits visually wreck the world), and the atlas **manifest
> `data/texture/atlas/atlas_blur.txt` is most likely the live path→rect table**
> (`atlases.txt`, a named boot entry listing the two `.png` atlas resources, is read
> at runtime — bogus names render the menu near-white — but a live swap of two rows
> was inconclusive). A byte-exact repack
> route ( `repack_limbo.py --entry <path.d> --in <edited>` → swap
> `limbo_boot.pkg` → launch) was proven: zeroing the L plane of the menu title
> sprite removed the LIMBO title, and a bulk extract → human repaint → pack loop put
> edited art for a menu sprite and two atlas members into the live game.

## Setup
- Steam install of Limbo (appid 48000) at `...\Steam\steamapps\common\Limbo`.
- `limbo_boot.pkg` / `limbo_runtime.pkg` unpackable with a Python port of
  [Gibbed.Limbo](https://github.com/gibbed/Gibbed.Limbo). Filelists:
  `bin\projects\LIMBO\files\limbo_boot.filelist` / `limbo_runtime.filelist` (they name
  1,088 of 1,410 boot entries and 222 of 455 runtime entries; NOTE the installed boot
  pkg for build 18220724 actually holds **1,600 entries** of which 1,091 are named —
  the filelist's own `1,088/1,410` head count is authored for an older build; the pkg
  hash is CRC32 of the lowercase '/' path).
- Working dir was a pristine copy of the install with an SHA-256 manifest, plus a
  save backup before anything was launched modded. Everything reverted afterwards.

## Route and why
- Route: **data / asset-only** — decode, edit, re-encode, repack the .pkg, swap in.
  Launches via Steam only (`um win launch --steam 48000`); the game window is
  `limbo` (1024×576 when windowed). It writes no logs. Steam does NOT revert
  swapped pkgs; swap back manually from backups.
- Anti-cheat: none. The exe carries Steam's SteamStub DRM wrapper; this route leaves
  the exe alone and changes only data files, so no hook is needed.
- Live workflow: back up install → `Copy-Item` modded `limbo_boot.pkg` over the
  live one → launch → screenshots via `um win shot <out> --exe limbo` → drive with
  `um win drive --proc limbo "focus" "key 0x0D"` (Enter) → confirm with the human →
  restore boot+runtime+settings from backup and delete the game's `derived` folder.

## How the game works (verified facts)
- PKG: u32 count; then count × (u32 name_hash, u32 entry_off, u32 size); blobs at
  table-end + entry_off. `.d` entries are zlib-deflated; repack wrote them back
  deflated, untouched entries by verbatim slice (no-op rebuild is SHA-identical).
- Texture file wrapper (all sprite + atlas files). The prefix is four u32s, then the
  path (layout per theberrigan's `tools_Limbo.py`, `checkSprites`):
  ```
  u32 = 9 ; u32 = 2 ; u32 flags (1, 9 or 17) ; u32 (varies)   # 16-byte prefix
  u8  pathLen ; ascii path (lowercase, '/' separators)
  ```
  The third u32 is the **file-type/'atlas variant' flag, not a variant id byte**: 1 =
  plain sprite, 9 = `.png_a` / `.pngblur` (blur pass), 17 = `.pngatlas` (ATLAS), i.e.
  bit 0 always set, bit 3 (8) for blur and bit 4 (16) for atlases; theberrigan's script
  labels those bits "black only" and "b/w atlas". The exe holds the matching name
  tokens `'ATLAS'` and `'BLUR'`. The
  fourth u32 **is not a path CRC** — brute-forced CRC32 with multiple seeds/xors over
  `path`, `derived/pc/path`, `path.d`, lower/upper all mismatch. Across 135 files it
  is either 0, `0x12345678`, `0x00FF00FF`, or (33 files) a 4-byte slice of what looks
  like an authoring-era absolute path `c:/derived/pc/data/sprites/...` (e.g. `c:/d`,
  `/der`, `it00`), so it is stale debug/authoring cruft the loader never validates.
  Treat it as opaque; never parse it.
  Then the **internal texture header, 18 bytes**, at 17 + pathLen:
  ```
  u32 = 7 ; u16 ; u16 W ; u16 H ; u16 usedW ; u16 usedH ; u16 ; u16
  pixel start P = 17 + pathLen + 18 ; texels run to exact EOF
  ```
  `unk6` (the u16 after the 7) is **0 in 139 of 142 containers — every plain sprite
  (137) and both atlases**; it is nonzero in **exactly the 3 BLUR textures** and only
  there: `edges/wood.pngblur` = `0x3333`, `props/rope/tile_cable_01.pngblur_a` =
  `0x0C0C`, `text/menu/uk/c_id#04.pngblur_a` = `0xC8C8` (the exact set theberrigan's
  script asserts, `unk6 in [0, 3084, 13107, 51400]`). Each value has **high byte ==
  low byte** (`0x0C/0x33/0xC8`), i.e. a byte duplicated into a u16 — consistent with a
  normalized 0..1 factor (12/51/200 ÷ 255 ≈ 0.05/0.20/0.78). So it is a **per-texture
  parameter carried only by BLUR ("black only") textures**, most plausibly a blur
  strength/opacity authored alongside them. Whether the runtime reads it is unknown;
  nothing here depends on it. The first trailing u16 has low byte 2 and a **high byte
  that counts mip levels**: title `0x0C02` (W=2048 → 12), chapters/1 `0x0B02`
  (W=1024 → 11), metal_heavy 512-wide `0x0A02` (→ 10), atlases `0x0602` (6). For the
  sprites that's log2(W)+1, the length of a full chain down to 1×1, but **the files
  store fewer levels**: the stored chain stops when the short side reaches 1 (the
  title's and chapters/1's texel data end at 2×1, 11 and 10 levels, see the sums
  below). For the atlases it equals the 6 stored levels, so a reader has to treat the
  two kinds differently. The
  second trailing u16 is `0x0A01` for sprites / `0x0A11` for atlases — its low nibble
  repeats the file-type flag (1 vs 17).
  Example (menu title, pathLen 38): W=2048 H=1024 usedW=1280 usedH=720,
  tail u16s = [0x0C02, 0x0A01]. chapters/1.png (1024×512): tail [0x0B02, 0x0A01].
  atlas_blur: W=4096 H=4096 used=4064×3984 tail [0x0602, 0x0A11].
- **Texel = D3DFMT_A8L8**: LE u16, low byte = L (luma), high byte = A (alpha).
  Confirmed by exe string `only 8A8L format supported`. White on screen ⟺ high L.
- **Standalone sprites = mip chain, no packing**:
  pixel bytes = 2 × (W*H + (W/2)*(H/2) + … + 2*1). Title: 2048×1024 chain =
  2,796,202 texels = 5,592,404 bytes = file−(P) exactly. chapters/1: 1024×512
  chain = 699,050 texels = 1,398,100 bytes = exactly.
- **W/H ARE stored in the header** (at `se+6`/`se+8`, for sprites and atlases
  alike), so dimensions need no guessing; and the mip levels are **2×2 floor
  averages of the L and A bytes taken independently** (a PIL/BOXCAR resize gives
  ~46% mismatched mip bytes; the integer floor average gives 0). Re-encoding a
  decoded level 0 and regenerating the chain by that rule reproduces the shipped
  file byte-exact on **140/140 standalone sprites** — so editing level 0 and
  regenerating mips is a lossless no-op when nothing is changed.
- **Atlas blob = 6-level mip chain, CONFIRMED by decoding level 1**:
  - `atlas_blur.pngatlas`: header W=4096 H=4096 usedW=4064 usedH=3984; texel data =
    22,364,160 texels = 4096² + 2048² + 1024² + 512² + 256² + 128² exactly. Reading
    the bytes after the first 4096² as a 2048×2048 image yields a half-size copy of
    level 0 (corr 0.999999 vs a 2×2 box downsample) — this is a real mip chain, not
    a tall 4096×5460 sheet.
  - `atlas_norm.pngatlas`: own header **W/H = 4096 × 1024** (a 4×1 sheet, resolved —
    earlier the base was only guessed); usedW/usedH = 4064/720. Texel data = 5,591,040
    = 6-level chain of the 4096×1024 base (4096·1024 + 2048·512 + … + 128·32). Level
    1 (2048×512) is a half-size copy (corr 0.999998).
  - theberrigan's `parseSprite` also reads a 4096×4096 atlas as halving mip levels.
  - The member check below decodes level 0 at width 4096, which holds either way.
  - **Gotcha consequence:** editing level 0 alone leaves levels 1-5 holding old art
    (see Gotcha 5).
- **Channel semantics (live + shader)**: L drives a darkness/luminance pass.
  Whole-sheet edits prove the atlas is sampled (every texel 0xFFFF →
  "blocky-blobby, mostly black"); every-texel A=255 ≈ vanilla; every-texel L=255 →
  title screen pure black. **But A is not dead**: the shader sources shipped in the
  pkgs read the texel's alpha into the output alpha. `renderobject.fx` samples the
  texture's L and A together, scales them by the diffuse colour and writes the scaled
  A to the output alpha; in `fixedfunction.fx`, `FixedFunction3DColor[Specular]UVPS`
  multiply the vertex alpha by the texel alpha, `FixedFunction3DNUVPS` multiplies it
  by the texture factor's alpha, and `FixedFunctionOverDrawPS` passes it through;
  `watereffect.ps` uses the texel alpha as its alpha. So A is *used* by render paths
  (it feeds the alpha blend); the earlier "A effectively ignored" was an
  over-generalization from one whole-sheet A=255 test, whose pass simply didn't show
  it. Alpha is real; don't discard it when editing (see Gotcha 6).
- **UI/menu sprites are separate files, read at runtime**: zeroing L across all the
  menu title sprite's mips removed the LIMBO logo from the live main menu; the rest
  of the menu unchanged. The exe holds the strings `Loading atlas texture: '%s'`,
  `sprites/chapters/`, `sprites/text/`, `Atlases not found`/`Atlas not found [%s]`,
  `'ATLAS'`, `'BLUR'`, and `atlases.txt` — but no hardcoded `atlas_blur.txt` (the
  manifest path is derived from the `.png` name at runtime). `atlases.txt` (a named
  boot pkg entry) is just a 2-line list of `"data/texture/atlas/atlas_blur.png"` /
  `"data/texture/atlas/atlas_norm.png"` and IS read live: pointing it at bogus
  names rendered the menu near-white (mean 233 vs vanilla 45).
- **Boy / characters = atlas-only, CONFIRMED (no standalone sprite files)**. CRC32 of
  `derived/pc/data/sprites/characters/boy/...` variants for all 11 manifest boy
  members × 6 extensions (`.png` `.png.d` `.png_a` `.pngblur` …; 66 combos incl. the
  exact `head_cutoff.png.d`) matches **no entry in either the boot or the runtime pkg
  hash table**, and no pkg blob's internal wrapper path starts with
  `data/sprites/characters/boy/` in either pkg (the boot pkg has 84 blobs whose blob
  *content* mentions "boy", but all are cutscene scripts / ragdoll volumes). The boy
  exists only as **337 atlas manifest rects**; scenes/skeleton scripts reference those
  rects by path string.
- **The manifest is most likely the runtime rect source, but no live test has shown a
  row edit moving a sprite.** For it: `atlases.txt` is read live and names the two
  `.png` atlas resources, the exe has `Loading atlas texture: '%s'` but no hardcoded
  `atlas_blur.txt` (so the `.txt` path is derived from those names), and the rows
  match the atlas texels (42/42 members, see Verification). Against a clean answer:
  swapping the `myst` and `boy_default/head_cutoff` rows (texture untouched) produced
  only animation-noise pixel diffs in a clean single instance and no crash (see the
  retraction under Verification). Local pixel edits inside the boy's rects also
  showed nothing on screen — for zeroing his L that's a **black-on-black confound**
  (his texels are near-black); whites/A never visibly changed either path. A row swap
  between two visibly different members that are both on screen in a paused scene
  would settle it.
- Scenes / `skeleton.branch` reference sprites by path string plus per-instance
  floats (world size/basis), never by rect: e.g.
  `data/sprites/characters/boy/boy_default/head_cutoff.png` and
  `.../children/boy_skinny_01/l_thigh.png`.

## Build steps
The session's scripts are published at <https://github.com/hukultan/limbo-tools>
(MIT): `unpack_limbo.py`, `repack_limbo.py`, `limbo_tex.py` (inspect / extract /
pack / patch / round-trip), `limbo_workflow.py` (bulk extract/pack loop),
`make_titlezero.py`, `shot_diff.py`.
1. Unpack: `python tools/unpack_limbo.py pristine_pkg <filelist_dir> lab\boot`
   (boot and runtime). `.d` stored entries come out with the `.d` stripped.
2. Inspect: `uv run --quiet --with numpy python tools/limbo_tex.py inspect FILE`.
3. Hand-editing loop (decode → edit → encode → repack):
   ```
   # dump every sprite + atlas member to clean RGBA PNGs (L as gray, A as alpha)
   python tools/limbo_tex.py extract SPRITE.png --out edit.png            # dims from header
   python tools/limbo_tex.py extract ATLAS.pngatlas --rect 804,2345,215,206 --out head.png
   # ... human edits edit.png / head.png in any image editor ...
   python tools/limbo_tex.py pack  SPRITE.png  --out NEW --in edit.png     # rebuild + full mip chain
   python tools/limbo_tex.py patch ATLAS.pngatlas --out NEW --in head.png \
       --rect 804,2345,215,206 --mips                                       # edit rect in all 6 mips
   ```
   `pack`/`patch` keep the header verbatim and regenerate every mip level, so the
   file byte length is unchanged (safe for the `.d` deflate). A single old path:
   `tools/make_titlezero.py` zeroes the L byte of every texel in every mip of the
   menu title.
   For editing **many** assets at once, `limbo_workflow.py` wraps the same engine:
   `extract --boot lab\boot --out assets` dumps every standalone sprite and atlas
   member to RGBA PNGs (138 + 391) plus a `MANIFEST.json` of each PNG's source
   texture/rect and SHA-256; `pack --boot ... --assets ... --pkg-in ...
   --filelists ... --pkg-out ...` rebuilds **only** the PNGs that changed and
   repacks (untouched pkg entries copied verbatim).
4. Repack and swap:
   ```
   uv run python tools/repack_limbo.py pristine\Limbo\limbo_boot.pkg ^
       tools\Gibbed.Limbo\bin\projects\LIMBO\files ^
       lab\renders\limbo_boot_TAG.pkg ^
       --entry "derived/pc/data/sprites/text/menu/limbo title.png.d" --in NEWFILE
   Copy-Item lab\renders\limbo_boot_TAG.pkg "<install>\limbo_boot.pkg" -Force
   ```
   (Entry names are the boot-relative path + `.d`; a texture entry is deflated.)
5. Kill any running game by exact PID (`um win kill PID`), launch via Steam,
   screenshot (`um win shot out.png --exe limbo`), diff vs a vanilla capture with
   `tools/shot_diff.py` / numpy, verify with the human.
6. Restore: copy backed-up boot+runtime+settings.txt back and delete
   `<install>\derived`.

## Verification
- **Byte-exact round trip: 140/140 sprite files** parse → re-emit → identical SHA.
- **Extract→pack identity: 140/140 standalone sprites.** Decode level 0 to RGBA,
  re-encode, regenerate the mip chain by integer floor averaging → byte-identical
  to the shipped file. So the edit round trip is lossless when nothing changes.
- **Surgical repack (verified):** editing 2 PNGs (one sprite, one atlas member)
  through the extract/pack loop changed exactly those 2 pkg entries and left the
  other 1,593 byte-identical.
- **Live proof (multi-asset human-edit loop, user-confirmed in the live game):** the
  bulk `limbo_workflow.py` loop was driven end to end. `extract` produced 138
  standalone sprites + 391 atlas members as editable RGBA PNGs; a human repainted
  three of them — `derived/pc/data/sprites/text/menu/howtoplay_pc.png` (a full
  2048×1024 menu sprite), plus the `head.png` rects of `characters/sister` and
  `animation/boy/bones` inside `atlas_blur`. `pack` rebuilt exactly those textures
  (2 pkg entries changed — the sprite and the shared atlas — the other 1,593
  byte-identical) into a 20,743,398-byte `limbo_boot.pkg`, verified so the user's
  red channel became L (byte-exact) and every mip level's change stayed confined to
  the union of the edited rects. Swapped over the live Steam install (windowed,
  backed up first), the human confirmed **the edited art renders in-game**. This
  exercises the whole standalone-sprite path *and* the `patch --mips` atlas path on
  the real characters. Reverted to vanilla afterwards (SHA-verified).
- **42/42 atlas members** decode pixel-identical to their standalone file (Jaccard
  1.0) at sheet width 4096 (level 0).
- **Repack identity**: rebuild with zero replacements is byte-identical to input.
- **Live proof (standalone/UI)**: with the title L-plane zeroed, two menu screenshots
  agree (mean 14.4 vs vanilla 25.7) and the diff is confined to the title band
  (x184–828, y116–466, centroid 538,255, max diff 255); the human confirmed the title
  is gone in-game. Reverted to vanilla afterwards (SHA-verified).
- **Live proof (atlas/manifest IS read)**: `atlases.txt` (named boot entry
  `atlases.txt`, lists `data/texture/atlas/atlas_blur.png` + `atlas_norm.png`) pointed
  at bogus names → menu renders near-white (mean 233 vs vanilla 45; 84.8% pixels
  differ >50). Restored to vanilla afterwards.
- **Retracted (an earlier version of this note had it wrong)**: swapping the `myst`
  and `boy_default/head_cutoff` rows of `atlas_blur.txt` was first reported as moving
  the darkness pass (menu mean 58.97 vs 45.45). A clean, controlled single-instance
  re-run reached the menu fine with no crash (mean 26.92 vs ~26.6; pixel diffs were
  animation noise only). The 58.97 figure came from a botched comparison — a second
  Steam launch captured mid title-fade, not a real rendering change. A cutscene-skip
  (S) was used for correct states. Treat rect-swap claims as needing the same clean
  single-instance protocol. So a live row edit moving a sprite is still unshown.
- Negative (informative, re-interpreted): "zeroing the boy's manifest rects → nothing
  visible" was a black-on-black confound (his L is ~8), not evidence the manifest is
  unused. No A-only edit has visibly changed anything yet, though the shaders read A.
- Verified this pass: atlases are real 6-level mip chains (level-1 decodes as a
  half-size copy, corr 0.999); atlas_norm's own header is 4096×1024; the first tail
  u16's high byte counts mip levels (12/11/10 sprites, a full chain to 1×1; 6 atlases);
  the 4th prefix u32 is authoring cruft, not a CRC; manifest cols 5-6 are
  offset/pivot, not used dims (see Gotcha 4); the boy has **no** standalone sprites
  (CRC32 absent from both pkg tables, and no blob's internal path is under his
  folder); Steam build ID 18220724.
- Not verified: that editing a manifest row moves a sprite in game, and whether the
  runtime reads `unk6`.

## Gotchas
1. **Don't assert the file-start magic for the sprite header**: the wrapper starts
   with u32 9, which differs from the internal header u32 `7` at `se`. Read the
   internal header from `pathHeaderEnd` (= 16 + pathLen + 1), and read W/H at
   se+6/se+8, usedW/usedH at se+10/se+12, pixels at se+18. Pixel bytes count against
   the mip-chain sum, not `2*W*H`.
2. **Separate runs differ in menu animation timing** → whole-screen diff means
   little; use two captures of the same mod run (they agree when the change is
   real) and compare against a vanilla same-state capture. **Capture while the game
   is paused, not during the title/cutscene transition** — `um win shot --hwnd <id>`
   (or `--exe limbo`) captures the game window even when a Steam overlay/splash is
   up; do a fresh vanilla capture for every modified-state comparison, never reuse a prior run's.
3. **zlib `.d` entries**: replace by compressing again (repack tool does it); a
   hand-built replacement must stay byte-compatible (same length is the safe path).
4. **The atlas manifest is most likely the runtime rect source** — `atlas_blur.txt` /
   `atlas_norm.txt` rows (`x y w h offX offY "path"`, TAB-separated, CRLF; see How the
   game works for the evidence and the inconclusive swap). **Columns 5-6 =
   offset/pivot (X/Y) — resolved, matching theberrigan's `tools_Limbo.py` labels —
   NOT used W/H.** Proof: for the 11 atlas members that ALSO exist as standalone
   sprite files, manifest cols 3-4 (`w h`) equal each standalone's **usedW/usedH**
   exactly (all 11; e.g. metal_heavy manifest `512 9` = standalone
   usedW=512 usedH=9), so cols 3-4 already carry the used dims and cols 5-6 must be
   the pivot (e.g. metal_heavy `32 27`). Editing a row's rect should *move* a sprite,
   but that hasn't been shown live yet. To repaint a sprite, keep its rect and edit
   its pixels in the `.pngatlas` texel data: the level-0 byte offset is
   `P + 2*(y*4096 + x)`. The boy's texels are near-black, so zeroing his L shows
   nothing; test edits on him need a visible change in L, and see Gotcha 5.
5. **Stale atlas mips.** **Symptom:** a pixel edit to an atlas member doesn't show,
   or shows only at some sizes. **Cause:** the atlases are 6-level mip chains
   (verified by decoding level 1), so editing level 0 alone leaves levels 1-5 holding
   the old art, and a sprite drawn small or through the blur pass may sample those.
   **Fix:** `limbo_tex.py patch ... --rect x,y,w,h --mips` writes the downscaled edit
   into every level (verified confined to the scaled rect at all 6 levels of
   `atlas_blur`).
6. **Editing channel:** the tools decode L into `R=G=B` of the output PNG, so when
   packing, the **PNG's R channel becomes L (luminance)** and its **A becomes A**;
   G/B are ignored. LIMBO renders grayscale, so a coloured edit shows up as its
   **red channel as gray** — paint in grays (or knowingly accept red-as-gray)
   rather than expecting the literal RGB colour to survive.

## Assets
None generated with AI yet; only numpy/PIL test patterns and the L-zero title.

## Cost and time
Single session; free (local numpy/PIL, no API spend).

## Open questions
- Whether editing a manifest row moves a sprite in game. The one row swap tried was
  inconclusive; swap two visibly different members that are both on screen in a
  paused scene.
- `unk6` (`0x0C0C/0x3333/0xC8C8`, only in the 3 BLUR textures): a normalized blur or
  black-only parameter, or authored metadata the runtime never reads?
- Any *fog-particle-specific* alpha use: the shaders that read `texel.a` are the
  object/fixed-function/water ones; no particle shader was singled out.
