# Minecraft 26.2 NeoForge modpack audit: diagnostics mod, javac builds, zombie-process and config-loop root causes, measured perf mods

Audited a 100-mod NeoForge 26.2 pack, built an observe-only diagnostics mod (metrics, sampling profiler, event
monitor, inspectors, benchmark) and a small fix mod, both compiled with plain javac, and verified everything in
the real client via a scripted lab instance (autobench + in-game screenshots, no OS input). Then A/B-tested the
usual performance mods per mod and per scene; only two of four gave a measurable gain.

## Setup
- Ownership: Minecraft: Java Edition through Xbox Game Pass (Java & Bedrock Edition for PC) on the author's
  Microsoft account. The two offline clients in Gotcha 30 were lab test clients of that owned copy, started by
  scripts on the same machine.
- TLauncher instance (`versions/<name>` is the gameDir), NeoForge 26.2.0.88 universal + patched client jar in
  `libraries/net/neoforged/...`; game runtime = Mojang `java-runtime-epsilon` (Java 25).
- Build JDK: any JDK 25. No Gradle needed.

## Route and why
Minecraft 26.x ships **unobfuscated**, so mods compile directly against
`minecraft-client-patched-<ver>.jar` + `neoforge-<ver>-universal.jar` + the libraries listed in the version json.
No remapping, no refmap. A tiny Python script builds the classpath from the version json and a UTF-8 javac
`@argfile` (needed when paths contain non-ASCII characters).
Related: [Fabric mods for Minecraft 26.x](../../techniques/fabric-mod-for-26-x-without-mappings.md) (the Fabric side
of the same unobfuscated toolchain) and
[testing a mod inside a large modpack, headless](../../techniques/testing-a-fabric-mod-inside-a-large-modpack-headless.md).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- GUI in 26.2: screens draw in `extractRenderState(GuiGraphicsExtractor, mx, my, pt)`; open via
  `mc.gui.setScreen()` / read `mc.gui.screen()`; HUD hidden flag = `mc.gui.hud.isHidden()`.
  HUD elements from other mods can end up above a screen's content; call `g.nextStratum()` before drawing.
- Keys: `KeyMapping(name, IKeyConflictContext, InputConstants.Type, code, KeyMapping.Category)`; categories are
  records registered via `RegisterKeyMappingsEvent.registerCategory`.
- Event bus 8.0.5: a listener added with `receiveCanceled=false` (the default) skips events an earlier listener
  cancelled, so use `receiveCanceled=true` for timing hooks. The bus drops that check for event classes that don't
  implement `ICancellableEvent` (`ListenerList` unwraps the filter), so the ClassCastException we saw with
  `receiveCanceled=false` on a non-cancellable event has some other cause; not resolved.
- Timing all listeners of an event = HIGHEST listener stores start, LOWEST(receiveCanceled) listener stores end.
- NeoForge `TimeTracker` (entity/BE) is shared between client and server threads -> racy in singleplayer; use own
  mixins on `ServerLevel#tickNonPassenger` and the `BlockEntityTicker#tick` call in
  `LevelChunk$BoundTickingBlockEntity#tick`.
- Stack frames carry the JPMS module name (= mod id for most mods); mixin handlers carry `$modid$` in the method
  name (`handler$abc000$modid$name`) -> per-mod attribution for a sampling profiler.
- `FramerateLimitTracker`: with `inactivityFpsLimit:"afk"` FPS is capped at 30 after 60 s without input. Any
  unattended benchmark must disable it or record the throttle reason.
- Client exit: `Main` ends but the JVM stays alive if any mod left a non-daemon thread.

## Build steps
1. Classpath from version json (libraries with os rules for windows) + patched client + NeoForge universal.
2. `javac --release 25 -proc:none @args`, copy resources (`META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`, mixin json, lang),
   `jar --create` with `Automatic-Module-Name`.
3. Mixin config: `"required": false`, `"defaultRequire": 0`, `@Pseudo` + `remap=false` for targets in other mods.

## Verification
- Lab copy of the instance launched with the same JVM args as the launcher, `--quickPlaySingleplayer`, and
  system properties driving an in-mod autobench (warmup, 60 s run, snapshot, quit) and an in-mod UI self-test
  (opens each tab, saves `Screenshot.grab` PNGs). Results read from JSON reports + `latest.log`.
- Root causes proven by A/B: process exit time (never exits by itself 6/6 without fix, killed after 35-90 s;
  exits in 1-3 s 7/7 with fix); config rewrite loop reproduced by running two instances with a shared config
  dir, gone with the fix.
- Behaviour of a patched machine mod checked without trusting mod code: a setup command file fills one machine
  of each kind with raw food + fuel, and after the run a ~100-line Anvil/NBT reader dumps their saved `Items` from
  `dimensions/minecraft/overworld/region/*.mca` (26.x world layout); with/without the fix must be identical.

## Performance mods on 26.2 (measured in this pack, 60 s runs, 8 GB heap, laptop i5-10200H + RTX 3060)
Base noise between two identical runs: MSPT ~1.5%, FPS ~1% standing; FPS ~8% in the crowd scene.
- Lithium 0.25.3 (NeoForge): server MSPT 20.7 -> 15.0-15.5 ms (-25..28%), worst second -30%, same in the
  crowd scene. 98 `@Overwrite`s, no conflict with ~100 other mods; machine/block-entity behaviour identical
  in the saved-world A/B dump. Kept.
- EntityCulling 1.11.3: standing in a field -> no change; sealed stone box 20 blocks ahead with 169 chests +
  338 NoAI mobs -> FPS 36-39 -> 47-51 (+22..36%), frame p99 -20%. Logs a harmless "refmap could not be read"
  (26.x is unobfuscated). Its licence (tr7zw Protective License) allows it in CurseForge- and Modrinth-hosted packs
  and no other redistribution of the jar, so a pack you zip up yourself can't carry it. Kept.
- FerriteCore 9.0.0 (Modrinth lists it for 26.1-26.1.2): live heap after full GC 1766 -> 1725 MiB (-2.5%);
  most of its old savings seem to be in vanilla by now. FPS -3% in 2 of 3 runs (noise level). Both it and
  Lithium `@Overwrite` `PalettedContainer.acquire/release`; no error or conflict warning in the log.
  Not kept: no real benefit.
- ImmediatelyFast 1.16.5: no effect beyond noise standing, in the crowd scene, or with the inventory + JEI item
  list open (+2% FPS). Not kept.
- World generation (spectator route, 24 blocks/s): two identical base runs differed x2.9 in MSPT, so no
  difference from any of these mods can be claimed.

2026-10-12 additions (same lab, interleaved, 2-3 repeats):
- C2ME (c2me-neoforge 0.4.2-alpha.0.98): spectator flight 24 blocks/s, new chunks/s 4.5-4.9 -> 9.2-10.9 in a
  Terralith all_skylands world (TPS 10 -> 17-19), Twilight Forest 13-16 -> 43, a custom sphere world 13.5 -> 28-30.
  FPS -4..-19% during that flight (client meshes more chunks). Terrain identical to vanilla; feature placement
  (trees, ore blobs, ice) differs between ANY two runs, vanilla included (neighbour-chunk generation order), and two
  C2ME runs differ from each other as much as from vanilla. Kept.
- Fast Noise 1.0.40: no effect alone or with C2ME. Moonrise 1.1.2: crashes at registration with Adorn (custom
  `Property` subclass lacks `moonrise$getIdFor`). ModernFix-mVUS 5.27.21: no startup gain here, and its
  "missing perf mods" warning screen blocks unattended launches (`mixin.feature.warn_missing_perf_mods=false`).
  Ksyxis: world join -1 s but stops keeping spawn chunks loaded.
- Quick Pack 1.5.1: boot to world 69.5 -> 53.4 s with a 20 MB zip resource pack (it speeds up zip pack listing). Kept.
- Get It Together Drops 1.5 + Clumps 26.2.1: 1178 dropped items + 600 XP orbs: entities 2150 -> 1230, FPS +19%,
  MSPT -20%. Kept.
- GC (Java 25, 8 GB, 4-core laptop): G1 and generational ZGC tie on mean FPS/MSPT; G1 uses half the heap
  (3.5-5 vs 7-7.8 GB) but frame p99 +4-6 ms and 60-100 ms max frames; ZGC kept. A first single round looked like a
  G1 win: repeat GC comparisons.

## Gotchas
1. When launched from a sandboxed agent shell on Windows, `HttpClient`/`Selector` creation can fail with
   "Unable to establish loopback connection" (AF_UNIX in TEMP). Fix for lab runs:
   `-Djdk.net.unixdomain.tmpdir=%PUBLIC%\<dir>` (a short ASCII path). Collective's update checker crashes mod construction otherwise.
2. Immersive Melodies 0.8.0 starts its MIDI poller as a non-daemon endless thread and opens Java's software
   sequencer (another non-daemon thread) -> `javaw.exe` never exits after closing the game.
3. Balm 26.2.0.9 enum/validated config values: validator accepts `null`, so missing keys are never written but
   their comments are "corrected" on every check. One instance: one rewrite. Two instances sharing `config/`:
   endless ping-pong via both FileWatchers (~2 writes/s) and eventually `WritingException REPLACE_ATOMIC`.
   Gotcha 2 + 3 together explain "the pack starts twice and then crashes on a config file".
4. A huge `-Xmx` with ZGC on a laptop: the heap grows to ~15 GB before a cycle; when the OS runs out of RAM the
   game stalls for seconds (MSPT 500 ms). 8 GB (live set after a full GC ~1.8 GB) removed the stalls.
5. Several mods ship pre-26.x data (item predicates `{"item":..}`, ingredient objects, recipe category "tools");
   26.2 rejects them at load. A small local data-pack mod with corrected copies (ordering AFTER) restores them; the
   copies are those mods' own data, so share such a pack only where their licences allow.
6. Bash heredocs from the agent tool can mangle backslashes in Python/Java snippets; write such files with the
   editor tool instead.
7. TLauncher memory: it takes the version json's `default_user_jvm` args, drops their `-Xmx` and appends its own
   `-Xmx<minecraft.memory.ram3>` last, so a heap limit cannot be pinned in the version json. A
   `-XX:SoftMaxHeapSize` there is worse: if the slider is ever set below it the JVM refuses to start. Set
   `minecraft.memory.ram3` in `%APPDATA%\.tlauncher\tlauncher-2.0.properties` while TLauncher is closed (it
   rewrites the file on exit) and keep the CRLF line endings.
8. `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram` (live-set measurement) stops the whole JVM for ~2 s on an 8 GB ZGC heap. The
   server logs it as "Can't keep up! ... 2xxx ms"; check those timestamps against the benchmark window. One of our
   runs had it land inside the window and looked like a -97% regression until it was rerun.
9. Standing-still benchmarks cannot show render-side mods. Use scenes: an open inventory with JEI's item list
   (GUI batching) and a sealed box of mobs + chests in view (occlusion culling).
10. Twilight Forest re26 4.8.4208 JEI plugin dies on the first call: `RecipeViewerConstants.getAllUncraftingRecipes`
   calls `assemble(CraftingInput.EMPTY)` on every crafting recipe and vanilla `DecoratedPotRecipe` (also
   `ImbueRecipe`, Crop Critters' `SeedBallRecipe`) throws AIOOBE on an empty grid, so every TF JEI category stays
   empty. Redirecting that call to "exception -> empty stack" restores the plugin; its uncrafting category then hits
   26.2's "Ingredients can't be empty" for cells whose items are all filtered out (59 recipes) - return null from
   the cell lambda and skip `add(null)`. Cost: TF's own recipe registration, JEI start 6.2 -> 7.9 s at world join.
11. Twilight Forest `EntityEvents.gatherPotentialSpawns` runs on every natural-spawn attempt in every dimension
   (thousands of calls per tick with ~2 300 chunks loaded) and its 64-entry cache is keyed by chunk x/z only (no
   dimension; thrashes). Remembering per StructureManager the chunks with no `ControlledSpawns` structure is exact
   (final once a chunk can tick, holds no StructureStart objects); compute chunks with TF structures fresh so the
   mutable "conquered" state never goes stale. A lab self-check mode recomputed 11.8 M overworld + 1.2 M TF-dimension
   answers: 0 mismatches. Effect: TF's share of server-thread samples halved, but MSPT only 15.5 -> 14.9 ms (-4%,
   ABAB without profiler). A profiled pair had shown -12.6%: the sampler inflates hot-call costs, so confirm
   gains with interleaved unprofiled runs.
12. Twilight Forest re26 port: `sounds.json` references 92 .ogg files the jar lacks (beetles, helmet crab, penguin,
   squirrel, troll, jar, candelabra, scepters). Upstream github.com/TeamTwilight/twilightforest (branch `latest`)
   has them unchanged under `src/main/resources/assets/twilightforest/sounds/`, but TF's README makes its sounds and
   structures All Rights Reserved (the other non-code assets are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), so they can't go into a resource
   jar you share. Report the missing files to the port's author.
13. JEI 30.x moved output computation into `SmithingCategoryExtension.setOutput`, which uses JEI's platform
   `RecipeHelper` (vanilla transform/trim only). Mods whose smithing extension subclasses that internal class
   without overriding `setOutput` (TF's NoTemplateSmithingExtension) now fail with "Unknown recipe type"; a mixin
   can add the missing `setOutput` with the erased signature `(SmithingRecipe, IIngredientAcceptor)`.
   26.2 also forbids `Ingredient.getValues()` on NeoForge custom ingredients - use `display().resolveForStacks`.
14. NeoForge 26.2 loads every file in `data/*/loot_modifiers/` as a modifier; the old
   `neoforge:loot_modifiers/global_loot_modifiers.json` list ({"replace","entries"}) is obsolete and logs
   "No key type". Mods' own modifiers still work; overriding the list with a no-op `neoforge:add_table` silences it.
15. Better Village 4.0.0 (26.2) ships a corrupted `desert_meeting_point_3.nbt` (gzip CRC error); the vanilla file
   from your own game jar is a drop-in replacement.
   2026-10-12: three more pieces in the same jar are corrupt (plains_small_house_4, savanna_small_house_6,
   snowy/streets/corner_03) - see gotcha 28.
16. Twilight Forest re26 4.8.4208, slow chunk loading in the TF dimension: its biome layer stack (`LazyArea` in front
   of each pure layer function) caches in a `ConcurrentHashMap` and evicts through a `LinkedBlockingQueue` locked on
   every miss, so all worldgen threads queue on one lock (profile: 95% of worker time in `LazyArea.getBiome`). A
   lock-free direct-mapped table of immutable (key, biome) entries (>= 8192 slots, THE_VOID not cached, as upstream)
   gives the same biomes (every pixel is a function of seed + x/z). Interleaved spectator flights, 90 s: new chunks/s
   4.0-4.3 -> 9.4-10.7, TPS 8.9 -> 17.6-18.5. A self-check that recomputes cache hits must not re-verify nested layers
   (ThreadLocal guard) or it grows exponentially; with the guard: 4.35e9 lookups, 0 mismatches.
17. OptiFine CTM resource packs (here Excalibur V26.3_01, whose `optifine/ctm/_transitions` overlays are
   pixel-identical to its 1.12 version) render on NeoForge 26.2 + Sodium 0.9.1 with Continuity 3.0.7+26.2 - but
   every chunk containing an overlay with `tintIndex=0` + `tintBlock=snow` failed to mesh and the client crashed: 26.2
   `BlockColors.getTintSource(state, index)` returns null when the block has no tint layer, Continuity's
   `RenderUtil.getTintColor` dereferences it. A HEAD mixin returning -1 (untinted, what OptiFine does) fixes it.
   Sources: both from CurseForge. Continuity 3.0.7+26.2 is "Continuity: NeoForged", aspctt's NeoForge port
   (project 1679396, file 8960914; also on Modrinth as `continuity-neoforged`, source
   github.com/aspctt/continuity-neoforge, whose 26.1+ branch calls `getTintSource(...).colorInWorld(...)` with no
   null check), not PepperCode1's Continuity. Excalibur V26.3_01 is file 8948603 of project 326818.
   Continuity (like OptiFine) loads CTM `.properties` from ALL packs: a same-path file in a higher pack does not
   replace the lower one, both rules run. Cost of the transitions here: -11% FPS (interleaved runs).
18. 26.2 mipmaps: one block sprite whose side is not a multiple of 16 caps the whole block atlas
   ("dropping miplevel from 4 to 0"); the log only names the sprites at each step down, so scan all
   `textures/block/**` PNG headers (+ `.mcmeta` frame size). Here 32 sprites in 4 furniture/food mods. Integer
   nearest-neighbour upscales look identical on models (UVs are fractions); large renders resampled by <2%. Expect the
   atlas to grow anyway: 26.2 `Stitcher` pads every sprite by `1 << mipLevel` on each side (16x16 -> 48x48), so 4875
   block sprites went 4096x2048 (mip 0) -> 8192x4096 (mip 4), ~+140 MB VRAM, +7 s to the menu, FPS unchanged, p99 -15%.
19. Porting 1.21.1 and 26.1 mods to 26.2 (YUNG's API 6.1.3 for 26.1.2; Ribbits 4.1.4 and NeoBiosphere 1.0.6 for
   1.21.1; javac only): `ResourceLocation` -> `Identifier`; `StructureProcessor` is an interface: `codec()` replaces
   `getType()`, the `STRUCTURE_PROCESSOR` registry holds MapCodecs (no `StructureProcessorType<T>`), and
   `StructureTemplate` calls `process(level, pos, refPos, original, processed, settings, template)` - the old
   `processBlock` arguments plus the template, so bodies port unchanged; `EntityType.X` constants moved to
   `EntityTypes`; entity `immuneTo` is a block tag; `FriendlyByteBuf.read/writeIdentifier`;
   `SpawnEggItem.getType(ItemStack)` is static and reads `DataComponents.ENTITY_DATA` (use
   `Item.Properties.spawnEgg(type)`; ENTITY_TYPE registers before ITEM); `Level.getDayTime()` ->
   `getOverworldClockTime()`; `FireBlock.setFlammable` is private again (use an `@Invoker`); `ItemBlockRenderTypes`
   is gone (the chunk layer comes from sprite transparency); `RenderTypes.entityCutout` has cull off (= old
   `entityCutoutNoCull`); `ItemInHandRenderer.renderArmWithItem` -> `submitArmWithItem`.
   GeckoLib 5.5 for 26.2 moved to package `com.geckolib`; per-frame bone visibility goes through
   `GeoRenderer.adjustModelBonesForRender(RenderPassInfo, BoneSnapshots)` + `BoneSnapshot.skipRender/skipChildrenRender`
   instead of mutating shared `GeoBone`s.
20. 26.2 data: the `minecraft:random_patch` feature type is gone ("Unknown registry key ... minecraft:random_patch",
   the whole registry load fails). Vanilla moved patches into placed-feature modifiers; convert
   tries/xz_spread/y_spread to `count` + `random_offset` with `trapezoid(-s..s, plateau 0)` (old offset was
   `nextInt(s+1) - nextInt(s+1)`) + the inner feature's filters; the configured feature becomes the inner feature.
21. Mixins targeting lambdas break silently: YUNG's API raises the jigsaw pool weight cap with a `@WrapOperation` on
   `lambda$static$1`, but in 26.2 the `Codec.intRange(1, 150)` call sits in `lambda$static$0`; with `require = 0`
   nothing applies and pools with weights > 150 fail later. A static check of every mixin's target class, method
   names, `@Shadow`/`@Accessor`/`@Invoker` names and `@At(target)` owners via `javap -p` caught it (and the
   renamed `ItemInHandRenderer` method) before any lab run.
22. Overworld-replacing generator (NeoBiosphere-style spheres) without touching other worlds: register a
   `NoiseBasedChunkGenerator` subclass + a world preset; build its settings at `ChunkMap.<init>` (the only
   `generatorSettings()` call that creates the `RandomState`) with `finalDensity` wrapped in
   `rangeChoice(sphereDistance, 0, 1, original, -1e6)`; gate every other mixin (aquifer, heightmap, biome source) on
   "this level's generator is the sphere generator". Biomes/structures of the pack (Terralith) then appear inside.
23. Cube Animals 2.1b: `CrocodileLeaveWaterGoal.findLandTarget` (from `canUse`, every 2 ticks per crocodile in water)
   walks radii 2..16 but rescans the whole (2r+1)^2 square each radius: ~36 000 columns x 6 heights x ~12 block reads
   when there is no land. 52 crocodiles in a swamp lab world: 86% of the server thread, TPS ~8. Same scan skipping
   already-checked inner squares (identical result) + a 10-tick retry after a miss: crocodiles 110 -> 3 ms/tick,
   TPS 20 (self-check vs the original loop: 0 mismatches).
24. Biome-gated content vs world presets: Terralith's `all_skylands` preset uses only 4 `skylands_*` biomes, so
   swamp-only structures (Ribbits villages) never generate there. Check the preset's biome list before promising
   content in an existing world.
25. Lab screenshots: `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` of the game window's rectangle captures whatever window is on top;
   `PrintWindow(hwnd, hdc, PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` grabs the GL window's own content without stealing focus.
   A user's screen-share/stream running in the background shifts FPS between sessions by 15-20%: compare FPS only
   inside one interleaved series.
26. Twilight Forest re26 hooks `Level.isRainingAt` in every dimension: in clear weather it walks 32 blocks up per call
   looking for its cloud blocks; dropped items/XP/mobs call it every tick (12% of the server thread with 2000 items).
   Check the chunk sections' palettes (`maybeHas(CloudBlock)`) first; verified 7M calls, 0 mismatches.
27. Twilight Forest re26 JEI plugin calls `Objects.requireNonNull(Minecraft.getSingleplayerServer())` -> NPE on any
   client that joined a LAN/remote world: no TF categories in JEI there. Feed it a `RecipeManager` filled from JEI's
   synced recipes (`mezz.jei.common.Internal.getClientSyncedRecipes()`) and have the host
   `OnDatapackSyncEvent.sendRecipes(...)` TF's uncrafting and drying types.
28. Better Village 4.0.0 ships FOUR corrupt `.nbt` pieces (desert_meeting_point_3, plains_small_house_4,
   savanna_small_house_6, snowy/streets/corner_03): gzip CRC errors and invalid NBT. `StructureTemplateManager`
   caches the failed load as empty until restart, so villages lose those houses. Copy the vanilla pieces from your
   own game jar into a local data pack at the same paths (they're Mojang's files: don't publish them) and report
   the corrupt files to Better Village. Scan every `.nbt` of every jar (1168 here) with a plain gzip+NBT parser;
   only these 4 were bad.
29. "Detected unsafe terrain read during worldgen ... step: minecraft:spawn" (vanilla logs one line, no stack):
   ~370k lines / 90 MB log per 40 min in a normal world. A mixin at `WorldGenRegion.warnIfReadOutsideWriteZone`'s
   log call that prints a stack for the first N cases named Naturalist 2.0.5 `Hippo.checkHippoSpawnRules`
   (33x3x33 water scan, `hasChunk` true for the region's neighbours). Treat only the centre chunk as loaded when the
   level is a `WorldGenRegion`.
30. In 26.2 the integrated server starts with `setUsesAuthentication(true)`: two offline lab clients cannot share a
   LAN world unless the lab build turns it off (lab only; normal LAN play keeps authentication on). Start the second
   client ~4 min earlier than you think: two clients on one machine boot slowly.
31. `/locate` (and anything using `findNearestMapStructure`) for a structure that cannot exist in the world (villages
   in Terralith all_skylands) froze the server 148 s.
32. TLauncher modpack folders carry `TLauncherAdditional.json` with URLs for the NeoForge libraries (incl. the patched
   client); `versions/<id>/<id>.jar` is byte-identical to Mojang's client.jar, which the launcher downloads from
   `downloads.client`. Don't hand the version folder around as a zip: besides Mojang's jar it holds every mod's jar,
   and many licences (EntityCulling's; Balm and Better Village are All Rights Reserved) don't allow re-hosting them.
   Share a mod list, or a CurseForge/Modrinth pack that downloads each mod from its own page.
33. Showcase filming: gfxcapture timestamps are wall-clock and fine; empty-sky takes came from starting camera moves
   before chunks existed. Pregenerate a dedicated "film world" (visit start/middle/end of every path, wait until all
   chunks within 7 of the CAMERA are on the client, save), then film from copies. Sodium's
   `isTerrainRenderComplete()` flickers and is useless as a readiness signal.
34. Move the camera every rendered frame with `LocalPlayer.snapTo(x,y,z,yaw,pitch)` plus `xOld/yOld/zOld` and head
   rotation from `RenderFrameEvent.Pre`: smooth paths, no tick interpolation steps. Cancel `ToastManager.addToast`
   while filming.
35. `um video compile` with Cyrillic titles: Space Grotesk (the default title font) has no Cyrillic, and older `um`
   read the EDL with the locale encoding (we ran it with `PYTHONUTF8=1` and swapped the font paths in a small
   wrapper). Fixed in `um` since (#259): EDLs are read as UTF-8, and the EDL theme's `title_font` / `body_font` /
   `mono_font` take .ttf paths, so point them at a font with Cyrillic (Segoe UI, Constantia).
36. Minecraft music OGGs sit in `assets/objects/<hash>` (index `assets/indexes/<id>.json`, key
   `minecraft/sounds/music/game/...`); `playsound ... master` of a music event did not end up in a process-loopback
   recording.
37. NeoBiosphere-style worlds: spheres radius 128, centres every 500 blocks at y 62 - orbit at ~235 blocks with render
   distance 20 to show a whole sphere.

# Porting Thaumcraft 4 (1.7.10 Forge) to Minecraft 1.20.1 Fabric

> An ongoing port of the Thaumcraft 4.2.3.5 mod (Minecraft 1.7.10, Forge) to Minecraft 1.20.1 on Fabric, keeping the
> original's behaviour, values and quirks. Each subsystem is checked by GameTests on a real dedicated test server
> (323 passing on 2026-10-10, from 859 decompiled original classes to about 77,000 lines of port code). Rendering,
> screens, the click path, natural world generation and the custom dimension are checked by screenshots from a real
> client driven by a scripted harness. This note collects the 1.20.1 engine facts that cost time. The method is the
> `port-a-mod` skill (`skills/port-a-mod/`); Forge 1.7.10 → Fabric 1.20.1 mappings are in its `references/` folder.
> The test traps that apply to any Fabric 1.20.1 mod have their own notes:
> `techniques/fabric-1-20-1-gametests-as-the-oracle-of-a-large-mod-port.md` (GameTests) and
> `techniques/a-scenario-harness-in-a-minecraft-fabric-dev-client-real-cli.md` (the client harness).

## Setup
- Minecraft Java 1.20.1, Fabric Loader 0.16.14, Fabric API 0.92.12+1.20.1, Yarn 1.20.1+build.10 (v2), Loom 1.6.12
  (1.7.4 since 2026-10-10, see gotcha 19), Gradle 8.8 wrapper, Java 17 (`release 17`; JDK 21 ran Gradle), on Linux
  cloud containers and on Windows 10 (Git Bash).
- The 1.7.10 reference: the Thaumcraft-1.7.10-4.2.3.5 jar (SHA-1 recorded), decompiled with Vineflower and remapped
  SRG → MCP `stable_12-1.7.10` with a token-replacing script (859 classes, 7 not decompilable). CFR was the fallback
  for the classes Vineflower could not decompile cleanly. The decompile and the original assets live in the port's
  **private** repository, so every fresh session can read them; they are never shipped.
- **Permission:** Thaumcraft is All Rights Reserved (Azanor). The port re-implements its code from the decompile and
  its build uses TC4's own textures and sounds (see Assets), so releasing the port would need Azanor's permission.
  The port's repository is private and this note links no release. Nothing from Thaumcraft (code, decompile,
  textures, sounds or data files) is in this repository; the note describes the original's logic in its own words.
- Target modpack pieces loaded in tests: Accessories 1.0.0-beta.48+1.20.1, cloth-config 11.1.118, Trinkets 3.7.2,
  accessories-tc-layer 3.8.1+beta.14, Cardinal Components.
- Builds ran offline from a populated Loom cache: `./gradlew build runGametest --no-daemon`. A fresh cloud container
  needs `maven.fabricmc.net`, `piston-meta.mojang.com`, `piston-data.mojang.com`, `libraries.minecraft.net`,
  `resources.download.minecraft.net` and each dependency's Maven allowed first.

## Route and why
- Route: Fabric loader API plus Mixin, with the original's behaviour re-implemented class by class against its
  decompiled source.
- Forge 1.20.1 was not chosen; the project targets Fabric.
- Data-driven features (dimension, biomes, worldgen, loot, tags) are datapack JSON; everything else is code.
- **How the port is organised** (details in the `port-a-mod` skill):
  - one source of truth: TC 4.2.3.5 only. The project had started from Thaumcraft 5 and switched; TC5 is never a
    reference (gotcha 24 shows what that cost);
  - an adaptation matrix (keep / adapt / replace / remove per area) and a status log with a section per unit:
    original classes, "quirks kept", deviations with their 1.20 reason, tests, "not ported";
  - the original's data (48 aspects, 457 object-aspect registrations, research tree, recipes) extracted from the
    decompiled `Config*` classes by Python tokenizers into JSON, never retyped;
  - one commit per unit; a handoff file for new sessions; completion graded by evidence level (implemented /
    GameTested / visually verified / unverified), not by commit count;
  - audits by layer (event handlers, packets, items, blocks, entities, GUIs, worldgen, loot, research, recipes,
    config, renderers) after the features existed.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **GameTest server:** it builds its world from the flat preset with only the vanilla dimensions, so datapack
  dimensions do not exist in `runGametest`. The NeoForge 1.21.1 note in this KB reports the same. Test dimension
  content in the overworld, and the dimension itself in a client run.
- **Flat generator:** `FlatChunkGeneratorConfig.createGenerationSettings` treats an all-air layer list as "no
  terrain" (`hasNoTerrain`) and then copies none of the biome's features, unless the biome is `minecraft:the_void`.
  A void dimension whose own biome feature builds everything needs one non-air, non-colliding layer:
  `minecraft:structure_void`, height 1.
- **Experimental-settings warning:** a datapack dimension marks the world experimental in two places.
  `DimensionOptionsRegistryHolder.toConfig` compares the dimension count with vanilla's, and
  `getLifecycle(RegistryKey, DimensionOptions)` flags non-vanilla entries. One mixin patches both: a `@Redirect` on
  `List.size()` in `toConfig` that leaves out the mod's namespace, and a HEAD inject returning `Lifecycle.stable()`.
  Both checks feed one value: `toConfig` creates the dimension registry with the count check's lifecycle, and
  `SimpleRegistry.add` merges each entry's lifecycle into it, so either check alone keeps the world experimental
  (read in the 1.20.1 bytecode during review; patching only one was not tried).
- **Biome reads are blended:** `World.getBiome(BlockPos)` (`BiomeAccess.getBiome`) picks a neighbouring 4x4x4 cell
  by a seeded offset (`SeedMixer.mixSeed`). A block near a cell edge can therefore report another cell's biome than
  the one just written with `Chunk.populateBiomes`. Gameplay checks that must agree with a biome you set should read
  `world.getBiomeForNoiseGen(BiomeCoords.fromBlock(x), BiomeCoords.fromBlock(y), BiomeCoords.fromBlock(z))`.
- **Enchanting power per block:** 1.20.1 has `#minecraft:enchantment_power_provider` (one point each). The count is
  int local 4 of the lambda `EnchantmentScreenHandler.method_17411(ItemStack, World, BlockPos)`, and `Random.setSeed`
  is called once after counting. A `@ModifyVariable(ordinal = 0)` at that `setSeed` INVOKE adds extra points (e.g. a
  block worth 2 shelves, Forge's old `getEnchantPowerBonus`). Do not hook `calculateRequiredExperienceLevel`: it runs
  three times inside a loop.
- **Forge `onItemUseFirst`:** in 1.7.10 it ran before the block's `onBlockActivated`; in 1.20.1 the block's `onUse`
  runs first and `Item.useOnBlock` only after the block passes. Fabric's `UseBlockCallback` fires before the block on
  both sides, so items that must win over the block (keys, wands) go there.
- **Cancelling an entity spawn:** Forge's `EntityJoinWorldEvent` cancel maps to `ServerEntityEvents.ENTITY_LOAD`.
  Check `age == 0` so chunk reloads are skipped, and queue the discard with
  `server.send(new ServerTask(server.getTicks(), entity::discard))`. `MinecraftServer.execute` runs the task
  immediately when already on the server thread, so it defers nothing.
- **Note-block hook:** every note actually played goes through `NoteBlock.playNote` → `World.addSyncedBlockEvent`;
  inject at that INVOKE. Setting a note block's state directly does not recompute its `instrument`.

## Build steps
1. `./gradlew build runGametest --no-daemon` runs every GameTest on a headless server and writes
   `build/gametest/junit.xml`; parse it rather than trusting the console.
2. A client harness (a gametest-source-set client entrypoint with `--quickPlaySingleplayer` on a prebuilt world)
   places blocks, teleports the player and saves screenshots for visual checks.
3. Look up Yarn names on the mapped jar in the Loom cache with
   `javap -cp .../minecraftMaven/.../minecraft-merged/1.20.1-net.fabricmc.yarn...-v2/*.jar <class>`, and use
   `javap -c -p` to find lambda names and local indexes for mixins.

## Verification
- **Oracles:**
  - GameTests on the real server (`runGametest`), for logic.
  - Screenshots from a real 1.20.1 client, for rendering and for the dimension: portal → `outer_lands`, arrival
    point, generated maze.
- **Each fact above was verified by:**
  - a failing then passing GameTest: biome reads, enchanting power, entity cancel, note hook;
  - a client run: flat layer, experimental warning, dimension;
  - bytecode reading with `javap`: `BiomeAccess`, the `EnchantmentScreenHandler` lambda.
- **Gotchas 19-21** were verified the same day with GameTests on the real jars (and a client start).
- **Gotchas 15-18 were verified on 2026-10-10** on a seed-12345 normal world (Windows 10, client window, no Xvfb):
  the log line counts before and after each fix, inspected screenshots, and a GameTest for gotcha 15 (313 passing).
- **Verified later (2026-10-10):** the real-client click path. A screenshot-harness scenario drives
  `ClientPlayerInteractionManager.interactBlock` / `interactItem` in survival (packets, then the server's use path)
  for the wand triggers, the research table, three screens and the infusion altar (refused without its research,
  formed with it): 9 of 9 checks passed. GameTests alone call the item logic directly and cannot show this.
- **Gotchas 31-58** were each found by a failing GameTest, a harness screenshot, a log check of the production
  client, or an audit against the decompiled original, as recorded per unit in the project's migration log. The
  full suite stood at 323 / 323 on 2026-10-10. The real-client progression scenario passed 28 / 28 (Thaumonomicon,
  crucible, worktable, research table, research note solved by dragging aspects, infusion, a golem placed and
  cored by hand).
- **Not verified:**
  - patching only one of the two experimental-warning checks, in game (both were patched together; the bytecode
    says both are needed);
  - Sodium / Indium with the port's FRAPI models (the dev runtime cannot run Sodium, gotcha 52);
  - a full survival playthrough, a full modpack instance, and multiplayer beyond a two-client smoke test.

## Gotchas
Traps that apply to any Fabric 1.20.1 GameTest suite or client harness are written up once, in the GameTest note
(`techniques/fabric-1-20-1-gametests-as-the-oracle-of-a-large-mod-port.md`) and the harness note
(`techniques/a-scenario-harness-in-a-minecraft-fabric-dev-client-real-cli.md`). They keep their number here and
point there.
1. **A dimension GameTest finds no world.** The GameTest server has no datapack dimensions: GameTest note, gotcha 7.
2. **Void dimension, but the biome feature never runs.**
   - **Cause:** all-air flat layers count as "no terrain", so features are skipped.
   - **Fix:** one `structure_void` layer.
3. **Every world load stops on the experimental-settings screen.**
   - **Cause:** the dimension-count and lifecycle checks.
   - **Fix:** the two-part mixin above.
4. **Crash "asking a region for a chunk out of bound", or log "setBlock in a far chunk", from a feature.**
   - **Cause:** 1.7.10 world generation wrote into neighbouring chunks; 1.20.1 features only see their chunk and a
     small margin.
   - **Fix:** split the generator so each chunk writes only inside itself.
5. **A biome was just written but the check says it wasn't, at some positions only.**
   - **Cause:** `getBiome` blends neighbouring cells by seed.
   - **Fix:** read the stored cell with `getBiomeForNoiseGen`.
6. **Unrelated tests start failing after new tests are added.** Global state keyed by position leaks between tests:
   GameTest note, gotcha 2.
7. **A mob on a pressure plate never presses it.** It had `setAiDisabled(true)`: GameTest note, gotcha 8.
8. **Mobs in other tests act strangely.** The in-world mock player is seen by every test in the batch: GameTest
   note, gotcha 3.
9. **`ctx.createMockPlayer()` does not compile on 1.20.1.** 1.20.1 has only the three `createMock*Player*` methods:
   GameTest note, gotcha 3.
10. **Boss entities spawned in corner chunks are not found by `getEntitiesByClass`.** Those chunks were not
    entity-ticking: GameTest note, gotcha 6.
11. **Crop "growth" code does nothing.**
    - **Cause:** 1.20 crops grow in `randomTick`; 1.7.10 used `updateTick`.
    - **Fix:** call `randomTick`.
12. **A note-block test hears nothing.**
    - **Cause:** the instrument property is not recomputed when the state is set directly, and a per-tick "heard
      notes" list was never cleared.
    - **Fix:** set `instrument` in the test, and clear the list at `END_WORLD_TICK`.

13. **A 1.7.10 multiblock's faces changed with their neighbours (connected textures), and 1.20 models cannot read
    neighbours.**
    - **Cause:** 1.7.10 picked icons at render time (`getIcon(IBlockAccess, x, y, z, side)`).
    - **Fix:** inside a formed structure those inputs never change. Compute them once when it forms, store them as
      block-state properties, and generate one model per state with a script that ports `getIcon`. For TC4's
      infernal furnace that was 231 states, and it keeps vanilla culling and AO.
14. **A screenshot harness reported success, but the picture was from an older run.** The harness's compile had
    failed and the old PNG was still on disk: harness note, "The wrapper script".
15. **Log "Tried to load a block entity for block X but failed" right after world generation.**
    - **Cause:** a 1.7.10 block class covered several metas, only some with a tile entity (`hasTileEntity(meta)`). Ported as
      one `BlockWithEntity` per meta, every state counts as having a block entity. `ChunkRegion.setBlockState` then queues
      a dummy block entity for each placed block, and `createBlockEntity` returns null for the metas without one.
    - **Fix:** only the metas `hasTileEntity` lists implement `BlockEntityProvider` (a subclass); the rest extend `Block`.
      Seen with TC4's eldritch obelisk body; the warning went from 4 per new world to 0.
16. **"Detected setBlock in a far chunk ... currently generating: <your decorator feature>".**
    - **Cause:** a 1.7.10 `BiomeGenBase.decorate(world, rand, x, z)` port keeps populate's frame: it decorates
      x + 8 .. x + 23, the corner of the next chunks. A 1.20 feature may write only 16 blocks around its own chunk, so
      wide trees near the +x / +z edge are refused (clipped) and logged.
    - **Fix:** shift the frame by -8 (`x = chunkX * 16 - 8`): the same 16 x 16 square lands on the decorated chunk and
      trees get 16 blocks of margin on every side. Densities stay the same; positions move 8 blocks for a given seed.
17. **A scripted screenshot client lands underwater or on the ground after a long teleport, though it was flying.**
    Creative flight switches off in unloaded chunks; use spectator mode: harness note, gotcha 2.
18. **Finding a naturally generated jigsaw piece (a modded village house) in a test world.** Walk the structure
    set's placement cells to `STRUCTURE_STARTS` and match pieces by template id: harness note, "Natural generation".
19. **"Mod was built with a newer version of Loom (1.7.413), you are using Loom (1.6.12)" when adding a dependency.**
    - **Cause:** Loom refuses to remap a mod jar whose manifest `Fabric-Loom-Version` is newer than the build's Loom.
    - **Fix:** raise Loom to at least that minor (1.6.12 -> 1.7.4 worked on Gradle 8.8 with no other change; 314 tests
      unchanged). Patching the jar's manifest also works but leaves a modified third-party jar to maintain.
20. **`NoClassDefFoundError: net/fabricmc/mapping/tree/TinyMappingFactory` at launch after adding cloth-config.**
    Its pom pulled an old fabric-loader and Fabric API onto the dev runtime; use `{ transitive = false }`: GameTest
    note, gotcha 12.
21. **Trinkets and the Accessories "Trinkets compat layer" in one pack (1.20.1).**
    - **Fact:** accessories-tc-layer 3.8.1+beta.14 declares `"provides": ["trinkets"]` and ships the Trinkets API
      classes. With Trinkets 3.7.2 also installed, Fabric Loader 0.16.14 keeps the layer (higher version) as
      `trinkets` and silently drops real Trinkets: it is not in the loaded-mod list.
    - **Consequence:** an Accessories-based mod needs no Trinkets adapter; Trinkets-API mods see its items through the
      layer (`TrinketsApi.getTrinketComponent(player).isEquipped(item)` was true for items worn in Accessories slots).
      With real Trinkets and no layer, the two inventories are separate and that call returns false.
22. **"No data fixer registered for <modid>:<entity>" ERROR lines at every start, also on a production server.**
    - **Cause:** `EntityType.Builder.build(id)` calls `Util.getChoiceType` only to validate the id against vanilla's
      data fixer schema and drops the result; mod ids are never in it.
    - **Fix:** a `@Redirect` of that call in `EntityType.Builder.build` returning null for your namespace. Saving and
      loading do not depend on it; all 318 tests still passed. Fabric API's `FabricEntityTypeBuilder` avoids the line
      without a mixin: in Fabric API 0.92 (1.20.1) its `build()` constructs the `EntityType` directly and never makes
      that call.
23. **Testing the release jar, not the dev runtime.**
    - **How:** the official server launcher `https://meta.fabricmc.net/v2/versions/loader/<mc>/<loader>/<installer>/server/jar`,
      the remapped jar plus real dependency jars in `mods/`, `eula=true`, pipe `stop` once the log says `Done (`, then
      fail on `/ERROR]` lines or stack-trace lines. Do not fail on every line mentioning "Exception": Accessories logs a
      WARN with `ClassNotFoundException` for its client-only mixin target on servers.
24. **Code and assets still following the version the port was first based on.**
    - **Symptom:** the project had been switched from a Thaumcraft 5 base to Thaumcraft 4, and every audit
      compared gameplay with TC4, yet the wand was still drawn with TC5's OBJ mesh and TC5 textures, and
      several projectile and hole renderers, an input handler and a swing hook still did what TC5 did.
    - **Fix:** grep comments and identifiers for the old version's name ("TC5", "1.8.9") and audit each hit
      against the real reference; hash every texture and model and compare with the reference jar's assets
      (here 16 textures and a whole folder of OBJ meshes had no TC4 origin; 9 icons that looked new were exact
      crops of a TC4 sprite sheet). Removing an unused leftover is safe only after grepping for its path.
25. **A regression test that could not fail.** 40 ticks of key repeat on a mod-3 toggle gave the buggy code the
    right answer too: GameTest note, gotcha 1.
26. **Systematic renderer drift that per-feature tests never catch.**
    - **Symptom:** every gameplay test passed, yet the thaumometer was invisible, infused ores were solid tinted
      cubes, glows were cut into hard blobs and many item icons faced the wrong way.
    - **Fix:** a read-only audit per renderer group (tile, block / ISBRH, entity, item), each comparing the port's
      code with the original renderer line by line (GL state, matrix sequence, brightness, UVs) and returning
      findings ranked by visibility; then one harness scenario that places every flagged object and is re-run after
      each fix. About 60 differences surfaced in one pass; none was TC5-derived. Details of the GL11 to 1.20 mapping:
      `techniques/porting-1-7-10-gl11-render-states-and-iitemrenderer-frames-t.md`.
27. **Item icons of TESR-drawn blocks a quarter-turn off.**
    - **Symptom:** chests showed their back, tables and the bore base faced away; adding TC4's own
      renderInventoryBlock rotations did not help.
    - **Cause:** the shared `builtin/entity` item model used vanilla 1.20's GUI rotation (30, 225, 0); 1.7.10's
      INVENTORY_BLOCK frame works out to (30, -45, 0) (RenderItem's z flip, 210 X, 45 Y, -90 Y).
    - **Fix:** give the shared builtin model the 1.7.10 frame; then each item replays the original's own turns
      exactly.
28. **A visual check that "found nothing" because of the camera, not the code.**
    - **Symptom:** a 1-in-20 random overlay never appeared in screenshots; forcing it on every face showed it.
    - **Cause:** the creative player fell after the teleport, so the "overview" was a close-up containing none of
      the predicted positions. The positions were confirmed with jshell (java.util.Random), then in the game log.
    - **Fix:** for random decorations, compute the expected positions with the original RNG first and aim the
      camera at them (and remember a teleported creative player does not keep flying).
29. **A refusal that was silent only in the port.**
    - **Symptom:** holding the thaumometer on most things did nothing at all; server-side GameTests of scanning
      passed.
    - **Cause:** TC4 ran the scan's validity check on the client first and told the player why ("study <parent
      aspect>", "nothing can be learned"); the port kept only the server's re-check, which refuses quietly.
    - **Fix:** port the client-side pre-check with its message. Found only by driving the item through the real
      client (use key held) in a scripted scenario, not by server tests.
30. **Synthetic `mouseClicked` calls on the Thaumonomicon did nothing, or clicked the wrong node.** TC4's screens
    pick their hover target while rendering, from the real mouse position; move the mouse first, and add small
    read-only hooks for node, tab, hex and palette centres: harness note, gotcha 12.

31. **Every block in the game lost its mipmaps ("limits mip level from 4 to 1").**
    - **Cause:** a handful of 1.7.10 textures 6 or 8 px wide (animated strips, one leftover 8 x 8) in the block atlas
      cap the mip level of the whole atlas.
    - **Fix:** upscale them by whole factors with nearest-neighbour (8 → 16, 6 → 48 px); they look the same. Found
      only by checking the log of a production-style client launch.
32. **AI checks fire every 10 ticks instead of every 15.**
    - **Cause:** 1.20's `GoalSelector` tries to start goals every 2nd tick; 1.7.10's task list every 3rd. Delay counters
      inside a start condition scale with it.
    - **Fix:** documented as a platform deviation; scale the counter if exact timing matters.
33. **A mob sent to an exact block stops a block short.**
    - **Cause:** `startMovingTo` treats arriving within about a block as done; 1.7.10's pathfinder walked onto a solid
      target.
    - **Fix:** path to the exact point, or to the air above a solid target.
34. **Ported biomes appear but have no features, ores or spawns.**
    - **Cause:** Fabric API 0.92 (1.20.1) has no overworld biome injection, and `BiomeModifications`'
      `foundInOverworld()` is evaluated against the overworld biome source's list in the `MinecraftServer` constructor,
      before any lifecycle event.
    - **Fix:** a `MultiNoiseBiomeSource` mixin that rolls ~256-block regions at the original odds and adds the biomes to
      the source's list (entries from `DynamicRegistrySetupCallback`). TerraBlender is the library alternative.
35. **Ported biomes have no lakes, dungeons, geodes, ores or carvers.**
    - **Cause:** 1.7.10's shared `BiomeDecorator` gave every biome these; a 1.20 biome JSON has only what it lists. It
      also has no 1.7.10 default spawn list, `topBlock` or computed sky colour.
    - **Fix:** copy vanilla's carvers and non-vegetation features into each biome, write the default spawns in, store
      the sky colour from the 1.7.10 formula, sample the real surface instead of `topBlock`.
36. **Underground logic sees a cave biome.** 1.7.10 biomes were per column; 1.20 cells are 3D. Ported logic (node and
    infused-stone placement) should read the column's surface biome.
37. **A ported structure never generates (0 mounds in 4225 chunks).**
    - **Cause:** the original's site test (five points of a 19 x 19 area within one block of the corner height) almost
      never passes on 1.20 terrain; a third of the rolls also land in ocean.
    - **Fix:** count rolls against placements with a temporary counter before assuming generation is broken. Relaxing
      the check is a fidelity decision for the user.
38. **Ported trees have leaves that decay, or a tree test keeps 733 of 734 leaves.** Schedule a block tick for every
    leaf a generator places so 1.20 computes `DISTANCE`; checks must tolerate a cut-off leaf.
39. **1.7.10 village houses as jigsaw pieces.**
    - **How:** a script replays each `StructureVillagePieces` component's build code into structure templates (desert
      variants through the 1.7.10 block-swap functions). The templates go into the vanilla house pools at
      `SERVER_STARTING` with weights scaled to the pool. A `StructurePoolGenerator` mixin enforces the per-village
      limit.
    - **Check:** 150 villages gave 73 towers and 74 banker homes, never two of a kind.
    - **Gotcha:** profession villagers with 0 experience and no job site lose their profession
      (`LoseJobOnSiteLossTask`); give them 1 experience.
40. **A client with default config can't break a block on a server with another config.**
    - **Cause:** the original read the config inside `getBlockHardness`; 1.20 bakes hardness into
      `AbstractBlock.Settings`, so client mining prediction disagrees.
    - **Fix:** a mixin on the state's hardness returning the live config value (synced by a config packet sent last
      on join).
41. **Holding a toggle key toggles repeatedly.** `KeyBinding.wasPressed()` counts OS key repeats; drive toggles from
    press edges. 1.20 vanilla also owns F (swap hands), which 1.7.10 did not: swallow it while the mod's item is held.
42. **Special item entities shoot up in water and lava.**
    - **Cause:** in liquids 1.20 applies item buoyancy instead of gravity; the 1.7.10 counter-gravity lift adds to it.
    - **Fix:** add the lift only on ticks that apply gravity.
43. **A sneak-click with an item never reaches the block.** In 1.20 a sneaking player holding an item does not get to
    `Block.onUse`; the port documented it (the action needs an empty hand).
44. **Wand on a table: the screen of the new block did not open.** In 1.7.10 one click ran the item hook and then the
    activation of the block the hook had just placed; open the new block's screen explicitly after converting.
45. **Recipes changed shape or lost entries after conversion.**
    - **Causes:** 1.20 trims blank pattern rows and columns; in 1.7.10 registration a bare Block ingredient meant every
      variant and a bare Item meant meta 0; lookups were first-match in registration order; one research entry adds
      the same aspect twice (ESSENTIARESERVOIR: VOID twice = 8), which an extractor that overwrites map keys loses.
    - **Fix:** encode the rules in the extractor, keep the original order, accumulate instead of overwriting, and check
      every cross-reference resolves. An audit found 17 recipes silently skipped at load; logging the skip count drove
      it to 0.
46. **NBT outputs, strict NBT inputs, and smelting into two items** have no vanilla 1.20.1 JSON: custom serializers
    (`shaped_nbt`, `shapeless_nbt`, `smelting_count`) and Fabric's `fabric:nbt` ingredient.
47. **Assets from the 1.7.10 jar fail to load.** Paths were mixed case (`Bore.png`) and the jar held junk
    (`es_i_1 - Copy.png`); lower-case every path and reference, skip non-identifiers, namespace `sounds.json`, and
    convert `.lang` to JSON keeping the old keys.
48. **Additive particles turned black while a lightning bolt was alive.**
    - **Cause:** CUSTOM-sheet particles flushed just before render layers whose lightmap phase switches the lightmap
      off.
    - **Fix:** each custom particle sheet turns the lightmap back on in `begin()`.
49. **OBJ meshes from the original: textures on the wrong faces, seams at edges.** Forge 1.7.10's `WavefrontObject`
    read `vt u v` as (u, 1 - v) and inset each UV 0.0005 towards the face average. Flip V and apply the inset.
50. **1.7.10 post-effect shaders (warp screen effects).** Run them as `PostEffectProcessor`s at HUD time; port custom
    programs from GLSL 120 to 150 and move global-initialiser work into `main()`. The warp mist's `GL_EXP` fog became a
    linear fog ending at 3 / density.
51. **A 16-pass texgen "starfield" (end-portal style).** 1.20 has no texgen; one core shader computes all layers, and
    its formula was checked against a numeric emulation of the 1.7.10 GL pipeline (difference < 1e-11).
52. **Sodium cannot be tested in the dev runtime.** Sodium 0.5.11 refuses the dev LWJGL snapshot
    (`-Dsodium.checks.issue2561=false` gets past it), then fails with `NoSuchFieldError CommonVertexAttribute.COUNT`;
    2025 Sodium / Indium jars also need Loom 1.9. FRAPI block models need Indium under Sodium: check in a real pack.
53. **Zombie subclasses gained drowned conversion and reinforcements.** A 1.20 superclass adds behaviour 1.7.10 lacked;
    list it and switch off what the original did not have. The 1.7.10 zombie-villager variant was part of `EntityZombie`
    (inherited by subclasses); in 1.20 it is a separate entity, so the port reimplemented it in the subclass.
54. **Behaviour inherited from 1.7.10 vanilla changed.** Big-oak trees, slime hops, the old flight movement, the
    villager model and the zombie box (0.6 x 1.8) all differ in 1.20; port the 1.7.10 versions.
55. **Damage that ignored armour, magic, fire.** 1.7.10 `DamageSource` flags are 1.20 damage-type tags
    (`#bypasses_armor`, `#witch_resistant_to`, `#is_fire`...); custom sources are new damage types. Forge's
    `ISpecialArmor` was ported as is and runs from a mixin on `applyArmorToDamage` only for wearers of a special piece.
56. **Baubles on Fabric.** Accessories' default slots (`necklace` x1, `ring` x2, `belt` x1) are Baubles' AMULET, RING,
    RING, BELT. A thin `BaublesApi` facade keeps every reader unchanged; Accessories is a compile-only, `suggests`
    compat module; each wearable is registered with `AccessoriesAPI.registerAccessory` and
    `AccessoriesRendererRegistry.registerNoRenderer` (TC4 drew nothing worn).
57. **Ore-dictionary compat ("for each metal found").** Use `c:<metal>_ores` / `c:raw_<metal>_ores` /
    `c:<metal>_ingots`, rebuild lookups on `TAGS_LOADED`, gate recipes with `fabric:item_tags_populated`, and
    resolve "the first ingot" results from the tag when used (tags are synced to clients). 1.20 ores drop raw metal and
    have deepslate variants: extend ore-processing tables to both.
58. **Dead code in the original.** 7 FX classes were never called and 3 packets never sent in TC4 4.2.3.5; check call
    and send sites in the decompile before porting, and record what was skipped.

## Assets
The port's private build uses the original mod's own textures and sounds (Azanor's, All Rights Reserved; see
Setup). None of them are in this repository. No generated assets.

## Cost and time
Many sessions. One full `build runGametest` takes about 1–2 minutes from a warm Loom cache.

- Answered from the 1.20.1 bytecode during review: neither experimental-warning check is enough alone (How the game
  works), and AI-disabled mobs skip their block collisions because `Entity.move` never runs for them (GameTest note,
  gotcha 8).
- Does the port hold up under Sodium and Indium in a real modpack (gotcha 52)?

# Resident Evil 2's live picture composited into Minecraft with depth

> Minecraft Java 26.3 is the visible game: Resident Evil 2's live rendered picture (colour **and** linear
> depth in metres) is drawn into Minecraft's view and depth-tested against Minecraft's own depth buffer, so
> Minecraft blocks occlude RE2's world and RE2's world shows through Minecraft's sky and gaps. RE2 keeps
> camera and input authority (Leon drives; his view is mirrored into Minecraft's camera). It runs in the
> real games: a two-game session verified the F8 fixture stone occluding RE2's picture and RE2's night sky
> replacing Minecraft's day sky through the probes and screenshots, with Minecraft's clouds and terrain
> still winning where nearer. Local prototype, not published.

## Setup
- **Host PC:** Windows 11 build 26200, NVIDIA driver 616.56 (GL 3.3.0 NVIDIA),
  `d3d12.dll` 10.0.26100.9278, `D3D12SDKLayers.dll` absent (no D3D12 debug layer - see the technique note).
- **Resident Evil 2:** Steam app 883710 at `...\steamapps\common\RESIDENT EVIL 2  BIOHAZARD RE2`, RE Engine,
  `re2.exe` x64, always DX12 (`Capability/TargetPlatform/PCDXver=DirectX12` in `re2_config.ini`), no
  anti-cheat detected. **REFramework v1.5.9.1** (official `RE2.zip`, SHA-256 verified) installed into the
  game folder with the user's approval; saves backed up first (`um backup`, 19 files / 56 MB zip).
  `re2_config.ini` backed up next to itself as `re2_config.ini.dx12.bak` and restored after the final run.
- **Minecraft:** Java Edition **26.3**, Fabric Loader **0.19.5**, Fabric API **0.161.0+26.3**, Loom
  **1.18.2**, JDK **25.0.4.1**, development client with its own run dir and an isolated single-player world
  (the player's normal profile and worlds are never touched). Java 25 FFM needs
  `--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED` (from the sheet) for the Win32 shared-memory calls.
- **Bridge:** one MSVC-built native plugin (`leon_bridge_host.dll`, VS 2022 Build Tools, MSVC 14.44,
  `/std:c++20`) in `{game}/reframework/plugins`, one Lua probe in `{game}/reframework/autorun`, and a
  Fabric client mod. Design sheet (`design/sheets/vertical-slice.json`) is the source of truth:
  `tools/preflight_sheets.py --generate` emits the Java protocol constants **and** the C++ wire-struct
  header from it and validates every offset/width, so Java and C++ cannot drift.
- Credit: [REFramework](https://github.com/praydog/REFramework) (praydog) for the whole RE2-side hook
  surface; this repo's `examples/minecraft-gta5-passthrough` (MCPassthrough.fx depth maths, FrameExporter
  seqlock layout, GameRendererMixin injection points) was the port template - this note mirrors it with the
  games' roles reversed.

## Route and why
**Passthrough:** two unmodified games run side by side; a mod in each exchanges state over local shared
memory. Direction decided by the user: Minecraft visible, RE2 the picture source and the input/camera
authority (so the earlier camera-mirror slice was reused untouched). Alternatives considered:
- **ReShade compositor inside RE2** (archived design under `design/archive/`): wrong direction once RE2
  had to be the guest picture, and it would have shipped as an RE2-side screen overlay of Minecraft.
- **Wiring only `REFrameworkRendererData`'s D3D11 device:** our first capture path was D3D11-only, but RE2
  runs D3D12 - that path never fired once (see Gotcha 9). The SDK isn't D3D11-only (its example plugin
  branches on `renderer_type` for D3D11 and D3D12); the plugin now queries the swapchain.
- **A screen-in-world stepping stone** (RE2 on a monitor block first): skipped; the user wanted the full
  depth-aware composite as the first picture milestone.
- **Reimplementing either game:** never sensible for a picture-in-picture effect.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **RE2 capture (D3D12).** Colour comes from the swapchain backbuffer (1920x1080, format 28 = `R8G8B8A8`
  sRGB); depth comes from a device-side `CreateDepthStencilView` wrap that keeps a DSV table and prefers the
  backbuffer-sized handle. RE2's depth renders at **2880x1620 = exactly 1.5x supersample** of the colour, so
  depth is accepted under an exact-match-or-uniform-supersample rule and nearest-mapped to picture
  dimensions. Three hardcoded command-list/device vtable slots do the hooking:
  **`ResourceBarrier`=26, `OMSetRenderTargets`=46, `CreateDepthStencilView`=21** (fixed by the D3D12 COM
  ABI, so RE2 updates can't move them).
- **Depth maths.** RE Engine is reversed-Z (1.0 = near, 0.0 = far); stored depth linearises to metres with
  `z = n*f / (n + d*(f - n))` using the clip snapshot the pose writer publishes (probe: near 0.01, far
  3000, fov 74.8). Published frames carry metres, flags `1|4` (bottom-up rows, reversed Z).
- **Transport.** Windows named mapping `Local\LeonRe2FrameV1` (199,069,696 bytes): 4096-byte header, three
  128-byte descriptors at `256 + 128*slot`, two RGBA8/r32f layers up to 3840x2160, seqlock (sequence odd
  while writing, reader re-checks after use), stale limit 250 ms, future allowance 50 ms. The 200-byte
  camera pose record uses the same seqlock idea on a second mapping at ~52 Hz. All constants are generated
  from the sheet - the fake producer and the dump tool read the same sheet so they cannot drift from the
  reader.
- **Minecraft internals (26.3).** The composite injects at `GameRenderer.renderLevel` just before
  `render3dHud` (world complete, hand not yet drawn). `GameRenderer.render()` works on `mainRenderTarget`'s
  **offscreen** textures; `GlSurface.blitFromTexture -> present()` rewrites default FBO 0 *after* the
  inject, so the pass draws into a private FBO built over main's colour+depth via `GlTexture.glId()`
  (identity-checked, recreated when the window resize swaps textures, 5 s retry, fail-closed).
  Minecraft 26.3's projection is ZERO_TO_ONE reversed-Z (`b = -1`, `func=GEQUAL`, ortho when `b == 0`); a
  fragment distance maps to window space with `window(dist) = (c - a*dist) / (d - b*dist)` - no `0.5(·+1)`
  GL shift. Minecraft's far clip is **1024 m** against RE2's real 3000 m (Gotcha 2). The hand is suppressed
  with a cancellable `renderItemInHand` HEAD mixin while the pass is active; RE2's frame carries Leon and
  his HUD.
- **Input.** Minecraft 26.3 key bindings use **SDL scancodes** (`KEY_F8 = 65`), not GLFW codes (Gotcha 5).
  The F8 fixture places one `minecraft:stone` three units ahead of the mirrored camera, refuses without a
  fresh RE2 pose, and never replaces a non-air block.

## Build steps
```powershell
# 1. Sheet -> generated Java + C++ protocol (validates cells, offsets, widths)
uv run --offline --with pillow tools\preflight_sheets.py --generate     # 63 cells, 0 unresolved

# 2. RE2 side: build the plugin with MSVC x64 (/std:c++20), then - WITH THE USER'S APPROVAL - install
#    hash-verified into {RE2}/reframework/plugins (+ the Lua probe in reframework/autorun).
#    Backup first: um backup (Steam remote saves), copy re2_config.ini -> re2_config.ini.dx12.bak

# 3. Minecraft side (development client, isolated run dir)
$env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-25.0.4.1"
.\gradlew.bat build --no-daemon
.\gradlew.bat runClient --no-daemon

# 4. Iteration tools (no RE2 needed for the first three)
uv run --offline tools\fake_frame_producer.py                 # synthetic colour+depth writer; stop it
                                                              # by exact PID before opening live RE2
uv run --offline --with pillow --with numpy tools\dump_live_frame.py   # live slot -> PNGs, stats, RANSAC
uv run --offline --project <universal-modder> um win shot --exe java out.png
uv run --offline --project <universal-modder> um win drive --proc java "focus" "key 0x1B"  # close MC's pause menu
```

## Verification
- **Harnesses first (no games):** Java decoder self-test 23/23 checks (torn/stale/future/malformed pose
  records); frame protocol self-test 41/41 (25 rejection paths); fake producer cross-process run accepted
  1409 frames / 0 torn / 0 rejected at ~29.6 fps, then correctly rejected as stale after the writer exited.
- **Capture, live RE2:** first-capture log line with geometry and `invalid=0`; 30 s heartbeats with
  `frame==total` (zero rejects); depth range 0.11..3000.00 m across a real session. Oracles: statue-room
  colour/depth silhouette pixel-aligned (Leon nearest ~1.34 m); eyeballed wall 2.6-2.7 m predicted vs
  ~2.9-3.1 m measured (wall angled); open-sky aim puts 49.0% of pixels at exactly 3000.000 m (an inverted
  reversed-Z would read ~0.01 m); floor plane fit rms 3.6 cm agreeing with the game's own camera height
  within 1.5 cm.
- **Composite, fake producer then live:** with the real depth test (`func=GEQUAL`, `glError=0x0`, private
  `main FBO` attached), the fake checkerboard fills sky/gaps and vanilla clouds/terrain occlude it; the
  stale path reverts to vanilla; the hand stays hidden. Live two-game run: pose connected and calibrated,
  frames ~30 fps, fov tracking the probe, F8 stones placed at `(47,78,-5)` and `(47,78,-6)`; sky probes
  `before=184,210,255` (Minecraft day blue) `after=15,19,23 / 13,17,20 / 7,8,8` (RE2 night), centre stone
  probe `68,68,69` unchanged through the draw (Minecraft wins), MC's day clouds and lit grass winning
  where nearer, HUD on top, no hand; window resize re-attached the FBO and kept working.
- **Not verified:** third-person avatar hand policy (out of the first-person slice); audio of either game
  in the mix; whether the sky-flag `ModifyArg` actually suppresses Minecraft's sky (the beyond-clip floor
  made it moot - probes show MC's sky colour present *before* our draw); long-session (>1 h) stability;
  other GPUs/drivers (one NVIDIA 616.56 machine); no showcase video; no release (no one-click install path
  for the Fabric side yet - stays local/draft-only).

## Gotchas
1. **Composite draws but the screen never changes.** Probes right after the draw show the right colours on
   `fbo=0`, the picture is still vanilla. **Cause:** `GameRenderer.render()` writes `mainRenderTarget`'s
   offscreen textures and `GlSurface.blitFromTexture -> present()` rewrites default FBO 0 *after* the
   `render3dHud` inject, erasing the draw every frame. **Fix:** build a private FBO over main's colour+depth
   textures (`GlTexture.glId()`), identity-check each frame, recreate on texture swap (resize), retry 5 s,
   fail closed.
2. **Guest sky never wins: open-sky pixels keep Minecraft's sky.** **Cause:** RE2's real depth reaches
   3000 m but Minecraft's far clip is 1024 m; `window(dist)` extrapolates *negative* past the clip (and can
   NaN), so every beyond-clip pixel lost `GEQUAL` against Minecraft's cleared/sky depth. The fake
   producer's 700 m sky sat inside the clip and hid this for days. **Fix:** floor the guest depth at
   `1e-6` (the far end of Minecraft's own clip) in the fragment shader - ordering stays correct for every
   distance Minecraft can render (view distance 16), because no host geometry exists past the clip.
3. **Depth comparison looks inverted/garbage with the textbook GL formula.** **Cause:** 26.3 uses
   ZERO_TO_ONE reversed-Z: the logged matrix decodes `a=4.883051E-5 b=-1.0 c=0.05000244 d=-0.0` (near 0.05
   -> 1.0, far 1024 -> 0), so the classic `0.5(·+1)` shift is wrong. **Fix:**
   `window(dist) = (c - a*dist) / (d - b*dist)`, `func=GEQUAL`, ortho guard `b == 0`; print `a,b,c,d` plus
   `fdNear/fdFar` from the shader once to decode any future matrix change.
4. **Camera publishes fov=2.0 and near=2.0 for 27 minutes while the probe reads 74.8.** **Cause:**
   REFramework's `InvokeRet` is one union (bytes[128] with `float f` / `double d` aliasing) and float-returning
   getters are widened to double by the invoke wrapper; reading the *float* view gets the low 4 bytes of the
   double. Values whose float bits end in `010` decode to exactly `2.0` - inside the plausible-magnitude
   window - and RE2's `74.8` (`0x4295999A`) and `0.01` (`0x3C23D70A`) both do; 7 of 8 bit patterns fall
   outside the window and happened to read correctly. **Fix:** read the double view first (matching
   REFramework's own parser), keep the float view only as fallback for genuinely raw-float returns (whose
   double view is denormal and fails the window).
5. **F8 does nothing although options.txt shows a binding.** **Cause:** Minecraft 26.3 input uses SDL
   scancodes (`InputConstants.KEY_F8 = 65`), while the saved binding and GLFW say `key.keyboard.297`;
   vanilla F-keys worked only because they use their own scancode constants (F3 = 60). **Fix:** sheet
   `triggerKeyCode` 297 -> 65 (source of truth; preflight regenerates the protocol), patch the saved
   binding, and keep a raw-poll fallback trigger while diagnosing. Disassemble the Loom-mapped jar to read
   the real constants.
6. **Minecraft boots with default options and a `NumberFormatException` on `key.keyboard.g`.** **Cause:**
   PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding UTF8` wrote a UTF-8 BOM; MC failed to parse `version:`, ran the
   legacy key datafixer, and misread the named format. **Fix:** never BOM-write Minecraft config files from
   PS 5.1 - no-BOM or line-scoped edits only.
7. **Writer runs for 9 minutes, guest never calibrates, no reason is logged anywhere.** **Cause:** publish
   gates early-returned silently (one-shot latch, silent world-matrix/forward early-outs) so the reader
   only ever saw "no record". **Fix:** log every blocked-publish reason *on change*, throttled to 5 s, with
   per-getter status and raw values; give the reader an `explainRejection` that re-reads seqlock misses and
   names the exact rejection (torn, timestamp, clip range, short forward).
8. **`E_INVALIDARG` creating what looks like a valid D3D12 readback texture.** **Cause:** D3D12 forbids
   textures on UPLOAD/READBACK heaps, and a `ROW_MAJOR` texture is only legal on a cross-adapter shared
   heap. **Fix:** buffer-based readback (`GetCopyableFootprints` + `CopyTextureRegion` into a READBACK
   buffer) - full rule matrix in the companion technique note. With no debug layer installed, the HRESULT
   was the only diagnostic: prove the rule matrix in a tiny harness against **WARP** first (it matched
   NVIDIA exactly, i.e. spec, not driver).
9. **Our D3D11 capture path never fires.** **Cause:** the first plugin only wired D3D11, but RE2 runs D3D12.
   The SDK isn't D3D11-only: REFramework's example plugin branches on `renderer_type` for D3D11 and D3D12,
   and `PluginLoader::init_d3d_pointers` sets it from the active hook every frame. **Fix:** branch on
   `REFrameworkRendererData::renderer_type` (as the example plugin does) or query the swapchain; on D3D12
   hook `ResourceBarrier=26`, `OMSetRenderTargets=46`, `CreateDepthStencilView=21` (fixed by the D3D12 COM
   ABI), track DSVs in a table, refuse MSAA/unsupported depth with bounded logs.
10. **First-person hand renders on top of the composite.** **Cause:** the inject point precedes
    `renderItemInHand`. **Fix:** a single cancellable `@Inject(method="renderItemInHand", at=HEAD)` mixin
    that cancels while the composite is active (screen effects keep running; third-person avatar untested).
11. **RE2 paused/minimized would freeze a ghost frame over Minecraft.** **Cause:** no new guest frames.
    **Fix (by design):** fail closed past the 250 ms stale limit - Minecraft renders completely vanilla,
    and recovers when frames resume; keep the stale reason logged so silence isn't misread as failure.
12. **Screenshots keep catching Minecraft's pause menu.** **Cause:** Minecraft opens its game menu within
    ~1 s whenever its window loses focus during these two-game runs (every switch away to RE2 or chat does
    it). **Fix:** focus the Minecraft window and send Esc in one `um win drive` invocation (only with the
    user's approval - input automation needs asking), then shoot immediately.
13. **`GL_COLOR_ATTACHMENT0` does not compile.** **Cause:** it lives in `GL30`, not `GL11`. **Fix:**
    reference `GL30`; keep a `glGetError` probe after every composite draw anyway.
14. **F8 on an occupied cell logs nothing at all.** **Cause:** the never-overwrite refusal path is silent
    (no placement happened - the safety rule holds - but the user can't tell a refusal from a dead key).
    **Fix:** add a bounded refusal log line (noted, not yet done).
15. **Depth picture is 1.5x bigger than colour.** **Cause:** RE2 renders depth at 2880x1620 while the
    swapchain is 1920x1080. **Fix:** accept exact-match or uniform-supersample ratios only, nearest-map depth
    to picture dimensions, and keep provenance flags from the source storage (values stay metres).

## Assets
No game assets are shipped or republished: RE2's picture is read at runtime and never leaves the machine,
screenshots stay outside the repo, and the only "art" is the synthetic checkerboard/depth ramp from
`tools/fake_frame_producer.py` plus F8-placed stones in the isolated dev world.

## Cost and time
Two calendar days (2026-10-05 to 2026-10-06), six logged combined game runs plus tool-only iterations, one
56 MB save backup, no API spend (everything local), no new hardware. Most time went to three root causes
(FBO present-order, InvokeRet union, far-clip extrapolation) that all hid behind "it looks fine but isn't".

## Open questions
- Third-person avatar policy (out of the first-person slice; presumably suppress like the hand).
- Whether the sky-flag `ModifyArg` is needed at all now that beyond-clip guest depth is floored.
- Audio mixing between the two games (RE2's audio is the natural choice but nothing is wired).
- One-click/launch story: there's no one-click install path for the Fabric side yet; the project stays
  local/draft-only until then.
- A showcase video (`um video` contact sheets / EDL) and a `media/` thumbnail for the note.
