---
# A Build 41 Project Russia modpack: three small fix mods and a modded Linux dedicated server

> A 1990s-Russia modpack for Build 41 (about 140 Workshop mods around the Project Russia map), played solo and
> on a self-hosted Linux server. Three small mods were written and published on the Workshop along the way: a
> Build 41 port of a texture mod that only worked on Build 42, a clothing-loot rebalance that hooks the
> distribution tables, and an item-script patch so Project Russia's Soviet radios can tune True Music Radio.
> All three work in game and on the server. The server notes cover `Map=`, spawn regions, checksums and why
> joining reloads Lua.
>
> **Age warning:** this is old data. The work was done in May–June 2026 on Build 41.78.16 by older models
> (Claude Opus 4.7, then 4.8), and only written up in October 2026. That session got several diagnoses wrong
> before finding the real cause; only the confirmed results are kept here, but re-verify anything you build on.

## Setup
- Client: Project Zomboid **41.78.16** from Steam on Windows 10. Mod lists managed with Star's Mod Manager (its
  presets live in `Zomboid\Lua\saved_modlists.txt`; the game's own enabled list is `Zomboid\mods\default.txt`).
- Server: Ubuntu 24.04 VPS (4 vCPU, 8 GB), Project Zomboid Dedicated Server **app 380870** installed with
  SteamCMD, run as a `pzserver` user under systemd (`start-server.sh -servername servertest`), Java heap set with
  `-Xmx6500m` in `ProjectZomboid64.json`, leaving about 1.5 GB for the OS and Workshop downloads. UDP 16261/16262 and the
  Steam query ports 8766/8767 open.
- Mods built here: "Hidden Backpack Straps b41 Fix" (texture port), "Equipment Distribution Setting for
  ProjectRussia by RedSuper" (loot rebalance), "Project Russian - True Music Radio Compatch" (radio ranges).

## Route and why
The game's own mod loader (`loader-api`): `mod.info` + `media/` folders, Lua in `media/lua/{shared,client,server}`,
item scripts in `media/scripts`. Each fix is a separate small mod loaded after what it fixes, so nobody else's
files are edited. Publishing went through the in-game Workshop uploader, the only B41 path that worked first time.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
**B41 only reads `mod.info` at the mod-folder root.** Build 42 mods often ship `mod.info` only inside `42/` (or
`42.x/`), which B41 doesn't look into, so the mod is simply absent from the B41 mod list.

**B41 and B42 keep worn-bag textures in different places.** B41 resolves backpack textures flat in
`media/textures/<Name>.png` (vanilla has `BigHikingBagBlue.png`, `schoolbag.png` there). B42 nests them in
`media/textures/Clothes/Bag/`. A B42 texture-replacement mod loads under B41 but changes nothing until the files
are moved flat. Only names matching B41 items do anything (18 of the 64 textures in the mod we ported).

**B41's `mod.info` parser matches keys by substring.** It reads each line and tests "contains `id=`" before
"contains `url=`" (`ZomboidFileSystem.readModInfoAux`). A line like
`url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3450978326` contains `id=`, so it **replaces the
mod's id** with the rest of that line. The server then logs that the required mod isn't found on every boot and
the client mod list shows it as `[Not found]`. Plain `url=` lines without `?id=` are harmless.

**Loot tables are one shared global.** `ProceduralDistributions.list.<ListName>.items` is a flat array of
alternating item id and chance; every mod `table.insert`s into the same arrays (they append, they don't
overwrite). A handler on `Events.OnPreDistributionMerge` runs once at world start, after all mods have added
their entries and before the game merges them, which is the right moment to edit or remove entries. Our probe
counted 720 lists and 20,278 entries with this modlist. Some packs also add their own container lists (survivor
crates, pistol cases, army medkits).

**Loot is rolled when a container is first generated** and then saved with the world. Testing a distribution
change needs a new world and buildings nobody has entered.

**Small chances still show up.** With the list totals around 400, items at chance 0.002–0.003 still appeared in
about 2 of 4 wardrobes, so a chance behaves like a per-item, per-roll chance rather than a share of the list
total. Useful vanilla anchors: the Big Hiking Bag sits around 0.05 in civilian wardrobes and the katana at 0.001
in the hobbies list.

**Lua scope load timing.** `shared` and `client` files load at start-up; `server` files only when a world
starts. A test that launches to the main menu and quits can't tell you whether a `server/` file loads.

**True Music Radio needs an exact channel match.** It plays only when a radio's channel equals one of the
`TMRChannel1..5` sandbox values exactly; the server logs "Sending play to clients" when it does. Radio item
scripts set `MinChannel`/`MaxChannel`; Project Russia's AFN sub-mod redefines the radios with Soviet ranges (for
example 12–72 MHz), so they can't reach True Music's default 94 MHz, and vanilla FM radios (88–108) can't reach
low Soviet bands.

**A radio's range is stored on the radio, not read from the script.** The script's `MinChannel`/`MaxChannel` are
copied into the item's `DeviceData` when the radio is created and saved with it (we read this in the `Radio` /
`DeviceData` classes). Changing the script changes only radios created afterwards.

**Server and client must run identical mod files.** With `DoLuaChecksum=true`, a client whose copy of a mod
file differs from the server's is kicked on join; this happened for a `.lua` file and for an item-script `.txt`.

**Joining a server reloads Lua when the mod sets differ.** The client loads Lua from its own enabled list
(`mods\default.txt`) at launch; the server's `Mods=` decides the session. If they differ in content or order,
the client reloads Lua on join and again on leaving. The server doesn't change the client's list (its timestamp
stayed put).

**`Map=` on a dedicated server is the list of map folders to load.** Single player loads all enabled map mods;
the server loads only what `Map=` names, by **folder name** (`Project Russia` with its space, `DolgoprudnyPR`).
`Zomboid/Server/<name>_spawnregions.lua` is read at server start, so spawn edits need a restart. City names in
the spawn screen come from the map's translation files and can differ from folder names
(`Bolotnoe` shows as "Sloboda").

## Build steps
**Porting a B42-only texture mod to B41:** copy `mod.info`, `poster.png`, `icon.png` from `42/` to the mod
root; move bag textures from `media/textures/Clothes/Bag/` (and `Clothes/Hat/`) to flat `media/textures/`;
restart the game fully and test in a new save. Ask the original author before publishing a port, and credit
them in the description.

**Workshop upload (B41):** stage `Zomboid\Workshop\<Folder>\workshop.txt` + `preview.png` +
`Contents\mods\<ModFolder>\...`; main menu → Workshop → Create → pick the folder → Test → Upload. Steam writes
the new `id=` into `workshop.txt`; uploading again from that folder updates the same item.

**Distribution rebalance:** one table mapping item ids to per-list weights, one handler on
`Events.OnPreDistributionMerge` that walks every list, rewrites chances for mapped items and removes the id and
its chance (two array slots) for items that should never spawn. Only touch lists you have classified; leave
other packs' custom containers alone. The files live in `media/lua/shared/` so the same code runs in single
player and on the server.

**Radio compatibility patch:** an item-script file in a mod loaded after `projectrussia` and `projectrussiaafn`
that redefines the five Soviet radios with `MaxChannel = 108000` (min unchanged). The server log shows the
override order as `mod "X" overrides media/scripts/items_radio.txt`; the last one wins.

**Server:** both `Mods=` (mod ids) and `WorkshopItems=` (workshop ids); `Map=` with every map folder from the map
author's Steam page plus `Muldraugh, KY` last; set `RCONPassword` and send `save` (then `quit`) through an RCON
client such as `mcrcon` before restarting, because the systemd unit had no stdin to type console commands into.

## Verification
- Texture port: the mod appeared after the `mod.info` move, and bags showed without straps after the texture
  move (player's screenshots, new save). Later confirmed on the server after the `url=` fix.
- `mod.info` bug: the server's "required mod not found" warning, present on every boot, was gone on the next
  start after removing the `url=` line; the Workshop item was updated the same way.
- Loot: a probe inside the handler logged 619 mapped items, 720 lists, 3,030 entries changed and 0 remaining
  entries for removed items; the player checked closets in fresh worlds over several rounds of tuning.
- Radio: the server log shows the patch loading after both Project Russia mods; the player confirmed True Music
  plays on radios that can reach the channel. The fresh-radio test for already-saved radios wasn't reported back.
- `Map=`: after listing every map folder (and restoring the spawn region, then restarting) the player had no
  further reports about that city; not confirmed explicitly.
- Not verified: whether `print()` from a mod is really absent from `console.txt` (it never showed up in our runs);
  how `chance` exactly maps to spawn probability; what happens to sandbox values below a client's local `min`.

## Gotchas
1. **A Workshop mod tagged "Build 41, Build 42" doesn't appear in the B41 mod list.** Cause: `mod.info` only in
   `42/`. Fix: copy it (with poster and icon) to the mod-folder root.
2. **The ported texture mod is listed and enabled but changes nothing.** Cause: B42 texture paths
   (`textures/Clothes/Bag/`). Fix: move the files flat into `media/textures/`.
3. **"Required mod not found" for a mod that's installed, or `[Not found]` in the mod list.** Cause: a `url=`
   line containing `?id=` overwrote the mod id. Fix: drop `url=` or leave `?id=` out of it.
4. **A test `server/` Lua file "never loads".** Cause: the test quit at the main menu; `server/` only loads when a
   world starts. We first concluded that local mods can't load `server/` Lua and moved everything to `shared/`;
   that works, but the conclusion was probably wrong.
5. **The game hung on a black screen at start-up** after we added `error()` calls at file scope for diagnosis;
   it started again once they were gone. Fix: keep diagnostics inside the event handler. A deliberate syntax error
   is a safer "is this file loaded?" test: it shows up as a Kahlua parse error in `console.txt`.
6. **Tuned loot still looks wrong in a world you've been testing.** Cause: those containers were already rolled.
   Fix: new world, unvisited buildings.
7. **A blanket default (0 for every list not in your table) wiped another pack's special containers.** Fix:
   apply a default only to items you want removed everywhere; leave unknown lists alone.
8. **The radio patch "didn't work": an old car radio still stops at 78 MHz.** Cause: the range was saved on that
   radio when it was created. Fix: test with a newly spawned radio.
9. **Kicked on join right after a quick fix on the server.** Cause: a mod file edited on the server only; the
   checksum no longer matched the client's Workshop copy. Fix: never hot-edit Workshop files on the server; ship
   an update to the Workshop item.
10. **True Music stays silent after moving its channels to 65.2 MHz.** Cause: the channel values had to be
    unlocked in the server's copy of the mod's `sandbox-options.txt` (`min = 88000`); clients still had the
    original. Fix we kept: leave True Music on its default FM channels and widen the Soviet radios' range
    instead (gotcha 8 applies).
11. **`Object tried to call nil in mapLoadingRadios` every minute or two.** Cause: Project Russia places radio
    sprites as map decoration that aren't radio objects; True Music's map-load callback fires for them. Old logs
    showed it months before the server existed. Log noise, not why radios were silent.
12. **A city's spawn preview is blank on the server but fine in single player.** Cause: `Map=` named only the
    parent map, and with the wrong folder name (`ProjectRussia` instead of `Project Russia`). Fix: list every map
    folder.
13. **A spawn region edit doesn't show up.** Cause: spawn regions are read at server start. Fix: restart.
14. **Lua reloads every time you join the server.** Cause: the client's enabled list differs from `Mods=`. Fix:
    make the client's list match the server's order exactly, or ignore it; nothing is overwritten.

## Assets
Only the original mod's textures, moved (credited, linked to the original). No new art.

## Cost and time
Many sessions between 2026-05-24 and 2026-06-07, most of it on the loot rebalance (tier design with the player)
and the radio diagnosis. Written up 2026-10-04 from the session transcripts and the project's notes.

## Open questions
- Does a chance of exactly 0 stop an item from spawning, or only removal? We removed entries and never isolated
  that.
- What does a client do with a sandbox value below its local `sandbox-options.txt` minimum? Reading
  `IntegerConfigOption` suggests it rejects it and keeps the default, but we didn't test it.

# A 130-mod Build 42.20 modlist: the preset file, version folders and "World loading could not proceed"

> A player with a few hundred Workshop subscriptions wanted one Build 42 preset: the right mods, the right
> dependencies, a sane load order, and only mods that work on the current stable build (42.20.3). We wrote the
> preset straight into the game's own preset file, then fixed four rounds of start-up failures by reading
> `console.txt`. The game now starts a new world with 132 mods. Most of the time went into traps the mod menu
> doesn't show: a preset format that silently fails, one-folder-per-version loading, a dependency library that
> pruned templates other mods still used, and a recipe calling for a fluid that doesn't exist.
>
> **Age warning:** the work was done in August 2026 on 42.20.3 by an older model (Claude Opus 5) and written up
> in October 2026, after 42.21 went stable. The engine behaviour is likely to still hold; the per-mod findings
> (which uploads break, which forks work) date fast. Re-check them against the build you run.

## Setup
- Project Zomboid **42.20.3** from Steam (`version.txt` in the user's `Zomboid` folder shows the build), work done
  2026-08-25/26. Build 42 went stable as 42.20.0 on 2026-07-29, with hotfixes 42.20.1/.2 (2026-08-05), 42.20.3
  (2026-08-17) and 42.20.4 (2026-08-26, right after this work); **42.21 went stable on 2026-09-28** and is newer
  than anything here. Dates from the Steam news feed (`ISteamNews/GetNewsForApp`, app 108600).
- Workshop content in `<Steam library>\steamapps\workshop\content\108600\<workshop id>\mods\<mod folder>\`.
- User data in `C:\Users\<user>\Zomboid\`: `console.txt` (latest run), `Logs\` (older runs),
  `Lua\pz_modlist_settings.cfg` (presets), `Saves\`.
- Nothing in the game install was modified. All work was reading files, writing one line of the preset file, and
  reading logs.

## Route and why
The game's own mod loader (route `loader-api`): we only choose which Workshop mods are active and in what order.
A preset in the vanilla Mods screen is the unit the player loads, so we generated that preset rather than editing
per-save `mods.txt` files. We didn't use a mod-manager mod: the vanilla B42 screen already has presets.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
**The preset file belongs to the game, not to a mod.** `Lua\pz_modlist_settings.cfg` is read and written by the
vanilla Lua in `media/lua/client/OptionScreens/ModSelector/` (`ModSelectorModel.lua` loads and saves it,
`ModListPresets.lua` applies a preset). Format: one line per preset, `Name:modid;modid;...;`, and the first line
is the favourites line `!fav!:`. The whole file is rewritten from memory when the game saves it.

**Applying a preset matches entries against mod ids exactly.** The apply code walks every installed mod, enables
it if its `mod.info` id is a key in the preset, and lists every preset key that matched nothing in a
"MISSING MODS" window. So each entry must be the bare `id=` value. The presets already on this install had a
backslash before every id (`\damnlib;\tsarslib;...`); copied in that form, every entry came up missing.

**The load order followed the preset line.** We wrote the line in load order and the game loaded the mods in
exactly that order (checked in `console.txt`). The apply step also inserts each mod's `require=` entries ahead of
the mod.

**Mods ship one folder per game version, and only one is used.** A B42 mod folder can hold `42.0/`, `42.13/`,
`42.17/`, `42.20/` ... next to `common/` (and sometimes a legacy root `mod.info` + `media/` for Build 41). The
game uses `common/` plus a single numbered folder; everything we saw fits "the newest folder not above the
running build". Files that exist only in an older numbered folder are **not** merged in. Each numbered folder has
its own `mod.info`, so the id, `require=` and `versionMin` can differ per version: More Traits' root `mod.info`
says `id=ToadTraits`, its `42.x` ones say `id=1299328280/ToadTraits` (workshop id prefixed), and its
`42.17`/`42.20` ones add `require=UnifiedCarryWeightFramework`.

**`require=` values can carry a leading backslash** (`require=\tsarslib,\KillCount`). Strip it before comparing
ids.

**Two installed items can declare the same `id=`.** Typical case: a B41-only upload and its separate B42 re-upload
(Tsar's Common Library, Moodle Framework, True Music, Auto Mechanics ...). `ModSelectorModel.reloadMods` builds its
table keyed by id and skips an id it has already seen, so the Mods screen shows one entry per id. We did not prove
which copy wins.

**`console.txt` lists the active mods.** Each active mod logs `LOG  : Mod  f:0> loading <id>`; inactive installed
mods don't appear. Diffing those lines against the intended preset is the fastest way to see what actually ran.

**Unresolved vehicle parts and recipe fluids are fatal; Lua errors are not.** When these scripts fail to resolve,
world creation aborts after the map loads with `zombie.world.WorldDictionaryException: World loading could not proceed,
there are script load errors. (Actual error may be printed earlier in log)` and the game shows
"Sorry, an unexpected error occurred". Two kinds we hit:
- `ERROR: template "X" not found` / `ERROR: part "X" not found` while vehicle scripts load;
- `ScriptManager.PostWorldDictionaryInit> Exception thrown ... Fluid not found: Alcohol. line: fluid 0.1 [Alcohol]`
  from a craft recipe. 42.20 has no fluid named `Alcohol` (the closest is `RubbingAlcohol`); the vanilla fluid
  list is in `media/scripts/generated/fluids*.txt`.

A recipe input that names a missing **item** (`Invalid input. line: item 1 [Base.MRE] mode:destroy`) is only
logged and the world still loads. Lua exceptions (`Lua((MOD:...)).fn> Exception thrown`) and the many
`require("...") failed` warnings don't stop loading either.

**that DAMN Library moved its templates.** Its template counts per folder: `42.0` 412, `42.13` 349, `42.17` 349,
`42.20` 19, `common/` 336. The per-vehicle profession templates (`DAMN86fordE150<company>`, `DAMN83amgeneralM923`)
exist only in `42.0`. Vehicle mods that still ship only a `42.0` folder and reference them now fail. Other vehicle
mods reference parts that are defined nowhere, in any of their own folders or any damnlib folder
(`BR89SpareTiresPD`, `JP82SpareTireRear`, `BUSHTires`, `P19ABigTrunkCompartment2`); presumably lost when files
were split into version folders.

## Build steps
1. **Index what's installed.** Walk `workshop/content/108600/*/mods/*/` and record every `mod.info`: the root one
   and one per numbered or `common` folder (names are `42`, `42.0`, `42.13`, `42.20`, not just `42`). Keep
   `id`, `name`, `require` (backslash stripped), `versionMin`, and the folder list.
2. **Check each mod against the build** with Steam data (build tags, last update vs. 2026-07-29) and the folders
   it ships; see the technique note "Checking Steam Workshop mods against a game version". Prefer a fork whose
   title and folders say 42.20 over a stale original.
3. **Resolve dependencies** from the `require=` of the folder the game will actually use, recursively.
4. **Order** libraries and frameworks first, then body/character mods, clothing, compatibility patches, content,
   QoL, visuals, diagnostics last; patches after what they patch.
5. **Write the preset with the game closed.** One line `Name:id;id;...;` with bare ids, appended to
   `pz_modlist_settings.cfg`, keeping the other lines. Back the file up first.
6. **In game:** Mods screen, pick the preset, check the active count, start a **new** world.
7. **On a crash:** open `console.txt`, find `WorldDictionaryException`, then search upward for
   `ERROR: template|part ... not found` and `PostWorldDictionaryInit`. Grep the Workshop folder for the missing
   name to find who references it and whether anyone defines it, then disable the referencing mod or swap it for
   a maintained fork.

## Verification
- Oracle: starting a new world and reading `console.txt` afterwards. Final run: 133 `loading` lines matching the
  preset, no `WorldDictionaryException`, world loads and plays.
- The only Lua exception left was Braven's Achievements throwing `Object tried to call nil in everyFiveMinutes`
  on a timer; it was then disabled (132 mods).
- Each fix was confirmed by the next run's log: the template errors went 95 → 0 after disabling the referencing
  vehicle mods; with the original Common Sense replaced by its 42.20 fork, the world loaded.
- Not verified: which copy loads when two installed items share an id; how the Save button in the Mods screen
  writes entries (we wrote the line ourselves); long-term play with every mod.

## Gotchas
1. **Every mod in the preset shows up in "MISSING MODS", each with a leading `\`.** Cause: entries written as
   `\modid`; the apply code compares raw entries to mod ids. Fix: write bare ids. We copied the backslash form
   from presets already in the file, so don't trust existing lines as a format reference.
2. **You edit the preset, but the game loads the old list.** Cause: the game keeps the presets in memory and
   rewrites the whole file on exit, so an edit made while it runs is lost. Seen as 10 removed mods coming back.
   Fix: edit only with the game fully closed (check for the `ProjectZomboid64` / `javaw` process).
3. **A dependency is reported missing although the mod "has no requires".** Cause: you read the root (B41)
   `mod.info`; the 42.x one declares more. Fix: read the `mod.info` of the folder the game will use.
4. **A scanner finds the mod but not its B42 id (`YakiHRB42` "not installed").** Cause: version folders are named
   `42.0`, `42.13`, `42.20`; matching only `42` misses them. Fix: match `4\d(\.\d+)*` and `common`.
5. **`ERROR: template "DAMN86fordE150..." not found`, world won't load.** Cause: that DAMN Library dropped those
   templates after its `42.0` folder; the '86 Econoline "Expanded" module (and the '83 M923) only ship `42.0`.
   Fix: disable the referencing modules (the base Econoline and its other variants loaded fine).
6. **`ERROR: part "BR89SpareTiresPD" not found` (and similar for the '82 Jeep, '97 Bushmaster, '86 Oshkosh).**
   Cause: referenced but defined nowhere. Fix: disable those mods. Popularity didn't help: the Bronco and the Jeep
   each have over 1.2M subscribers and hardly any recent comments.
7. **`Fluid not found: Alcohol`, world won't load.** Cause: Common Sense (original upload) has a craft recipe
   using a fluid B42 doesn't have, plus three more Lua errors (`BB_CS_Fireplace.lua:42`, `BB_CS_RecipeCode.lua:13`,
   `BB_CS_GunStats_UI.lua:147`). Its comments are disabled, so nobody could report it. Fix: the separate
   "Common Sense [B42.20+]" upload (`id=VB_CommonSense`).
8. **The mod menu shows one entry for a mod you have twice.** Cause: two installed items with the same `id=`
   (B41 and B42 uploads). Fix: if you only play B42, unsubscribe the B41 copy; if you keep both, know the menu
   picks one.
9. **A "fixed fork" keeps the original's id.** "Reorder The Hotbar (B42+ Fixed)" declares `REORDER_THE_HOTBAR`, the
   same as the discontinued original; others (Equipment UI, Draw On The Map) chose new ids. Fix: unsubscribe the
   original when the fork reuses its id.
10. **GaelGunStore and the combined Brita port don't mix.** GaelGunStore's page says it replaces and edits all
    vanilla firearms and ammunition and is incompatible with any weapon mod that touches vanilla guns or ammo; the
    combined Brita weapon+armour port uses vanilla magazines. Fix: GaelGunStore for guns plus the armour-only Brita
    port ("Brita's Armor Pack B42.20 - Standalone Armor Port").
11. **A mod the player "just installed" has no folder in `content/108600`.** Cause: Steam is still downloading it
    (items in progress sit in `steamapps/workshop/downloads/108600/<id>`, a 3-4 GB pack takes a while), or the
    subscription never registered. `steamapps/workshop/appworkshop_108600.acf` lists what the account is actually
    subscribed to; one mod the player believed installed wasn't in it at all. Fix: check both before writing the
    mod into a preset; the real id is only in the downloaded `mod.info`.

## Assets
None; no files were created except the preset line and our own scripts.

## Cost and time
One long session with four start-up test runs by the player.

## Open questions
- Everything mod-specific here is as of 42.20.3. On 42.21 mods may ship `42.21/` folders (which would replace
  their `42.20/` contents), and the broken vehicle and Common Sense uploads may have been fixed or broken anew.
- Which copy wins when two installed items share an `id=` (load-order position, scan order, or folder name)?
- Does the Mods screen's own Save write the backslash form, and does such a preset apply when the game itself
  wrote it?
- PoweredBuildings V2 logs 16 `require(...) failed` warnings for its own action files; we didn't check whether its
  actions work in play.

# Creatures in Build 42: dressed zombies, ports from other games, other chassis and NPC frameworks

> How custom creatures are built on Project Zomboid Build 42, read from mods that ship them: Svide's *Cry of Fear
> Monsters* (23 humanoid monsters, each a **zombie wearing an invisible whole-body clothing item** whose model is
> the monster), a local Half-Life Houndeye port on the turkey's animal rig, and three NPC frameworks (Bandits,
> CompanionDogs, ProjectALife). The animal route is in main's
> [CDDA ants note](cdda-enemy-pack-ants-custom-hostile-animals-a-breeding-colon.md) and isn't repeated here. This
> is a survey of other people's mod files plus javap listings; nothing was built and run in game.

## Setup
- Project Zomboid **42.21.0**, Steam, Windows 10. General mod layout and the Lua runtime: the
  [orientation note](b42-modding-orientation-layout-lua-runtime-tooling-interop-ui.md); Java names: the
  [Java-surface note](b42-java-surface-lua-callable-api-and-engine-internals.md).
- Mods read (structure only, described in our own words):
  - *Cry of Fear Monsters* by Svide (Steam Workshop), v0.68.25, `versionMin=42.20`: about 13k lines of Lua in
    `42/media/lua/{shared,client,server}`, data in `common/media/{models_X,anims_X,clothing,scripts,sound,
    textures,fileGuidTable.xml,registries.lua}` and `42/media/{AnimSets,sandbox-options.txt}`. Its files carry
    the authors' own bug history in comments.
  - *HLMonsters*: a Half-Life Houndeye port that only exists in the contributor's local `Zomboid/mods` folder; it
    was never published.
  - Bandits (Workshop 3268487204), CompanionDogs (3740052292) and ProjectALifeNPCs (3803984183).

## Route and why
Loader API: everything below is the game's own Lua plus its asset pipeline. The first decision is the chassis:

| | Dressed zombie (Cry of Fear) | B42 animal ([CDDA note](cdda-enemy-pack-ants-custom-hostile-animals-a-breeding-colon.md)) |
|---|---|---|
| Base object | `IsoZombie` wearing a custom whole-body clothing item | `IsoAnimal` (a subclass of `IsoPlayer`) |
| Free | hunting and attacking players, hit reactions, deaths, crawling, fake-dead, vehicle hits, netcode | pathing, eating, fleeing, growth, butchering, saving |
| You build | the look (body item, model, AnimSet nodes), identity, spawning | the whole attack brain in Lua |
| Skin to | the `Bip01` human rig (Bob/Kate) | the closest animal rig (pig, turkey, raccoon ...) |
| Best for | humanoids that hunt players | creatures with their own behaviour, packs, colonies |

Rule of thumb from the ports: if the creature should hunt the player like a zombie, use a zombie and get the AI
free; if it needs its own behaviours, use an animal and write the brain.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### The dressed-zombie chassis (Cry of Fear Monsters)
- **One new body location.** `common/media/registries.lua` is one call,
  `ItemBodyLocation.register("COF:MonsterBody")`. At `OnGameBoot` a shared Lua file takes the "Human"
  `BodyLocationGroup`, calls `getOrCreateLocation` for the new location and `moveLocationToIndex` to put it at the
  `UNDERWEAR_BOTTOM` index, the lowest body layer. The monster's model then replaces the zombie's visible body and
  ordinary clothing still renders over it.
- **The body is an invisible clothing item:** a script item with `ItemType = base:Clothing`,
  `ClothingItem = COF_<Monster>Body`, `BodyLocation = COF:MonsterBody`, `WorldRender = false`, `hidden = true`,
  `Tags = base:noragdoll`.
- **The clothingItem XML** points `m_MaleModel`/`m_FemaleModel` at the mesh in `models_X`, has one fixed GUID,
  sets all 16 `m_Masks` (hiding the base body), `m_Static` false and one `textureChoices` atlas. A matching
  corpse XML per monster keeps the look on dead bodies. Every clothing XML's GUID goes into `fileGuidTable.xml`.
- **Identity is the outfit, not mod data.** Each monster is a persistent outfit containing only its body item.
  `dressInPersistentOutfit(name)` applies it, `getOutfitName()` reads it, `isPersistentOutfitInit()` says whether
  the game has dressed the zombie yet.

### Why identity is the hard part (from the mod's own bug notes)
- **The engine recycles zombie objects.** A recycled zombie keeps its old `getOutfitName()` until it's re-dressed,
  which happens when it comes into view. Controllers that claim zombies by outfit name then grab the wrong one,
  and two controllers strip each other's body item (a naked zombie playing the wrong sounds).
- **Mod-data marks get lost** when a monster leaves and re-enters the loaded area, so unmarked types spawn again
  (their log: 13 of one monster and endless flowers in an hour).
- **Their fix:** in `OnZombieCreate`, when `isPersistentOutfitInit()` is false, clear the stale outfit with
  `getHumanVisual():setOutfit(nil)` and immediately `dressInPersistentOutfitID(getPersistentOutfitID())`, so the
  controller owns the zombie before it's ever seen. The high half of `getPersistentOutfitID()` is the outfit
  index, and a table learned from dressed monsters maps index to monster.
- **One dispatch point:** every controller registers with the mod's dispatcher on `OnZombieUpdate`; a weak-keyed
  "previous identity" table spots a recycled zombie and gives the old controller one cleanup pass (stop loops,
  drop tables).

### Animation plumbing
- **The stack:** an AnimSet (per entity, `media/AnimSets/<entity>/<state>/*.xml`), an ActionGroup state machine
  over its states (`media/actiongroups/`), and `animNode` XML: `m_AnimName`, `m_Looped`, `m_BlendTime` and
  `m_Conditions` on animation variables that Lua sets with `character:setVariable("Name", value)`.
- **Merge, don't replace.** Mod XML under `media/AnimSets/zombie/<state>/` merges into the zombie's graph. Cry of Fear
  adds nodes to the vanilla states (`attack`, `walktoward`, `idle`, `hitreaction`, `lunge`, `getup`, `eatbody`,
  `fakedead`, `bumped`, the vehicle-collision and corpse-drag states ...) gated on `COF_Is<Monster> == true`, and
  picks attack clips through a STRING variable the conditions read. The vanilla `ZombieBiteDone` variable gates
  bite damage, and controllers set it themselves. Their `COF_AnimTemplates/` folders are reference copies that
  the game doesn't load (only `media/AnimSets/` is read).
- **Clip folders:** only `anims_X` subfolders named by the model's `animationsMesh` script entry are scanned, with
  the prefix that entry sets; human rigs scan `Bob/` and `Kate/` with `Bob_`/`Kate_` prefixes, which come from
  each ActionGroup root's `animNodeFilter` (`media/actiongroups/zombie.xml`, `player.xml` ...). The install's
  `Master_Variables.xml` lists the variables conditions can read.
- **Formats:** `.glb` (recommended, hot-reloadable; the Paddlefruit community rig and its
  `PY-BobBatchExportGLB.py` exporter, 30 fps), `.fbx`, or vanilla text `.x`. Import vanilla `.x` into Blender with
  the "DirectX X Importer" extension or ZomboidAssetConverter. Models load through the game's assimp
  (`jassimp64`), so no conversion to `.x` is needed. AnimZed, TIS's own tool, was announced but not released at
  research time.
- `media/animscript/combat.xml` is a second, older AnimStates language (`<PlayAnim>`/`<Out>` states); don't mix
  it up with AnimSet `animNode` files.

### Spawning
- **Outfits** are `media/clothing/clothing.xml` entries per sex: a name, a GUID and items by clothingItem GUID with
  optional probabilities and alternates. Every item GUID must be in your `fileGuidTable.xml` or the outfit
  silently fails.
- **Zone spawn tables:** `media/lua/shared/NPCs/ZombiesZoneDefinition.lua` maps a map zone name to
  `chanceToSpawn`/`toSpawn` and outfit entries (`name`, `toSpawn`, `gender`, `mandatory`, `room`, `chance`). A mod
  adds keys from a shared Lua file: that's how "special zombies in special places" works (vanilla: a wedding party
  in a church).
- **By hand:** `addZombiesInOutfit(x, y, z, count, outfit, femaleChance, ...)` needs the zombie population on.
  With population None, Cry of Fear calls `VirtualZombieManager.instance:createRealZombieNow(x, y, z)` and sets
  everything itself (`setFemaleEtc`, `dressInPersistentOutfit`, `setCrawler`, `setFakeDead`, `setHealth` ...).
  It works only on the server (an MP client gets an empty result), and an old version read a Java field there and
  spawned nothing.
- On top sits the mod's own spawn system: weighted rarity per monster independent of the zombie population,
  per-monster sandbox toggles and rarity enums, a night event, spawn diagnostics in the log, and debug
  right-click spawns.
- Multiplayer: creation is server-only, controllers early-return on `isServer()` and the factory on `isClient()`;
  the server tells clients "this zombie is monster X" and each client sets the variables and visuals locally. See
  the [multiplayer note](b42-multiplayer-internals-packets-gameserver-sync.md).

### Porting a creature from another game: three asset routes
- **A. The other game's own assets** (Cry of Fear Monsters ships Cry of Fear's models, animations and sounds;
  its Workshop page credits them to Team Psykskallar and states no licence or permission). If the source game
  exports skinned meshes and clips as `.fbx`/`.glb`/`.x`, they load directly.
- **B. Converted assets** (HLMonsters): Half-Life `.mdl` -> Crowbar (or similar) to `.smd`/`.fbx` -> re-skin to a PZ
  rig -> text `.x` (`media/models_X/Skinned/Houndeye.x`, clips in `media/anims_X/houndeye/he_*.x`, an
  `animationsMesh` with `animationDirectory = houndeye`, `animationPrefix = he_`). Its AnimSet is a copy of the
  turkey's state folders with `he_` entries.
- **C. Generated assets** (the CDDA ants): no source assets at all; the pipeline is in the CDDA note's Assets.
- **Rights:** A and B are another game's copyrighted content, taken from your own install. Keep such a port
  private; a public release needs the rights holder's permission, or your own assets (route C). Converting a
  format doesn't change who owns it. HLMonsters stays local for this reason.
- **Skeleton:** reuse a PZ rig (`Bip01` or an animal's) so the vanilla AnimSet works; a custom skeleton means
  authoring every state. Rename source clips into PZ's state folders on export, and make sure the clip name
  inside each file matches `m_AnimName`.

### Other chassis (catalogue; none of these was tried)
| Body | Engine object | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Friendly or neutral humanoid | `IsoZombie` that never gets a target | `clearAggroList`, no `spotted(player)`, steer with `pathToLocationF`/`pathToCharacter`; other zombies, melee auto-aim and player panic still treat it as a zombie |
| Pet or pack animal | `IsoAnimal` on a lead | `IsoPlayer:addAttachedAnimal`, `checkAnimalAttachedToRope`; troughs, milk, eggs |
| Static figure | `IsoMannequin` | `mannequin` script blocks, `registerMannequinZone` (on `IsoWorld` and `IsoMetaGrid`); poses, no skeletal animation |
| Turret, mimic, plant | `IsoThumpable` | `Thump`, `WeaponHit`, `animalHit`, `changeSprite`; no locomotion; tick it with `IsoCell:addToProcessIsoObject` |
| Visual only | `IsoObject` + sprites | `addAttachedAnimSprite` overlays; `WorldSoundManager.instance:addSound` for noise |
| Boss or swarm | several of the above | one controller, shared ModData pool; reassemble after chunk unload |

Whether Lua can drive the `Bullet` physics wrapper or `ModelManager.addStatic` directly is unknown; plan around the
engine's own hit and vehicle paths. `playerVoiceSound` is player-only: NPC barks are positioned `sound` entries,
and overhead speech text is `IsoGameCharacter:addLineChatElement(text, r, g, b ...)` (BeyondOneWeek uses it with
`getSpeakColour()` for debug lines).

### NPC frameworks in the wild
- **Bandits** (survivor NPCs on zombies):
  - identity is a boolean animation variable, read with `zombie:getVariableBoolean("Bandit")`, plus a brain table
    per bandit (`BanditBrain.Get(zombie)`) keyed by a stable id, and position-only "light" caches for the per-tick
    path;
  - verbs are 49 action modules in `shared/ZombieActions/` with `onStart`/`onWorking`/`onComplete(zombie, task)`
    (walking, climbing, aiming, shooting, reloading, looting, bandaging, fishing, generator work, burying ...);
  - programs in `shared/ZombiePrograms/` (`ZPBandit`, `ZPCompanion`, `ZPLooter`, `ZPThief` ...) are state machines
    that return `{status = ..., next = "State", tasks = {...}}`;
  - locomotion uses the player-style animation channel on the zombie: a `BanditWalkType` variable,
    `setBumpType("IdleToRun"|"IdleToWalk")`, `pathToLocationF` and `faceLocationF`, with the mod's own AnimSets
    and actiongroups;
  - in MP only the owning client steers (`BanditUtils.IsController(zombie)` gates the path calls), and
    `OnZombieUpdate` returns early on the server, so the brains run on clients and sync through commands.
- **CompanionDogs** builds a dog on the **raccoon**: `cd`-prefixed animNodes merged into
  `media/AnimSets/raccoon/`, a radial command menu (`ISRadialMenu`), status, stray-scan and bag windows.
- **ProjectALife** splits an NPC suite into subsystem folders, a shared `alife_runtime` catalog that several
  scenario mods build on, and a `Compat/` folder with one adapter per other mod.

## Build steps
1. Chassis (table above); write down which free systems you rely on.
2. Dressed zombie: register a body location in `common/media/registries.lua` and move it to the
   `UNDERWEAR_BOTTOM` index at `OnGameBoot`; skinned mesh in `models_X/<Monster>/`; clothingItem XML with all 16
   masks, a fixed GUID and a texture atlas, plus a corpse variant; GUIDs in `fileGuidTable.xml`; an invisible
   clothing item on your location; an outfit with only that item.
3. AnimSet nodes under `media/AnimSets/zombie/<state>/` keyed on `MyMod_Is<Monster>`; clips in
   `anims_X/<Monster>/` matching the `animationsMesh` entry.
4. A controller per monster behind one `OnZombieUpdate` dispatcher keyed on the persistent outfit; set the
   variables at claim time, drive attacks with `ZombieBiteDone` and a clip-select variable, clean up on identity
   change.
5. Spawn on the server only: `createRealZombieNow` + `dressInPersistentOutfit`, or `addZombiesInOutfit` when the
   population is on; sandbox toggles and rarities; debug right-click spawns for testing.
6. On `OnZombieCreate`, clear the stale outfit and re-dress before the zombie is seen.

## Verification
- Survey only: the mods' files were read end to end (structure, names, comments); none of them was run for this
  note, and no creature was built. The Java names were checked against the unofficial 42.21.0 javadocs
  (albion.codeberg.page/PZ-JavaDocs) at review time, and the Bandits identity check against a public copy of its
  42.20 Lua.
- For your own creature: `console.txt` after every session, the `-debug` animator window to watch which
  animNode plays, and debug spawn entries.
- Not verified: Cry of Fear's MP layer on a dedicated server; whether the persistent-outfit timing changed after
  42.21; any of the "other chassis"; Bandits in MP.

## Gotchas
1. **A monster's controller grabs the wrong zombie.** Cause: recycled zombies keep a stale outfit name.
   Fix: on `OnZombieCreate`, `getHumanVisual():setOutfit(nil)` when not `isPersistentOutfitInit()`, then
   re-dress from `getPersistentOutfitID()`.
2. **Duplicate spawns over time.** Cause: mod-data marks don't reliably survive chunk unload and reload. Fix:
   identify and count monsters by persistent outfit, not marks.
3. **A naked zombie playing the wrong sounds.** Cause: two controllers on one zombie. Fix: one dispatch point,
   previous-identity tracking, a cleanup pass on change.
4. **Looping monster sounds outlive the monster.** Fix: stop them in the identity-change cleanup, not only on
   death.
5. **`addZombiesInOutfit` does nothing.** Cause: zombie population set to None. Fix: server-side
   `createRealZombieNow` and set the properties by hand.
6. **Custom attack clips never play.** Cause: vanilla bites need the target within reach (about 0.72 tiles, CDDA
   note), a check Lua can't call. Fix: your own attack variables, a clip-select string variable, and set
   `ZombieBiteDone` yourself.
7. **The clothing body vanishes across saves or in MP.** Cause: a clothing XML without its `fileGuidTable.xml`
   entry. Fix: a unique, stable GUID per clothing XML.
8. **The monster turns back into a zombie after a reload.** Cause: the body item was lost while the zombie
   persisted. Fix: a corpse body variant, and the controller re-adds the body item while the identity holds.
9. **Vanilla hands or head poke through the monster.** Fix: all 16 `m_Masks`, `m_Static` false, no attach bone.
10. **The new AnimSet replaces movement instead of adding to it.** Cause: replacing the base set (the same
    failure as the animal-animset copy in CDDA gotcha 1). Fix: add nodes into the vanilla state folders, gated
    on variables.
11. **An animation file never loads, with no error.** Cause: the `anims_X` folder or file prefix doesn't match the
    `animationsMesh` entry (or the `Bob_`/`Kate_` prefixes for humans), or the clip name inside the file differs
    from `m_AnimName`. Fix: match all three.
12. **A recycled Bandits-style NPC keeps its flag.** Cause: animation variables stay on the zombie object. Fix:
    clear them in the same recycle cleanup as outfits.
13. **A friendly zombie still behaves like a zombie.** Cause: other zombies, melee auto-aim and player panic key
    on the zombie type. Fix: budget overrides, or use a mannequin or an animal.
14. **Publishing another game's assets gets the mod pulled.** Fix: keep such ports private, get permission, or
    generate your own assets.

## Assets
- Meshes in `models_X/<Monster>/`, texture atlases in `textures/` (`textureChoices`), clips in
  `anims_X/<Monster>/`, sounds in `sound/<mod>/` bound by `sound` blocks (category `Zombie`, 3D falloff, several
  `clip {}` variants per sound).
- Credit: Svide's *Cry of Fear Monsters* for the dressed-zombie technique (Cry of Fear's assets belong to Team
  Psykskallar); the Bandits, CompanionDogs and ProjectALife authors for the NPC architectures.

## Cost and time
Part of one research session on 2026-10-12.

## Open questions
- How much of Cry of Fear's net layer a listen-server co-op needs versus a dedicated server.
- A hybrid: an animal body with a zombie-hunter brain (the CDDA note shows hostile animals; zombie-vs-animal
  targeting crashes, see its gotcha 5).
- Whether a non-network `IsoPlayer` can be spawned as a puppet; the smallest workable AnimSet for a custom
  skeleton; `zombie.popman` hooks for horde-scale monster populations.

# Build 42 content as data: script blocks, entities and fluids, skills, traits and media files

> Build 42 defines almost all content in `media/scripts/**/*.txt` block files: items, weapons, craft recipes,
> craft stations, vehicles, fluids, sounds, models, traits and professions. Custom skills are a `media/perks.txt`
> file, and radio shows, CDs, music and fonts are data too. This note is a census of the block types in a
> 42.21.0 install, the syntax they share, the entity/component system behind `entity` blocks, and the character
> data (skills, traits, professions, play-as and challenges). It's a survey: nothing was built and run in game.
> Start with the [orientation note](b42-modding-orientation-layout-lua-runtime-tooling-interop-ui.md).

## Setup
- Project Zomboid **42.21.0**, Steam, Windows 10. Census of the install's `media/scripts/`: `entities/` (craft
  stations and world entities), `generated/` (items, recipes, characters, sounds, vehicles, weapons, physics),
  `ragdolls/`, `xui/`.
- A mod adds the same blocks in its own `media/scripts/*.txt`, inside `module Base { }` (the vanilla namespace)
  or its own `module MyMod { }` (ids become `MyMod.Thing`). `imports { Base }` inside a module lets it refer to
  vanilla blocks and `base:` tags.

## Route and why
Data first. Before writing Lua, check whether the content is a script block; Lua is for behaviour only.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Block census (42.21.0 install, approximate counts)
| Block | Count | What it is | Vanilla files to copy |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item` | 5105 | every inventory item | `generated/items/{weapon,food,clothing,drainable,container,literature,normal,...}.txt` |
| `model` | 3835 | mesh + texture + shader + `animationsMesh` | `generated/vehicles/*_model.txt` and other `model_*.txt` |
| `sound` | 3038 | named sounds: category, 3D falloff, clip variants | `generated/sounds/**` |
| `craftRecipe` | 969 | B42 crafting recipes (replaces B41 `recipe`) | `generated/recipes/recipes_*.txt` |
| `xuiSkin` | 254 | skins for the entity UI | `entities/**/entity_*_xuiSkin.txt`, `xui/` |
| `vehicle` | 241 | vehicles, including templates | `generated/vehicles/`, `template_*.txt` |
| `entity` | 239 | placeable workstations and objects built from components | `entities/<domain>/...` |
| `timedAction` | 119 | script-declared timed actions | `generated/`, with Lua in `TimedActions/` |
| `character_trait_definition` | 97 | traits | `generated/characters/character_traits.txt` |
| `physicsShape` | 90 | physics colliders | `generated/physics/` |
| `template` | 77 | reusable block templates | `vehicles/template_*.txt` |
| `animationsMesh` | 75 | binds a model to an animation folder and prefix | `model_*.txt` files |
| `ragdoll` | 66 | ragdoll definitions | `ragdolls/` |
| `evolvedrecipe` | 63 | add-ingredient cooking (soups, stir fry) | `generated/recipes/` |
| `fluid` | 61 | B42 fluid types | search `generated/` for `fluid ` |
| `mannequin` | 30 | mannequin outfits and poses | `generated/` |
| `fixing` | 29 | item repair recipes | search `generated/` for `fixing ` |
| `character_profession_definition` | 25 | professions | `generated/characters/character_professions.txt` |

Also present in small numbers: `physicsHitReaction`, `clock`, `energy`, `soundTimeline`, `vehicleEngineRPM`,
`animation`, `xuiConfig`, and `itemMapper` sub-blocks. `media/items/items.xml` is a generated registry, not
the authoring format.

### Shared syntax
- A block is `name Id { key = value, ... }` inside `module X { }`; `;` separates list values.
- Item references: `[Base.Axe;Base.Saw]` is an explicit list; `tags[base:saw;base:crudesaw]` means any item whose
  `Tags` include one of them; `mapper:name` resolves the output through an `itemMapper` block with a `default`.
- Recipe input flags: `mode:keep` (a tool, not consumed) vs `mode:destroy` or the default (consumed);
  `flags[Prop1]`/`flags[Prop2]` pick the hand slot in the craft UI, `MayDegradeLight` costs a little condition,
  `InheritCondition` passes condition to the output.
- `template! = Name` inherits a `template` block and overrides keys (vehicle variants use it heavily).
- `Icon = Foo` resolves `media/textures/Item_Foo.png`. Display strings are translation keys
  (`DisplayName`, `Tooltip`, `UIName`).

A recipe in the vanilla shape (ids made up):
```
module MyMod {
  imports { Base }
  craftRecipe SawHardwood {
    timedAction = SawLogs,
    time = 300,
    Tags = InHandCraft;CanBeDoneFromFloor,
    category = Carpentry,
    xpAward = Woodwork:8,
    inputs {
      item 1 [MyMod.HardwoodLog] flags[Prop2],
      item 1 tags[base:saw] mode:keep flags[MayDegradeLight;Prop1],
    }
    outputs {
      item 4 MyMod.HardwoodPlank,
    }
  }
}
```
`timedAction` names a `timedAction` block (here a vanilla one); `category` is the craft UI tab. Recipes that
belong to a station are listed in that entity's `CraftBench` component instead of being global.

### Items, weapons and vehicles
- **Items:** `ItemType = base:weapon|food|clothing|drainable|normal|...`, `Weight`, `DisplayCategory`, `Tags`,
  `ClothingItem` + `BodyLocation` (clothing), `AttachmentType` (hotbar slot), `EatType`, `PourType`,
  `ReplaceOnUse`, `UseDelta`, `WorldStaticModel` (the model on the ground).
- **Weapons** are items: damage (`MinDamage`/`MaxDamage`), reach (`MinRange`/`MaxRange`), `BaseSpeed`,
  `CriticalChance`, `KnockdownMod`, `PushBackMod`, condition (`ConditionMax`, `ConditionLowerChanceOneIn`),
  `Categories`, `SwingAnim`/`IdleAnim`/`RunAnim`, and sounds (`SwingSound`, `HitSound`, `BreakSound`,
  `EquipSound`, `BringToBearSound` ...), plus ammo, magazine and fire-mode fields for guns. There are no new
  damage types: a special attack is an existing damage path plus Lua (Java-surface note).
- **Vehicles:** `model { file, scale, offset }` pointing at a `model` block, `skin { texture }` (several = paint
  jobs, PNGs in `media/textures/Vehicles/`), `extents`, `mass`, `centerOfMassOffset`, `physicsChassisShape`,
  shadow, `attachment` (trailer, seats, doors), `crawlThroughWheel`, and `template! = ...` for parts, engine and
  sounds (`template_*.txt`, `vehicleEngineRPM`). Part ids such as `Engine`, `GasTank` and the door parts drive
  the mechanics Lua in `client/Vehicles`: rename meshes freely, keep the part ids (the
  [vehicle-port technique note](../../techniques/porting-a-vehicle-semantic-traps.md)
  covers the semantics side of a port).

### Entities: the B42 component runtime
- `entity` blocks build **`GameEntity`** objects from components. The runtime is the `zombie.entity` package
  (`GameEntityManager`, `GameEntityNetwork` for MP sync, `MetaEntity`/`MetaEntitySystem` for entities in unloaded
  chunks, `EntityBucket` batching, `ComponentScriptFactory`). It is not `zombie.characters.ecs`, which is a
  small scaffold on characters (five public classes).
- Component packages in `zombie.entity.components`: `attributes`, `build` (`BuildLogic`), `combat`
  (`Durability`), `contextmenuconfig`, `crafting` (`CraftBench`, `CraftLogic`, `FurnaceLogic`, `DryingLogic`,
  `MashingLogic`), `fluids` (`FluidContainer`, `FluidType`, `PoisonEffect` ...), `lua` (`LuaComponent`), `parts`,
  `resources` (`Resource`, `ResourceChannel`, `LogisticsSystem`), `signals`, `sounds`, `spriteconfig`, `ui`.
  Components are Java types; a mod composes them in script data and adds behaviour through `LuaComponent`.
- An entity in the vanilla shape (ids made up):
```
entity MyMod_SmokerDrum {
  component UiConfig { xuiSkin = default, entityStyle = ES_MyMod_SmokerDrum, uiEnabled = true, }
  component CraftBench { Recipes = MyMod_SmokeMeat, }
  component SpriteConfig { health = 100, skillBaseHealth = 20,
    face SINGLE { layer { row = mymod_smoker_01_0, } } }
  component CraftRecipe { timedAction = BuildLowNoTool, time = 50, category = Cooking,
    Tooltip = Tooltip_MyMod_SmokerDrum,
    inputs { item 1 [Base.MetalDrum], item 2 [MyMod.WireRack], } }
}
```
  `SpriteConfig` names the sprite per facing, `CraftRecipe` is what building it costs, `CraftBench` lists the
  recipes it runs. Each vanilla entity pairs its `entity` file with an `entity_*_xuiSkin.txt` that defines the
  `entityStyle`. The vanilla `entities/` folders (agricultural, animals, appliances, barricades, blacksmith,
  fences_low, furniture, misc, outdoors, stairs, walls) are the only schema reference: copy the closest one.
- **Fluids:** a `fluid` block defines the type; containers and food declare capacity and contents. The
  `FluidContainer` API: `addFluid`, `adjustAmount`, `canAddFluid`, `getAmount`, `getCapacity`,
  `getFreeCapacity`, `getPrimaryFluid`, `getRainCatcher`, `getPoisonEffect`/`getPoisonRatio`, `copyFluidsFrom`,
  `CanTransfer`/`Transfer`, `Empty`. Fluids mix, have colours and can be poisonous; `ISFluidContainerMenu` is the
  vanilla UI.
- When to use what: an `entity` for interactive objects that stock components cover (it saves and syncs);
  a global-object system for behaviour no component covers (world note); a plain item for anything without a
  world presence.

### Characters: custom skills, traits, professions
- **Custom skills are data.** `CustomPerks` (with `CustomPerk`: `id`, `parent`, `passive`, `translation`, `xp`)
  loads `media/perks.txt`. B42 mods ship it, e.g. The Only Cure's `42/media/perks.txt`. The shape:
```
VERSION = 1,

perk MyMod_Beekeeping
{
    parent = Survivalist,
    translation = MyMod_Beekeeping,
    passive = false,
    xp1 = 75, xp2 = 150, xp3 = 300, xp4 = 750, xp5 = 1500,
    xp6 = 3000, xp7 = 4500, xp8 = 6000, xp9 = 7500, xp10 = 9000,
}
```
  `parent` is the skills-panel category (a parent of `None` makes a new category, as The Only Cure does).
- **The Java route** is `PerkFactory.AddPerk(perk, name, [parent,] xp1, ..., xp10 [, passive])`: four overloads,
  each with **10** ints. `PerkFactory.Perk` has `getXp1`...`getXp10`, `getXpForLevel` and `getTotalXpForLevel`,
  so the ints are the XP for each level, as in perks.txt. Use perks.txt unless the values must be computed.
- Registered perks show up in the skills panel (`ISCharacterInfo`, `ISPlayerStatsUI` read `PerkFactory`).
  Levels: `getPerkLevel(perk)`, `setPerkLevelDebug(perk, n)`; XP: `getXp():AddXP(perk, amount)`. A perk does
  nothing by itself: your Lua reads the level and applies the effect.
- **Traits and professions** are `character_trait_definition` (cost, `MutuallyExclusiveTraits`, `XPBoosts`,
  `GrantedRecipes`, `IsProfessionTrait`, `DisabledInMultiplayer`, `UIName`/`UIDescription`) and
  `character_profession_definition` (adds free clothing and starting items) blocks. In 42.21 Lua checks a trait
  with `player:hasTrait(trait)`, where `trait` is a `CharacterTrait` (constants such as `CharacterTrait.ATHLETIC`,
  lookup with `CharacterTrait.get`), and reads or edits the set through `player:getCharacterTraits()`
  (`getKnownTraits`, `add`, `remove`, `set`). Stock trait effects are hard-coded; a custom trait's effect is
  your Lua. The creation screen is `client/OptionScreens/CharacterCreationProfession.lua`.
- **Play as someone else:** `media/lua/shared/NPCs/SurvivorSwap.lua` is a vanilla table behind the debug
  "Survivor Swap" menu. `SurvivorSwap.applyCharacter(player, data)` rewrites name, profession, traits, perk levels
  (through `setPerkLevelDebug`), weight, sex, voice (type, pitch, prefix), hair, beard and skin, then calls
  `resetModel()`. `SurvivorSwap.Survivors` and `Loadouts` are tables a mod can extend.
- **Challenges** (`media/lua/client/LastStand/`): a Lua table registered with `addChallenge(table)`, with hooks
  such as `OnGameStart` and `OnInitWorld` (which overwrites `SandboxVars`) and a same-named `.png` thumbnail.
  Vanilla examples: `AReallyCDDAy` blows up a room at spawn with
  `IsoFireManager.explode(getCell(), square, 100000)`; `WinterIsComing.lua`, `28MinutesLater.lua` and
  `TopOfTheWorld.lua` show the other hooks.

### Media data files
- **Radio and TV:** `media/radio/RadioData.xml` drives every broadcast: `VoiceEntry` (speaker id and colour),
  `Adverts`, and per-channel `ScriptEntry` blocks (`startdelay`, `loopmin`/`loopmax`) of `BroadcastEntry` items
  with a `day` index (how broadcasts run out as the apocalypse goes on) and `LineEntry` lines. Dynamic channels
  (the weather report) are Lua in `server/radio/ISDynamicRadio.lua`; text lives in `RadioData.json` and
  `DynamicRadio.json`.
- **Recorded media (CDs, VHS):** `media/lua/shared/RecordedMedia/recorded_media.lua` is a generated table of
  `RecMedia["<guid>"] = { title, author, category = "CDs"|..., spawning, lines = { { text, r, g, b, codes } } }`
  where every string is an `RM_<guid>` translation key. Line `codes` such as `LEAR...` grant skill XP while
  watching. A custom tape = a new entry, its `RM_` keys and an item that references the GUID.
- **Music:** `media/lua/client/Music/MusicChoices.lua` scores tracks against a drama value (from the visible and
  chasing zombie counts); `media/music/luatriggered/` holds cues that only play when Lua triggers them; same-named
  files replace the menu theme.
- **Fonts and effects:** `media/*.fnt` with `*_0.png` pages are AngelCode bitmap fonts; `media/effects/*.txt`
  are key-value parameter files for bullet tracers and similar effects; `media/shaders/` holds GLSL pairs plus a
  `README-Shaders.txt` on the GL 2.1 fallback (whether a mod can override a shader is untested). Videos are
  Bink (`.bik`).

## Build steps
1. Pick the block type, copy the nearest vanilla file's shape into `media/scripts/mymod_<thing>.txt` under your
   own `module` (or `module Base` when vanilla code must find it by its plain name).
2. Translation keys (`ItemName_`, `Tooltip_`, `UI_trait_`, `Sandbox_` ...) in
   `media/lua/shared/Translate/EN/*.json`; icons as `media/textures/Item_<Name>.png`.
3. A station: an `entity` block and its `xuiSkin` file, copied as a pair from the closest vanilla entity.
4. A skill: `media/perks.txt`; read its level from Lua where it should matter.
5. Launch with `-debug` and read `console.txt`: script errors name the module, block and line.

## Verification
- Survey only. Read on 42.21.0: the `media/scripts` block counts, the vanilla `entities/` tree,
  `SurvivorSwap.lua`, the `LastStand` challenges, `RadioData.xml`, `recorded_media.lua`, `MusicChoices.lua`, and
  javap listings of `zombie.entity`, `PerkFactory` and `CustomPerks`.
- At review time the Java names were checked against the unofficial 42.21.0 javadocs
  (albion.codeberg.page/PZ-JavaDocs), and the perks.txt shape against The Only Cure's `42/media/perks.txt`.
- Not verified: anything in game. Not tried: a new entity from scratch, a custom `xuiSkin`, `LuaComponent`'s
  script grammar, a perks.txt skill, a custom radio channel or CD, `clock`/`energy` blocks.

## Gotchas
1. **A recipe doesn't show in the craft UI.** Cause: a missing translation for its `category`, or `Tags` that
   don't allow where you craft (`InHandCraft`, `CanBeDoneFromFloor` vs bench-only). Fix: add the key; check the
   tags.
2. **The tool got consumed.** Cause: no `mode:keep`. Fix: `item 1 tags[base:saw] mode:keep ...`.
3. **The wrong output variant.** Cause: the input isn't listed in the recipe's mapper, so it falls through to the
   `itemMapper`'s `default`. Fix: map every input.
4. **`base:` tags fail in your module.** Cause: no `imports { Base }`. Fix: add it.
5. **The item icon is invisible.** Cause: `Icon = X` without `media/textures/Item_X.png`. On the ground it also
   needs a `WorldStaticModel` pointing at a `model` block.
6. **A vehicle spawns as a cube or with odd collision.** Cause: `model.file` must name a `model` block that
   points at the mesh, and the scales differ between the mesh and the vehicle model block in vanilla. Fix: copy a
   vanilla vehicle's model/script pair and change one thing at a time.
7. **An entity builds but has no UI.** Cause: its `entityStyle` isn't defined in an xui skin file. Fix: copy the
   vanilla `entity` + `entity_*_xuiSkin.txt` pair together.
8. **A trait does nothing.** Cause: stock trait effects are hard-coded to the vanilla traits. Fix: your Lua checks
   `player:hasTrait(trait)` and applies the effect.
9. **Redeclaring a vanilla item doesn't stick, or breaks another mod.** Cause: two mods redeclaring
   `item Base.Foo` resolve by load order. Fix: change single fields at `OnGameBoot` through
   `getScriptManager():getItem("Base.Foo")` instead.
10. **A container shows empty and can't be filled.** Cause: only half the fluid pair was copied (the `fluid` type
    or the container's capacity fields). Fix: copy both sides from a vanilla container.
11. **Skill or XP changes made on an MP client don't stick.** Cause: B42 MP is server-authoritative. Fix: grant XP
    on the server.
12. **Trait edits don't show in the character screen.** Cause: the info panel caches them. Fix: SurvivorSwap sets
    `refreshNeeded = true` on the panel's `charScreen` (it gets the panel with the Lua function
    `getPlayerInfoPanel`).
13. **Hair or outfit edits don't redraw.** Cause: the avatar isn't rebuilt. Fix: `resetModel()` after visual
    edits.
14. **A challenge starts with the player's preset values.** Cause: `OnInitWorld` didn't set every `SandboxVars`
    value it relies on. Fix: set all of them.
15. **A custom CD shows raw keys.** Cause: lines that aren't `RM_<guid>` keys in the translation files. Fix: add the
    keys; set `spawning` for loot eligibility.
16. **A broadcast never airs.** Cause: its `day` is outside the world's day range. Fix: check `day` and the loop
    values.

## Assets
- Items, vehicles and entities are script plus textures and models; entity sprites come from tile definitions
  (`.pack`/`.tiles`, CDDA note); vehicle paint jobs are PNGs in `media/textures/Vehicles/`.
