# The Java surface of Build 42: Lua-callable methods and the engine internals behind them

> A map of what Lua can call on the classes modders touch (from javap listings of 42.21.0's
> `projectzomboid.jar`), and of the engine systems behind them: the AI state machine and pathfinding, the
> animator, FMOD audio, the climate simulation, the body simulation and the damage and noise paths. It's for
> answering "does the game expose X?" before writing code. Every name here is public in the unofficial 42.21.0
> javadocs, but this is a survey: none of it was called in game for this note. Lua calls these as
> `obj:method(args)` (see the [orientation note](b42-modding-orientation-layout-lua-runtime-tooling-interop-ui.md)).

## Setup
- `javap -cp projectzomboid.jar zombie.characters.IsoZombie` lists the public surface (JDK 25 here); `-p` adds the
  private members, which Lua can't reach; `-c` prints bytecode. The CDDA note's Setup has the jdeps form and a
  reflection lister.
- Signatures with parameter names: the Umbrella stubs or the javadocs. Behaviour: ZomboidDecompiler; describe what
  you learn in your own words and never commit decompiled code.
- Where to look in the jar: `zombie.iso` (the live world, objects, weather), `zombie.characters` (characters,
  body damage, traits, skills), `zombie.ai` and `zombie.pathfind`, `zombie.scripting` (the script parser and
  block types), `zombie.entity` (entity components), `zombie.inventory`, `zombie.vehicles`, `zombie.audio`,
  `zombie.network` and `zombie.popman` (multiplayer note), `zombie.randomizedWorld` and `zombie.iso.worldgen`
  (world note), `zombie.debug`, `zombie.commands` (admin commands), `zombie.Lua` (`LuaManager`, the Kahlua
  bindings and event dispatch). Native libraries ship beside the jar: `PZBullet64` (physics), `PZPathFind64`,
  `PZPopMan64`, `jassimp64` (model import), the FMOD and networking DLLs.

## Route and why
Loader API. This note is an index of that API, plus the internals that explain what it does.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Characters
- **`IsoZombie`:**
  - dress and identity: `dressInPersistentOutfit`, `dressInPersistentOutfitID`, `dressInNamedOutfit`,
    `dressInRandomOutfit`, `getOutfitName`, `isPersistentOutfitInit`, `getPersistentOutfitID`, `getHumanVisual`,
    `getOnlineID`, `isRemoteZombie`, `getOwnerPlayer`;
  - senses and targeting: `spotted`, `isTargetInCone`, `RespondToSound`, `isRespondingToPlayerSound`, `addAggro`,
    `clearAggroList`, `pathToCharacter`, `pathToLocationF`, `setWalkType`, `setSpeedTypeFromWalkType`;
  - state: `setCrawler`, `setCanCrawlUnderVehicle`, `setFakeDead`, `setForceFakeDead`, `setKnockedDown`, `knockDown`,
    `setOnFloor`, `setCanWalk`, `setSitAgainstWall`, `setReanimatedForGrappleOnly`, `GetAnimSetName`;
  - combat and voice: `Hit`, `setAttackOutcome`, `playHurtSound`, `getVoiceSoundName`, `getBiteSoundName`,
    `updateVocalProperties`; lifecycle: `removeFromWorld`, `isDead`, `setHealth`.
- **`IsoGameCharacter`** (base of players, zombies and animals): animation variables `setVariable`,
  `getVariable`, `getVariableBoolean`, `clearVariable`, `getAdvancedAnimator`, `reportEvent`; `getModData`;
  position `setX`/`setY`/`setZ` with `setLastX`/`setLastY`; `getCurrentSquare`, `getInventory`,
  `getPrimaryHandItem`/`setPrimaryHandItem`, `getWornItems`, `setInvisible`, `setGodMod`, `pathToLocation`,
  `pathToCharacter`, `setDirectionAngle`, `MoveForward`, `faceThisObject`, `getBodyDamage`, `getXp`,
  `hasTrait`, `getCharacterTraits`, `getPerkLevel`, `setPerkLevelDebug`, `setHealth` (doesn't clamp at 1 for
  animals, per the CDDA note).
- **`IsoPlayer`:** `getDescriptor`, `resetModel`, `getStats`, `getNutrition`, `getFitness`, `getMoodleLevel`,
  `hitConsequences`, `playerVoiceSound` (and `transmitPlayerVoiceSound`, `stopPlayerVoiceSound`), `setVoicePitch`,
  `playGainExperienceLevelSound`, `isAsleep`, `allPlayersAsleep`, `getZombieKills`, the lead system
  (`addAttachedAnimal`, `getAttachedAnimals`, `checkAnimalAttachedToRope`), and the bump sequence (`setBumpType`,
  `setBumpFall`, `setBumpFallType`) that the CDDA note uses for knockdowns.
- **`IsoAnimal`:** `getBehavior()` returns a `BaseAnimalBehavior` (`goAttack`, `forceFleeFromChr`; its busy flag
  `isDoingBehavior` is a field, so Lua can't read it), `pathToLocation`, `pathToCharacter`, `pathToTrough`,
  `fleeTo`, `respondToSound`, `changeStress`/`getStress`, `isAlerted`/`setIsAlerted`, `hitConsequences`,
  `setHitReaction`, genetics (`getFullGenome`, `copyGenome`), `getBreed`, milk and eggs (`canBeMilked`,
  `milkAnimal`, `createEgg`, `getEggsPerDay`), `pathFailed`/`shouldFollowWall`, and `save`/`load`/`unloaded`.
  The CDDA note documents how these behave.
- **`zombie.characters.BodyDamage.BodyDamage`** (`player:getBodyDamage()`): `AddDamage`,
  `AddGeneralHealth`/`ReduceGeneralHealth`, `DamageFromWeapon`, `applyDamageFromWeapon`, `DamageFromAnimal`,
  `AddRandomDamageFromZombie`, `damageFromSpikedArmor`, `IsBandaged`, `IsBleeding`, `IsDeepWounded`,
  `getNumPartsBleeding`, `IsFakeInfected`, `getApparentInfectionLevel`, `setInfected`, `ReducePanic`,
  `JustAteFood`, `JustTookPainMeds`, `WasBurntToDeath`. Body parts are a fixed `BodyPartType` list.
- **`Stats`** (`player:getStats()`): `get`/`set`/`add` per stat, `getNumVisibleZombies`, `getNumChasingZombies`,
  `getNumVeryCloseZombies`, `getVisibleZombies`, `setTripping`.

### World, objects and data
- **`IsoGridSquare`:** `getObjects`, `AddTileObject`/`RemoveTileObject`, `getRoom`, `getBuilding`, `isInARoom`,
  `isFree`, `has(...)` (the 42.21 name for flag checks; `Is` was removed), `hasWater`, `getZone`, `getFire`,
  `splatBlood`, `removeBlood`, `removeCorpse`, `removeGrime`, `removeGraffiti`, writeable light
  (`GetRLightLevel`/`SetRLightLevel` and G/B), and the MP verbs `transmitAddObjectToSquare`,
  `transmitRemoveItemFromSquare`, `transmitModdata`.
- **`IsoCell`** (the loaded world): `getGridSquare(x, y, z)` (nil outside the loaded area), `getZombieList`,
  `getObjectList`, `getRoomList`, `addToProcessIsoObject` (per-tick updates for an object), `addLamppost`
  (a light source), `addMovingObject`.
- **`IsoWorld`:** `getCell`, `getMetaGrid`, `getWorldAgeDays`, `getWeather`/`setWeather`/`transmitWeather`,
  `registerZone`, `registerVehiclesZone`, `registerMannequinZone`, `registerRoomTone`, `registerWaterZone`,
  `registerWaterFlow`, `registerSpawnOrigin`, `getRandomizedBuildingList`, `getRandomizedVehicleStoryByName`,
  `getRandomizedZoneStoryByName`, `getSpawnRegion`/`setSpawnRegion`. Time of day is
  `getGameTime():getTimeOfDay()`.
- **`IsoMetaGrid`** (`getWorld():getMetaGrid()`, works for unloaded areas): `getZonesAt`, `registerZone`,
  `registerAnimalZone`, `registerGeometryZone`, `registerMannequinZone`, `registerRoomTone`.
- **`VirtualZombieManager.instance`:** `createRealZombieNow`/`createRealZombie`/`createRealZombieAlways`,
  `createCorpseZombie`, `createEatingZombies`, `createHordeFromTo`, `addZombiesToMap`, `removeZombieFromWorld`,
  `addToReusable`/`isReused` (the recycling pool behind the creatures note's identity bugs),
  `spawnBuildingKeyOnZombie`, `AddBloodToMap`.
- **`ItemContainer`:** `AddItem` (several overloads), `AddItemBlind`, `contains`, `getItemFromTypeRecurse`,
  `getCapacity`/`setCapacity`, `getEffectiveCapacity`, `isExplored`/`setExplored` (the "already looted" flag),
  `getNumberOfItem`. **`InventoryItem`:** `getModData`, `getType`, `getCategory`, `getWorldItem`,
  `loadCorpseFromByteData` (a corpse stored as an item), the equip and drop sound getters,
  `registerWithSoundLimiter`, `UseAndSync`.
- **`BaseVehicle`:** keys (`createVehicleKey`, `putKeyToZombie`, `addKeyToGloveBox`), engine
  (`getEngineCondition`, `setEngineSpeed`), paint (`getSkinCount`, `setSkinIndex`, `updateSkin`,
  `LoadVehicleTexture`), parts (`getPartById("Engine")`, `getPartCount`, from `VehiclePartOwner`),
  `playPartAnim`, `playPartSound`, `toggleLockedDoor`, `setGeneralPartCondition`, `isHornSounding`.
- **`ScriptManager.instance`:** `getItem`, `FindItem`, `getAllItems`, `getRecipe`, `getVehicle`,
  `getModelScript`, `addModelScript`, `getAnimationsMesh`, `getGameSound`, `getSoundTimeline`,
  `getGameEntityTemplate`, `getMannequinScript`, `getSpriteModel`, `getScriptsForType`.
- **`IsoObject`:** `getSprite`/`setSprite`, `getContainer`, `getModData`/`hasModData`, `getDamage`/`setDamage`,
  overlay sprites (`addAttachedAnimSprite`, `addAttachedAnimSpriteByName`, `clearAttachedAnimSprite`), and MP sync
  (`sync`, `syncIsoObject`, `transmitModData`).

### Damage, noise and feedback
- **Damage entry points** (pick the nearest real path so armour, pain, blood and sync come with it):
  `DamageFromWeapon`/`applyDamageFromWeapon`, `DamageFromAnimal` (claws and bites; it plays no pain voice and
  fires no damage event, per the CDDA note), `AddDamage`, `hitConsequences` (stagger and death presentation),
  `applyDamageFromVehicleHit`. Explosions and fire: `IsoFireManager.explode(cell, square, power)` (the vanilla
  challenge uses 100000) and `IsoFireManager.StartFire`.
- **Noise that zombies and animals hear** goes through `WorldSoundManager.instance:addSound(source, x, y, z,
  radius, volume, ...)` (six overloads), `addSoundRepeating`, `getSoundZomb`, `getSoundAnimal`. Creatures react
  through `RespondToSound` (zombies) and `respondToSound` (animals). This is separate from the audio players
  hear (below): a loud custom sound needs both.
- **Ballistics:** `BallisticsController` getters expose the live aim (`getMuzzlePosition`,
  `getMuzzleDirection`, `getTargets`, `getSpreadData`, `getTargetedBodyPart`). `zombie.core.physics.Bullet` wraps
  Bullet physics (`addRagdoll`, `applyImpulse`, constraint helpers); whether Lua can use it directly is unknown.
- **Visual feedback:** `ModelInstance` attachment sockets (`getAttachmentById`, `getAttachmentWorldPosition`,
  `setItemVisual`) and `dismember`; blood through `IsoGridSquare.splatBlood` and
  `VirtualZombieManager.AddBloodToMap`; overlay sprites on objects.

### The body simulation
`Nutrition` (`getCalories`/`setCalories`, carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, `getWeight`, `canAddFitnessXp`),
`Metabolics` (activity levels with `MetToW`, `getMet`), `Thermoregulator` (`getCoreTemperature`,
`getCoreHeatDelta`, `getBodyHeatMultiplier`, `getExternalAirTemperature`, `getCatchAColdDelta`), `Fitness`
(`exerciseRepeat`, `setCurrentExercise`, `incRegularity`, stiffness). Food, clothing warmth, wetness and wind
already feed these; a mod adds its own effects by reading them or writing the setters. Weight moves through
`Nutrition`, not `Stats`. Exercise definitions are Lua data in `shared/Definitions/FitnessExercises.lua`.
`MoodleType` (in `zombie.scripting.objects`, like `CharacterTrait`) has `register` and `get` in 42.21, so the older
"moodles are a fixed enum, fake them with a UI icon" advice may be out of date; whether a mod can register a
working moodle is untested. Body parts are still a fixed `BodyPartType` enum.

### AI and saves
- `zombie.ai`: every character owns a `StateMachine` over state classes in `zombie.ai.states` (about 90 public
  ones shared by players, zombies and animals: `PathFindState`, `AttackState`, `LungeState`,
  `ZombieHitReactionState`, `FakeDeadZombieState`, the climbing and grapple states ...). Paths come from
  `zombie.ai.astar.AStarPathFinder` (and the native `PZPathFind64`). `MapKnowledge` and `KnownBlockedEdges`
  remember blocked edges; `ZombieGroupManager` handles groups.
- What Lua can do: choose targets, issue paths, set locomotion, set animation variables and report events, and
  make noise. What it can't: add states, change path costs or edit the state machine. A "new behaviour" is a Lua
  controller choreographing existing states (the Cry of Fear and CDDA brains).
- `zombie.ai.sadisticAIDirector` holds `SleepingEvent`/`SleepingEventData`; the Lua
  `server/NPCs/SadisticAIDirector/SadisticMusicDirector.lua` picks music intensity from the visible and chasing
  zombie counts.
- Saves: `zombie.savefile` has `PlayerDB`, `ClientPlayerDB` and `ServerPlayerDB` (player data lives in a database,
  not loose files). Plain Lua globals don't survive a save; use ModData.
- `zombie.characters.ecs` (`ECSEntity`, `ECSComponent` and three lifecycle hooks) is a small scaffold; the
  component runtime mods use is `zombie.entity` (data note).

### The animator
- `char:getAdvancedAnimator()` returns an `AdvancedAnimator`: `setState`, `getCurrentStateName`,
  `containsState`, `setAnimSet`, `getRootLayer`/`getSubLayerAt`/`getSubLayerCount` (layers: an upper-body layer
  over locomotion, as in aiming while walking), `addAnimCallback`, `debugGetVariables`, `updateSpeedScale`,
  `Reload`.
- Variables are typed slots (bool, int, float, string, enum and callback variants in
  `zombie.core.skinnedmodel.advancedanimation`); animNode conditions read them. Clips fire named `AnimEvent`s
  (footsteps, hit frames); `BaseGrappleable` and `GrappleOffsetBehaviour` place grappling characters;
  `DeadBodyAtlas` renders corpses.
- Prefer driving variables and letting transitions run: `setState` fights the AI states.

### Audio (FMOD)
- `GameSound` is a named bank of clips (`getRandomClip`, `getCategory`, `isLooped`, `getUserVolume`);
  `GameSoundClip` has the FMOD event, volume, pitch, distances, `hasParameter`, `hasSustainPoints` and
  `checkReloaded`. Parameters are global (`FMODGlobalParameter`) or per instance (`FMODLocalParameter`).
- `FMODAmbientWalls`, `ObjectAmbientEmitters` (loops attached to world objects) and `TreeSoundManager` are the
  ambience layers; `SoundInstanceLimiter` with `SoundLimiterParams` caps concurrent clips (items opt in with
  `registerWithSoundLimiter`); `MusicIntensityConfig` and `MusicThreatConfig` drive dynamic music. Dedicated servers
  use `DummySoundBank`/`DummySoundEmitter`.

### Weather and climate
- `getClimateManager()`: `getClimateFloat`/`getClimateBool`/`getClimateColor` (typed channels from
  `ClimateValues`), `getAirTemperatureForSquare` and `getAirTemperatureForCharacter` (temperature varies by square),
  `getAirMass`, `getCloudIntensity`, fog and night colours (`getColFog`, `getColNight`), `getClimateForecaster`,
  `getClimateHistory`, `CopyClimateValues`, `execute_Simulation`, `forceDayInfoUpdate`, `getThunderStorm`.
- `ThunderStorm`: `startThunderCloud`, `stopAllClouds`, `triggerThunderEvent`, `applyLightningForPlayer`,
  `isModifyingNight`, and `readNetThunderEvent`/`writeNetThunderEvent` (thunder is synced in MP). Weather radio
  reports read the forecaster.

## Build steps
1. Before calling a method, find it here or with javap on the build you target; confirm it's public and on the
   class you hold (or a superclass).
2. Get argument names and types from the Umbrella stubs or the javadocs.
3. For behaviour, decompile with ZomboidDecompiler outside your repo and write down what you learn in your own
   words.
4. After a game update, re-run javap on the classes your mod uses and diff the method names.

## Verification
- Survey only: names from javap listings of 42.21.0, reading the install's Lua, and the Cry of Fear and CDDA mods'
  use of some of them. At review time every class and method name here was checked against the unofficial
  42.21.0 javadocs (public members only); names that weren't public there were removed or corrected.
- Not verified: calling any of this in game for this note; argument lists (use the stubs); which of these classes
  Kahlua exposes (`Bullet`, `BallisticsController`, `ModelManager`, the popman classes); the behaviour claims
  about the animator, audio and climate beyond what the names say.

## Gotchas
1. **`attempted index` on a Java object.** Cause: reading an instance field (`obj.field`, or
   `BaseAnimalBehavior.isDoingBehavior`). Fix: find the getter.
2. **The wrong overload runs.** Cause: Kahlua picks by argument count and type (`AddItem(String)` vs
   `AddItem(InventoryItem)`). Fix: pass exactly the types the overload you want takes.
3. **A javap name fails from Lua.** Cause: `javap -p` lists private and package-private members too, and some
   names in vanilla Lua are Lua functions, not Java (`getPlayerInfoPanel`). Fix: list without `-p`, or check the
   javadocs.
4. **`attempted to call nil` on `IsoGridSquare:Is`.** Cause: 42.21 renamed it (`has`, `hasWater`). Fix: re-check
   names on every build (CDDA note gotcha 11).
5. **`BodyDamage` can't be found as an inner class.** Cause: `zombie.characters.BodyDamage.BodyDamage` is the class
   `BodyDamage` in the package `zombie.characters.BodyDamage`. Fix: use that full name with javap; from Lua,
   `player:getBodyDamage()`.
6. **Your change never reaches MP clients.** Cause: a plain setter on the server. Fix: the `transmit*`/`sync*`
   verbs (multiplayer note).
7. **`getGridSquare` returns nil.** Cause: the square isn't loaded. Fix: work with `IsoMetaGrid` zones and build when
   the square loads.
8. **A container won't refill.** Cause: it's marked explored. `setExplored(false)` makes it lootable again; state
   flags like this exist on many classes, so search the listing before deciding something is impossible.
9. **A custom creature makes no sound for zombies.** Cause: it only played audio. Fix: also
   `WorldSoundManager.instance:addSound(...)`.
10. **Forced animator states flicker.** Cause: `setState` against the state machine. Fix: drive variables.
11. **A loop keeps playing after its object unloads.** Cause: emitters need an explicit stop. Fix: stop loops on
    unload and on identity changes.
12. **A climate write snaps back.** Cause: the air-mass simulation keeps running. Fix: write the values, then step
    the simulation, and on a server send `transmitWeather`.
13. **Server code waits on a sound.** Cause: dedicated servers use dummy sound banks. Fix: never gate gameplay on
    audio.

## Assets
None.

Part of one research session on 2026-10-12.

- The full `ClimateValues` channel list (the debug weather window shows it) and whether the forecaster is seeded per

# Build 42 modding orientation: mod anatomy, the Lua runtime, tooling, interop and the ISUI framework

> Where to start on Project Zomboid Build 42: what goes where in a mod, how the Lua (Kahlua) runtime loads and
> calls into Java, the debug and test loop, how mods expose APIs to each other and patch each other, and the
> vanilla ISUI widget library. It's a survey of a 42.21.0 install (its `media/` tree and Lua, javap listings)
> and of other people's mods; nothing here was built and run in game. Five companion notes go deeper:
> [data](b42-data-scripts-entities-skills-traits-media-files.md),
> [creatures](b42-creatures-dressed-zombies-ports-and-npc-frameworks.md),
> [Java surface](b42-java-surface-lua-callable-api-and-engine-internals.md),
> [multiplayer](b42-multiplayer-internals-packets-gameserver-sync.md) and
> [world](b42-world-loot-stories-zones-tiles-maps-worldgen.md).

## Setup
- Project Zomboid **42.21.0** from Steam (app 108600), Windows 10. Install: `projectzomboid.jar` (all game code,
  unobfuscated Java), `jre64\`, `media\` (all vanilla data and Lua, readable: the reference for every format),
  `Workshop\ModTemplate\` (the official upload template, including a two-map example), `mods\`.
- Already covered on main, so not repeated here:
  - the B42 mod layout (`mods/<id>/42/{mod.info, poster.png, media/...}` plus `common/`), the `mod.info` keys and
    the sandbox-option format: [CDDA ants note](cdda-enemy-pack-ants-custom-hostile-animals-a-breeding-colon.md),
    Setup and "Other mod.info / sandbox facts";
  - how the game picks one numbered version folder plus `common/`, the user-data folders (`console.txt`, `Logs`,
    `Saves`, `Lua\pz_modlist_settings.cfg`), Workshop download paths and `require=`:
    [42.20 modlist note](b42-20-modlist-preset-and-world-load-errors.md);
  - the javap command line and the reflection lister for checking what Lua can call: the CDDA note's Setup.
- No loader to install: the game is the mod loader. The `-debug` launch option turns on the debug menus.

## Route and why
Loader API. PZ mods are data plus Lua that the game loads natively; there is no BepInEx-style loader and none is
needed. The jar is unobfuscated, so bytecode patching is possible, but it can't be shipped on the Workshop and the
mods surveyed here never needed it.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Mod anatomy additions
- `mod.info` keys seen beyond those in the CDDA note: repeatable `description=` lines, `icon=`, `versionMin`,
  `map=` (map mods, see the world note). Keep the file name lowercase `mod.info` for Linux servers.
- **Lua and other files override by relative path.** A mod file at the same path as a vanilla file
  (`media/lua/shared/...`, `media/AnimSets/...`, `media/scripts/...`) replaces it, and between two mods the
  later one wins. Put your files in a subfolder named after the mod (`media/lua/shared/MyMod/...`).
- What each `media/` folder holds:

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `lua/{shared,client,server}` | Lua; see "Load lifecycle" below |
| `scripts/` | `module X { ... }` block files: items, recipes, models, sounds, vehicles, entities (data note) |
| `models_X/`, `anims_X/` | meshes (`Skinned/` for rigged) and animation clips: `.x` (text DirectX), `.fbx`, `.glb` |
| `AnimSets/<entity>/<state>/*.xml`, `actiongroups/` | animation state graph (creatures note) |
| `clothing/clothingItems/*.xml`, `fileGuidTable.xml` | clothing definitions and the GUID registry every clothing XML needs |
| `textures/` | PNGs; `Item_<Name>.png` is the icon for `Icon = <Name>` |
| `texturepacks/*.pack` | tile sprite packs (format in the CDDA note) |
| `sound/`, `music/`, `videos/` | `.ogg`/`.wav` bound by `sound` script blocks; music; Bink video |
| `sandbox-options.txt` | sandbox options (format in the CDDA note) |
| `lua/shared/Translate/<LANG>/*.json` | translation keys (`IG_UI_`, `Sandbox_`, `Tooltip_`, `ItemName_`, `ContextMenu_` ...) |
| `maps/<MapName>/` | map mods (world note) |

### Load lifecycle
1. `shared/` runs first in every context, then `client/` (single player and MP clients) or `server/` (single
   player's internal server and dedicated servers). Single player runs both. `shared/` also runs at main-menu
   boot, before any world exists, so guard world code behind `OnLoad`/`OnGameStart` or a non-nil `getCell()`.
   (The [B41 note](b41-modpack-fix-mods-and-linux-dedicated-server.md) found `server/` files only load when a
   world starts.)
2. `require 'X'` resolves from the `media/lua/` roots, `shared/` first; keep one file per name.
3. Returning to the main menu and loading a save runs the Lua again. Register handlers once (guard with a flag)
   or they multiply.

### Calling Java from Lua
- Kahlua is a Java Lua close to 5.1. Lua calls **public methods** of exposed classes (`z:getHealth()`,
  `Class.staticMethod()`); it can't read an object's Java **fields** (`manager.choices` is nil). Find the
  getter. Singletons are reached through their static `instance` (`ScriptManager.instance`,
  `VirtualZombieManager.instance`), as vanilla Lua and the mods surveyed do.
- Useful globals: `getCell()`, `getWorld()`, `getPlayer()`, `getGameTime()`, `getScriptManager()`,
  `getSoundManager()`, `ZombRand`, `instanceof`, `Events`, `SandboxVars`, `ModData`, `getText`,
  `isClient()`/`isServer()`, `sendClientCommand`/`sendServerCommand`, `getActivatedMods()`,
  `getModFileReader`/`getModFileWriter`.
- Kahlua picks an overload by argument count and types; a wrong argument type can silently call the other
  overload (`ItemContainer.AddItem` has several).
- Names move between 42.x builds (`IsoGridSquare.Is` became `has` in 42.21; CDDA note gotcha 11). Check every
  `obj:method(` your mod calls against a javap or reflection dump of the build you target, and against the
  [Java-surface note](b42-java-surface-lua-callable-api-and-engine-internals.md).
- All vanilla Lua is readable under `media/lua/`, and `media/luaexamples/` has small timed-action, UI and
  `ISTimer` examples. Grep them before inventing an API.

### Events
`Events.<Name>.Add(fn)` / `.Remove(fn)`; the Umbrella stubs list every event with its arguments. The families a
mod uses most:
- boot and time: `OnGameBoot`, `OnGameStart`, `OnLoad`, `OnSave`, `OnInitWorld`, `OnTick`, `OnTickEvenPaused`,
  `EveryOneMinute`, `EveryHours`, `EveryDays`;
- world: `OnGridSquareLoaded`, `OnObjectAdded`, `OnWorldSound`, `OnDeadBodySpawn`, `OnSeeNewRoom`;
- characters: `OnZombieUpdate`, `OnZombieCreate`, `OnZombieDead`, `OnCharacterDeath`, `OnPlayerUpdate`,
  `OnPlayerGetDamage`, `OnWeaponHitCharacter`, `OnWeaponSwing`;
- menus: `OnFillWorldObjectContextMenu`, `OnFillInventoryObjectContextMenu`;
- network: `OnClientCommand` (fires on the server), `OnServerCommand` (fires on the client),
  `OnReceiveGlobalModData`; input and UI: `OnKeyPressed`, `OnCustomUIKey`, `OnCreateUI`, `OnResolutionChange`.

`OnZombieUpdate` fires for every zombie on every update: keep the handler O(1) and do heavy work on a staggered
think window (the CDDA ants use 15-tick windows).

### Timed actions, context menus, settings, persistence
- **Timed actions:** subclass `ISBaseTimedAction` (`media/lua/shared/TimedActions/` in B42; client-only ones such
  as reading stay in `client/TimedActions`), implement `isValid`, `update`, `start`, `stop`, `perform` (and
  `complete` for the authoritative effect, per the CDDA note), queue with
  `ISTimedActionQueue.add(MyAction:new(character, ...))`. Copy the nearest vanilla action rather than starting
  blank; script-side `timedAction` blocks declare the data.
- **Context menus:** `Events.OnFillWorldObjectContextMenu.Add(function(player, context, worldobjects, test) ...)`
  then `context:addOption(getText("ContextMenu_MyMod_DoThing"), target, MyMod.doThing, arg)`. When `test` is
  true the game only asks whether you would add options: change nothing. Vanilla reference:
  `ISWorldObjectContextMenu`.
- **Settings:** `PZAPI.ModOptions` (`media/lua/client/PZAPI/ModOptions.lua`) is the vanilla in-game mod-settings
  UI. `PZAPI.ModOptions:create(modID, name)` (as Bandits 42.20 calls it) returns an options object with
  `addTitle`, `addDescription`, `addTickBox`, `addComboBox`, `addTextEntry`, `addKeyBind` ..., read back by
  option id. Use it for per-player preferences and `sandbox-options.txt` for world settings that belong in the
  save.
- **Persistence:** `ModData.getOrCreate(key)` (global, plain data only) and `obj:getModData()` (per object,
  item or character). Neither syncs by itself in MP: see the multiplayer note.
- **Translations:** `getText("Key")` reads `Translate/<LANG>/*.json`; a missing key or an invalid JSON file shows
  the raw key.

### Tooling and the debug loop
- **Launch options:** `-debug` (debug menus, Lua debugger, animator and object inspectors, item spawner, cheat
  toggles such as god mode and no-clip), `-debuglog=<channels>` (filters `DebugLog` channels, names from the
  `zombie.debug.DebugType` enum), `-cachedir=<path>` (use a scratch profile so test saves and options don't touch
  the real one), `-nosteam`. `options.ini` in the profile sets windowed or full screen.
- **`zombie.debug`** (jar) holds the debug windows (`BaseDebugWindow` subclasses, including the animator window
  that shows a character's live AnimSet state and variables), `DebugOptions`/`BooleanDebugOption`, the `DebugLog`
  engine, `LineDrawer` (world-space debug lines) and `DebugCSVExport*` dumpers. These are developer tools, not a
  runtime API to build features on.
- **Reading a Lua error in `console.txt`:** stack frames name the mod file (`function: <name> -- file: <path>`)
  followed by the Kahlua error. `attempted index of nil` is usually a `.field` read or a nil getter result,
  `number expected, got table` a wrong argument type, and `se.krka.kahlua...` frames mark the Java boundary. A Lua
  error kills that call, not the game: a broken `OnZombieUpdate` handler just stops your creatures, so read the
  log after every test. `console.txt` is rewritten at each launch (copy it first) and holds every world load
  of that launch (CDDA note gotcha 18).
- **Iteration:** script, texture and sound changes load with the world; Lua changes need a return to the main menu
  and a reload of the save, not a restart. Keep one test save per feature and use debug spawns.
- **Scripted in-game checks:** launch windowed at a fixed size (`-debug -cachedir=<scratch> -width 1280 -height
  720`), drive the menus with `um win` (see the `game-automation` skill), let an `OnTick` test file spawn, check
  and print `[TEST] PASS/FAIL` lines, then parse `console.txt` and screenshot checkpoints. Kill the game by
  exact PID (`um win kill <pid>`).
- **Reading the code:** javap for "does it exist" and ZomboidDecompiler (Vineflower plus Rosetta parameter names)
  for "how does it work". Keep decompiled output outside any repo you publish and describe it in your own words.
  The official javadocs live at `projectzomboid.com/modding/`; the Umbrella stubs give IDE autocomplete for the
  whole API but can lag a new build, where javap is current.

### Interop between mods
- **Dependencies:** `require=` in `mod.info` is a hard dependency and its mods load first; the preset note covers
  how the load order follows the preset line. `id=` is the key others require; the folder name and the Workshop
  id are different strings.
- **A public API is a global table:** `MyMod = MyMod or {}` with functions in `shared/` is callable from every
  mod that loads later. Add `MyMod.API_VERSION` so dependents can feature-gate, and prefer registration hooks
  (`MyMod.registerThing(fn)`) over letting others wrap your functions.
- **Soft dependencies:** feature-detect (`if type(OtherMod) == "table" then ... end`) rather than checking
  `getActivatedMods()`, because mod ids differ between uploads. Do cross-mod registration late (`OnGameStart`)
  when every `shared/` file has run, and keep every touch of another mod's globals in one compat file per mod
  (ProjectALife ships a `Compat/` folder of such adapters, see the creatures note).
- **Global namespaces collide:** Lua file paths, script `module` names, ModData keys, outfit names, sound names,
  clothing GUIDs and sandbox option namespaces (`SandboxVars.MyMod.Option`) are all shared. Prefix every one.
- **Four shipped ways to build on another mod** (file inspection of the Workshop mods, 42.x):
  - *Content registered into a framework:* **BanditsWeekOne** (on the Bandits NPC framework) ships a
    `registries.lua` per version folder plus its own event scheduler (police, SWAT, medics, firefighters, hazmat
    call-outs with per-service on/cooldown knobs) and three broadcast networks (`media/sound/Broadcasts/...`
    plus a generated sound table) that tell the outbreak through radio and TV.
  - *Wrapping another mod's functions:* **BeyondOneWeek** patches BanditsWeekOne by prepending gates to its
    global functions (`FDUtils.PrependFunction(BWOEvents.CallHazmats, chanceFunc)`) or replacing one wholesale,
    in a file whose banner says it overrides BWO functions. Wrap rather than copy, so updates of the host still
    flow through; label every override file; tune through `SandboxVars`.
  - *A bridge between two frameworks:* **CDALifePatch** (no assets) translates one mod's relation vocabulary into
    another's, detects the other mod's actors by a ModData flag behind `hasModData()` guards and `pcall`, and
    returns an explicit "unknown" stance instead of guessing.
  - *A custom data format:* **ALifeKnoxFractured** ships `.alife` text files that its framework parses after
    reading them with `getModFileReader(modID, relativePath, false)`, and registers the records additively ("no
    base records replaced"). Any mod can ship its own file format this way.

### The ISUI framework (`media/lua/client/ISUI/`, about 140 files)
- A retained-mode widget library: `ISUIElement` (base), `ISPanel`, `ISCollapsableWindow`, `ISButton`,
  `ISTickBox`, `ISComboBox`, `ISTextEntryBox`, `ISScrollingListBox`, `ISTabPanel`, `ISRichTextPanel`,
  `ISModalDialog`, progress bars, colour pickers, `ISRadialMenu` and its variants, `ISUI3DModel` (a live 3D
  model in a panel, as in character creation), and the XUI skin/layout classes (`ISXuiBuilder`, `ISXuiSkin`,
  `ISXuiTableLayout`). Feature windows worth copying: the inventory pages, `ISTradingUI`,
  `ISFluidContainerMenu`, `ISDesignationZonePanel`, the map windows.
- A custom window: `MyWin = ISCollapsableWindow:derive("MyWin")`, `initialise()` calling the parent's,
  `createChildren()` adding widgets with `self:addChild`, then `addToUIManager()`; toggle with `setVisible`. Lay
  out in pixels (anchor to `getCore():getScreenWidth()/getScreenHeight()` on resolution change) or with the XUI
  layout classes. Controller support is a separate code path (`ISPanelJoypad` and the other `Joypad` classes).
- World-space drawing: `ISCoordConversion.ToScreen/ToWorld` with `getRenderer()` (vanilla
  `ISBuildingBlueprintManager` is the example) and the UI draw events. Input: `shared/keyBinding.lua` (bindable
  keys), `Events.OnKeyPressed`, and `media/gamecontrollerdb.txt` (SDL pad mappings).

## Build steps
1. `Zomboid/mods/<id>/42/mod.info` plus `media/` (layout in the CDDA note); enable it in the Mods screen.
2. Lua in `media/lua/{shared,client,server}/MyMod/`: definitions and guarded event registration in `shared/`, UI
   and context menus in `client/`, world changes and spawning in `server/`.
3. Data (items, recipes, models, sounds) as `media/scripts/*.txt` blocks: see the data note.
4. Settings: `sandbox-options.txt` plus `Translate/EN/Sandbox.json` for the world, `PZAPI.ModOptions` for player
   preferences.
5. Test with `-debug`, read `console.txt` after every session, script the repeatable checks.
6. Publish from `Zomboid/Workshop/<id>/` (layout in the CDDA note's Build steps and the B41 note):
   `workshop.txt` takes `version=1`, `title`, repeatable `description=` lines, `tags` (allowed values in the
   install's `media/WorkshopTags.txt`) and `visibility`; `preview.png` is 256x256. Upload from the main menu's
   Workshop entry; uploading again from the same folder updates the item.

## Verification
- Survey only. Read on 42.21.0: the `media/` tree and Lua cited above (`ISUI/`, `PZAPI/ModOptions.lua`,
  `TimedActions/`, `luaexamples/`, `WorkshopTags.txt`, `Workshop/ModTemplate`), javap listings of the
  `zombie.debug` package, and the files of BanditsWeekOne, BeyondOneWeek, CDALifePatch and ALifeKnoxFractured.
- At review time the Java names in this note were checked against the unofficial 42.21.0 javadocs
  (albion.codeberg.page/PZ-JavaDocs).
- Not verified: anything in game. That includes the scripted-test loop, building a window, `PZAPI.ModOptions`
  calls (copy them from the vanilla file), every event's exact arguments on 42.21 (use the Umbrella stubs), and
  the load order of mods that don't depend on each other.

## Gotchas
1. **`attempted index ... of non-table: null` on a Java object.** Cause: reading a Java field (`obj.someField`);
   Lua only sees public methods. Fix: find the getter or another exposed path.
2. **A handler runs two or more times.** Cause: the Lua runs again when a save is reloaded and `Events.X.Add`
   wasn't guarded. Fix: `if MyMod._registered then return end MyMod._registered = true`.
3. **`getCell()` is nil in a `shared/` file.** Cause: shared Lua also runs at main-menu boot. Fix: touch the
   world from `OnLoad`, `OnGameStart` or later.
4. **A vanilla feature broke after adding a mod file.** Cause: a generic file name at a vanilla path replaced the
   vanilla file (Lua, AnimSets, scripts). Fix: mod-named subfolders and file names.
5. **Another mod's file silently "doesn't run".** Cause: two mods ship the same relative path; the later one wins
   with no warning. Fix: namespace your paths; check other mods' paths when two conflict.
6. **The mod doesn't load at all.** Cause: `mod.info` only in `common/`, a version folder the build doesn't pick
   (preset note), or a hidden `.txt` extension on `mod.info`. Fix: `42/mod.info`, file extensions shown.
7. **A context-menu option changes things while the menu is only being built.** Cause: work done while `test` is
   true. Fix: return early when `test` is true.
8. **Arguments vanish in `sendClientCommand`.** Cause: only plain data crosses (numbers, strings, booleans, plain
   tables). Fix: send `getOnlineID()` or coordinates and look the object up on the other side.
9. **`getText` shows the key.** Cause: a missing key, an invalid JSON file, or a folder not named exactly
   `Translate`. Fix: validate the JSON; match the key exactly.
10. **A tick or zombie-update handler silently stops.** Cause: a Lua error ends that call every time it fires.
    Fix: read `console.txt` after every test; wrap risky think functions in `pcall` and log.
11. **Behaviour differs without `-debug`.** Cause: debug options and cheats (god mode, invisible) change what
    the AI does. Fix: do the final check of a feature without `-debug`.
12. **Your `print` lines are missing.** Cause: a `-debuglog=` filter that hides the channel `print` uses.
    Fix: test without the filter, prefix your lines (`MyMod[topic]`) and grep.
13. **The window never appears.** Cause: no `addToUIManager()`. A window re-created every frame flickers and leaks
    instead: create once, then `setVisible`.
14. **An `ISUI3DModel` panel stays empty.** Cause: it renders through the same model scripts as the world, and a
    bad model script fails silently. Fix: test the model in the world first.
15. **UI code errors on a dedicated server.** Cause: ISUI is client-only and a dedicated server has no renderer.
    Fix: keep UI in `client/` and guard shared code with `isClient()`.
16. **A wrapper around another mod's function does nothing.** Cause: it ran before that mod's `shared/` file
    defined the function. Fix: `require=` the host mod or wrap late (`OnGameStart`).
17. **Two content packs register the same records twice after a reload.** Cause: a non-idempotent bootstrap.
    Fix: a `Pack.installed` style guard (ALifeKnoxFractured).
18. **Removing a mod mid-save leaves its data behind.** Cause: ModData, spawned objects and registrations persist.
    Fix: document a clean-removal path.
19. Also on main: `%` in sandbox labels breaks the options screen (CDDA note gotcha 7), and an offline Lua 5.3+
    harness lacks `math.atan2` (CDDA note gotcha 19).

## Assets
- Icons: `Item_<Name>.png` in `media/textures/`. 3D: `.glb` for new work; import vanilla `.x` with the "DirectX X
  Importer" Blender extension or ZomboidAssetConverter (more in the creatures note).
- Audio: `.ogg` Vorbis or `.wav`, bound by `sound` script blocks (data note). The CDDA note has a full generated
  asset pipeline.

## Cost and time
Part of one research session (about half a day for this layer), on 2026-10-12.

## Open questions
- Whether `PZAPI.ModOptions` covers every widget vanilla panels use, and whether `client/PZAPI` loads on a
  dedicated server (probably not; keep it in `client/`).
- The load order of independent mods (no `require=` between them) beyond the preset line.
- The full `DebugType` channel list for `-debuglog=` on 42.21, and whether a mod can add its own debug window by
  subclassing `BaseDebugWindow`.

# Build 42 multiplayer for modders: commands, sync verbs, ownership, anti-cheat and the packet layer

> Since 42.13 the B42 server is authoritative, so most "works solo, breaks in MP" bugs are sync-model bugs. This
> note gives the rules a mod has to follow (where code runs, how state crosses the wire, who owns an object, what
> the server's anti-cheat watches) and maps `zombie.network` and `zombie.popman` behind them. It's a survey of
> javap listings, the install's Lua and other mods' files; no server was run for it. Single-player basics are in
> the [orientation note](b42-modding-orientation-layout-lua-runtime-tooling-interop-ui.md); a modded B41
> dedicated server (`Mods=`, `WorkshopItems=`, `Map=`, checksums) is in the
> [B41 note](b41-modpack-fix-mods-and-linux-dedicated-server.md).

## Setup
- Project Zomboid **42.21.0**, Steam, Windows 10; the dedicated server is Steam app 380870. Multiplayer returned to
  B42 in 42.13 (December 2025).
- Vanilla references: `media/lua/client/ServerCommands.lua` and the server-side command tables, plus Cry of Fear
  Monsters' network split (creatures note).

## Route and why
Loader API. The network layer is Java, but mods reach it through Lua commands and the engine's `transmit*`/`sync*`
verbs; mods can't add packet types.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Where code runs
- `shared/` runs everywhere; `client/` on single player and MP clients; `server/` on single player and the server.
  A dedicated server never runs `client/` (no UI, no renderer), and an MP client never runs `server/`.
- Change world state on the server (`server/` files, or shared code behind `isServer()`); keep presentation (UI,
  sounds, particles, animation variables a client reads locally) on clients.

### Commands: the mod-level wire
- **Client to server:** `sendClientCommand(module, command, args)` (Lua global; Java `GameClient`). The server
  receives it with `Events.OnClientCommand.Add(function(module, command, player, args) ... end)`.
- **Server to client:** `sendServerCommand(module, command, args)` to everyone or
  `sendServerCommand(player, module, command, args)` to one player (Java `GameServer`). Clients receive it on
  `Events.OnServerCommand`.
- `args` must be plain data (numbers, strings, booleans, nested plain tables). Send `getOnlineID()` or coordinates
  and look objects up again on the other side.
- **Global mod data:** `ModData.transmit(key)` sends a table, `ModData.request(key)` asks the server for it, and
  `Events.OnReceiveGlobalModData` receives it (the table can be `false` in a reply to a request). Keep authoritative
  data on the server; a client's copy isn't kept across reconnects.

### Transmit and sync verbs: the engine-level wire
- Squares: `sq:transmitAddObjectToSquare(obj)`, `sq:transmitRemoveItemFromSquare(obj)`, `sq:transmitModdata()`.
- Objects: `obj:transmitModData()` (capital D on `IsoObject`), `obj:sync()`, `syncIsoObject`, the fluid-container
  sync. Also `transmitPlayerVoiceSound`, and `getWorld():transmitWeather()` after a server-side weather change.
- A plain setter on the server changes the server's world silently; clients don't see it. Damage applied on the
  server should be followed by a `sendServerCommand` for the presentation (the Cry of Fear pattern).

### Ownership and remote objects
- `isRemoteZombie()`, `getOwnerPlayer()`, `getOwner()` and `getOnlineID()` say who drives a zombie. A remote zombie
  is a view of another client's simulation: changing it locally ghosts the state. Bandits only lets the owning
  client steer (`BanditUtils.IsController`).
- `zombie.popman` is the population layer behind this: `ZombiePopulationManager`, `NetworkZombieManager`,
  `NetworkZombieSimulator`, `NetworkZombiePacker`, `ZombieCountOptimiser`, `Ownership`, `LoadedAreas`, and
  `popman.animal.AnimalController`. It's Java-internal; mods reach it through `VirtualZombieManager` and the
  population sandbox settings. A zombie you see may be simulated by another client, so identity must live on the
  object itself (a persistent outfit), never in a client-side table.

### Server anti-cheat
`zombie.network.anticheats` has about 20 check classes (`AntiCheatSpeed`, `AntiCheatNoClip`,
`AntiCheatHitDamage`, `AntiCheatHitLongDistance`, `AntiCheatXPUpdate`, `AntiCheatSafeHouseMember`, ...) plus
`PacketValidator` and `SuspiciousActivity`, and `ServerOptions` has matching switches (`antiCheatSpeed`,
`antiCheatNoClip`, `antiCheatHit`, `antiCheatXp`, `antiCheatChecksum`, `antiCheatSafeHouse`, ...). A mod that
moves players, deals damage or grants XP on a client instead of the server can trip them. `ChunkChecksum`
compares client and server chunks, and `AddWarningPointPacket` exists: client-side world edits look like cheating.

### The packet layer (`zombie.network`)
- `GameServer` and `GameClient` are the two endpoints; `ServerOptions`/`ServerSettings`;
  `GameServerWorkshopItems` syncs Workshop items to clients.
- `zombie.network.packets` has one class per action (272 public types in the 42.21 javadocs, 112 in the top
  package; the jar holds 296 `.class` files counting inner classes): `AddItemToMapPacket`,
  `AddExplosiveTrapPacket`, `AddXPMultiplierPacket`, `BodyDamageUpdatePacket`, `AddWarningPointPacket` ... A mod
  doesn't create packets; it calls the API whose packet already exists, or uses commands.
- Hosting from the game client runs an in-process server (`CoopMaster`/`CoopSlave`). Chunk sync and integrity:
  `ClientChunkRequest`, `ChunkChecksum`, `ClientServerMap`. Other classes in the package: `FakeClientManager`
  (fake clients for load tests), `BodyDamageSync`, `BanSystem`, and `DiscordBot`/`DiscordSender` (server messages to
  Discord); none of these were tried.

## Build steps
1. Spawn creatures and change the world only on the server (`createRealZombieNow`, `addAnimal`, object adds); never
   on a client, or you get duplicates or phantoms.
2. Brains that change damage, aggro or spawns run on the server; clients present (sounds, particles, the animation
   variables their AnimSets read).
3. Identity crosses the wire once: the server says "this zombie is monster X", each client sets its variables and
   visuals locally (Cry of Fear's remote presentation). Don't push Lua state every tick.
4. Use commands for your own messages and the `transmit*`/`sync*` verbs for stock object changes.
5. Test with co-op hosting from the client plus a second client, or the dedicated server on the same machine; read
   `console.txt` on each side.

## Verification
- Survey only. Class names from javap listings of 42.21.0, checked at review time against the unofficial 42.21.0
  javadocs (public types only); the command directions and Lua signatures from `LuaManager.GlobalObject`,
  `GameClient` and `GameServer` there. The patterns from reading Cry of Fear Monsters and Bandits.
- Not verified: anything on a running server, `FakeClientManager` or `DiscordBot` use from a mod, Workshop sync
  edge cases, B42 dedicated-server start flags.

## Gotchas
1. **"Module not found" only on a server.** Cause: a table the server needs lives in `client/` (or the reverse).
   Fix: shared tables in `shared/`.
2. **A spawn works in single player and does nothing (or duplicates) in MP.** Cause: client-side spawning. Fix:
   spawn on the server.
3. **A command's arguments arrive empty.** Cause: Java objects, functions or userdata in `args`. Fix: plain data.
4. **A remote zombie ignores your changes or flickers.** Cause: `isRemoteZombie()` is true; another client owns it.
   Fix: change it through the owner or the server.
5. **Square ModData syncs but object ModData doesn't.** Cause: `IsoGridSquare.transmitModdata` covers the square.
   Fix: `IsoObject.transmitModData()`, `obj:sync()` or your own command.
6. **Players get flagged or kicked after a mod action.** Cause: B42's server anti-cheat (`zombie.network.anticheats`,
   `ServerOptions` `antiCheat*`) saw a client-side move, hit or XP change, or chunks diverged. Fix: do it on the
   server.
7. **Client code silently does nothing on a dedicated server.** Cause: `client/` isn't loaded there. Fix: log once
   from `shared/` with `isServer()`/`isClient()` so you know where each file ran.
8. **The server errors in UI or render code.** Cause: a dedicated server has no renderer. Fix: keep that code in
   `client/`.
9. **Weather or thunder differs between players.** Cause: changed on one side. Fix: change it on the server and
   `transmitWeather()`; thunder events are written by the server and read by clients.

## Assets
None.

## Cost and time
Part of one research session on 2026-10-12.

- B42 dedicated-server start flags for headless testing, and how B42 Workshop sync differs from the B41 note.
- Whether animals are virtualised like zombies (`popman.animal.AnimalController`).

# The Build 42 world for modders: loot, stories, zones, world systems, tiles, maps and worldgen

> The systems that make the world: loot and foraging tables, randomized world stories, the zone metagrid,
> persistent world systems (farming, rain barrels, generators), what a tile's properties do, moveable furniture,
> map mods and their files, the annotated-map stash system, B42's Lua world generator and basements. Most of it is
> Lua tables or text files a mod extends. It's a survey of a 42.21.0 install; nothing was built and run in game.
> Start with the [orientation note](b42-modding-orientation-layout-lua-runtime-tooling-interop-ui.md).

## Setup
- Project Zomboid **42.21.0**, Steam, Windows 10. The systems live in `<install>/media/lua/{server,shared,client}/`
  (readable), `media/maps/`, `media/*.txt`, and the jar's `zombie.iso`, `zombie.randomizedWorld`,
  `zombie.iso.worldgen`, `zombie.basements` and `zombie.erosion` packages.
- On main already: how `ProceduralDistributions` lists work, `Events.OnPreDistributionMerge` as the moment to edit
  them, and that loot is rolled when a container is first generated
  ([B41 note](b41-modpack-fix-mods-and-linux-dedicated-server.md)); cells of 256x256 squares, `getZonesAt` on
  unloaded areas, and the `.pack`/`.tiles` formats for custom tiles
  ([CDDA ants note](cdda-enemy-pack-ants-custom-hostile-animals-a-breeding-colon.md)).

## Route and why
Loader API: data tables, text files and exposed Java calls. For internals that aren't exposed, decompile and
describe; never ship patched classes.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Loot
- `media/lua/server/Items/Distributions.lua` (with `SuburbsDistributions.lua` and the junk files) maps room types
  and container types to item lists; `ProceduralDistributions.list` holds the named tables containers reference.
- `ItemPickerJava.getLootModifier(item)` is the rarity modifier, and the `RemoveStoryLoot` sandbox option filters
  story clutter. `ScriptManager.instance:FindItem("Base.X")` checks an item id; use it at boot to log bad ids in
  your entries, because a typo just never spawns.

### Foraging (`media/lua/shared/Foraging/`)
A complete data system; `forageDefinitions.lua` documents every field inline.
- Item definitions: `type`, `minCount`/`maxCount`, `skill` and `perks`, `xp`, visibility gates (`recipes`,
  `traits`, `itemTags`), `categories`, weather and time chances (`rainChance`, `snowChance`, `dayChance`,
  `nightChance`), `zones = { Forest = n, DeepForest = n, ... }` where **n is a roll count, not a percent**,
  months (`months`, `bonusMonths`, `malusMonths`), `spawnFuncs`, placement flags, poison fields.
- Zone definitions: zone type, icon density, `refillPercent` per day, `abundanceSetting` (the `NatureAbundance`
  sandbox key) and `containsBiomes`. Category definitions: roll `chance`, the perk that identifies the category,
  floor rules, search-focus chances.
- Zone state lives in the `"forageData"` ModData. New forageables = an item definition, optionally a category.

### Randomized world stories
`zombie.randomizedWorld` (Java) with `server/RandomizedWorldContent/StoryTable_Initialization.lua` and
`StoryClutter/`: boarded houses, corpses with loot, burnt houses, crashed cars and table settings, attached to
rooms and roads at world generation. `RandomizedWorldBase` subclasses are offered candidate rooms by room type and
zone; clutter goes through `StoryTables.addItemToClutterTable`, which validates ids and applies the sandbox
blacklist. A new story *class* needs Java; loot-only stories are Lua tables. Stories only exist where the world
is generated after the mod was added.

### Zones (the metagrid)
- `getWorld():getMetaGrid()` is the zone registry and works for unloaded areas. Registration calls used by
  `server/metazones/metazoneHandler.lua` with map-provided data:
  `getWorld():getMetaGrid():registerAnimalZone(name, type, x, y, z, w, h, properties)` (it's on `IsoMetaGrid`,
  not `IsoWorld`), `registerGeometryZone(name, type, z, geometry, points, properties)` (polygons, also on
  `IsoMetaGrid`), and `getWorld():registerMannequinZone(...)`, `registerRoomTone(...)`, `registerWaterZone`,
  `registerWaterFlow`, `registerVehiclesZone`, `registerSpawnOrigin`.
- `AnimalsPathConfig.lua` and `BiomeMapConfig.lua` show habitats as zones with property maps; a custom creature can
  get natural habitats the same way.

### Persistent world systems
- **The pattern:** a server-side `SGlobalObjectSystem` (state, save and load, MP sync; Lua in
  `server/Map/SGlobalObjectSystem.lua`, Java in `zombie.globalObjects`), a client twin `CGlobalObjectSystem`
  (`client/Map/`), a context-menu entry and a timed action for the long verb. Rain barrels
  (`client/RainBarrel/CRainBarrelSystem.lua`), farming (`client/Farming/CFarmingSystem.lua`) and generators are
  built this way; the rain barrel is the smallest complete example to copy. Register both halves by the same name.
- Other loops: fishing (`client/Fishing/`: manager, handler, states), traps (items, trap objects,
  `AddExplosiveTrapPacket` in MP), fire (`IsoFireManager`). Prefer an `entity` with stock components when one
  fits (data note).

### Tiles, objects and moveables
- Every tile in a `.tiles` file has a property set; the install's readable `.tiles.txt` sidecars (such as
  `newtiledefinitions.tiles.txt`) show which properties vanilla uses: `container = <type>` (makes the tile a loot
  container of that type), `Door`, `doorN`/`doorW`, `WallN`/`WallW`, `solid`/`solidtrans`, `collideN`/`collideW`,
  `floor`, `water`, `bed`, `sittable`, `Table`, `Material`/`MaterialType` (hit sounds and scrap), `CanScrap`,
  `BlocksPlacement`, `Facing`, `FloorHeight`, `stair`, `tree`, `bush`. Unknown keys are ignored: copy names from
  the sidecar.
- Object classes on squares (`zombie.iso.objects`): `IsoDoor`, `IsoWindow`, `IsoCurtain`, `IsoBarricade`,
  `IsoThumpable`, `IsoGenerator`, `IsoStove`, `IsoFireplace`, `IsoCompost`, `IsoMannequin`,
  `IsoWorldInventoryObject` (items on the ground), `IsoLightSource`, `IsoJukebox`, `IsoDeadBody`, `IsoFire`,
  `IsoTrap`, `IsoWaveSignal` (radios and TVs), `IsoCarBatteryCharger`. Place a plain object with
  `IsoObject.new(cell, square, spriteName)` and `square:AddTileObject(obj)` (CDDA note).
- **Moveables:** `shared/Moveables/ISMoveableDefinitions.lua` and `ISMoveableSpriteProps.lua` decide which sprites
  can be picked up, with which tool and skill, the break chance and the resulting item; `ISMoveablesAction` is the
  timed action. Custom carryable furniture = entries for your sprites plus the tile properties.
- **Without TileZed:** `media/spriteModels.txt` puts a 3D `model` on a tile sprite (`tileset { name, tile { xy,
  modelScript, translate, rotate, scale } }`); `media/seating.txt` gives furniture tiles seat anchors per direction.
  A chair needs both the `sittable` property and a seating entry. Wall cutaways use the shared mask PNGs
  (`wallcutaways.png`, `mask_transparency_*.png`).

### Map mods and map files
- `media/maps/<MapName>/` with `map.info` (`title`, `description`, `lots = Muldraugh, KY` to stitch the map onto
  the world), `spawnpoints.lua`, `thumb.png`, and the binary cells. `mod.info` names the map with `map=` and its
  tilesets with `tiledef=`/`pack=`.
- A B42 town folder (`media/maps/Muldraugh, KY`) is a grid of `<x>_<y>.lotheader` and `chunkdata_<x>_<y>.bin` pairs,
  one pair per 256x256 cell, plus `WorldGenOverride.lua` (worldgen settings for the wilderness around that town),
  `basements.lua` and `objects.lua`. Missing either half of a pair corrupts the cell.
- Map mods replace whole cells; there are no partial-cell edits, and two mods replacing the same cell can't both
  win. Build maps with the community TileZed/WorldEd forks (B42 builds of the official tools weren't out at
  research time); `IsoChunk`, `IsoChunkLevel`, `ChunkSaveWorker` and `LotHeader` read the binaries.
- **The in-game map:** `client/ISUI/Maps/` (`ISWorldMap`, `ISMiniMap`, `ISMapSymbols`, a world-map `Editor/`);
  `MapSymbolDefinitions.getInstance():addTexture(name, texturePath, category)` registers stamps (categories
  Symbols, Loot, Locations; register at `OnGameBoot`). `zombie.worldMap` stores symbols on map items.
- **Annotated-map stashes:** `shared/StashDescriptions/*StashDesc.lua` with `StashUtil.lua`. In the vanilla shape
  (values made up):
```lua
local s = StashUtil.newStash("MyModStash1", "Map", "Base.MuldraughMap", "Stash_AnnotedMap")
s.spawnOnlyOnZed = true
s.buildingX, s.buildingY = 10000, 9000           -- the target building, in world coordinates
s.spawnTable = "MyModCache"                      -- the loot table for the placed container
s:addContainer("GunBox", "mymod_tiles_01_0", nil, "livingroom")
s:addStamp("X", nil, 9998, 8999, 1, 0, 0)        -- a symbol (or nil and a text key)
```
  A stash can also spawn zombies, traps and barricades at the target. `StashDebug.lua` shows them in `-debug`.

### Worldgen and basements
- `server/WorldGen/` (`Biomes.lua`, `Features.lua`, `Roads.lua`, `Veins.lua`, `Selection.lua`, `biomes/`,
  `features/`, `prefabs/`) fills a global `worldgen` table that `zombie.iso.worldgen` consumes (`WorldGenReader`,
  `WorldGenParams`, `WorldGenChunk`, `WorldGenSimplexGenerator`, `PrefabStructure`, `StaticModule`, and
  sub-packages `biomes`, `roads`, `rules`, `veins`, `zones`, `blending`, `attachments`). Vanilla wilderness is
  generated around the authored cells; a map mod can ship its own `WorldGenOverride.lua`. The table schema is
  only documented by the Lua files themselves.
- Basements: `Basements.getAPIv1()` (Lua) has `registerBasementSpawnLocation(mapID, name, type, x, y, z, w, h,
  properties)`. Prefab pieces are `media/basement_access/*.pzby`, a binary format (header `PZBY`, a tileset-name
  string table, then tile records); the runtime is `zombie.basements`.
- Seasons and overgrowth: `zombie.erosion` (`ErosionMain`) with `client/erosion/`; erosion tiles come from
  `media/tiledefinitions_erosion.tiles`, so a modded tile only takes part if it carries the matching properties.

## Build steps
1. Loot: append to the lists from a shared or server Lua file before containers are generated (the B41 note
   edits and removes entries in `Events.OnPreDistributionMerge`), and validate every id with
   `ScriptManager.instance:FindItem`. Forageables: an item definition in a shared file.
2. A persistent device: copy the rain-barrel `SGlobalObjectSystem`/`CGlobalObjectSystem` pair.
3. An interactive tile: the property set in your `.tiles`, a `seating.txt` or `spriteModels.txt` entry where needed,
   moveable definitions to make it carryable.
4. A map: TileZed/WorldEd cells into `media/maps/<name>/`, `map.info` with `lots =`, `spawnpoints.lua`, and
   `map=` in `mod.info`.
5. A treasure map: `StashUtil.newStash` in a shared file, symbol textures through `MapSymbolDefinitions`.
6. Zones: register on the server at world init; query anywhere with `getZonesAt`.

## Verification
- Survey only. Read on 42.21.0: the Lua and data files cited (distributions, foraging, story tables,
  `metazoneHandler.lua`, the global-object systems, moveables, stash files, `spriteModels.txt`, `seating.txt`,
  the Muldraugh map folder, `server/WorldGen/`), plus javap listings of the packages named. At review time the
  Java names were checked against the unofficial 42.21.0 javadocs (albion.codeberg.page/PZ-JavaDocs).
- Not verified: anything in game, custom worldgen prefabs, the full `Basements` API, hand-written map binaries,
  exporting annotations from the map editor, a dedicated server.

## Gotchas
1. **A loot entry never spawns.** Cause: a typo in the item id; vanilla only logs it. Fix: check ids with
   `FindItem` at boot and print the failures yourself.
2. **Foraged items far too common.** Cause: a zone value read as a percent; it's a roll count. Fix: compare with
   vanilla values.
3. **A story mod doesn't appear in an old save.** Cause: stories are placed when the world is generated. Fix: test
   in a new world or unexplored areas.
4. **Story items disappear with `RemoveStoryLoot`.** Cause: clutter goes through the sandbox blacklist. Fix: check
   `ItemPickerJava.getLootModifier` for your items.
5. **`registerAnimalZone` "doesn't exist" on `getWorld()`.** Cause: it's an `IsoMetaGrid` method. Fix:
   `getWorld():getMetaGrid():registerAnimalZone(...)`.
6. **A global-object device works in single player only.** Cause: only one half (server or client system) was
   registered. Fix: register both, paired by name.
7. **A stove that isn't a container, a chair you can't sit on.** Cause: a misspelled property (ignored silently),
   or a missing `seating.txt` anchor. Fix: copy property names from the sidecar; add both halves for seats.
8. **Picked-up custom furniture breaks.** Cause: the moveable `breakChance` rolls on pickup. Fix: set it (and the
   skill gate) deliberately.
9. **A map mod stands alone instead of joining Knox Country.** Cause: no `lots = ...` in `map.info`. Fix: add it.
10. **Two map mods fight over a cell.** Cause: cells are replaced whole. Fix: list the cells you replace in the
    mod description.
11. **The X lands on the neighbour's house.** Cause: stash stamps use world coordinates. Fix: read the coordinates
    in `-debug`; give `addContainer` a room name that exists in the target building.
12. **Map stamps don't show.** Cause: `addTexture` ran after the map UI was built. Fix: register at `OnGameBoot`.
13. **A basement registration does nothing.** Cause: the map id isn't an installed map. Fix: use the exact map id.
14. **Modded tiles don't erode.** Cause: missing erosion properties. Fix: copy them from
    `tiledefinitions_erosion.tiles`.

## Assets
- Map symbols: small PNGs in `media/ui/LootableMaps/`. Tile sheets and definitions: TileZed, or the hand-written
  `.pack`/`.tiles` formats in the CDDA note.

Part of one research session on 2026-10-12.
