# QoL suite and stack limits on the Schedule I 0.4.7 IL2CPP beta with MelonLoader

> These are two MelonLoader mods for the Schedule I 0.4.7 IL2CPP beta, both written as C# Harmony mods (the managed-patch route).
>
> - **IncreasedStackLimit-Latest** (based on froggy's original IncreasedStackLimit) raises stack limits for each item type.
> - **PocketPlug** is a QoL suite. It adds a deal compass with the customer's portrait, name and distance, plus Bank and Settings apps built from scratch on the phone. It also removes the weekly ATM deposit limit and adds dealer bank transfers, ready alerts, deal reminders and endless skating.
>
> Both run in the real game on Linux/Proton. Most pieces were checked with the MelonLoader log and with in-game screenshots taken by Unity itself, driven by a dev command file; the rest are listed as not verified under Verification.

## Setup
- **Game:** Steam, Linux, through GE-Proton11-6.
  - The `beta` branch is IL2CPP, 0.4.7f9 (buildid 25698382).
  - The `alternate-beta` branch is Mono, 0.4.7f6. It's the same C# as the matching IL2CPP build and decompiles to near-source, so use it as the readable reference.
- **Loader:** MelonLoader 0.7.3 (2026-05-14), installed as the `version.dll` proxy.
  - Steam launch option: `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="version=n,b" %command%`.
  - The first IL2CPP launch generates `MelonLoader/Il2CppAssemblies` with Cpp2IL and Il2CppInterop, which takes about 30 s. Expect "Failed to restore 885 methods / 3 fields"; it's harmless.
- **Build:** .NET SDK 10, targeting `net6.0`.
  - Reference `MelonLoader/net6/{MelonLoader,0Harmony,Il2CppInterop.Runtime,Il2CppInterop.Common}.dll` and `MelonLoader/Il2CppAssemblies/*.dll`.
- **Lab without Steam:** `umu-run` with `GAMEID=umu-3164500` and `PROTONPATH=<GE-Proton>`, plus `steam_appid.txt` in the game folder. Steam must be running.
  - Saves then land under `Saves/TempPlayer/` instead of your SteamID.
- **Multiplayer:** Schedule I has FishNet co-op over Steam. These mods, and PocketPlug's Backroom menu (items, money,
  player speed, teleports, every console command), are for single player or a lobby you host with friends who agreed
  to them. Don't use them in someone else's lobby. Several patches (gotchas 14 and 20) are only correct on the host
  anyway.
- **S1API (ifBars):** broken on 0.4.7 at the time of writing ([S1API#305](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API/issues/305)). These mods don't depend on it.

## Route and why
Harmony patches plus direct field writes through the Il2CppInterop assemblies. No asset bundles; all UI is built at runtime with uGUI.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Stack limits
- The limit lives on the definition: `ScheduleOne.Core.Items.Framework.BaseItemDefinition.StackLimit` is a public int (it moved to `ScheduleOne.Core.dll` in 0.4.7).
- `BaseItemInstance.StackLimit` just reads `_definition.StackLimit`.
- Several systems read the **definition field directly**: `DeliveryInstance`, `DeliveryShop.WillCartFitInVehicle`, the shop `Cart`, `Supplier` dead drops and `SpecialCustomerLeader`. So patching only the instance getter (what older mods did) leaves those on vanilla sizes. Writing the definition field covers everything.
- **Where to write:** loop over `Registry.GetAllItems()`. `Registry` is a `PersistentSingleton` and is filled in `Awake`. Postfix `Registry.AddToRegistry(ItemDefinition item)` to catch definitions added at runtime.
- **New product mixes** are `Object.Instantiate(DefaultWeed)` (and the same for meth, cocaine and shroom). They copy the template's *current* `StackLimit`, so remember originals or multipliers compound.
- **Vanilla limits on 0.4.7f9:** only 1, 10 or 20, across 227 items.
- **Item classification:** use the definition class, since the `EItemCategory` buckets are coarse.
  - `ProductDefinition` (Weed, Meth, Cocaine and Shroom subclasses) derives from `PropertyItemDefinition`, which is also the mixer class, so check product first.
  - The other classes: `PackagingDefinition`, `QualityItemDefinition`, `SeedDefinition`, `SoilDefinition`, `AdditiveDefinition`, `SporeSyringeDefinition`, `ShroomSpawnDefinition`, `BuildableItemDefinition`.
- **Ammo has no type of its own.** Find it as `Equippable_RangedWeapon.Magazine` on `ItemDefinition.Equippable`; on 0.4.7f9 that's `shotgunshell`.
- **Guns and melee** are found the same way: `Equippable_RangedWeapon` / `Equippable_MeleeWeapon` on the equippable.

### Compass
- `CompassManager` (singleton) creates one `Element` per quest entry: `QuestEntry.CreateCompassElement` uses `ParentQuest.IconPrefab`.
- `Element.DistanceLabel` is a TMP `Text` child. The game only fills it within 50 m, using `UnitsUtility.FormatShortDistance`, which follows the Metric/Imperial setting.
- Deals are `Contract` quests (`Contract.Contracts`). `Contract.Customer` is a `NetworkObject`, so call `GetComponent<NPC>()` on it.
- The portrait the Contacts app shows is `NPC.MugshotSprite` (`RelationCircle.HeadshotImg`).
- Element children are `QuestElement(Clone)`, which contains `Text` plus the quest icon clone.
- The element container `Quests` is **800×30 with a `RectMask2D`**, so anything drawn under a marker is clipped unless you set `RectMask2D.padding` (we use `(0,-60,0,0)`).

### Phone apps
- Native apps are `App<T> : PlayerSingleton<T>`. You can't subclass that from an IL2CPP mod (injecting a generic-derived type isn't practical), so build an app by hand instead, the way [S1API's PhoneApp](https://github.com/ifBars/S1API) does:
  - Add a page under `HomeScreen.transform.parent/AppsCanvas`.
  - Clone `HomeScreen.appIconPrefab` into `appIconContainer`, then add it to `homeScreen.appIcons` and `homeScreen.uiPanel`.
  - Open and close by repeating `App.SetOpen`: `AppsCanvas.SetIsOpen`, `HomeScreen.SetIsOpen(!open)`, `Phone.ActiveApp = page`.
  - Hook `Phone.closeApps` and `GameInput.RegisterExitListener`. Convert the delegate with `DelegateSupport.ConvertDelegate<GameInput.ExitDelegate>`.
- AppsCanvas is 1201×655 (landscape). Portrait apps are 655×1201 pages rotated **90°**; the native Messages app does the same.
- To open the phone from code, call `GameplayMenu.Open()` then `SetScreen(EGameplayScreen.Phone)`. `Phone.SetIsOpen` alone only sets state.
- `NotificationsManager.SendNotification(title, subtitle, sprite, duration, sound)` shows the game's own notification toast.

### Money
- `MoneyManager.ChangeCashBalance(delta, visualize, sound)` changes cash. `CreateOnlineTransaction(name, unit, qty, note)` is a ServerRpc with `RunLocally`, and it changes the bank balance and appends to `ledger`.
- The ledger is session-only. It is not saved.
- The weekly deposit limit is `ATM.WeeklyDepositLimit = 10000` (a **const**), enforced only inside `ATMInterface`. `ATM.WeeklyDepositSum` (static) also triggers `Quest_CleanCash` once it reaches 10000.
- On IL2CPP, the online balance's SyncVar property can't be used from C#. Call `sync___get_value_onlineBalance()`.

### Dealers
- `Dealer.AllPlayerDealers`, `Dealer.Cash` and `Dealer.SetCash`.
- `NPC.MSGConversation.CreateSendableMessage(text)` adds a player message option with `onSent` (an `Il2CppSystem.Action`) and `ShouldShowCheck` callbacks.

## Build steps
1. Install MelonLoader 0.7.3 into the IL2CPP install and launch once to generate the assemblies.
2. Clone the mod repo and run `dotnet build src -c Release -p:GameDir="<Schedule I>" -p:DeployToGame=true`.
3. Launch from Steam. Settings are in `UserData/<Mod>.cfg`.

## Verification
- **Oracle:** the MelonLoader log (`MelonLoader/Latest.log`) plus a dev command file read by the mod. It only works when `UserData/PocketPlug.dev` exists. The commands:
  - `load` calls `LoadManager.StartGame(SaveGames[0])`.
  - `phone open`, `app <id>`.
  - `click <app> <path>` invokes a button's `onClick`.
  - `shot` calls `ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshot`, which works even when the game window is on another Wayland workspace.
  - `dump <name>` writes the transform tree with rects, rotation, colors and fonts.
  - `fakedeal` adds a compass element on a real NPC.
  - `money` logs cash and bank.
- **Verified in game:**
  - Stack limits: 133 of 227 items raised; the shotgun shell is the only stackable item left unchanged; toggles and live config reload work.
  - Settings app toggles and +/- buttons write the config and reapply immediately.
  - Bank app deposit and withdraw conserve money (cash 1542→1442→1542, bank 0→100→0).
  - Notifications show.
  - The compass marker shows the portrait in a green ring, the name, and the game-unit distance ("45ft"), seen in a screenshot.
- **Play-tested by the user:** stack limits and bank app (which found a duplication bug, now fixed; see Gotcha 4).
- **Not yet verified in game:** ready alerts on real stations, deal reminders, dealer transfers (the save had no recruited dealer or active deal), endless skating, and the ATM no-limit patch at a physical ATM.

## Gotchas
1. **froggy's original IncreasedStackLimit "works" but deliveries ignore it.** Cause: it only postfixed the instance getter, and delivery, cart and dead-drop code reads `BaseItemDefinition.StackLimit` directly. Fix: write the definition field.
2. **Raising some stack limits causes bugs.** The user's report, not ours: ammo misbehaves above its vanilla limit. Fix: never touch weapons, ammo (detected from `RangedWeapon.Magazine`) or limit-1 items, and never lower a limit.
3. **Custom phone app opens, but the scroll list is empty.** Cause: the app page is rotated 90°, and `RectMask2D` clips in canvas space, so it clips everything. Fix: use a stencil `Mask` (an `Image` with alpha 1, `showMaskGraphic = false`).
4. **Bank app duplicated money on real clicks**, though `onClick.Invoke()` once was correct. Cause: a clicked uGUI `Button` becomes the selected object, and the game's Submit input then fires `onClick` again. Fix: set `navigation.mode = None` on the mod's buttons, plus a 0.3 s guard on money actions.
5. **`NPC.MugshotSprite` throws a NullReferenceException** for NPCs without appearance data, and it does so inside the IL2CPP getter. Fix: wrap it in try/catch.
6. **Name and distance under a compass marker are invisible.** Cause: the 30 px `Quests` container has a `RectMask2D`. Fix: extend `padding` downward.
7. **Harmony stacked `[HarmonyPatch]` attributes don't give multiple targets.** Fix: use `TargetMethods()` to mask the weekly sum around each `ATMInterface` method. The limit is a const, so it can't be patched directly; the mod temporarily swaps `ATM.WeeklyDepositSum` for a huge negative number and restores the real value plus any deposit afterwards.
8. **MelonPreferences does not reload `MelonPreferences.cfg` when it's edited under Wine.** Fix: `category.SetFilePath(own file)`, poll its mtime about once a second, and call `LoadFromFile`.
9. **The dev command file ran twice under Wine,** because the delete lags behind the read. Fix: remember the file's last-write time and skip a file you've already handled.
10. **Steam-launched Proton prefix `compatdata/3164500` doesn't exist** until the first Steam launch of that install. A fresh lab prefix saves under `Saves/TempPlayer/`. Moving a save between them is fine for the host, because `PlayerManager.TryGetPlayerData` loads `Player_0` for the host first.
11. **The lab was Mono, but an old mod in it was an IL2CPP build** (it referenced `Il2CppInterop` and `Il2CppScheduleOne.*`). Backend-mismatched mods fail at load, so check the references before trusting an installed mod.

12. **Regular ~200 ms freezes every 2 s.** Cause: polling with `Object.FindObjectsOfType<T>()` for seven station/pot types. In this IL2CPP scene each pass cost about 190 ms. Fix: walk `Property.OwnedProperties[i].BuildableItems` instead, cache each item's `TryCast` type once, and check 12 items per frame. Found with a dev perf probe that logs frames over 150 ms and features over 2 ms. After the fix: 0 hitches after load.

13. **A Harmony hook on a tiny non-virtual IL2CPP method misses the native callers that inlined it.** Postfixing `MixingStation.GetMixTimeForCurrentOperation` (null check plus a multiply) to halve mix time changed what the mod's own code saw, but the game's native `OnTimePass` and `IsMixingDone` had it inlined: a mix read `39/30, done=False` and finished at 60. Fix: hook the virtual `OnTimePass(int minutes)` instead and double `minutes` in a prefix (verified on 0.4.7f12: 20 items in 30 in-game minutes). As a bonus the saved progress stays in vanilla units. Verify every IL2CPP hook's effect in game, not through the mod's own reads.

14. **FishNet server RPCs land a tick later, even on the host.** `Dealer.SetCash` only writes the RPC, so read-cash-then-`SetCash` twice in one tick paid the bank twice. Fix: call the generated `RpcLogic___SetCash_431000436` directly. That skips the network, so it's only right where the caller is the server (single-player is always host). `MoneyManager`'s online balance getter also lags a tick behind its ledger, so test money moves against the ledger.

15. **"Mod stutter" was the laptop overheating.** The game ships with VSync off and `targetFrameRate` 500. On an MSI Cyborg 15 A13VE under Proton the CPU sat at 93-96 °C, and `nvidia-smi` throttle reason `0x20` (SW thermal) was active 100% of the time uncapped, versus 0% at 60 fps. Sustained drops (seconds at ~20 fps) never trip a single-frame hitch logger, so log per-second fps with GC and game-log counts, and check `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=clocks_throttle_reasons.active` and `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/thermal_throttle/` before blaming a mod.

16. **A full-screen mod menu over the running game: push a game `State`, not the pause menu.** In single player the Esc menu always freezes time (`Settings.PausingFreezesTime` is forced on with one player). Instead, `new State(name, new IStateMachine(SceneState.Current.InGame.Pointer))` with custom `StateProperties` (mouse free, movement and look locked, blur off), `EnableAutoExitListener()` for Esc, `PushToDefaultParent()` / `RemoveFromDefaultParent()`, plus `PlayerCamera.AddActiveUIElement`. Popping the state hands movement, camera and cursor back automatically, and `State.IsAcceptingInput` starts a frame late, so the open key can't also close it. A menu like this is a trainer: keep it to single player or your own lobby (see Setup).

17. **Runtime uGUI + TextMeshPro pitfalls (IL2CPP).** A `TextMeshProUGUI` with `overflowMode = Ellipsis` in a box shorter than one line height (~1.36 em for OpenSans) renders **nothing** (`characterCount` 0), which looks like a broken font; size every label box at least 1.45 x font size. `RectTransform.GetWorldCorners(new Vector3[4])` returns zeros (the interop passes a copy of the managed array), and layout groups don't run while the canvas is inactive (a menu built behind the loading screen), so compute positions arithmetically (passing an `Il2CppStructArray<Vector3>` you keep a reference to should avoid the copy; not tried here). The game's `OpenSans-* SDF` TMP font assets are reusable via `Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<TMP_FontAsset>()`.

18. **Product quality lives on the instance, not the definition.** `ProductDefinition` is not a `QualityItemDefinition`; `ProductItemInstance` is a `QualityItemInstance`. Check a sample `GetDefaultInstance(1)` before showing a quality picker.

19. **An `InteractableObject` on something resting on furniture loses to the furniture.** A laptop placed on a table: the table's own trigger volume sat 1 cm in front of the laptop collider (1.51 vs 1.52 m), and `InteractionManager` ranks candidates by `Priority`, then distance, so E showed "View table". Fix: `Priority = 100` on the added interactable. Debug by sphere-casting along the look direction with `InteractionManager.Interaction_SearchMask` and logging each hit's `GetComponentInParent<InteractableObject>()`.

20. **Chained mixing (N ingredients in one go) without touching the save format.** A product is its drug type plus its effect set; one mix is `EffectMixCalculator.MixProperties(product.Properties, mixer.Properties[0], drugType)`, so a chain is that folded over the ingredients. The running `MixOperation` stays vanilla-valid (start product + first ingredient), and the rest of the chain lives in a side file, so without the mod the save just finishes a one-step mix. Postfixing `MixOperation.GetOutput` / `IsOutputKnown` reaches native callers (verified: the game's "New Mix Discovered" screen listed the chain's 4 effects). Take over `RpcLogic___TryCreateOutputItems_2166136261` for chains: the vanilla one records a `(product, first ingredient) -> final` recipe, which would be false. Take over `ProductManager.RpcLogic___FinishAndNameMix_4237212381`, which recomputes one step. Like gotcha 14, taking over `RpcLogic___` methods is only right where this machine is the server (single player, or your own lobby). Time: scale `OnTimePass` minutes by 1/N with a fractional carry. Oracle: doing the same three mixes one by one the vanilla way produced the identical product.

21. **Mod-side data that mirrors items must be written on the game's save, not on change.** Ingredients parked outside the game's slots are written only from `SaveManager.onSaveComplete` and read lazily at load (never cache an empty result while `LoadedGameFolderPath` is still null). Reloading without saving then restores both the game and the mod data to the same moment; writing on change would duplicate items (the slot reverts, the file doesn't). Guard pickup with a `CanBeDestroyed` postfix ("Contains items") so parked items can't be lost.

## Assets
- **Icons:** [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) SVGs (ISC), rendered with `rsvg-convert` and composited on gradient squares with Pillow (`scripts/make-icons.py` in the PocketPlug repo).
- **Compass ring and circle mask:** drawn procedurally. No generated art.

## Cost and time
About two working sessions, including recon, two mods and the in-game test loop. Each restart-to-in-game cycle takes about 2 minutes.

## Open questions
- The not-yet-verified features listed under Verification.
- Co-op behaviour. Both mods are single-player only. Stack limits would need the same config on every client.
- Whether `ATMInterface.ProcessTransaction`, a coroutine, needs anything more once the mask is in place. It reads the real sum, so it should be fine.

# Shadow of Mordor Nemesis system across Cartel and Police factions in Schedule I

> A port of the Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor Nemesis system into Schedule I 0.4.7f12, written with MelonLoader
> 0.7.3 and HarmonyX. No Shadow of Mordor files are involved; the rules are written from scratch in the mod. Both
> the Cartel and the Police keep persistent, evolving hierarchies:
> - grunts promoted on player kills;
> - procedural traits (immunities, vulnerabilities, enrages);
> - cheat-death with scars;
> - a living-world turn simulation;
> - an in-game IMGUI Army Screen.
>
> In the real game, the mod loads cleanly, seeds both hierarchies and opens its Army Screen. The combat and
> world-turn rules are covered by unit tests; their in-game check isn't recorded yet (see Verification).

## Setup
- **Game:** Steam on Windows 10/11 x64, Schedule I `0.4.7f12` (AppID 3164500, `beta` branch, buildid `25796331`).
- **Loader:** MelonLoader `v0.7.3` Open-Beta (2026-05-14 release, installed as the `version.dll` proxy).
  - MelonLoader `v0.7.2` crashes during `Il2CppAssemblyGenerator` on build 25796331 (gotcha 1), so use 0.7.3.
- **Build environment:** .NET SDK 10 compiling for `net6.0` (`LangVersion=latest`, `AllowUnsafeBlocks=true`).
  - References `MelonLoader/net6/{MelonLoader,0Harmony,Il2CppInterop.Runtime,Il2CppInterop.Common}.dll` and
    `MelonLoader/Il2CppAssemblies/*.dll`.
- **Multiplayer:** Schedule I has FishNet co-op over Steam. The mod changes NPC health, damage and survival, so
  it's for single player or a lobby you host with friends who agreed to it. Don't use it in someone else's lobby.
  It was built for the host (the FishNet server owns NPC health); clients were never tested.
- The other Schedule I note,
  [QoL suite and stack limits](qol-suite-and-stack-limits-on-the-schedule-i-0-4-7-il2cpp-be.md), covers the same
  MelonLoader setup on Proton, and the Mono `alternate-beta` branch as a readable reference for the IL2CPP build's
  C#.

## Route and why
We used the `managed-patch` route via MelonLoader and HarmonyX:
- The game is Unity 2022.3.62f2 IL2CPP.
- MelonLoader generates strongly typed C# interop assemblies for the game's code (`Assembly-CSharp.dll`,
  `Il2CppScheduleOne.Core.dll`).
- Harmony hooks on `PlayerHealth`, `NPCHealth`, `CartelGoon`, `PoliceOfficer` and `SleepController` intercept
  combat, death, promotions and time skips without altering native binaries or asset bundles.
- Persistence is kept apart in `UserData/Schedule1Nemesis/NemesisData.json`, so the game's own save files are never
  written.
- For how the real Nemesis system is laid out in data (tribes, roles, captains), see the
  [Shadow of War tribe note](../middle-earth-shadow-of-war/goblin-tribe-a-new-nemesis-tribe-via-game-gamedb.md).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### NPC Factions & Hierarchy Binding
- `CartelGoon` and `PoliceOfficer` derive from `Il2CppScheduleOne.NPCs.NPC`.
- Rather than subclassing IL2CPP components, a managed singleton registry maps `NPC.Pointer` (IntPtr) to active
  `NemesisEntity` records.
- Stat adjustments (health bonuses, a scale multiplier for intimidation, `transform.localScale *=
  nemesis.ScaleMultiplier`) are applied when the NPC starts.

### Combat, Damage Types & Trait Resolution
- **Player damage:** `PlayerHealth.TakeDamage(float damage, bool flinch, bool playBloodMist)` and
  `PlayerHealth.Die()`.
  - Attacking NPCs are tracked during damage events. When `Die()` runs, a killer who is already a Nemesis Captain
    gains Power Level and memory logs. A killer who is an unnamed grunt is promoted into a vacant Captain slot.
- **NPC damage:** `NPCHealth.TakeDamage(float damage, bool isLethal = true)` and `NPCHealth.Die()`.
  - Immunities (`immune_bullets`, `immune_melee`, `immune_explosions`) intercept `TakeDamage` in a Harmony prefix
    that returns `false`, so the damage never lands.
  - Vulnerabilities multiply incoming damage (e.g. 2.0x for `weak_to_melee`).
  - Enrages (`enraged_by_guns`, `enraged_by_lowhealth`) trigger temporary speed and damage boosts.

### Cheat Death & Scars
- In `NPCHealth.Die()`, if the defeated NPC is a Nemesis, a cheat-death roll runs (35% base, 75% for
  `cheat_death_master`).
- If it succeeds:
  - the vanilla `Die()` is cancelled (the prefix returns `false`);
  - the NPC gets temporary invincibility (`_invincible = true`), is restored with `RestoreHealth()`, and is
    deactivated or moved to simulate an escape;
  - the Nemesis gains a scar title ("the Scarred", "the Undying"), mutates new traits (such as
    `enraged_by_lowhealth`), enters `Recovering` status for 1-2 world turns, and returns stronger.

### Living World Turn Simulation
- Advances on player death, on sleep via `SleepController.StartSleep()`, or on day rollover via
  `TimeManager.PassMinute()`.
- Wounded Nemeses heal and re-enter active rotation.
- Vacant Warchief slots are filled by the highest Power Level Captain.
- Captain rivalries simulate background turf struggles (winners gain +2 PL; losers are demoted or wounded).

### In-Game UI & Cursor Handling
- An Army Screen (`F7` or `Insert`) shows the active hierarchy for Cartel and Police, Captain cards, traits and
  memory dossiers.
- The first-person controller keeps `Cursor.lockState = CursorLockMode.Locked` and `Cursor.visible = false`. An
  IMGUI menu has to set `Cursor.lockState = CursorLockMode.None` and `Cursor.visible = true` in `Update()` while
  it's open (gotcha 5).

## Build steps
1. Install MelonLoader 0.7.3 into the Schedule I directory. Launch once to generate `MelonLoader/Il2CppAssemblies`.
2. In the mod project (`net6.0`), reference the MelonLoader assemblies and the Il2Cpp assemblies.
3. Build with `dotnet build -c Release`.
4. Deploy the compiled `Schedule1Nemesis.dll` into `Schedule I/Mods/`.
5. Launch the game from Steam. On first launch, the mod seeds initial hierarchies and writes
   `UserData/Schedule1Nemesis/NemesisData.json`.

## Verification
- **Oracle (logs and persistence):**
  - `MelonLoader/Latest.log` shows `Schedule 1: Shadow of Mordor Nemesis System v1.0.0` initializing with zero
    errors and `Loaded World Turn 1 with 6 Cartel and 6 Police officers.`
  - `UserData/Schedule1Nemesis/NemesisData.json` is generated with 12 seeded officers, trait IDs and memory banks.
- **Automated tests:** 5 xUnit tests in `Tests/NemesisSystemTests.cs` cover trait manipulation, timeline ordering,
  relationship graphs, trait catalog validation and JSON round-trip fidelity.
- **In game:**
  - The game window (`MelonLoader v0.7.3 Open-Beta - Schedule I 0.4.7f12`) opens.
  - `F7` opens the Army Screen with working tabs and buttons.
- **Not recorded as checked in game:**
  - a grunt promoted after killing the player, and a Captain gaining Power Level;
  - immunities, vulnerabilities and enrages in a real fight;
  - a cheat-death escape and the Nemesis coming back scarred;
  - a world turn on sleep or day rollover.
- **Not verified:** multiplayer clients (the mod was built for single player and the host).

## Gotchas
1. **MelonLoader 0.7.2 crashes on Schedule I 0.4.7f12 with a NullReferenceException during assembly generation.**
   - *Symptom:* `Il2CppAssemblyGenerator` outputs `Error Generating Interop Assemblies! System.NullReferenceException
     at Il2CppInterop.Generator.Passes.Pass11ComputeTypeSpecifics.ComputeSpecifics`. Bypassing the generator's hash
     checks makes `Schedule I.exe` crash at once with access violation `0xc0000005` in `coreclr.dll`.
   - *Cause:* MelonLoader 0.7.2's bundled Il2CppInterop can't process the 0.4.7f12 build's Unity 2022.3.62f2
     metadata.
   - *Fix:* Upgrade to MelonLoader 0.7.3 (`MelonLoader.x64.zip`), which handles it cleanly.

2. **`NPCHealth.Health` is read-only.**
   - *Symptom:* Compiler error `CS0200: Property or indexer 'NPCHealth.Health' cannot be assigned to -- it is read
     only`.
   - *Cause:* The setter is private: it writes the FishNet SyncVar that holds the NPC's health.
   - *Fix:* Modify `_MaxHealth_k__BackingField` directly and call `RestoreHealth()` or
     `sync___set_value__currentHealth()`.

3. **`NPCHealth.npc` field is not present in 0.4.7f12 interop.**
   - *Symptom:* Compiler error `CS1061: 'NPCHealth' does not contain a definition for 'npc'`.
   - *Cause:* The back-reference field was stripped or unmapped in the dumped assembly.
   - *Fix:* Get the parent NPC component with `__instance.GetComponent<NPC>()`.

4. **Harmony fails to find `TimeManager.StartSleep`.**
   - *Symptom:* `Failed to HarmonyInit PatchAll: Undefined target method for patch method TimeManager_StartSleep_Patch`.
   - *Cause:* Sleep logic was refactored into `Il2CppScheduleOne.GameTime.SleepController`.
   - *Fix:* Patch `SleepController.StartSleep()` instead.

5. **First-person cursor lock prevents clicking IMGUI menu buttons.**
   - *Symptom:* The F7 Army Screen appears, but the mouse cannot move or click any buttons.
   - *Cause:* The first-person controller locks and hides the cursor every frame.
   - *Fix:* In `Update()`, while the menu is open, set `Cursor.lockState = CursorLockMode.None` and
     `Cursor.visible = true`. For a full-screen menu that also stops movement and camera look, the other Schedule I
     note's gotcha 16 pushes a game `State` instead, which hands the cursor back when it's popped.

## Cost and time
One continuous session covering recon, the MelonLoader 0.7.3 upgrade, the Nemesis implementation, unit tests, and
live game testing.

## Open questions
- An in-game run of the combat loop (a promotion, a cheat-death escape, a world turn), to move `status` to
  `working`.
- Whether co-op clients see the Nemesis changes the host makes (scale, health, invincibility).

# Rigged mesh hobble dress for eBody Reborn + Waifus: headless Blender build, own Collada writer, .anim animations

> A wearable rigged-mesh leather hobble corset dress for the eBody Reborn body with the Waifu breast add-on,
> with a PBR leather material (seams, topstitching, zippers), four LODs, two cutouts, and a hobble walk and
> stand that an LSL script swaps in through SL's animation override. Everything is generated by headless
> Blender scripts from the body's dev kit; the user had no 3D experience. Verified by the user in world on the
> Aditi beta grid with their own shape, over about a dozen upload iterations.

## Setup
- Viewer: Firestorm 7.2.4.80712, Windows 11. Firestorm ships SL's skeleton definitions in
  `<viewer>\character\avatar_skeleton.xml` and the shape-slider definitions in `avatar_lad.xml`; both were
  used as the source of truth.
- Blender 4.5.10 LTS, run headless (`blender -b <kit.blend> --python script.py`). **No Avastar** installed.
  4.5 still has the Collada exporter (gone in Blender 5.0), but see Gotcha 1: we didn't use it.
- eBody Reborn Dev Kit 2.0: obtained through eBody's application form (no store needed). It includes Blender
  kits for 2.79 / 2.93 / 3.6.7 / 5.0.1 (Avastar), Maya/DAE kits, and skin/material kits. The 3.6.7 .blend
  opens in Blender 4.5. Its terms forbid redistributing kit files (keep them and any .blend that contains the
  kit body out of git and releases) and require products to need the base Reborn body.
- Test loop: Firestorm **Build → Local Mesh** (free, only you see it; wear a prim, select it, Apply) for
  fit; the **Aditi** beta grid (free uploads) for anything needing a real upload (materials, scripts,
  animations).

## Route and why
Content route only: rigged mesh `.dae` + glTF material + animations, uploaded through the viewer, plus one
LSL script. Second Life is online; nothing about the viewer or protocol is touched.
- Fit against the body's official dev kit, used under its license. Never fit against mesh exported from the
  viewer or its cache (copybot-style ripping of another creator's body or clothing): SL's terms and the body
  makers' licenses forbid it, and the dev kit exists for exactly this job.
- Considered: building on SL's default avatar. Rejected: clothing has to be fitted to the body's dev kit
  (its shape and weights), otherwise it won't follow that body's sliders.
- Considered: Avastar (the usual SL rigging add-on, paid). Not installed; a ~200-line Collada writer
  (Gotcha 1) and an `.anim` writer (Gotcha 10) did the job without it.
- Considered: Maitreya LaraX instead of eBody. Its kit application is selective ("if your store is
  selected"); eBody's kit came quickly without a store.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Frames.** The kit rig in Blender faces −Y with +X as the avatar's left. SL's skeleton faces +X with +Y
  left, Z up. Export rotates the mesh by Rz(+90°). Every SL joint has an identity rest orientation, so a
  joint's local axes at rest are the world axes.
- **Rigged-mesh skinning.** The viewer uses the DAE's inverse bind matrices with its own skeleton:
  world(joint) is a translation chain of `pos` for bones, and T(pos)·R(rot, XYZ degrees)·S(scale) for
  collision volumes (BUTT, LEFT_PEC, CHEST…); IBM = inverse(world). The volumes' scale (0.05 to 0.2) must be
  in the IBM. Verified by matching the eBody kit's own SL-ready DAE (BUTT IBM translation 0.6/0/−9.67).
- **Rest pose.** SL's skeleton rests in a **T-pose**; the eBody kit rig rests in an **A-pose**. Animations
  are local rotations relative to SL's rest frame. To preview them on the kit rig, convert per bone:
  D = rotation(SL rest bone direction → kit rest direction), then posed world = W_SL · D⁻¹ · kit rest.
- **Shape sliders = bone transforms**, defined in `avatar_lad.xml`. Example: Breast Size (id 105) drives
  Big_Chest (id 626) with w = (v−0.5)/0.5 above 0.5; Big_Chest scales LEFT/RIGHT_PEC by +0.0273·w (base 0.05)
  and moves them (0.038, ±0.024, −0.016)·w metres in SL axes. At slider 79: ×1.32, 2.2 cm forward, 1.4 cm
  out, 0.9 cm down. Applying these to the kit rig in Blender reproduced in-world problems exactly; the kit's
  default shape hid them (Gotcha 6).
- **Uploader rules.** Physics shapes may not contain sliver triangles (`MAV_FOUND_DEGENERATE_TRIANGLES`).
  Error details, including the triangle's index and vertices, are in
  `%APPDATA%\Firestorm_x64\logs\Firestorm.log`. All LOD files should share one joint list.
- **Animations.** The `.bvh` importer expects Y-up, +Z-forward, inches; joints use the classic names
  (hip, abdomen, lThigh…); a channel order Z X Y equals Blender Euler 'YXZ'. It compresses keyframes on
  import (Gotcha 10). Firestorm also uploads SL's native **`.anim`** (LLKeyframeMotion v1.0) with **no
  settings dialog and no preview**: priority, loop and ease come from the file, the asset name from the
  filename.
- **Animation override.** `llSetAnimationOverride("Walking"/"Standing", anim)` from an attachment needs
  PERMISSION_OVERRIDE_ANIMATIONS, which attachments get without a dialog. Whichever object set a state last
  wins, so an AO can take it back; re-applying on a timer works. Reset the overrides on detach.
- **PBR materials** upload as a materials-only glTF (Build → Upload → Material). A material can't be applied
  to a Local Mesh surrogate; that needs a real upload (Aditi).

## Build steps
1. Get the dev kit; pick the body variant object (here `RebornBody+Waifus`, parented to armature `Avatar`).
2. Build the garment procedurally (`build_dress.py`), all in rest pose:
   - per height level, take the 2D convex hull of a body slice (arm vertices excluded by weight), offset 4 mm;
   - front and back panels as separate grids, welded below the armholes and at the collar;
   - push-out against a BVH of the skin, plus a "reverse" pass that pushes faces any skin vertex pokes through;
   - recompute UVs from final positions;
   - transfer weights with a DATA_TRANSFER modifier (nearest face, interpolated), drop forearm and hand
     groups, cap at 4 influences, normalise.
3. LODs: rebuild at lower ring counts (72/48/32/24 around), don't decimate. Every level then gets the same
   fit and UVs.
4. Export with your own Collada writer (Gotcha 1); pass the HIGH joint list to every LOD; use a 12-triangle
   box as the physics shape.
5. Texture: generate base colour / normal (OpenGL +Y) / ORM in numpy in UV space, plus a materials-only
   `.gltf`.
6. Animations: write SL-frame local rotations per frame, then emit `.anim` directly (or `.bvh`).
7. LSL: override Walking/Standing on attach, re-apply every 5 s, reset on detach.

## Verification
- **In world (the real oracle):** the user wore every version on Aditi and sent screenshots, some
  annotated (e.g. one region circled red "moves with the arms", another yellow "never moves"). That
  annotation is what cracked the armhole bug.
- **Automated Blender checks, with the user's shape applied:**
  - leg skin outside the posed dress over every walk/stand frame (hands excluded — Gotcha 9);
  - arm vertices behind the dress surface, arms down;
  - non-arm skin poking through, with the shape applied;
  - sharp corners along armhole edges (turning angle > 50°);
  - "WIDE": dress vertices beyond the torso width.
- **File checks:** the DAE inverse bind matrices against the kit's SL-ready DAE; `.anim` files decoded back
  to check headers, key counts and pelvis offsets.
- **Not verified:** other eBody add-ons or the plain Reborn body (the cleavage cutout needs Waifu); shapes
  other than the user's and the kit default; main-grid upload (done on Aditi only); land impact and fee
  numbers.

## Gotchas
1. **Rigging broken: all-zero inverse bind matrices.** Blender 4.5's Collada exporter on the Avastar kit rig
   (493 constraints, 6 drivers) writes 0 for every bind pose, with or without `open_sim` and in REST pose.
   It also can't express collision-volume scale. **Fix:** write the DAE yourself; take joint matrices from
   the viewer's `avatar_skeleton.xml`, compute IBM = inverse(world), and rotate the mesh Rz(+90°).
2. **Upload fails with MAV_FOUND_DEGENERATE_TRIANGLES.** The physics shape defaulted to the lowest LOD, which
   had a sliver triangle near the hem (named in Firestorm.log). **Fix:** a box `.dae` as the physics shape;
   worn attachments never use physics.
3. **Seams wobble and zig-zag in the texture.** UVs were assigned at layout, before smoothing and push-out
   moved the vertices. **Fix:** compute UVs from the final positions (u = angle around the body centre line,
   v = height; lift u on faces that straddle the wrap).
4. **Pointed flaps at the collar corners in world.** The closed collar ring started at 1.575 m, where a body
   slice includes the tops of the shoulders. **Fix:** start the collar band where the neck stands clear
   (~1.60 m) and shape it from the neck slice only; trim halter slices to the cut width + 3 cm.
5. **Dress "torn" at the back of the armpits with arms down.** The dress had no shoulder/upper-arm weights
   (all arm groups dropped) while the skin beneath has them, and arm and torso skin overlap there anyway.
   **Fix:** keep shoulder and upper-arm weights; cut a racer back clear of where the arm rests; slope-limit
   the armhole edge angle ring to ring (no single-ring jumps) so it is one smooth U.
6. **Armhole notch and tip only in world.** The kit's default shape hid them. Angles were measured from each
   slice's centroid, and at bust height the bust drags it about 10 cm forward. The "side seam", and the
   armhole bottom with it, landed on the side of the breast, 78% weighted to PEC; Breast Size 79 then pulled
   the front and back edges apart. **Fix:** hold the torso centre (from below the bust) through the armhole
   region; fade PEC out around the armhole bottom; reproduce the user's sliders from `avatar_lad.xml` in
   every test.
7. **Large breast slider pushes skin through the bust.** Weight smoothing had diluted the dress's PEC weight
   to ~0.65 where the skin's is ~0.98. **Fix:** set the dress's PEC to at least 0.97 × the average of the 6
   nearest skin vertices. Blend left/right PEC across the centre line: one centre vertex on RIGHT_PEC beside
   one on LEFT_PEC folded a cutout edge into a point when the slider moved each PEC outward. Smooth PEC
   across the under-bust bridge (vertices off the skin by more than max(6 mm, 0.6 × ring spacing)), or it
   forms a stepped shelf.
8. **Calves through the hobble skirt on every step, or the skirt "splits" between the legs.** Unblended
   weights split the tube like trousers; blended weights lag the calves. **Fix:** blend weights in a
   central band and bulge that band outward by as much as the blend lags; keep the steps small (±2° at the
   hip). The quantity that matters is the leg separation at the hem.
9. **Clipping meter stuck at "102 vertices, 14 mm" whatever changed.** It was the hands: they hang beside the
   thighs and counted as skin outside the dress. **Fix:** exclude arm and hand vertices from leg checks.
10. **Small ankle-pivot sway: feet slide, then the body "juts".** The feet stay fixed only if the pelvis
    translation and the pelvis/leg/ankle rotations cancel exactly. After `.bvh` import they didn't (both
    sign variants failed), most likely because import compresses small position and rotation changes
    differently. **Fix:** write `.anim` directly, with every frame as a key. The feet stayed planted, and the
    user found the `.anim` walk "a lot smoother" than the `.bvh` one. Pelvis position keys in `.anim` are
    offsets from rest (confirmed in world). A rotation-only `.bvh` fallback can't slide, but the sway was
    barely visible and it stuttered at the loop.
11. **Zipper slider invisible at the collar.** Parts sized in texture pixels: around the neck one u-pixel is
    ~0.2 mm of fabric, at the hips ~0.6 mm. **Fix:** size texture details in millimetres using a per-row
    metres-per-u measured from the mesh; draw the slider before the teeth and remove the teeth under it.
12. **Leather looked silver in previews.** It was preview lighting: a bright grey world, strong area lights
    and Filmic. **Fix:** Standard view transform with a dim world. Separately, a fully matte black zipper
    tape reads grey under light; roughness ~0.45 reads black.
13. **Doubled side seam.** The u=0/1 wrap is one seam; listing both 0.0 and 1.0 drew it twice. Edge
    stitching also skipped faces whose u is just past 1. **Fix:** list the seam once; stamp boundary
    segments at u−1, u and u+1.

## Assets
No generated art or AI-made assets. All mesh is procedural from the kit body's shape (no kit geometry
shipped). Textures are procedural numpy (pebbled grain, seams, topstitching, interlocking zipper teeth,
slider and pull tab) at 2048². Animations are hand-specified joint curves (sines) in SL's rest frame. The
box image is two transparent EEVEE renders composited with Blender text objects.

## Cost and time
One long session of about 25 in-world iterations (fit, armholes, cutouts, animations). Upload costs only for
the final main-grid release; all testing used Local Mesh and Aditi.

## Open questions
- Exactly how the `.bvh` importer reduces keys (thresholds, and whether position and rotation are reduced
  separately) — inferred from behaviour, not read from the source.
- Generalising the fit to other eBody add-ons and to the plain Reborn body (would need separate cutout
  variants).
- Main-grid land impact and upload fee for the four LODs (~17k / 7k / 3k / 1.4k triangles).

# A new civilization with an animated 3D leader scene on a stock leader rig in Civilization V

> A playable civilization ("Demons") with:
> - Lua gameplay systems: mid-game emergence, a terrain plague, a unique building and a unit;
> - its own 2D art, ground decals, and a unit model on a stock skeleton;
> - a fully animated 3D diplomacy leader. The leader is a user-supplied model retargeted onto Nebuchadnezzar's
>   stock leader rig, using all 39 of his animations, his voice slowed down, and a user-supplied 3D throne and
>   location.
>
> It's a pure data/Lua/art mod (no DLL). It's verified in the real game on DX9 and DX11 at max settings:
> screenshots, video, a game-only audio recording, and Lua.log. It's released on the Steam Workshop (file
> 3814750314), uploaded without ModBuddy.

## Setup
- **Game:** Steam build 1.0.3.279 (2014-11-19), all DLC. It's 32-bit, with three exes:
  - `CivilizationV.exe` (DX9);
  - `CivilizationV_DX11.exe`;
  - `CivilizationV_Tablet.exe`.
- **SDK:** "Sid Meier's Civilization V SDK" (Steam). We used:
  - `CvGameCoreSource` (the C++ of the shipped gameplay DLLs);
  - `Nexus\x86\Firaxis.Framework.Granny*.dll` (managed wrappers around RAD Granny, with the native Granny inside).
- **Our tools:**
  - **gr2tool**, a C# tool compiled with `csc` against those DLLs. It's built twice, x86 and x64, each next to its
    own copy of the Nexus DLLs.
  - **Blender 5.2** (FBX/GLB import, bakes, previews).
  - **Python** for packing, textures, retargeting maths and the validator.
  - **lupa** (Lua 5.1) for headless Lua tests of the mod scripts.
- **User data:** `Documents\My Games\Sid Meier's Civilization 5\`:
  - `MODS\`;
  - `Logs\` (needs `LoggingEnabled = 1` in `config.ini`);
  - `cache\Civ5DebugDatabase.db`, the merged SQLite of the loaded ruleset;
  - `ModdedSaves\`.

## Route and why
A **data mod**: XML/SQL for the database, Lua addins for the gameplay, and art loaded by name from the mod's VFS.
- **No DLL:** the official GameCore source in the SDK answered every rules question, so no DLL was needed.
- **No exe patching:** the renderer and the asset loader live in the closed exe and were never touched.
- **Art on stock templates:** all art goes into copies of stock `.gr2` files whose meshes/materials are swapped. The
  game's leader shaders, state machines and animation graphs are then reused by name.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Layers
- **Gameplay rules** live in `CvGameCore_Expansion2.dll`. The SDK source matches the shipped DLLs: each
  `CvDllVersion.h` GUID is present byte-for-byte in its DLL.
- **Game data** is XML/SQL merged into a SQLite cache.
- **UI** is Lua 5.1 + XML.
- **Art and audio** are in `.fpk` packages under `Resource\{Common,DX9,DX9_Low}`. There is **no DX11 asset set**:
  only the shader path differs.

### Packages and models
- **`.fpk` layout:**
  - header: `u32 6, "FPK_", u16 0, u32 count`;
  - per entry: `u32 namelen, name, pad to 4, u64, u32 size, u32 offset`;
  - data stored uncompressed.
- **`.gr2`:** RAD Granny revision 7 (Oodle1-compressed sections). Strings in stock files are 32-bit hashes of entries
  in the package's `.gsd` string database: CRC-32 without the final inversion.
  - The SDK's managed loader reads models.
  - It **refuses files without meshes or animations** (cameras, light rigs). Read those natively instead:
    `GrannyReadEntireFileFromMemory` + `GrannyGetFileInfo`.
  - To write such a file: `GrannyBeginFile` → `BeginFileDataTreeWriting` → `WriteDataTreeToFileBuilder` →
    `EndFile`, with the source's magic and type tag.
- **x86 vs x64 saves:** files saved by the x64 Granny library are **invisible as units**. Ground decals load them
  fine. Save unit and leader art with the x86 build.
- **Unit art** is one `.fxsxml` (Mesh, Animations with event codes, Textures, BoneUsage, TimedTrigger `.ftsxml`,
  AnimGraph `.dge`, StateMachine `.fsmxml`). Animations are found by name in the game's packages.
- **Texture names are stored twice in materials:**
  1. in the Granny texture maps;
  2. as strings in the material's FGX shader-parameter data (ExtendedData).

  The game binds the **second**. Change both, or the model draws with the template's textures.

### Leader scenes
- **The scene XML:** `Leaders.ArtDefineTag` names it. Its root is
  `<LeaderScene lights= camera= ColorKey= cubemap_prefix= FallbackImage=>`, with these children:
  - `LineLightSettings`: flicker for line lights;
  - `HackLightSettings`: one extra directional light;
  - one `LeaderObject`;
  - any number of `BackgroundObject`.

  Each child names an `.fxsxml`. `lights=` may name a light-rig `.gr2` directly.
- **FallbackImage** is shown instead of the 3D scene when "leader quality" is minimum (`UseScreenShots = 1`).
- **ColorKey:** a 1024x576 `.tga` whose top 32 rows hold a 32-tile LUT (x = red, y = blue, tile = green).
- **Cube maps:** `<prefix>_Environment_diffuse/reflection.dds`, DXT1, 128x128, 8 mips. The diffuse one is the
  scene's ambient term, bound per material ("Civ5LightingTextures").
- **Background meshes:** copies of stock scene meshes keep their shaders:
  - lit: shader "Leader", maps Diffuse/Normal/SREF/Irradiance/Environment;
  - matte cards: "Leader_Opaque_Matte".

  One mesh holds at most 65,536 vertices (uint16 indices). Split large models.
- **Camera rig:** bone 1 is the camera; its ExtendedData holds the horizontal FOV in radians. Frames are 16:9.
- **Light rig:** one skeleton per light. The record is the bone's ExtendedData `LightInfo`, a 3ds Max export: near/far
  attenuation, shadow flags, colour, intensity…
  - **Line lights** are lights under a dummy parent. `LineLightSettings` must only name those (see Gotcha 4).
  - **Adding a light:** deep-copy an existing light's model + skeleton (with its record), rename it, and append it to
    the file's Models and Skeletons arrays. The game uses it.
- **InitialPlacement:** a leader model's `InitialPlacement` (in `granny_model`) places it in the scene. A stock leader
  rig can sit anywhere: we used translation, Z rotation and uniform scale.

### Leader animation and props
- **Animations** are per-bone curves bound by bone name (track group = model name). The stock
  `LEADER_FULL_STATE.fsmxml` and `*_GRAPH_LEADER.dge` drive them by the event codes listed in the leader's
  `.fxsxml`.
- **Retiming:** works by scaling every curve's knots plus Duration/TimeStep, per curve format:
  - K16u/K8u: the uint16 `OneOverKnotScaleTrunc`, the top half of a float;
  - D4n: real32 `OneOverKnotScale`;
  - K32f: the knot array.

  The stock state machine still drives the retimed files.
- **Proportions:** Nebuchadnezzar's rig is a baked control rig.
  - Lengths are constant x-translations of driver bones.
  - Chain roots (`ARM_<s>_PARENT_jor`, `HEAD_SPOT_PARENTER_jor`) carry animated world positions.
  - Apply the same deltas to the model's rest pose and to every animation, and the stock animations drive the new
    proportions.
- **Skinning a rigid slot:** a mesh can take another mesh's vertex type and get new bone bindings. That turns a rigid
  slot (his helmet) into a skinned one: our head with jaw/mouth bones.
- **Props:** a leader's prop (his chalice) is a **separate model** (`CUP_Point`) with one bone and a rigid mesh.
  - Only the INTRO animation moves it: held, thrown, landed.
  - Every other animation keeps it constant on the floor.
  - Its track is independent of the hand. Retarget it yourself (Gotcha 10).
  - It needs its own `InitialPlacement`.
- **INTRO plays only at first contact:** the AI's first greeting when it meets the human (`Team:Meet(t, false)`). A
  player-opened diplomacy screen right after meeting replaces it with the default greeting.

### Sound
- **Speech:** `Audio_Sounds` (`SoundID`, `FileName`, `LoadType DynamicResident`) + `Audio_2DSounds` (`ScriptID`,
  `SoundType GAME_SPEECH`) rows in mod XML, `.mp3` files in the VFS, and `ReloadAudioSystem` 1 in the `.modinfo`.
- **Triggers:** the leader's `TimedTrigger` plays ScriptIDs by event code and time.

### Gameplay facts (all from the SDK source, verified in game)
- **Combat death:** `UnitPrekill` then `UnitKilledInCombat`. There is no `CombatResult` event.
- **`CityCaptureComplete`** fires only if the city survives.
- **Saved state:** `Player`/`Plot:SetScriptData` are saved; `City` has none.
- **Optional args:** `luaL_optint` flags (`City:CanConstruct`, `CanTrain`) need numbers, not booleans.
- **Reviving a slot:** a dead player slot can be revived with `Player:InitCity` (its first city gets the palace).
  `Game.AddPlayer` is never safe. `Game.SetAIAutoPlay` kills the active player's units without an observer slot.
- **Diplomacy text:** `GetDiploResponse` pools a leader's rows with GENERIC ones weighted by Bias, and finds tags only
  through `Language_en_US`. An en_US row is required even in a Russian game.
- **Civ list:** the front end's `UniqueBonuses.lua` breaks the list for a civ with fewer than two unique items. A
  building class without a default building, overridden by one civ, counts as one.
- **Ground decals:**
  - the game binds their textures from the material's FGX parameters (`BaseTextureMap`/`HeightTextureMap`);
  - `ArtDefine_Landmarks.Scale` is honoured;
  - they need `ReloadLandmarkSystem` 1;
  - hex row neighbours are 64 units apart.

## Build steps
1. **Rules:** XML/SQL rows (Civilizations, Leaders, Traits, Units, Buildings, Diplomacy responses, art defines) plus
   Lua addins. A Python build script writes the `.modinfo` with MD5s and deploys the mod to `MODS\`.
   - Stamp the `.modinfo` mtime on every deploy (Gotcha 12).
   - Put a version in the folder name so the human can see which build is installed.
2. **Unit and leader art:**
   1. Skin the model to a stock skeleton in Blender (fit the bones, transform vertices fit-bone → stock-bone).
   2. Pack raw vertex/index buffers in the template mesh's own layout (e.g. stride 42/53 skinned, 34 rigid).
   3. In gr2tool, `replace-meshes` a **copy of the stock .gr2**. Spec lines include `mesh`, `blank`, `vertextype`,
      `bindings`, `bonepos`, `placement` and `material` (a mesh gets its own deep copy of a shared material).
   4. Retexture both the maps and the FGX strings.
3. **Leader animations:** `stretch-anim` (retime + bone-position edits + time-varying track offsets) on every stock
   animation. The leader `.fxsxml` = the stock one with our model, animations, textures and trigger file.
4. **Light rig:** `lights` (move, recolour, re-range, add lights) on a stock rig.
5. **Scene:**
   - throne/location meshes go into copies of the stock lit scene meshes;
   - the painting goes on a matte card;
   - the scene XML sets camera, lights, cube maps (tinted copies of a stock pair) and a ColorKey.
6. **Test** before every in-game run (see Verification).
7. **Release on the Steam Workshop:**
   1. Package a `.civ5mod`. It's a 7z (LZMA) archive with the mod's files at its root next to
      `<Name> (v N).modinfo`, the layout ModBuddy writes. We build it with py7zr and read it back.
   2. Upload. The SDK's ModBuddy uploader is a thin layer over the SDK's `SteamworksSharp.dll`:
      - static `Valve.Steamworks.Initialize/RunCallbacks/Shutdown`;
      - `RemoteStorage.FileWrite` for the package and the preview;
      - `PublishWorkshopFile(file, preview, consumer app 8930, title, description, visibility, tags, Community)`;
      - `CreatePublishedFileUpdateRequest` + `UpdatePublishedFile*` + `CommitPublishedFileUpdate` for later
        versions.

      A small x86 C# tool next to that DLL, `steam_api.dll` and `steam_appid.txt` = 16830 (the SDK's app, as
      ModBuddy runs) publishes without ModBuddy.
   3. On launch, the game downloads the subscribed package into `MODS\` and unpacks it into a folder named after
      the `.modinfo`'s `<Name>`, not the archive's.

## Verification
- **Before the game:**
  - the validator applies the mod's XML to copies of the game databases and resolves every model/texture reference
    in the scene;
  - Lua unit tests run under lupa: 4 suites, 355 tests.
- **In game:** driven with `um win drive/shot/record` in a 1600x900 window.
  - Settings are backed up and restored around every test.
  - Every check is on high/max settings: the human plays DX11 at max, and that path differs (Gotcha 1).
- **Seen in game:**
  - scene neutral and at war;
  - first-contact INTRO (video, 2 fps frames: prop in hand → thrown → on the floor);
  - two stock leaders after ours;
  - save → full exit → load;
  - `Lua.log` with 0 Runtime Errors.
- **Speech:** a game-only audio recording was cross-correlated with our `.mp3` files (0.93–0.98) to prove the mod's
  voice plays, not the stock one.
- **Animation edits:** sampled back through Granny itself (`GrannySampleModelAnimations` + `GrannyBuildWorldPose`)
  and compared with the intended curves (≤ 0.4 in).
- **Workshop release:** published (file 3814750314), subscribed, and installed by the game itself. The unpacked
  folder is byte-identical to the source (189 files). The human then played that copy and confirmed it works.
- **Not verified:**
  - multiplayer;
  - the Tablet exe;
  - DX9 at max settings after the last lighting change;
  - a game without the Babylon DLC, where Nebuchadnezzar's rig, animations and voice come from (the Workshop page
    says the mod was tested only with it).

## Gotchas
1. **Scene fine on DX9, mostly black at max settings.**
   - **Cause:** DX11 with `EnableShadows = 1` (max) casts shadows from the rig's lights, and DX9 tests had shadows
     off. A shadow-casting light left every background model black. That happened even after the light was moved to
     an unobstructed spot; the leader object itself stayed lit.
   - **Fix:** no shadow-casting lights on scenes whose background is your own meshes. Before that, the light also
     sat inside the throne's crest: check light visibility with ray casts whenever a light moves.
2. **Background barely lit in either renderer.**
   - **Cause:** the scene's ambient comes from the diffuse cube map, and a dark tint leaves far geometry at the
     colour key's black level.
   - **Fix:** add dedicated low lights near that geometry (copies of an existing rig light). Don't brighten
     everything.
3. **DX11 exe started directly comes up as DX9.**
   - **Cause:** the exe hands over to Steam, which starts the default launch option.
   - **Fix:** `steam://launch/8930/dialog` starts the last chosen option (DX11 once chosen) without asking.
     `steam://rungameid/8930` starts the default.
4. **Every light in the scene went out.**
   - **Cause:** `LineLightSettings` named a root light (one without a dummy parent).
   - **Fix:** only name line lights there.
5. **A light near a model lit nothing close to it.**
   - **Cause:** 3ds Max-style near attenuation fades light *in* from the source.
   - **Fix:** turn near attenuation off.
6. **Unit model invisible in game.**
   - **Cause:** saved by the x64 Granny library.
   - **Fix:** save with an x86 build.
7. **Model drew with the template's textures.**
   - **Cause:** the material's FGX parameter strings still named the old files.
   - **Fix:** replace those strings too.
8. **Prop got the head's textures.**
   - **Cause:** the prop mesh and our head (a re-used helmet slot) shared one material object.
   - **Fix:** give the mesh a deep copy of the material before retexturing.
9. **Retargeted leader: hands off the armrests.**
   - **Cause:** the stock seated pose puts the hands ~20 cm beyond a short armrest.
   - **Fix:** measure the forearm/hand undersides over the idle animations and fit the throne. Stretch the armrests
     forward, raise them per side, keep the throne symmetric.
10. **Thrown prop floats beside the hand, then lands off-screen.**
    - **Cause:** the prop's track was authored for the stock body. Our proportions moved the hand (here by a constant
      2–3 in), and the stock landing spot fell below our lower camera's frame.
    - **Fix:** a time-varying offset on the prop's position curve:
      - the hand delta while held;
      - a blend over the flight;
      - a resting offset chosen by ray-casting a screen point onto the platform.

      Quantized curves (D3K16uC16u) must be re-quantized after editing.
11. **INTRO never seen in tests.**
    - **Cause:** it plays only at first contact, and opening diplomacy right after `Meet` replaces it.
    - **Fix:** a debug button that only calls `Team:Meet(t, false)`.
12. **Rebuilt mod hidden from the Mods screen.**
    - **Cause:** the game caches mods by `.modinfo` file time.
    - **Fix:** touch the `.modinfo` on every deploy.
13. **Mod types missing in addins after an unmodded game in the same process.**
    - **Cause:** state from the earlier ruleset.
    - **Fix:** restart the game process between tests.
14. **"Retargeted" mesh shows dark patches around the mouth.**
    - **Cause:** a Meshy FBX imports flat-shaded, and the facets were baked into the normal map.
    - **Fix:** set `use_smooth = True` before baking.
15. **Blotchy textures at a distance on AI-generated models.**
    - **Cause:** ~20k tiny UV islands bleed at the mip levels the scene samples.
    - **Fix:** re-unwrap into large charts (xatlas on a smoothed copy) and re-bake the supplied PBR maps.
16. **Old screenshot fooled an automated wait.**
    - **Cause:** a file left over from the previous run satisfied the check while the game never started.
    - **Fix:** delete the file before waiting for a new one.
17. **Blender 5 can't open a supplied `.dae`.**
    - **Cause:** its Collada importer is gone.
    - **Fix:** an Assimp export is simple XML (one triangle list, all inputs on one index, Y up, `<unit meter>`), so
      read it in Python and weld positions to recover topology.

18. **ModBuddy won't start: "Cannot find one or more components. Please reinstall the application."**
    - **Cause:** it needs the Visual Studio 2010 isolated shell.
    - **Fix:** skip it. Call the SDK's `SteamworksSharp.dll` directly (Build step 7).
19. **Russian title/description would arrive garbled.**
    - **Cause:** `SteamworksSharp` marshals strings with `StringToHGlobalAnsi` (the system code page), and Steam reads
      UTF-8.
    - **Fix:**
      - pass each string as its UTF-8 bytes decoded with the ANSI code page, and check that round trip before
        sending;
      - keep cloud file names ASCII.
20. **`SteamAPI_Init` fails while Steam is running.**
    - **Cause:** the SDK's old `steam_api.dll` checks `HKCU\Software\Valve\Steam\ActiveProcess\pid`, and the
      value was a dead pid.
    - **Fix:** point it at the running `steam.exe` (Steam rewrites it on its next start). That's a registry write,
      so ask the human first.
21. **`SubscribePublishedFile` returns Fail.**
    - **Cause:** subscriptions belong to the game's app; we called it from the SDK's (16830).
    - **Fix:** run the call with `steam_appid.txt` = 8930.
22. **The item page seemed to say "removed for violating guidelines" and "incompatible".**
    - **Cause:** those are hidden templates (`display: none`) in every item page's HTML.
    - **Fix:** check the HTML, not a page summary.

## Assets
- **Supplied by the human:**
  - the leader (a Meshy model with a Mixamo rig);
  - two thrones;
  - a location;
  - a unit model;
  - the 2D art sheets (generated images);
  - a demon-skull ring model, cut to a skull for the thrown prop.
- **How we treated the models:** never decimated. Re-unwrapped and re-baked where their atlases were unusable.
- **Voice:** the stock leader's lines through ffmpeg: slowed with `asetrate`, a rubberband sub-voice, bass, and a short
  echo. The animations were stretched by the same factor so the mouth stays in sync.
- **Derived from the game's files, and in the released package:** Nebuchadnezzar's 39 animations (retimed and
  edited), his voice lines (slowed and processed), and copies of stock `.gr2` files, light and camera rigs and cube
  maps with our content swapped in. None of it is in this repo. Before releasing something similar, read the game's
  mod terms, and reference stock files by name wherever the game allows it (unit animations, for example, are found
  by name in the game's packages).

## Cost and time
About four days of agent sessions over the whole mod. The animated leader alone took two (retargeting, voice,
lighting, then the DX11 and prop fixes).

## Open questions
- **Why do shadow-casting lights blacken background models in DX11?** Hypothesis: the shadow cube map's depth range
  doesn't fit a scene this size (~24 units per metre).
- **Can a prop's rest *orientation* be changed?** That needs editing the D4n quaternion curves and the constant
  orientation in every other animation. Our prop lands showing its back.
- **Can the leader be lit for both renderers at once?** DX9's ambient makes the same rig brighter than DX11's.

# In-game F1 cheat menu with BepInEx 6 IL2CPP and IMGUI

> A BepInEx 6 IL2CPP plugin for SiNiSistar 2 (Unity 2022.3, IL2CPP) that draws an IMGUI window on F1. The window
> covers survival (god mode, infinite HP/MP/clothing durability, refill), relics (currency), giving items and
> wands, and combat (one-hit kills, damage multiplier, crit). Verified in a real save via screenshots, the HUD,
> the BepInEx log and the human playing through fights with it on.

## Setup
- SiNiSistar 2 v1.3.1 (Steam 4466620), Windows 11, fullscreen 1920x1080.
- Unity 2022.3.62f2, IL2CPP, `global-metadata.dat` **version 31**.
- BepInEx `6.0.0-be.788+5b766a3` IL2CPP win-x64 (bleeding-edge build server). Unzip into the game folder;
  the first launch generates interop in about 40 s (it reports roughly 8k of 9.3k method bodies unstripped).
- Cpp2IL `2022.1.0-pre-release.21` for type and field stubs (`--output-as diffable-cs`).
- Plugin: `net6.0` class library referencing `BepInEx/core/*` and `BepInEx/interop/*` (`SiNiSistar2.dll`,
  `Il2Cppmscorlib`, `UnityEngine.CoreModule`, `UnityEngine.IMGUIModule`, `Unity.InputSystem`) with
  `Private=false`. Built with the .NET 10 SDK, which needs `CheckEolTargetFramework=false`.

## Route and why
`managed-patch`: BepInEx 6 + Harmony through Il2CppInterop. There is no community loader or API for this game. The
game does ship an official `Mod\` folder, but it only covers sprite skins (`Mod\Player\<Skin>\Animation|Portrait`,
PNG frames) and localization JSON (`Mod\Localize\<Name>\LocalizeTable*.json`), so it can't change gameplay.
MelonLoader would work equally well; BepInEx was picked as the usual IL2CPP default.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- All game code is in the `SiNiSistar2` assembly. **`SiNiSistar2.Manager.ManagerList`** exposes static getters for
  every manager: `PlayerStatus`, `Debugger`, `Damage`, `Time`, `Map`, `Event`, `Gallery`, `SaveData`, `Input`,
  `UIList`, and others. `ManagerList.HasCompletedFirstInitialize` is false until the game has booted; check it
  before touching anything.
- **`SiNiSistar2.Obj.PlayerStatusManager`** holds the player state:
  - `HP`, `MP` and `Durability` (clothing) are all subclasses of `BattleMainParameter`, which has `Current`,
    `Max`, `SetCurrentValue(int, bool silent)`, `Sub(int, bool)`, `Recover` and `DontSub`.
  - `RecoverHP/RecoverMP/RecoverDurability(RecoverCalcType{Rate, DirectValue, Additive}, value, ...)`.
  - `Relics` is the currency. Its setter is private; use `AddRelics(int n, bool addGameOver, bool immediate)`
    or `SubRelics`.
  - `InventoryHandler.AddItem(ItemID, count)`, `GetItemCount`, `RemoveItem`; `EquipWand(ItemID)`.
  - `DamageInvincible` is a getter only (computed), so patch it with a Harmony postfix.
- `ItemID` is in the global namespace, with values 0–29 (for example `PortionHP`=0, `Elixir`=27, and wands
  `WeaponYew/WeaponAspen/WeaponSwordWand/WeaponTranquebar/WandIron/WeaponWeak`).
- Enemies are `EnemyObject : SiNiObject`, and `SiNiObject.HP` is the same `HP : BattleMainParameter` type, so a
  single prefix on `BattleMainParameter.Sub` can tell player and enemy apart by comparing the instance pointer with
  `PlayerStatus.HP/MP/Durability`.
- A developer **`Debugger`** manager ships in the build with flags such as `IsPlayerSuperTough`,
  `CriticalDamage`, `IsOverwriteDamage/OverwriteDamageValue` and `StopEnemyPoiseIncrementRecover`. It is not
  yet known whether it is instantiated in release builds or whether gameplay code reads these flags.
- Input uses the **new Input System**: read keys with `UnityEngine.InputSystem.Keyboard.current.f1Key`.
- The save folder is `%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Uu\SiNiSistar2\SaveData_S`.

## Build steps
1. Back up the save folder.
2. Unzip BepInEx 6 be.788 IL2CPP win-x64 into the game folder. Launch once and wait for
   `Chainloader startup complete` in `BepInEx/LogOutput.log`.
3. Create a `BasePlugin` and in `Load()` call `new Harmony(guid).PatchAll(typeof(Patches))` and
   `AddComponent<CheatMenu>()`. The MonoBehaviour needs the `(IntPtr)` constructor.
4. In the menu MonoBehaviour, `OnGUI` calls `GUI.Window(id, rect, (GUI.WindowFunction)Draw, title)`. Draw only with
   `GUI.Label`/`GUI.Button`/`GUI.DragWindow` and hand-computed `Rect`s (see Gotcha 1).
5. Patches:
   - a prefix on `BattleMainParameter.Sub` that returns false for the player's bars when the matching cheat is on,
     and raises `sub` for non-player `HP` (`TryCast<HP>()`) when one-hit or a multiplier is on;
   - a postfix on the `PlayerStatusManager.DamageInvincible` getter.
6. Every frame, top up the bars with `SetCurrentValue(Max)` while the infinite toggles are on.
7. `dotnet build -c Release` with a post-build Copy into `BepInEx/plugins`. Close the game first, because it locks
   the DLL.

## Verification
The oracle was the real game: load a save, press F1, click buttons, and check full-resolution screenshots
(`um win shot`) and the HUD, plus `BepInEx/LogOutput.log`.
- Verified: the menu opens and closes and shows live HP/MP/clothing values. Refill took clothing from 0 to 100, and
  the portrait changed. +1000 relics changed the HUD from 44 to 1,044. Give+equip of `WeaponAspen` worked, and the
  portrait wand changed. Items +1/+10 took `PortionHP` from 0 to 11 and `Elixir` from 0 to 10.
- God mode was verified by the human in real fights: with god mode on and infinite durability off, HP never drops,
  but clothing durability still takes damage. Player HP and clothing are separate `BattleMainParameter`s, so the
  toggles are independent. The log showed `BattleMainParameter.Sub hook active` with no errors, which confirms that
  `Sub` is the damage path. The human reported the rest of the menu working as intended; I did not separately
  measure the damage multiplier or crit.

## Gotchas
1. **IMGUI calls throw `NotSupportedException: Method unstripping failed`.** **Cause:** the game never used
   `GUILayout.Toolbar` (and probably other GUILayout helpers), so IL2CPP stripped them, and Il2CppInterop
   could not restore the body. `GUI.Window` still drew its frame, but the window function threw. **Fix:** build
   the UI only from `GUI.Label`, `GUI.Button` and `GUI.DragWindow` with manual `Rect` layout. Draw toggles as
   `[ON]/[off]` buttons and the slider as -/+ buttons, and use tabs instead of a scroll view.
2. **`GUILayout.X(..., null)` causes compiler error CS0121 (ambiguous call).** **Cause:** the interop generates
   both an `Il2CppReferenceArray<GUILayoutOption>` overload and a `params GUILayoutOption[]` overload. **Fix:**
   pass no options argument at all.
3. **Cpp2IL 2022.0.7 is too old.** **Cause:** metadata v31 (Unity 2022.3). **Fix:** use the
   `2022.1.0-pre-release.x` line.
4. **Mouse clicks do nothing on the title menu.** **Cause:** the game's own menus are keyboard/gamepad-driven.
   **Fix:** to automate, press Enter on splash, Enter on Continue (preselected), then wait about 15 s to load.
   IMGUI windows do receive mouse clicks normally.
5. **Building fails with MSB3027 "file is locked by SiNiSistar2.exe".** **Cause:** BepInEx keeps the plugin DLL
   open. **Fix:** kill the game by PID before building, or copy the DLL afterwards.
6. **Click coordinates computed from the IMGUI rect miss.** **Cause:** the IMGUI window position in the capture did
   not match the window rect in pixels (it rendered lower and further right than expected at 1920x1080 fullscreen).
   **Fix:** measure button positions from a screenshot and scale them back up, rather than computing them.
7. **`Plugin.Log` hides `BasePlugin.Log` (warning CS0108).** **Fix:** declare it as
   `internal static new ManualLogSource Log`.

## Assets
None.

## Cost and time
About 1 session (around 1.5 h wall-clock), including recon, dumping, two UI iterations and in-game checks.

## Open questions
- Is the `Debugger` manager non-null in release builds, and are its flags (`IsPlayerSuperTough`, `CriticalDamage`)
  read by gameplay code?
- Grab and instant-game-over events probably bypass HP entirely, so god mode won't stop them.
