# OpenTDU — Test Drive Unlimited source port

OpenTDU (`opentestdriveunlimited/OpenTestDriveUnlimited`) is an open-source **decompilation-based source port of Test Drive Unlimited PC (MC 1.66A)**. It reconstructs the original 32-bit x86 game — structs, classes and functions — in C++17 with Ghidra and reimplements the runtime on Vulkan. It ships **no game assets** and requires the user's own legal copy (`README.md:10`). It is explicitly **work in progress** (`README.md:6`); progress is tracked per game mode (VideoBumper and CarShowCase done; **FreeRide in progress**, `README.md:33-37`).

## Setup

- Clone recursively (third_party is a submodule): `git clone --recursive git@github.com:opentestdriveunlimited/OpenTestDriveUnlimited.git`.
- Prerequisites: CMake ≥ 3.15, a C++17 compiler, Vulkan SDK ≥ 1.3.204 (`README.md:17-20`, `CLAUDE.md:23`).
- Own a legal copy of TDU PC MC 1.66A; the port reads the original `TestDriveUnlimited.exe` to extract packed config and shaders and cannot run without it.
- Run `opentdu_assetExtractor` **once before the first game run**; it pulls shaders + `.ini` from the original executable and generates SPIRV (`README.md:26-28`).

## Route and why

- **Route: decompilation-based reimplementation.** Not a binary patch, DLL proxy or emulator. The authors decompile the original with Ghidra and rewrite it in modern C++ (Vulkan instead of D3D9), reconstructing each function from P-Code (`CLAUDE.md:7`). It is not a clean-room reimplementation — it is derived from the retail binary.
- Engine is left `unknown`: the repo never names one. TDU1 predates the named Eden branding of later titles. (Disrupt and Anvil are Ubisoft engines used by the Watch Dogs and Assassin's Creed lines; they are unrelated to TDU.)
- TDU1 counterpart to the TDU2 NULL-pointer crash work elsewhere in this workspace; the two share RE conventions.

See also `games/test-drive-unlimited/savegame-and-config-formats.md` for the TDU1 `tdudec` XTEA variant, `commondt.sav`/`playersave` offsets and the `XMBF` container — independent RE of the same game's save/config data.

## How the game works

### RE workflow conventions

- Ghidra P-Code is cleaned **first**, then translated to the project's C++ style (`.clang-format`).
- Every reconstructed function carries its original address as the first body line, a `FUN_01234567`-style comment, to cross-reference Ghidra and the port (`CLAUDE.md:13`).
- `OTDU_UNIMPLEMENTED` marks a stub awaiting decompilation — asserts in dev builds, no-op in release (`CLAUDE.md:14,76`).
- `OTDU_SIZE_MUST_MATCH(Type, n)` statically asserts that a struct read directly from a disk asset exactly matches the on-disk byte size; required for any such struct (`CLAUDE.md:77`). E.g. `OTDU_SIZE_MUST_MATCH( FlashTag, 0x8 )` (`source/flash/implementation/flash_tags.h:30`).

### x86 pointer emulation

- The original TDU binary is 32-bit, and many asset formats embed 32-bit pointers fixed up at load time (`CLAUDE.md:82-84`).
- On 64-bit hosts, `x86Pointer_t` / `OTDUPointer` (`source/x86_pointer_emulation.h`) stores a 32-bit `ID` and resolves the real pointer through a runtime pointer cache (`gPointerRegister`). A static assert pins it to 4 bytes: `static_assert( sizeof( x86Pointer_t ) == 4, "Must match to ensure correct assets loading!" )` (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:87-88`).
- The copy operator deliberately copies the **pointed-to value**, not the cache ID, so two pointers don't alias one register slot — matching the 32-bit build (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:23-30`).
- Asset pointers migrate to a widened native layout via `AssetPtr<T>`, `GeoPtr<T>` (3DG meshes: `3dg.h`, `geometry_buffer.h`) and `ScenePtr<T>` (3DD scenes: `3dd.h`), each gated by its own `OTDU_NATIVE_MATERIAL` / `OTDU_NATIVE_3DG` / `OTDU_NATIVE_3DD` flag (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:90-139`). An "asset upgrader" will repack 32-bit-pointer blobs into native layout so `x86Pointer_t` can be retired.

### Flash / SWF UI (`.vmf`)

- `source/flash/` reconstructs an SWF runtime: tags, sprites, ActionScript interpreter, display list (`CLAUDE.md:86-94`). Header reference: `https://www.m2osw.com/swf_tags` (`flash_tags.h:10`).
- Historical quirk: during `.vmf` parsing the original 32-bit build **overwrote the 32-bit tag-ID field with a vtable pointer and the tag-size field with a `pNextTag` pointer in place** (`flash_tags.h:13-17,32-37`). Because those had to fit 32-bit fields, the vtable could not be a C++ vtable — it is a hand-built `FlashTagVTable` struct of explicit function pointers (`Execute`, `Draw`, `Initialize`, `Destroy`, `GetType`) (`flash_tags.h:38-63`).
- Current x64 code instead **keeps** the on-disk `TagId`/`TagSize` (8-byte header) and derives the vtable and next tag at access time via `getVtable()` and `getNextTag()` (`flash_tags.h:18-29`). `OTDUPointer::reset()` clears a stale emulation ID before the first assignment onto raw asset bytes overlaid as a tag (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:13-19`).

### Filesystem and formats

- `source/filesystem/` holds the virtual filesystem and bank/archive readers. `bank.h` defines groups keyed by subfolder under `EURO/BNK/` (e.g. `AG_Vehicle = 9 → EURO/BNK/Vehicules`, `AG_Common = 0xe → */common_*.bnk`) and types `AT_3DD=0`, `AT_3DG=1`, `AT_TireProfile=2`/`AT_2DM`, `AT_2DB=3`, `AT_PhysicsBinary=4` (`source/filesystem/bank.h:4-30`).
- `source/player_data/` holds `Savegame { uint32_t saveIndex; SavedProfile profile; SavedCarReserve carReservations; }` (`source/player_data/save_game.h:6-15`), plus profiles, garage, eBay state and a save-game manager (`saved_garage.*`, `saved_ebay_state.*`, `save_game_manager.*`).
- `source/core/` holds CRC32/CRC64 hashing, TEA crypto, BCPL random and threading (`CLAUDE.md:50`); `source/physics/` is a **Jolt** integration (`CLAUDE.md:56`).
- `opentdu_assetExtractor` (`tools/asset_extractor/main.cpp`) walks a compiled-in master shader table, seeks each entry to `OffsetInExecutable - 0x400000` (PE image base), validates the D3D9 `CTAB` marker and reads 16-bit words until the `0xffff` end marker (`main.cpp:390-413`); translates each DXSO shader to SPIRV via bundled DXVK `dxso`, optionally to GLSL via SPIRV-Cross with `-gen_shader_source` (`main.cpp:427-522`; `imgui`/`dbg_font` load from precompiled `.dxso` `.bin`, `main.cpp:352-384`); and unpacks six XOR-obfuscated `.ini` blobs baked into the exe (`readByte ^= currentByte`, `main.cpp:91-104`) at `SystemPC.ini @0x00f9c460`, `GamePC.ini @0x00f9c7b8`, `DevicesPC.ini @0x00f9dc68`, `Audio.ini @0x00f9f1b0`, `Replay.ini @0x00fa0418`, `Physics.ini @0x00fa0820` (`main.cpp:72-88`). Args: `-executable`, `-asset_output_path`, `-skip_glsl`, `-force`, `-gen_shader_source` (`main.cpp:123-138`).

## Build steps

```sh
./build_unix.sh                 # Linux / macOS: builds third_party, then port
build_win.bat x64               # Windows x64 (value passed to CMake -A)
```

- `build_unix.sh:2-16` builds `third_party` via `build_thirdparty.sh`, then runs `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release` and `cmake --build . --parallel=12`.
- Incremental: same cmake configure then `cmake --build build -j$(nproc)` (`CLAUDE.md:31-35`).
- Output lands in `build/bin/` (`OTDU_BIN_FOLDER`, `CMakeLists.txt:9`; `CLAUDE.md:37`). Port binary is `opentdu_<platform>_vulkan` (or `opentdu_unix_vulkan` / `opentdu_darwin_vulkan`) (`CMakeLists.txt:761-765`).
- Tools are separate CMake targets added at `CMakeLists.txt:805-807`: `opentdu_assetExtractor` (`tools/asset_extractor/CMakeLists.txt:13`), `opentdu_savedecryptor` (`tools/save_decryptor/CMakeLists.txt:5`), `opentdu_zcuncompressor` (`tools/zc_uncompressor/CMakeLists.txt:7`); flavours append `_${CMAKE_GENERATOR_PLATFORM}` / `_unix` / `_darwin`.
- There is **no test suite** (`CLAUDE.md:37`).

## Verification

Verified by **reading source** on 2026-10-05: project shape, prerequisites, build scripts and output dir (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `build_unix.sh`, `build_win.bat`, `CMakeLists.txt:9,690,805-807`); tool names, CLI args and behaviour (`tools/*/main.cpp`, `tools/*/CMakeLists.txt`); `x86Pointer_t` layout, 4-byte assert, value-copy semantics and migration flags (`source/x86_pointer_emulation.h`); Flash tag header handling and hand-built `FlashTagVTable` (`source/flash/implementation/flash_tags.h`); zlib load path and reversed-magic check (`source/filesystem/file_direct_access.cpp:281-320`, `file_direct_access.h:43`); bank groups/types (`source/filesystem/bank.h:4-30`); save struct (`source/player_data/save_game.h:6-15`); TEA schedule (`source/core/crypto/tea.h:3-22`).

**NOT run:** I did not build, launch or run any tool or the game, and no game assets, binaries or the original executable were executed. Args and addresses above are as read from source, not confirmed at runtime.

## Gotchas

1. **Black screen / missing shaders on first run** → asset extractor never run → run `opentdu_assetExtractor` once (extracts shaders + config from the original exe and generates SPIRV; `README.md:26-28`).
2. **Stale assets used instead of fresh ones** → existing outputs are skipped → pass `-force` to overwrite (`main.cpp:57-61,169`).
3. **Garbled pointers reading asset structs on 64-bit** → an on-disk struct with embedded 32-bit pointers was treated as native → use `x86Pointer_t` / `AssetPtr<T>` and keep the 4-byte static assert (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:87-88`).
4. **Flash UI crashes / aliased ActionScript pointers** → copying an `OTDUPointer` by cache ID aliased two pointers into one register slot (e.g. advancing `FlashAction::pActions` moved `pCurrentAction`) → the copy operator copies the pointed-to value, and `reset()` must precede the first assignment onto raw `.vmf` bytes (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:13-30`, `flash_tags.h:32-37`).
5. **No backend fallback** → the renderer is **Vulkan-only** (`CLAUDE.md:98`).
6. **No regression net** → there is **no test suite** (`CLAUDE.md:37`); changes are validated by running the game.
7. **`-skip_glsl` confusion** → GLSL is optional and only emitted with `-gen_shader_source`; omitting it does not break the Vulkan path (`main.cpp:50-55,234-245`).
8. **`opentdu_savedecryptor` writes to a hardcoded path** `D:/playersave_out.sav` (`tools/save_decryptor/main.cpp:64`); on systems without a `D:` drive the write can fail — the tool still demonstrates the TEA block logic.

## Assets

- **None distributed.** The port deliberately ships no game assets (`README.md:10`). Shaders and six packed `.ini` configs are extracted from the user's own `TestDriveUnlimited.exe`; everything else is read from the user's installed copy (banks under `EURO/BNK/`, save files).
- `vmf_to_swf.py` (`tools/`) converts the game's `.vmf` UI files to standard SWF for inspection.

## Cost and time

- The first build compiles the third-party tree (SDL, JoltPhysics, DXVK pieces, Vulkan-Headers, VMA, zlib, SPIRV tooling) — the bulk of the time; rebuilds are incremental (`CLAUDE.md:31-35`).
- `opentdu_assetExtractor` is a one-time step per install (unless `-force`); it translates every shader in the master table, so expect a few minutes (`main.cpp:336-339` logs progress every 100 shaders).
- A Vulkan SDK ≥ 1.3.204 and matching drivers are mandatory.

## Open questions

- **Which engine is TDU1?** The repo never names one; left `unknown`.
- **Asset-upgrader plan**: the per-type flags (`OTDU_NATIVE_MATERIAL`, `OTDU_NATIVE_3DG`, `OTDU_NATIVE_3DD`) are transitional; no unified flag or completed rewriter exists (`x86_pointer_emulation.h:90-139`).
- **`FlashTagVTable` retirement**: the code comments wish for a `.vmf`/`.2db`/`.2dm` asset rewriter so x86 pointer emulation can be dropped (`flash_tags.h:36-37`) — not implemented.
- **ZC magic value / `getZCMagic()`**: the reversed-bits check is present (`file_direct_access.cpp:305-312`) but the constant itself was not traced.
- **FreeRide completeness**: only VideoBumper and CarShowCase are Done; FreeRide is in progress (`README.md:33-37`).
- **Savegame coverage**: unclear from headers alone how much of `Savegame`/`SavedProfile` is implemented vs `OTDU_UNIMPLEMENTED`.

# TDU savegame encryption and the CarVST/XMBF container

> Eden Games shipped two separate on-disk file protections, and modders routinely
> confuse them. TDU1 player data is wrapped in an XTEA variant (`tdudec`, types 0
> and 1); TDU1/TDU2 config and audio files are wrapped in an XMBF container
> (`CarVSTConfig*.xmb`, `SystemDefault`). This note records the algorithms, the
> key layout, the file paths per game, and the byte-level offsets that are known.
> Status is deliberately **in-progress**: the XTEA and XMBF formats are solved and
> tools exist, but TDU2's PC save layout is still undocumented.

## Setup

- **TDU1 (Atari / Eden Games, 2006) PC.** Save directory:
  `%USERPROFILE%/Documents/Test Drive Unlimited/savegame/`. Contains
  `commondt.sav` (account data), `playersave` (character/progress), and
  `ProfileList.dat` (plaintext profile-name registry).
- **TDU2 (Eden Games, 2011) PC.** Save directory:
  `%USERPROFILE%/Documents/Eden Games/Test Drive Unlimited 2/savegame/`.
  Layout differs: profiles are directories `<Profile>/PLAYERSAVE/{DATA,KEYMAP,OPTIONS}`
  plus `ProfileList.dat` at the root. The PC `PLAYERSAVE/DATA` is **not** XTEA
  ciphertext — see "TDU2 differences" below.
- Building the reference tool (`tdudec`): `gcc tdudec.c -o tdudec`. Single C file,
  no deps, GPL-2.0. A prebuilt `tdudec.exe` ships alongside it for Windows.
- The Rust editor (`tdu_savegame_account_editor`) is a separate cargo project
  (`TDU_savegame_account_editor/`); build with `cargo build --release`. It ports
  the XTEA core to `src/tdudec.rs` and the hashing to `src/util.rs`.
- The XMBF tools (workspace-local `carvst editor/`, unpublished) need only Python 3
  stdlib, or JDK 8+ for the Swing GUI.
- All analysis was read-only; save/config edits are done on copies.

## Route and why

- **Route: `data`** — pure on-disk file-format work. The algorithms are public
  (`tdudec`) and the container is reversible, so the shortest path is
  decrypt → edit bytes → re-encrypt, with no executable patching.
- **Why not a native hook:** the encryption key is static and shipped in the
  executable; there is no runtime check worth defeating. Decryption is a
  stdlib-style transform, so a standalone tool is enough.
- The one place a hook *is* justified (TDU2 gauges, TDU1 savedata integrity-hash
  mismatch) is documented in the sibling note and `offsets_and_formats.md` but is
  out of scope here.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### 1. Save/config encryption — `tdudec` (XTEA variant)

The algorithm is **standard XTEA with 32 rounds** and the canonical delta
`0x9E3779B9`. The `tdudec` code expresses the delta as `0x61C88647` added per
round on encrypt; since `0x61C88647 == -(0x9E3779B9)` mod 2^32, adding it is the
same as subtracting `0x9E3779B9` — i.e. standard XTEA. Data is processed as
independent 8-byte blocks (`u32 y, z` in little-endian). There is no per-block
chaining in type 0.

`tdudec.c` holds a single 32-byte key buffer holding **two 16-byte keys
concatenated**. The raw bytes are public in the source; they are deliberately not
reproduced here — the key *layout* is what matters:

- **`SAVE_KEY`** (first 16 bytes) — used for `type 0`, TDU1 savegame/playersave files.
- **`OTHERS_KEY`** (second 16 bytes) — used for `type 1`, everything else
  (`.btrq`, `.db`, `.cpr` config files, and the "special type").

| | type 0 — savegame | type 1 — others |
|---|---|---|
| key used | first 16 bytes | second 16 bytes (offset +16) |
| header | none | 8-byte header skipped on decrypt |
| block select | `y=d[0], z=d[1]` | `y=d[2], z=d[3]` (XOR-chain) |
| decrypt write | `d[0]=y, d[1]=z` | `d[0]^=y, d[1]^=z` |

Type 1 is **XOR-chained**: block *i*'s first 8 bytes are used as an IV/feedback
for the ciphertext that follows, so tampering with one block corrupts the next.
Type 0 has no such coupling — a plain XTEA decrypt of the whole file.

**Encrypting a type-1 file** prepends the 8-byte header that decrypt strips:
`u32 timestamp` followed by `u32 ~timestamp` (bitwise NOT), both little-endian.
The C tool uses `time(NULL)`; the Rust port writes the constants `42` and `!42`
(see Gotchas). Because the header is a plain timestamp, re-encrypting an unmodified
file still produces a different byte stream than the original even when the body
is identical.

Round-trip note: `tdudec d` then `tdudec e` does **not** reproduce the original
bytes for type 1 (new timestamp) and, in the Rust port, may pad (see Gotchas 3).

Config files that go through type 1 (`.txt` ↔ `.cpr`):
`Physics`, `Quality_Settings`, `Shadows`, `SystemPC`, `GamePC`.
`./tdudec e Physics.txt Physics.cpr 1`.

### 2. Account hashing (TDU1)

`playersave` stores a CRC-32-family digest of the nickname/email/password so
`commondt.sav` and `playersave` must agree. `src/util.rs::hash_byte_string`
reimplements it: a 256-entry CRC table generated with polynomial `0xEDB88320`
(the reflected CRC-32 polynomial), an update loop
`uVar1 = uVar1 >> 8 ^ pad[(byte ^ uVar1) & 0xff]`, then the final value is
bitwise-NOT-ed and emitted **big-endian**. The comments pin the original
locations in the **TDU 1.66a** executable: table build at `0x00622f50`, update
loop at `0x00624440`. On disk the hashes are stored little-endian-at-offset as
`u32` (the tool writes `to_be_bytes()` into the save — the two disagree on paper;
trust the tool output, see Gotchas 5).

### 3. TDU1 decrypted layout (offsets)

`commondt.sav` (decrypted with tdudec type 0):

| Offset | Size | Field |
|--------|------|-------|
| `0x91` | 1 | `01` = online, `00` = offline |
| `0x98`–`0xB7` | 32 | nickname (null-padded, ≤30 bytes usable) |
| `0xBA`–`0xED` | 52 | email (≤50 bytes) |
| `0xF0`–`0x10F` | 32 | password (≤30 bytes) |

`playersave` (decrypted with tdudec type 0):

| Offset | Size | Field |
|--------|------|-------|
| `0x06`–`0x07` | 2 | sensitive to nickname + online state; purpose unresolved |
| `0x08`–`0x0B` | 4 | nickname hash |
| `0x0C`–`0x0F` | 4 | email hash (`0` when offline) |
| `0x10`–`0x13` | 4 | password hash (`0` when offline) |
| `0x1A`–`0x39` | 32 | nickname (plaintext) |

`ProfileList.dat` is **plaintext**, not encrypted: a sequence of length-prefixed
profile names, each `<u16_le len><bytes>`, terminated by an `0xFF`-sentinel
trailer (`write_profile_list` emits `ff ff 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00` after the
last name). The two bytes that follow the trailer encode the active profile
(`0x96 0x8B` = first active, `0xF7 0x0C` = second) and appear to be a hash of the
active name — writing `00 00` is accepted.

Memory-side (from Ghidra/x64dbg, for the optional hook route):
`0x0089A730` parses and checks playersave against nickname/email/password;
`0x0089A79E` reads the three hashes from the decrypted buffer; `0x00624880`
computes them. The hash check can be NOP-ed so any playersave pairs with any
commondt.

### 4. The XMBF container (CarVST/TDU audio config)

`CarVSTConfig*.xmb` (sampled: `CarVSTConfig.xmb`, `CarVSTConfig3.xmb`,
`CarVSTConfig5.xmb`; a standalone copy also lives at `TDU-CarVST-Config/CarVSTConfig.xmb`)
is the per-car vehicle-audio config. Format name "XMBF", version `0x00000101`,
all little-endian.

Header (28 bytes):

| Offset | Size | Field |
|--------|------|-------|
| `0x00` | 4 | magic `"XMBF"` |
| `0x04` | 4 | version `0x00000101` |
| `0x08` | 4 | string-pool offset (always `0x1C`) |
| `0x0C` | 4 | schema-table offset |
| `0x10` | 4 | data-section offset |
| `0x14` | 4 | count1 |
| `0x18` | 4 | count2 |

Three sections follow the header: a **string pool** (null-terminated Latin-1
strings), a **schema table** (8-byte entries pairing a name-string index and a
type-flags word; first 5 entries are typedefs), and the **data section**.

Data section header: `+0` `wav_count u32`, `+12` `bank_count u32`, then
`wav_count` u32 WAV-pointer entries; records start at
`data_off + 24 + wav_count*4`.

Records are a fixed **82-byte stride**: `GAP(30) + BankBody(40) + CurveSet(12)`.
Each bank record carries an identity block (`nCarID`, `nWaveIndex`,
`nReverbInternal`, `fBaseVolume`, `bIsTrigger`, `nMustBeLooped`), clipping/tracking
factors (`fClipNear/Far`, `fRefractionFactor`, and `fTracking*`), and pointers into
the event data. `Bank` tag is `1` at record+30; `CurveSet` tag is `6` at record+70.

**Event blocks** are `[13 volume floats][EventName\0][descriptor bytes]` — the 13
floats sit *before* the name, not after. Indices 10/11/12 are Road/Tarmac, Grass and
Dirt volumes (confirmed); 0–9 are unlabelled. Event names follow the rule "first
char uppercase, second lowercase" (`RollingRoadExternal`, `EngineLoad_0`), which
is how the scanner separates event names from `SLIP_idle.wav`-style WAV filenames
and from schema strings. Descriptor bytes after the name are raw u32 pointers/ints;
for Engine events they chain RPM→pitch curves.

The same `XMBF` magic appears outside CarVST: TDU2's `SystemDefault` engine-settings
blob is also XMBF. So XMBF is a **shared Eden serialization container** across both
games, not audio-specific.

TDU1 controller/game configs also use this family — `DevicesPC.cpr` maps USB
VID/PID to per-device `.xmb` profiles.

### 5. TDU2 differences (why tools must not be crossed)

- TDU2 saves are **not** TDU1 saves. Different directory, different on-disk
  layout; running the TDU1 account editor on TDU2 saves corrupts them.
- TDU2's PC `PLAYERSAVE/DATA` is **not** tdudec XTEA ciphertext: it has no STFS
  (`CON`/`LIVE`/`PIRS`) or XMBF magic, and tdudec type 0 with the shipped key
  yields garbage. The retail TDU2 executable does contain an XTEA
  decrypt/encrypt pair (VA `0x95EA60`/`0x95EAD0`, ImageBase `0x400000`; initial
  sum `0xC6EF3720`, delta `0x61C88647` — the *same* variant), but its 16-byte key
  matches TDU1's `tdudec` key #1 and is used for `.btrq`/`.db` files, not the save.
- TDU2 save editors that exist are for the **Xbox 360 STFS** container (money at
  `0x4362`, etc.); those offsets land on random bytes in the PC `DATA`.

## Build steps

```sh
# 1. Reference decrypt/encrypt tool
cd game-tools/TDU/tdudec
gcc tdudec.c -o tdudec

# 2. Decrypt a TDU1 save (type 0, default)
./tdudec d savegame/playersave playersave.dec
./tdudec d savegame/commondt.sav commondt.dec
# Re-encrypt after editing
./tdudec e playersave.edited playersave 0

# 3. Config files (type 1) — CRLF and trailing binary bytes required
./tdudec e Physics.txt Physics.cpr 1
./tdudec e Quality_Settings.txt Quality_Settings.cpr 1

# 4. XMBF audio config round-trip (local, unpublished carvst editor/ tools)
cd "<local carvst editor dir>"
python xmbf_convert.py verify CarVSTConfig.xmb   # byte-perfect check
python xmbf_convert.py to-xml CarVSTConfig.xmb
python xmbf_convert.py patch  CarVSTConfig.xmb  CarVSTConfig.xml out.xmb
```

## Verification

- **XTEA:** round-trips on TDU1 saves in the editor's dev helpers
  (`test_commondt_*`, `test_playersave_write`) and community use of upstream
  `Kethen/TDU_savegame_account_editor`. The type-0/type-1 split and 8-byte
  timestamp header are confirmed by reading `tdudec.c` and its Rust port side by
  side.
- **Hashing:** the two exe addresses (`0x00622f50`, `0x00624440`) were located in
  TDU 1.66a; the port matches observed save behaviour when renaming a profile.
- **XMBF:** `xmbf_convert.py verify` asserts a **byte-perfect** `xmb → xml → xmb`
  round-trip; bank stride (82) was confirmed by measuring 5 consecutive records,
  and Road/Grass/Dirt float indices by user confirmation.
- **Not verified / open:** the PC TDU2 `PLAYERSAVE/DATA` struct layout; where
  CarVST event-float indices 0–9 point; whether edited TDU1 saves survive any
  server-side account check; and the Rust `encrypt_others` padding correctness
  (see Gotchas).

## Gotchas

1. **Symptom:** config file edited in a text editor, re-encrypted with tdudec,
   game then crashes or silently ignores the setting. **Cause:** LF-only line
   endings and/or the trailing binary bytes after the last text line were
   stripped. **Fix:** keep CRLF (`unix2dos`), never strip the trailing bytes
   (inspect with `xxd` before/after), edit as raw bytes so French accents and
   trailing blobs survive.
2. **Symptom:** `tdudec e file.txt out.cpr 1` differs from the original `.cpr`
   even though the plaintext is unchanged. **Cause:** type 1 prepends a fresh
   8-byte `timestamp`/`~timestamp` header and XOR-chains from it. **Fix:** expected;
   compare *decrypted* bodies, not ciphertext.
3. **Symptom:** Rust `encrypt_others` output is larger/different than expected, or
   a re-encrypted config fails to decrypt cleanly. **Cause:**
   `src/tdudec.rs` pads with `input.len() % 32` bytes (remainder, only when ≥1
   block) instead of the exact `32 - (len % 32)` needed for alignment, and writes
   a fixed `42`/`!42` header rather than a timestamp. **Fix:** for byte-exact
   configs prefer the C `tdudec`; treat the Rust port as save-oriented. Re-check
   against the C tool before trusting it on type 1.
4. **Symptom:** TDU2 save corrupted after using a TDU1 tool. **Cause:** the two
   games use different save containers (TDU2 PC `DATA` is not XTEA-wrapped).
   **Fix:** never run `tdudec`/the account editor on TDU2 saves; use the TDU2
   notes (`tdu2-savegame-and-gauge-formats.md`).
5. **Symptom:** nickname/email/password edit accepted in the editor but the game
   rejects the profile. **Cause:** `playersave` and `commondt.sav` hash fields
   disagree. **Fix:** update **both** files together (`patch_commondt` +
   `patch_playersave`); offline saves use zero email/password digests. The
   byte-order comments in `util.rs` (`to_be_bytes` written into the save) are the
   reference — trust the tool, not a naïve re-derivation.
6. **Symptom:** XMBF `patch` throws "Missing `<RawSections>`" or produces a
   non-matching file. **Cause:** the XML was hand-written instead of produced by
   `to-xml`; field editing requires preserving the base64 raw blobs.
   **Fix:** always `to-xml` first, edit only the decoded field nodes, then `patch`.
7. **Symptom:** event names or banks missed in the XMBF decode. **Cause:**
   naïve scanning picks up float bytes that look like ASCII (e.g. `1.0` =
   `0x3F800000` leaks `?`), or matches WAV names as events. **Fix:** use the
   strict whitelist + "uppercase-first/lowercase-second" event rule and the
   82-byte stride scanner already in `xmbf_convert.py`; don't re-anchor on `?`.
## Assets

No art/audio generated. Relevant reference material:

- `tdudec.c` — canonical XTEA implementation + key layout (GPL-2.0, Luigi

- `tdu_savegame_account_editor/TDU_savegame_account_editor/src/tdudec.rs` — Rust

  `commondt`/`playersave`/`ProfileList` read-write, plus

## Open questions

kind: game
title: "Binding of Terraria: Terraria bosses, weapons, minions and a hotbar inside Isaac Repentance+"

# Binding of Terraria: Terraria bosses, weapons, minions and a hotbar inside Isaac Repentance+

> A vanilla Isaac Lua mod (no native hooks) that swaps every Isaac boss, story bosses included, for one of
> sixteen Terraria bosses at spawn time (custom themed boss rooms, versus screens and completion marks to
> match), puts 21 Terraria weapons and 12 summon staffs into the item pools with a 1-0 hotbar that replaces
> tears, and runs Terraria sprites and sounds converted from the player's own Terraria install. Verified in
> the real game by screenshots and a recorded clip: real boss rooms show the versus screen with the Terraria
> boss, the fight runs, the room clears, and Mom's and It Lives' rooms still hand out the Polaroid/Negative,
> trapdoor and beam of light.

## Setup
- Isaac: Repentance+ v1.9.7.17 (Steam 250900). Mods folder is `<install>/mods` (savedatapath.txt in the
  install folder says so; the Documents folder only holds options.ini and log.txt). Saves are in Steam
  userdata, backed up with `um backup create` first.
- `options.ini`: `EnableMods=1`, `EnableDebugConsole=1`, `Fullscreen=0` for stable screenshots.
- The mod folder is an NTFS junction (`mklink /J`) from the mods folder to the git repo's `mod/`.
- Terraria 1.4.5.8 for assets only (never launched). node 24 + `npm install github:LeonBlade/xnbcli`.
- `um win setup` for the gfxcapture ffmpeg; add `%LOCALAPPDATA%\universal-modder\ffmpeg\bin` to PATH for
  `um video`.

## Route and why
Mashup pattern 1 in `skills/mashup-mods/SKILL.md` (port the content into the host) + asset conversion.
Isaac's Lua API covers everything in the brief: custom NPCs with Lua AI (bosses), custom collectibles and item pools, custom familiars, a HUD
drawn in MC_POST_RENDER, keyboard input. Terraria as host was rejected because the user wanted Isaac's
characters and runs. No decompiling of either game was needed.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Entity types.** Custom NPCs use a type id vanilla doesn't use (790; vanilla types jump from 413 to 801,
  effects are 1000) with explicit variants; `Isaac.GetEntityTypeByName` / `GetEntityVariantByName` resolve them. Types >= 10
  are EntityNPC; type 3 = familiar, 1000 = effect.
- **Boss replacement.** `MC_PRE_ENTITY_SPAWN(type, variant, subtype, pos, vel, spawner, seed)` returning
  `{790, v, 0, seed}` replaces the vanilla boss before its init, for room-placed bosses and console `spawn`.
  Room clear, boss drop and trapdoor still work because the replacement entity has `boss="1"`. Larry Jr /
  Pin rooms place several segment entities, so extra spawns are turned into a poof effect.
- **Boss rooms** all live in `00.special rooms.stb` in Repentance (not the stage files); the game picks the
  boss from the stage's boss pool, then a boss room whose `subtype` equals that boss's BossType id. A mod's
  `content/rooms/00.special rooms.stb` with weight 40 rooms per boss id wins almost every floor. The STB1
  binary layout is Basement Renovator's `commonToSTBAB`; `tools/gen_rooms.py` writes it from Python.
- **Story bosses** can be replaced the same way (Mom 45.0, Mom's Heart 78.0/78.1, Isaac 102.0/1/2, Satan
  84.0, Lamb 273.0, Mega Satan 274.0, Hush 407, Delirium 412, Mother 912.0/912.10). The outcome of those
  rooms (Polaroid/Negative, trapdoor, beam of light) comes from Isaac's room-clear logic, not from the
  boss entity's death, so a replacement boss with `boss="1"` is enough. Their rooms place the vanilla
  entity several times (Mom x5), so dedupe with `Isaac.CountEntities`.
- **Completion marks** are 16x16 cells in `gfx/ui/completion_widget.png` and `completion_widget_pause.png`
  (384x384 on Repentance+; one row per difficulty, red at y=96 and dark at y=112: Polaroid 0, Negative
  16, Cross 32, Upside-down cross 48, Heart 64, Star 80, Mega Satan 96 and 112, Hush 128, Greed 144, then
  three newer marks). A plain PNG override in the mod's resources changes them, as long as it keeps that
  size and layout (gotcha 20).
- **Player look-alikes without touching the player anm2**: hide the body with `player.Color =
  Color(1,1,1,0,0,0,0)` each MC_POST_PLAYER_UPDATE (costumes go with it) and draw your own `Sprite` in
  MC_POST_PLAYER_RENDER at `Isaac.WorldToScreen(player.Position)`; nothing else in the game cares.
- **Character select sheet** `gfx/ui/main menu/charactermenu.png` (512x1024): 48x48 portrait cells
  (positions in characterportraits.anm2) and 80x32 name cells (charactermenu.anm2); a plain PNG override
  in `resources/` works on Repentance+ as long as the size stays 512x1024.
- **Versus screen** uses the room's original boss portrait; override `gfx/ui/boss/portrait_<id>_<name>.png`
  (192x192) and `bossname_<id>_<name>.png` (176x38) in the mod's resources. Rebirth-era bosses are numbered by
  entity type (20.0_monstro); newer ones by a different boss id (276.0_gurglings) or not at all
  (turdlings) - match by name. The exact file list is in `tools/ResourceExtractor/filelist.txt`.
- **anm2 format**: generated from Python (one spritesheet, one layer, frames crop a vertical strip). The
  `<Spritesheet Path>` is relative to the anm2's own folder.
- **Tears with custom sprites**: `player:FireTear(...)`, then `tear:GetSprite():Load(anm2, true)` and
  `FallingAcceleration < 0` so they never land; TearFlags give bounce/homing/pierce/boomerang for free.
- **Suppressing tears** while a weapon is selected: `player.FireDelay = max(FireDelay, 2)` each
  MC_POST_PEFFECT_UPDATE; `player:GetShootingInput()` gives the aim.
- **Familiars**: `player:CheckFamiliar(variant, count, RNG(), itemConfig)` in MC_EVALUATE_CACHE with
  CACHE_FAMILIARS; contact damage in MC_PRE_FAMILIAR_COLLISION; ranged minions `Isaac.Spawn` tears with
  the familiar as spawner (they count as player tears).
- **Hostile projectiles with custom sprites**: `npc:FireProjectiles` + MC_POST_PROJECTILE_INIT reading the
  spawner's data to `Sprite:Load` the Terraria sprite.
- **Item pools**: `MC_PRE_GET_COLLECTIBLE(poolType, decrease, seed)` returning a collectible id swaps the
  pull; a mod `content/itempools.xml` with `<Item Name=...>` also adds custom items to vanilla pools.
- **Terraria sprites**: XNB with LZX (flags 0x80); xnbcli decodes them. NPC sheets are vertical strips;
  frame count = Terraria's npcFrameCount (sheet height / frame count). Unrotated sprites face down, so
  rotation = atan2(dy, dx) - 90 degrees, exactly like Terraria's own code.
- **Isaac.ExecuteCommand** runs console commands from Lua (`restart`, `stage 1`, `debug 3`, `spawn 20`).
  Debug flags toggle.
- **Only the first MC_PRE_ENTITY_SPAWN callback that returns a value runs**; a second callback that only
  observes never fires once the first returned a replacement.
- **Input.IsButtonTriggered inside a 30 fps update callback misses short key presses**; poll
  `Input.IsButtonPressed` in MC_POST_RENDER (60 fps) and edge-detect yourself.

## Build steps
1. `um backup create` the Steam userdata save folder and the Documents options folder.
2. Set the options.ini flags; junction the repo's `mod/` into `<install>/mods/binding-of-terraria`.
3. `python tools/import_terraria.py` (xnbcli, then re-save PNGs with Pillow, fit 32x32 icons),
   `python tools/gen_anm2.py`, `python tools/gen_hud.py`, `python tools/gen_portraits.py`.
4. content/entities2.xml (bosses, minions, effects), items.xml, itempools.xml, sounds.xml; scripts in Lua.
5. Launch via Steam (`um win launch --steam 250900`), start a run, iterate with `luamod binding-of-terraria`
   (Lua) or a restart (XML/anm2, or `clearcache` for anm2 only).

## Verification
- Oracle: the game's `log.txt` (`Isaac.DebugString`) plus `um win shot` screenshots read at 0.5 scale, and a
  file bridge (`tools/bridge.py` <-> `scripts/bridge.lua`, see gotcha 8) that runs arbitrary Lua in the
  running game and returns results through the log. All testing used the vanilla launch, no --luadebug.
- Verified: every boss spawns, animates, moves and dies (Death animation, gibs); boss rooms on fresh floors
  (Larry Jr -> Eater of Worlds, Gurglings -> King Slime, Turdling untouched before the mapping was widened)
  show the versus screen with the override portrait and name, fight, clear the room and spawn the trapdoor;
  hotbar draws, keys 1-0 switch, swords swing in the aim direction, projectiles fly, falling stars land,
  minions chase and hit, imps shoot; a 92 s recorded take cut into a 38 s showcase.
- Verified later: custom boss rooms chosen on 11/14 sampled floors; every story boss spawns and fights;
  Mom's room and It Lives' room resolve normally after the Terraria boss dies.
- Not verified: controller input for the hotbar keys; co-op; Greed mode; the endings after Isaac, Satan,
  ???, Lamb, Mega Satan, Hush, Delirium and Mother (only Mom and It Lives were played through); The Beast
  and Dogma are untouched; balance (damage multipliers are guesses).

## Gotchas
1. **Boss spawns, health bar shows, nothing drawn, no log line.** Cause: the anm2's `<Spritesheet Path>`
   was written relative to `gfx/` ("terraria/x.png"); it is relative to the anm2 file's folder.
   `Sprite:IsLoaded()` still returns true. Fix: bare file name next to the anm2.
2. **Still invisible after the path fix.** Cause: PNGs written by xnbcli (pngjs) did not display. Fix:
   re-save every converted PNG with Pillow (`Image.open(p).convert("RGBA").save(p)`); the importer does it.
3. **`Sprite:HasAnimation` is nil.** Vanilla Repentance+ has no such method (REPENTOGON does). Just `Play`.
4. **Console `luamod` and `clearcache` close the console**; the rest of the typed batch goes into the game
   as WASD movement. Reopen the console after each.
5. **Console key on a UK keyboard is VK 0xDF (OEM_8)**, the key left of 1, not 0xC0. The first character
   typed after reopening sometimes becomes a stray space; send a Backspace first.
6. **`MC_EXECUTE_CMD` never fired for us on Repentance+ (v1.9.7.17).** Not a name collision: `bot`,
   `terraria` and `botx` typed in the console all just print the console's command list,
   `Isaac.ExecuteCommand("botx 1")` from Lua is silent too, and
   `Isaac.GetCallbacks(ModCallbacks.MC_EXECUTE_CMD)` shows the handler registered. IsaacDocs still says the
   callback is skipped only for the game's own commands. `lua <code>` works, and so does
   `Isaac.ExecuteCommand` for the game's own commands.
7. **Launching isaac-ng.exe directly with `--luadebug` blocks every later Steam launch.** Steam holds a
   hidden "launch with arguments?" dialog (`LaunchApp waiting for user response to ShowGameArgs` in
   Steam's console_log.txt). Fix: `steam.exe -shutdown`, start Steam again, launch through Steam.
8. **Automation without --luadebug.** `include("bridge.cmd")` re-reads the file from disk on every call, so
   a mod can poll `bridge/cmd.lua` every 10 render frames and run it when its `id` changes; results go to
   log.txt via `Isaac.DebugString`. Keep the last id in `_G` so a `luamod` reload does not re-run it, and
   ignore whatever the file holds at game start.
9. **Character select continues the previous run** (CONTINUE is preselected when a run exists). Use the
   console's `restart` for a fresh run; `stage N` regenerates a floor and the Level API
   (`level:GetRooms()`, `RoomType.ROOM_BOSS`, `game:StartRoomTransition(idx, Direction.NO_DIRECTION,
   RoomTransitionAnim.TELEPORT, player)`) teleports into its boss room. `goto s.boss` did nothing.
10. **`debug 3` toggles.** Calling it again per floor turned god mode off and the showcase player died.
11. **Spawning enemies into an already cleared boss room produced an instant death splash**; test spawns
    in a fresh room.
12. **Larry Jr rooms place several segment entities**; each became a full worm (4 worms). Dedupe in
    MC_PRE_ENTITY_SPAWN with `Isaac.CountEntities`.
13. **Isaac's shipped `tools/ResourceExtractor/ResourceExtractor.exe` seemed to write nothing.** Its first
    argument is the *input* (the game root; it appends `resources/packed` itself), so an output folder in
    that slot gives "No archive files found". Run it from its own folder with no arguments: it unpacks every
    `.a` of the install, Rep+ included (18.7k files, 1.2 GB), into `<game>/extracted_resources/resources*/`
    and logs each path to `ResourceExtractor_log.txt` next to it. That's where the vanilla anm2s and sheets
    for gotchas 20-21 come from. `filelist.txt` has the names.
14. **`um publish check --game` flags your own files** when the mod folder is a junction inside the game
    folder (it sees them as "game files copied verbatim"). Lint a `git archive` export instead.
15. **Hotbar vs boss bar.** Isaac's boss health bar sits at the bottom centre; draw the hotbar ~36 px up.
16. **Custom boss rooms in the stage files never get used.** `goto d.9000` found a test room in the mod's
    `01.basement.stb`, but boss rooms there were never picked. **Cause:** Repentance keeps every boss room
    in `00.special rooms.stb` (the console's `goto s.boss.<var>` searches stage id 0 and finds vanilla
    Basement boss rooms there). **Fix:** write them to `content/rooms/00.special rooms.stb`.
17. **Hotbar needed several presses.** `IsButtonTriggered` in MC_POST_PEFFECT_UPDATE (30 fps) misses
    presses shorter than a tick. **Fix:** edge-detect `IsButtonPressed` in MC_POST_RENDER.
18. **A sprite sheet that is a grid, not a strip** (Moon Lord's head, 573x804 = 3x3) shows three heads if
    cut as a vertical strip. Count transparent row gaps and columns before writing the anm2.
19. **Spawning a test boss in a room with pits** puts Isaac in a pit and respawns him at the door, so the
    screenshot shows no boss; test in plain rooms.
20. **Game hangs at file select, no log line, right after "Loading GameState".** Looks like a corrupt
    save; it is not. **Cause:** a 256x256 override of `gfx/ui/completion_widget.png` (Repentance's size
    and layout). Repentance+'s sheet is 384x384 with a new layout, 13 cells in one row (red/hard at
    y=96, dark at y=112, x=0..192: Polaroid, Negative, Cross, upside-down Cross, Heart, Star, two Mega
    Satan cells, Hush at 128, Greed at 144, three newer marks) and more paper variants, so its anm2
    crops past 256 px. Padding the 256 sheet to 512 stopped the hang but lost the character-select paper.
    **Fix:** start from the extracted Rep+ sheet (gotcha 13) and stamp at its coordinates, keeping
    384x384; same for `completion_widget_pause.png`. Bisect hangs by setting `EnableMods=0`, then
    removing overrides one at a time.
21. **Title-screen sheet override ignored.** `gfx/ui/main menu/titlemenu.png` (and `_2`, `_3`) in a mod's
    `resources/` changed nothing on Repentance+. **Cause:** Rep+ no longer keeps the logo in that sheet. Its
    `titlemenu.anm2` (extract it, gotcha 13) has `Logo` and `LogoShadow` layers that read
    `gfx/ui/main menu/logo.png` (480x320: logo in rows 0-159, its blurred shadow in rows 160-319);
    `titlemenu.png` only holds the background. This gotcha's earlier fix, an older (1.7.9b) `titlemenu.anm2`
    next to the PNG, only worked because that version still crops the logo from `titlemenu.png` at (0,272)
    480x111; don't use one. **Fix:** override `logo.png` alone, no anm2: keep "THE BINDING OF" from the
    vanilla top rows, paste your logo below, blur a grey copy into the bottom half. Verified on v1.9.7.17.
    The generator reads the vanilla `logo.png` from your own extraction (gotcha 13), so nothing from the
    game is committed or downloaded.

## Assets
All Terraria art and sound converted locally from the player's install by `tools/import_terraria.py`
(xnbcli unpack -> PNG/WAV, Pillow re-save, 32x32 nearest-neighbour icons from the item sprites, sizes.json
for the anm2 generator). Portraits are cut from the same sheets. The vanilla Isaac sheets the UI
generators start from (`logo.png`, `completion_widget.png`, `charactermenu.png`) are read from
`<game>/extracted_resources` (gotcha 13), not downloaded. The only committed art is the two hotbar
slot PNGs drawn with Pillow. No fal calls (the key had expired). The mod folder holds the converted
Terraria files and the UI sheets built from Isaac's own, so don't upload it to the Workshop as it is: share
the code and the importer, and let each player build from their own installs.

## Cost and time
One session, about 1 h 45 min wall clock from recon to showcase, most of it on the two invisible-sprite
causes (gotchas 1-2) and the console/Steam launch dance (gotchas 4-7).

## Open questions
- Versus-screen name plates use Impact; Isaac's hand-drawn font would fit better.
- Balance pass on damage/use times; Wall of Flesh for Mom and Moon Lord for Mom's Heart were not attempted
  because those fights have scripted room logic.
- Controller support for the hotbar (D-pad or bumpers).

# The Dark Legions Reloaded: crash fixes, a D3D8 -> D3D9Ex renderer, widescreen and new menus in one d3d8.dll

> **The Dark Legions Reloaded is a mod by GR33N**, built with Claude Code.
> The Dark Legions (Mascot Entertainment, 2004; in-house "Strategy 3" engine, 32-bit C++, Direct3D 8) crashed
> randomly after minutes of play and drew blue blotches on modern GPUs. One Rust `d3d8.dll` dropped next to
> the exe now fixes the crashes, replaces Direct3D 8 with its own D3D9Ex renderer (supersampling + MSAA +
> Lanczos, sharper than dgVoodoo2), adds true widescreen, rebuilt Video/Advanced/Interface/Audio menus,
> sharper fonts with Cyrillic, faster loading and a working cfg file. Verified by playing: a save that
> crashed within 2-8 minutes ran 49 minutes; every change was checked on screenshots by the player.

## Setup
- Retail install, `Dark Legions.exe` 1.1.0 (credits screen). The exe carries Windows compatibility flags
  (WinXP SP2) in HKCU, so it asks for UAC; tools that inject must handle that.
- Game data in one archive `s3tdl.med`; settings in `s3tdl.cfg`; audio settings in `players.prf`.
- The mod: `d3d8.dll` only. It writes `reloaded.ini` (commented defaults) and `reloaded.log` itself.

## Route and why
Native hooks from a proxy `d3d8.dll`. First tried: a `wsock32.dll` proxy for the patches plus dgVoodoo2 for
graphics. That worked, but needed two files and a config, and dgVoodoo could not fix things inside the
game's rendering (2D layout, menus). Making `d3d8.dll` ours gave one file and full control of every
draw. Every byte patch checks the original bytes first and logs instead of patching if they differ.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **The game logs everything to a disabled logger** (`#DEBUG:` lines through one function). Hooking it and
  writing the lines to our log was the single most useful source: texture names before each texture is
  created, screen names, load phases. We name textures by "Loading texture file:" / "Loading 2D Image:"
  lines and use the names to recognise screens (menus, HUD, splash) in the draw stream.
- **Crashes:** random heap corruption. Lists in the engine were re-initialised by setting their count to 0
  without clearing the nodes, so stale nodes kept pointers into freed memory. Calling the list's own Clear()
  before the reset (7 places) stopped it. A second crash was a dangling unit pointer after a tower is
  destroyed: a guard returns early. Objects with owner -1 read outside the players array: guarded.
- **Rendering:** projection with an infinite far plane (breaks table fog on today's drivers); the game turns
  D3DRS_CLIPPING off; asks for software vertex processing; rewrites managed vertex buffers hundreds of times
  per frame; the interface is XYZRHW quads in 1024x768 coordinates, big pictures cut into 256x256 tiles.
- **Menus** are widget containers built by one function per screen and driven by one click handler with
  the clicked widget's index; the same add-button / add-label / add-slider calls build our own screens, so
  new menus look exactly like the game's. Screen ids above the game's own are free to use.
- **Config bug:** the cfg reader accepts only CRLF lines, but the writer writes LF, so after the first
  save not one line is read again (63 "Invalid setting") and every option silently resets. Gamma and
  brightness are written as `int.(int - value)*100` ("1.-30"). Fixed by rewriting the file (CRLF, proper
  decimals) at start and right after the game saves it.
- **Audio:** one sound bank; a busy buffer skips a sound but keeps its volume, so the next play ignores the
  volume slider. Master volume is read as a constant 100 in five places.
- **File I/O:** the archive is read a few bytes at a time, each read with SetFilePointer + GetFileSize +
  ReadFile (1.4 million calls at start). A read-ahead buffer per read-only handle cut start-up from 5.2 s to
  1.7 s and a mission load from 8.4 s to under 1 s (with vsync off while loading).

## Build steps
1. `cargo build --release --target i686-pc-windows-msvc` (static CRT via `.cargo/config.toml`, version info
   from an `.rc`).
2. Copy `d3d8.dll` next to `Dark Legions.exe`. Remove dgVoodoo's `D3D8.dll` and any older proxy.
3. Start the game; edit `reloaded.ini` or use Options -> Video / Advanced graphics / Interface / Audio.

## Verification
- Crashes: WER LocalDumps + a triage script on every dump; long sessions on saves that crashed before.
- Graphics: frame-by-frame capture (every draw's state + picture after it, on a hotkey) to find which
  draw produced a bug; F11 screenshots at monitor resolution compared side by side with dgVoodoo.
- Performance: a sampling profiler on the main thread (1 ms) with phases from the game's log lines.
- Not verified: the Steam release (app 492530); multiplayer; hours-long AI-only soak tests; any PC but one
  (Windows 11, 2560x1600 monitor).

## Gotchas
1. **Blue blotches near the camera.** **Cause:** table fog + infinite-far projection. **Fix:** far plane 1e6.
2. **Wedges across the screen.** **Cause:** D3DRS_CLIPPING off. **Fix:** keep it on.
3. **Low FPS.** **Cause:** software vertex processing and managed-buffer rewrites. **Fix:** hardware VP and
   a range-only upload ring (see the D3D8 wrapper technique note).
4. **Leaves turned into blobs at 2x.** **Cause:** the tree textures rely on point filtering at 1x for their
   grain. **Fix:** per-texture filter by name (point / mixed / linear), anisotropic for everything else.
5. **The interface's first row/column shows the scene at 2x.** **Cause:** 2D corners at 0.5. **Fix:** map
   game x as (x - 0.5) * scale.
6. **Widescreen moved the mouse off the buttons.** **Cause:** centred menus. **Fix:** move the mouse back by
   the same offset; on stretched screens divide by the stretch.
7. **Small minimap icons from the menu folder dragged the whole HUD to the centre.** **Cause:** screens were
   recognised by texture folder. **Fix:** only pictures wider than 200 px mark a menu.
8. **Settings reset after every restart.** **Cause:** the LF/CRLF cfg bug above. **Fix:** rewrite the file.
9. **Splash and loading screens looked worse than under dgVoodoo.** **Cause:** linear filtering when
   stretching a 1024x768 picture. **Fix:** sharp-bilinear shader on those pictures, and stretch everything 2D
   in the same frame (progress bar, "Loading..."), or it drifts off the picture.
10. **The game kept running invisibly after Task Manager / Alt+F4.** **Fix:** terminate on WM_DESTROY after 3 s.
11. **Typed save names lost every non-ASCII letter.** **Cause:** a filter keeping only A-Z/0-9/_!.- .
    **Fix:** allow everything Windows allows in file names; Cyrillic glyphs drawn from a Windows font
    measured to the game's font metrics.

## Open questions
- Hours-long stability with AI-only games (the engine is full of "unreferenced pointer" warnings).
- A vector version of the game's fonts; an AI-upscaled texture pack.

---
kind: game
title: 'Kyo passed through from KOF XIII into a custom arena: stepped frames, native hit injection and a shared GPU layer'
game: The King of Fighters XIII
games_also: []
game_version: 'THE KING OF FIGHTERS XIII STEAM EDITION release v1.4b, Steam app 222940, build 151721, 32-bit kofxiii.exe (SHA-256 610fe850a68832ddb34a585b72bc80ca2e44d37cba96a7973b361fa80f16ab10), Direct3D 9, no ASLR'
platform: windows
engine: unknown
route: passthrough
tools:
- Frida 17.22.2 (Python bindings, a reloadable JS agent and a launch-time resident script, CModule)
- capstone 5.0.7 (offline disassembly of the installed exe)
- Python 3.12 + numpy 2.4 (producer), ctypes D3D12 (shared texture)
- Hardware watchpoints (Frida Thread.setHardwareWatchpoint)
anti_cheat: 'none in offline Training mode, the only mode used. Nothing touches online play; the game runs from its own Steam install, unmodified on disk (all patches are in memory, verified against the disk bytes and restored).'

# Kyo passed through from KOF XIII into a custom arena: stepped frames, native hit injection and a shared GPU layer

> Kyo Kusanagi from the real KOF XIII (Steam, offline Training) plays inside a separate arena host. The host drives
> him one battle frame per host tick. Hits, guards and contacts go through KOF's own hit records, so his reactions,
> pushback, hitstop shake and hit sparks are KOF's. His isolated sprite reaches the host as a shared D3D12 texture.
> The host's conformance kit passes, a human played it ("it feels good"), and it holds 60 ticks/s with about 0.1
> late frames per second on an Intel Iris Xe laptop.

## Setup
- KOF XIII Steam (app 222940, build 151721, release v1.4b), 32-bit `kofxiii.exe`, Direct3D 9, image base 0x400000
  with no ASLR, MSVC RTTI present. Windows 11, launched windowed (`-w`).
- Frida 17.22.2 spawns the game and loads a "resident" script before resume, so it can hook device creation.
  A hook-free agent script handles reads and patches and can be reloaded.
- **Offline only.** KOF XIII has online play; everything here ran in offline Training. The resident script is
  loaded at spawn and stays for the life of the process (device hooks, the Present replacement and, with
  free-run, the present interval), so a KOF launched this way is instrumented in every mode. Never take it
  online (ranked or player matches): quit it and start KOF from Steam first.
- The host is a small custom Rust/D3D11 arena with a length-prefixed JSON protocol over loopback TCP: hello /
  step / hit / contact, with step events and a shared-layer image mode. The approach applies to any host that steps
  a guest and wants its native mechanics.
- The repos are private. The note describes them in prose; ask if you need the code.

## Route and why
Passthrough: run the real game, freeze it, step it one frame at a time, and read state, boxes and an isolated
sprite each step. The host owns position and resolves contacts; the guest applies the outcome through its own
code.
- **Reimplementation was rejected.** Converting the character into the host means extracting data and copying
  the mechanics, and it is only ever approximately faithful.
- **D3D9On12 was rejected.** Creating the device through D3D9On12 (`Direct3DCreate9On12`), which would make its
  targets shareable as D3D12 resources, crashed KOF in `dxilconv.dll` (shader translation). So the plain D3D9
  device is kept, and pixels go through a CPU readback, then an upload into a D3D12 shared texture made by the
  producer.

Related: `knowledge/techniques/frame-compositing-depth-and-pose-sync.md` (as in its bridges, the pixels cross on
the CPU here; only the producer-to-host hop is a shared GPU texture) and
`knowledge/techniques/bridge-contracts-ownership-units-and-lifecycle.md` (the host owns position and contacts, KOF
applies hits, and a lease restores KOF if the producer dies).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
**Pause and step.**
- `GamePause` is a static object at `0x7f4980`. Its fields: `+8` pause request, `+9` "paused this frame", `+0xa`
  step request. Its update is vtable slot 1 at `0x443c90`.
- A step is complete when `+0xa` has been consumed **and** `+9` is back to 1. Reading as soon as `+0xa` clears
  races the battle update.
- The loop order per iteration is: `GamePause::update`, then render + Present, then the battle update. So a step
  always takes two iterations: the stepped battle update runs after that iteration's Present, and first appears
  in the next one.
- About 3 ms of other loop work runs before `GamePause::update`. Gating there instead of after Present lets that
  work overlap the wait for the host.

**Players.**
- `PlayerPort` is at `0x832098`, with the P1 controller at `+8` and P2 at `+0xc`. The AnimObj is
  `[[[controller+0x38]+8]+8]`.
- AnimObj fields: x / y / vy are floats at `+0x120` / `+0x124` / `+0x130`; action is at `+0x8c`, facing (float ±1)
  at `+0x138`. Controller fields: life `+0x50`, hitstop `+0xf4`, hitstun `+0x114`.
- The round-start separation is 384 world units. The host maps that to its own start distance.

**Input.**
- Each input object's held word comes from `0x443780` (the object is passed in `eax`); `0x443b30` stores it at
  `object+4`. P1's battle input object is `controller+0x18`.
- Raw words: right 0x1, up 0x2, left 0x4, down 0x8, LP 0x100110, HP 0x200440, LK 0x401220, HK 0x802080.
  Directions are screen-absolute.
- Replacing `0x443780`'s return value for that object drives Kyo whatever window has focus. KOF stops polling
  DirectInput while unfocused, so a DirectInput override died as soon as the host window had focus.

**Collision.**
- The manager is at `0x7eabf0`. It holds 2 × 5 per-frame circular lists from `+0x18`: 12 bytes per list, P2's block
  0x3c after P1's. Each node: next at `+0`, owner record at `+8`, box floats `[left, bottom, width, height]` at
  `+0xc` (y up), rect key at `+0x1c`.
- Lists: 0 push, 1 hit, 2 a proximity box (triggers guard stance), 3 hurt, 4 throw.
- The battle routine's passes: push `0x50d010` (0×0), clash `0x50d760` (1×1), `0x50da90` (1×2), hit `0x50db00`
  (1×3), throw `0x50ebd0` (4×3 and 4×0). Then the box display `0x50f210`, which runs after all of them and is a good
  snapshot point.
- Patching each pass's entry to `ret 4` (`ret` for the throw pass, whose manager is in `ebx`) switches off native
  interaction. The lists stay filled.

**Hit resolution.**
- The pair test `0x50db70` calls the resolver `0x50dca0(manager, &attacker record, &defender record)`. Records are
  `PlayerController::AvatarHook` owners; one record owns all of a fighter's boxes.
- The resolver writes its result into both records. Defender on hit: flags `+8 |= 0x1180`, damage at `+0xc` and
  `+0x18`, hitstop at `+0x10` and `+0x14`, reaction level `+0x20`, pushback float `+0x28`, attack id `+0x34`, last-hit
  stamp `+0x6c`, contact point `+0x88..`, spark id `+0x94`.
- On guard: flags 0x1c0, a guard value at `+0x24`, no damage. The attacker gets flags 0x800a on hit (0x800c on
  guard), its own hitstop at `+0x10` and the opponent's at `+0x14`.
- The controller reacts later in the same battle frame.
- **Injection:** write the same fields into Kyo's record at the entry of `0x50ca60` (the pass right after the hit
  passes). That reproduces a native hit or guard exactly. Damage and hitstop follow what you write; the reaction
  and its stun or blockstun length follow the attack id.
- Writing a spark id and contact point into the attacker's record makes `0x50ca60` spawn KOF's own hit spark, a new
  AnimObj drawn like a fighter.

**Attack data.**
- `0x50c170` is a named-parameter getter: the manager in `eax`, a rect key in `ecx`, an index 1–20 on the stack;
  it returns a float in ST0 (`ret 4`).
- Index names: Attack, AttackCore, HitBack, HitStop, HitStopCore, PushCore, PushedCore, AttackHard, AttackConcept,
  AttackAttribute, AttackKind, GaugeParam, RectType, guard_crash, stun, HitSlow, Score, Effect, ComboLimitRate,
  HitBackPattern.
- They are read from script tables. Called through a small thunk, this gives each hitbox's damage, hitstop,
  pushback, reaction id (RectType) and stun level. Block height is not among them.

**Rendering.**
- Each fighter is usually one `DrawPrimitive` (a 4-vertex strip) inside `AnimObj::Drawer::draw` (`0x40d8a0`, vtable
  slot 1; drawn object = `[[this+0x50]+8]`). Some moves add a second draw.
- They go into a 960×540 scene target through a vertex shader whose constants are: c0–c3 the sprite's world matrix
  (c3 = position, c0.x = −1 when facing right, since sprites are authored facing left), c4–c7 the view projection
  (one world unit = one target pixel; c7 holds the camera offset), c8 the viewport half-size.
- From those, each frame's crop and foot pivot are exact, with no camera address needed.
- KOF shakes the defender during hitstop by moving that transform about ±2.5 units. Anchor the pivot to the logical
  x, or the shake cancels out.
- The swap chain uses the default (vsync) present interval, and KOF resets the device after creating it.

## Build steps
1. **Launch.** Spawn `kofxiii.exe -w` with `SteamAppId=222940` under Frida, with Steam running (the variable only
   names the app; the Steam client still checks the licence). Load the resident before resume. It hooks
   `Direct3DCreate9`, then CreateDevice, Reset and Present (Present as a native replacement).
2. **Free-run (optional).** Set the present interval to immediate in both CreateDevice **and** Reset. Cap idle
   frames with a high-resolution waitable timer in Present.
3. **Isolation.** Pause through `GamePause`. Patch the five collision passes (checked against the disk bytes first,
   restored under a lease). Keep KOF's P2 a little ahead of Kyo on the host-facing side, so KOF's auto-turn agrees
   with the host.
4. **Each step,** through a shared-memory channel (a named mapping plus named events; the wake event is also the
   frame gate):
   1. write the placement, input and queued interactions, and set the step request;
   2. the stepped frame's box display gives the boxes and attack parameters;
   3. Kyo's draws, reported by a native DrawPrimitive filter, are replayed into a private A8R8G8B8 target with
      blending and depth off;
   4. at Present, read the state, StretchRect the crop into a 512×512 target, read it back, and copy it natively
      into the mapping, already premultiplied and mirrored to face right.
5. **Producer.** Upload the crop into a D3D12 shared B8G8R8A8 texture (a persistently mapped upload buffer and one
   CopyTextureRegion; a simultaneous-access texture needs no barriers). Send the layer description with its ready
   and release fences.
6. **While serving,** the native DrawPrimitive and Clear filters skip everything but Kyo, and the Present
   replacement skips the window swap.

## Verification
- **Conformance.** The host's kit passes in shared-layer and RGBA modes: 32 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings. It covers
  sequence/tick rules, validity, hit and contact operations, step events, defeat, reset and nine malformed-request
  checks.
- **Native-behaviour oracles.**
  - A traced native LP on P2 against an injected LP on Kyo: same life loss, hitstop, hitstun and reaction action.
  - Iori blocking natively against an injected guard: same block reactions (actions 34/35, blockstun 28/36).
  - Contact sheets of seven moves: every stepped frame shows Kyo's whole sprite.
  - Contact sheets of the spark on hit and guard.
  - Each frame's sprite draw x equals the state x read at the same Present.
- **Robustness.** A producer killed with `taskkill /F` mid-session leaves KOF unpaused and unpatched, and rendering.
- **Hand play.** Four sessions; each finding is a gotcha below.
- **Performance.** Step median 5.8 ms standalone; host 60.1 ticks/s with 3 of 1797 frames late; KOF 47% of one
  core while serving.
- **Not verified:** specials and supers beyond normals, throws, KO, other characters, other stages, and online
  anything.

## Gotchas
1. **Steps read half-updated state.** Cause: `GamePause +0xa` is consumed at the start of the stepped frame, before
   its battle update. Fix: wait for `+0xa == 0` and then `+9 == 1`.
2. **The resident script loaded but had no RPC exports.** Cause: an early hook threw on a 3-byte stub (an empty
   virtual), so `rpc.exports` was never assigned. Fix: define exports first and guard every hook.
3. **Heap scans timed out (30 s RPC limit).** Cause: JavaScript loops over about 100M dwords. Fix: CModule
   kernels, in batches.
4. **Input worked until the host window had focus.** Cause: KOF stops calling `GetDeviceState` while unfocused.
   Fix: override the held word at `0x443780` for P1's controller input object. A hardware write watchpoint on a
   known input word found the writer in one try.
5. **`Memory.alloc`'d thunks crashed later.** Cause: Frida frees `Memory.alloc` memory when the JS pointer object
   is garbage-collected, even if a `NativeFunction` still holds the raw address. Fix: keep every allocation
   referenced from module scope. Test with a forced `gc()`.
6. **KOF crashed when I installed a CModule replacement from a probe.** Cause: the CModule's own data page is not
   writable, so storing the trampoline into a CModule global faulted after `Interceptor.replaceFast` was already
   live, and the next call went to address 0. Fix: keep CModule state in JavaScript-allocated memory passed as
   symbols, and make the C code skip, not call, while the original pointer is null.
7. **Per-draw `Interceptor.attach` failed ("wrong type").** Cause: Frida will not attach to a function you
   replaced. Fix: make the native replacement report the draws you care about through a `NativeCallback`.
8. **The sprite vanished during HP.** Cause: the drawer issues two draws there, and only the last draw state (a
   floor draw) was replayed. Fix: replay every draw inside the drawer, and crop to the union.
9. **The hitstop "freeze" felt like a stall in the host.** Cause: native hitstop (7–13 frames) shown without KOF's
   spark and shake. The pivot taken from the draw transform cancelled KOF's ±2.5-unit defender shake. Fix: anchor
   the pivot to the logical x, spawn KOF's spark through the record, and shake the host's dummy too.
10. **Native stun length ignores what you write.** Cause: the reaction animation ends the stun (it even rewrites
    the counter), not the controller counter. Fix: pick the reaction by attack id (light or heavy). This diverges
    from a protocol where the attacker owns stun frames: an open issue.
11. **`--free-run` did nothing at first.** Cause: KOF resets the device after CreateDevice, with its own present
    parameters. Fix: set the interval in Reset too.
12. **The first frame gate made steps take 120 ms.** Cause: the promise resolved inside the Present callback, then
    the same callback waited at the gate, and Frida delivers an RPC reply only when that callback returns. Fix: never
    block in the callback that resolves. Polling gates with `Thread.sleep` also released late (Windows sleep
    granularity), so use a Win32 event.
13. **330 ms stalls on every hit.** Cause: without `step-events`, the host sent each hit as its own request, and the
    reply took an old capture path that waited out the gate. Fix: fold events into steps, and answer separate
    hit/contact requests from the cached frame.
14. **16–22 ms receive spikes in the host, independent of process priority.** Cause: a ~190 KB base64 image
    reply over loopback TCP; `TCP_NODELAY` and priority made no difference. Fix: the shared GPU layer.
15. **Capture readback waited 3–5 ms.** Cause: `LockRect` waits for the GPU, which D3D9 only submits at Present or
    lock. Fix: an event query with `D3DGETDATA_FLUSH` right after each replay (−0.8 ms per step), and StretchRect
    only the crop.
16. **The uncapped frame rate loaded the PC.** Cause: free-run removes vsync for menus too. Fix: cap Present with a
    high-resolution waitable timer while not serving. The frame gate already holds KOF while serving.

## Assets
None created. Nothing from the game is stored: all pixels are KOF's own, rendered live.

## Cost and time
Two days of sessions (2026-10-10 to 2026-10-11), each change verified live on the running game.

## Open questions
- The attacker-owned stun length on Kyo as defender (hold or cut KOF's reaction animation).
- KOF's own block-height field, probably in the RectType table.
- Throws and KO.
- Other characters: the drawer and hit-record approach should be generic.
- Zero-copy sharing of KOF's private target, which would need a D3D9Ex or D3D9On12 device. D3D9On12 crashed it, and
  D3D9Ex rejects managed-pool resources.
- Skipping KOF's whole render pass in the stale first iteration of each step, which would save CPU.
