# The Witcher 3 Remastered: .bundle container and CR2W, decoded

> Decoded the two file formats a Witcher 3 mod actually touches: the `.bundle` container in
> `content/content0/bundles/` and the `CR2W` resource inside it. Both layouts are public for older builds
> (WolvenKit-7); they were re-measured here byte-for-byte against the installed Remastered retail build,
> with the leaked 2021 next-gen engine source used for field names. Every number below is from that
> retail build. No mod has been built yet, so nothing here is proven in game; the oracle so far is a
> parser that round-trips the shipped files.

## Setup
- Linux (CachyOS), Steam, Proton. Game at `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/The Witcher 3/`.
- Retail build: buildid **25646871**, ~65 GB installed, `bin/x64_dx12/witcher3.exe` (90,674,640 bytes).
  The exe self-identifies as `v 5.00c` (find it with `strings` next to `LastLaunchVersion`). DX12 only;
  there is no `x64_dx11` directory in this build.
- REDkit 5.0 at `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/The Witcher 3 REDkit/` (Steam app **2684660**,
  buildid **25651183**, 104 GB).
- Tools used: `python3` with `zlib` and `struct` for the parser, `strings` for binary probing, and REDkit's
  `bundlebuilder.exe` for the packer test in gotcha 5.
- The leaked next-gen source tree was used as a hypothesis generator (the tree is `Main.Lava`), not as an
  oracle. The oracle is the shipped file.

## Route and why
`data`. The goal was a documentation stable enough to build a mod on later, so the work was format
decoding and measurement, not patching. The leak tells you what the format *was* in 2021; only the retail
build tells you what it *is*. Every claim was therefore re-measured, and each leak claim that the retail
build disagreed with is called out below.

The alternative route, hooking the loader with ASI/native hooks, is popular for W3 but is address-bound and
version-gated: the 2026-09-29 Remastered update already broke mods that ship XML, scripts or `.w3strings`.
Container and resource formats are version-stable, so they are the safer foundation.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### The `.bundle` container
31 bundles in `content/content0/bundles/`, about 20.6 GB total. Layout: a 32-byte preamble, then a table of
fixed-size entries, then the data region. All 31 files start with the ASCII stamp `POTATO70`.

Preamble (32 bytes), as observed on the shipped files:

| offset | size | meaning | retail value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 8 | stamp | `POTATO70` |
| 8 | 4 | file size, low half | file size mod 2^32 (see gotcha 3) |
| 12 | 4 | file size, high half | 1 on exactly the two bundles over 4 GiB, 0 on the rest |
| 16 | 4 | header size | `data offset - 32` |
| 20 | 2 | format version | **5** in every shipped bundle |
| 22 | 4 | data offset | `32 + header size` |
| 26 | 6 | zero | |

Entries are a **304-byte** stride: a 256-byte null-terminated resource path, a 16-byte resource hash, then
eight `u32` words in this order — data-offset low half, data-offset high half, uncompressed size, on-disk
size, payload CRC32, compression word, and two reserved words that are always 0. 365,866 entries in total;
188,762 of them are compressed. WolvenKit-7's pre-Remastered 320-byte entry orders its fields differently (an
`Empty` word, the two sizes, a u32 offset, date, time, 16 zero bytes, CRC, compression), so port the order
along with the stride.

The second word is **not** a flag: it is the high half of a **u64** offset. It is 0 in the 29 bundles under
4 GiB, and 0 or 1 in `buffers.bundle` (52,989 of 113,009 entries) and `movies.bundle` (624 of 1,236). Read the
pair as `offset = w0 | (w1 << 32)`; the u64 offsets are monotonic with 0 violations across all 113,009
`buffers.bundle` entries and all 1,236 `movies.bundle` entries. The CRC word is `zlib.crc32` of the
**decompressed** payload (8/8 sampled in `buffers.bundle`, 5/5 in `ep1.bundle`), not of the stored bytes.

Compression is per entry and only two values ship: `0` (stored, the two size words are equal) and `1`
(raw `zlib`, the classic `78 da` header). `zlib.decompress` reproduced the declared uncompressed size in
2,203 of 2,203 sampled compressed entries, and the size words were never out of order across 2,559 samples.
The engine source also names Snappy, DOBOZ, LZ4, LZ4HC and chained zlib, but this build does not use them.

Offsets are **u64, split across two words**, which only shows up in the two files over 4 GiB:
`buffers.bundle` (7.6 GB) and `movies.bundle` (7.7 GB) — the only two whose high half is ever 1, and the only
two whose preamble file size has a non-zero high word. 111 of 251 sampled entries in `buffers.bundle` decoded
only after adding 2^32, because the high half was being ignored.

Entry-name census: `levels` 117,802, `dlc` 94,896, `environment` 52,407, `characters` 30,633. All 113,009
`.buffer` entries live in `buffers.bundle`. Paths are plain Windows-style relative paths
(`characters\models\common\...\a0_01_ma__body.w2ent`) and match the directory roots the source tree uses.

### The `CR2W` resource
Extract an entry and you get `CR2W`. The header is **160 bytes**: magic `CR2W`, `u32` version, `u32` flags,
an 8-byte timestamp, `u32` build version, `u32` objects-end, `u32` buffers-end, `u32` CRC, `u32` chunk
count, then **ten 12-byte descriptors**, each `(u32 offset, u32 count, u32 crc)`. The 160 bytes come from
`40 + 10 * 12`; the engine source's `eChunkType` enum declares 10 slots even though the last three are
unused.

Chunks follow immediately with no padding, in enum order: Strings (index 0), Names (1), Imports (2),
Properties (3), Exports (4), Buffers (5), Embedded (6, per WolvenKit-7), then three more the retail files
leave empty. Entry sizes are fixed: a Name is 8 bytes, an Import 8, a Property 16, an Export 24, a Buffer 24.

A worked example, `characters\models\common\man_average\body\a0_01_ma__body.w2ent` from `r4items.bundle`
(2,520 bytes, uncompressed): version 164, flags 0, timestamp 0, build version 0, objects-end and
buffers-end both 2520, CRC `0x3208bf93`, 6 chunks. Chunks chain as Strings @160 count 456 (ends 616),
Names @616 count 39 x 8 (ends 928), Imports @928 count 1 x 8 (ends 936), Properties @936 count 1 x 16
(ends 952), Exports @952 count 3 x 24 (ends 1024), Buffers empty. The Strings blob holds the type names
you would expect from an entity template: `CEntityTemplate`, `properOverrides`, `Bool`/`entityBool`,
`entityObject`, `ptr:CEntity`, `CMeshComponent`, `CGUID`, `name`.

### Where mods live now
`bin/config/r4game/user_config_matrix/pc/` ships ten menu XMLs — audio, display, gameplay, gamma,
graphics, hdr, hidden, hud, input, localization — and **no `mods.xml`**. The exe's string table has no
`mods.settings` either, while it does have `\mods\`, `modsList`, `modsMetadata`, `mods_enabled`,
`AreModsEnabled`, `-disablemods` and the mod.io API routes. So hand-installed mods appear to still work
through a directory, but the classic load-order file and per-mod config menu have no counterpart in the
shipped tree. See gotcha 6 for why this is not settled.

### The shipped tools
`bin/x64_RedKit/` has `bundlebuilder.exe` (the packer) and `wcc_lite.exe`; `bin/tools/cooker/` has
`W3CookerTool.exe` plus the `toolchain/` step scripts. The cook sequence in the shipped batch files is:
`wcc exportbundles -platform=pc_dx12 -out=<temp>/bundles/pc_dx12/bundles.json -db=<cookdir>cook.db`, then
`bundlebuilder.exe -verbose -platform pc_dx12 -depotpath <cookdir> -cookedpath <cookdir> -definition
<bundles.json> -outputdir <out>`, then `wcc metadatastore -path=<out>/content/`. The packer reads its
bundle definition through an initialised depot, which is a real limitation (gotcha 5).

## Build steps
1. Install the game through Steam so `content/content0/bundles/` exists.
2. Read a preamble: open `<bundle>`, read 32 bytes, unpack the first 26 with `<8sQIHI` (bytes 26–31 are
   zero) — stamp, file size (u64), header size, version, data offset.
3. Walk entries from offset 32 in **304-byte** steps until you reach the data offset: `path = raw[:256]`
   split at the first NUL, then the 16-byte hash `raw[256:272]` and eight `u32`s from `raw[272:304]`.
4. For an entry with compression word `1`, slice on-disk-size bytes from `offset = w0 | (w1 << 32)` and
   `zlib.decompress` it; with word `0`, slice it as-is. No manual `+ 2^32` is needed once the high half is
   read.
5. Whatever you extracted should start with `CR2W`. Parse the 160-byte header, then the ten descriptors,
   then walk the chunk chain with the fixed entry sizes above.

A correct parser needs no game-specific tables: the file layout is self-describing apart from the 304-byte
stride; the offset pair is plain little-endian u64.

## Verification
- **Preamble:** all 31 shipped bundles matched the 32-byte layout field for field; the header-size word
  equals `data offset - 32` in every file.
- **Entries:** 365,866 entries walked with no stride drift; the two size words were ordered
  (`uncompressed >= on-disk`) in all 2,559 samples checked. Reading the offset as a u64 kept every entry in
  order — 0 violations across all 113,009 entries of `buffers.bundle` (last offset 7,640,451,552, file
  7,640,452,656) and all 1,236 of `movies.bundle` (last 7,679,472,832, file 7,680,309,920) — and the 0/1
  second word marked the high half on exactly the entries that need it (0 disagreements in 8,359 resolved
  samples: `dlc0` 5,800, `buffers` 2,545, `movies` 14; the unresolved rest are non-`CR2W` payloads). The CRC
  word equalled `zlib.crc32` of the decompressed payload in all 13 sampled compressed entries.
- **Compression:** 2,203 of 2,203 sampled compressed entries decompressed with `zlib` to exactly the
  declared uncompressed size and began with `CR2W`. Two entries that failed before the fix were explained
  by an offset read without its high half, not by a different codec.
- **CR2W:** the worked example's chunk chain consumed the file exactly (1024 of 2520 bytes of header and
  chunk region, then the declared buffers-end), and the string table contained coherent REDengine type
  names. Version 164 across all sampled resources.
- **Toolchain:** the shipped `bundlebuilder.exe` embeds build paths under `Main.Lava`, the same tree name
  the leak uses, and its CLI/error strings match the leaked `bundlebuilder/options.cpp` verbatim.
- **Not verified:** no mod has been loaded in game, so path resolution and override precedence are
  untested. The classic load-order file was not proven dead. REDkit's own cooked output was not captured,
  because its packer needs a generated depot.

## Gotchas
1. **WolvenKit-7 reads 320-byte entries; the Remastered files use 304.** **Cause:** pre-Remastered bundles
   use 320-byte entries (WolvenKit-7's `Bundle.cs` reads shipped bundles that way); Remastered 5.00c uses
   304. **Fix:** choose the stride by build; do not trust a hardcoded 320.
2. **The declared header version is 5, not the 3 the source describes.** **Cause:** the leak's tree is a
   2021 branch and the container version moved on. **Fix:** read the word, do not require 3.
3. **Offsets in `buffers.bundle` and `movies.bundle` point at the wrong place.** **Cause:** the data offset
   is **two `u32` words** — low, then high — and reading the high word as a 0/1 flag drops it, so every entry
   past 4 GiB wraps. **Fix:** read `offset = w0 | (w1 << 32)`; the pair is monotonic across all 113,009
   entries of `buffers.bundle`. The preamble's file size is the same kind of pair: low word at offset 8, high
   word at offset 12.
4. **`zlib.decompress` throws `Error -3` on some entries.** **Cause:** usually an offset read without its
   high half, pointing you into the wrong bytes — not a codec the parser does not know. **Fix:** fix the
   offset first; of roughly 3,700 compressed samples only a handful start with bytes other than `78 da`.
5. **`bundlebuilder.exe` rejects every definition file, including a minimal empty one, with "Definition
   file does not contain valid json data".** **Cause:** it resolves the definition through an initialised
   depot (`GDepot->GetBundles()`), which exists only after you run Generate depot in the editor (about
   60 GB). **Fix:** produce a bundle from the editor or a full cook, and treat the standalone packer as
   unusable. The definition schema (per the leaked source) is
   `{"bundles": [name, [ {Path, ID, FourCC, Compression}, ... ], ...]}`.
6. **Do not assume `mods.settings` still orders mods.** **Cause / limit:** the string is absent from the
   Remastered exe and `mods.xml` is absent from the config matrix, but absence of one literal is not
   proof, and hand-installed mods still have `\mods\` and `-disablemods` to go on. **Fix:** prove it with a
   real hand-installed mod before writing it down as fact.
7. **A warning about the leak as an oracle.** It is a 2021 branch of the *next-gen* build, not the
   Remastered build, and it is not the same commit. Treat every claim from it as a hypothesis and
   re-measure. Two of the four format facts above (entry stride, header version) differ from WolvenKit-7
   and are only settled by the shipped file.

## Assets
None. This note is format work only.

## Open questions
- Whether the classic `mods.settings` load-order file still applies on Remastered, and what replaces it.
  Needs one hand-installed mod.
- REDkit 5.0's cooked output: pack one bundle via the editor (after Generate depot) and diff its header
  against the retail table above. This is the check that would close the loop.
- `CR2W` chunk *contents* for the resource types a mod edits most (`.w2ent`, `.w2mesh`, `.w2quest`).
  Only the header, the chunk chain and the string table were decoded here.

# Film-style pistol reloads, a JSON QA bridge and physics magazines through a native ASI

Tomb Raider: Legend (PC, Steam) was modded with a C++ ASI (MinHook inline hooks, no on-disk exe edits) plus
replacement `.drm` files served from a `mods\` folder. (`.drm` is the cdc engine's data container for models,
animations and levels, not copy protection.) The mod adds new pistol models with extra rigid segments,
re-authored and newly added reload animations hosted on the weapon objects, a reload selector, pistol
slide/magazine/hammer motion, a slide-lock release mechanic, dropped magazines simulated by the mod, and a
JSON-lines QA bridge that lets an agent read game state and drive the game. The bridge, the reload selector and
the slide/magazine FX run in the real game (logs and screenshots). The animation variants, the magazine physics
and the slide lock ran in game the next morning: every variant played with its own animation id, the dropped
magazines fell, bounced and slept on the engine's own collision meshes (215 line-probe hits, no fallbacks), the
backpack tree deployed under the pack, and the slide lock engaged after every empty reload.

## Setup
- OS: Windows 11 Home 25H2 (build 26200), x64.
- Steam build of trl.exe (MD5 above). The `.text` section on disk is plain, so capstone disassembly of the file works;
  the Steam wrapper only means "never edit the exe".
- Loader: Ultimate ASI Loader renamed `binkw32.dll` (the original Bink DLL kept as `binkw32Hooked.dll`), because
  input is DirectInput8 over COM (a `dinput8.dll` proxy is never loaded) and `binkw32.dll` is a static import. The
  loader used is the copy shipped in `TR7-Menu-Hook.zip` from TheIndra55's TRLAU-menu-hook v2.5 release; its version
  resource only says 1.0.0.0, so identify it by hash (sha1 `9c349fc1c0d9bb721f1d28e6c77dee08f1a32abe`).
  TR7-Menu-Hook v2.5 (`TR7-Menu-Hook.asi`, sha1 `bcc67ed1642f32ff07da91313d42b0dcd7f7d668`) serves `pc-w\X.drm`
  from `<game>\mods\X.drm` by hooking archive init.
- tr7.pdb (from a different build) gives struct layouts only; every address was re-derived from this exe and is
  checked at startup against byte signatures ("sites"), with the mod refusing to install on a mismatch.
- Tooling:
  - MinHook v1.3.4 (commit `c3fcafd`), vendored. Master had rewritten its disassembler, so the tag was used.
  - MSVC 19.51 (toolset 14.51.36231, x64-hosted x86), CMake 4.4.3 + Ninja 1.12.1, static CRT, `/Brepro` for
    deterministic binaries.
  - A self-check executable that maps the exe at its preferred base and runs the hook logic against fake engine
    globals.
  - capstone 5.0.7 + pefile 2024.8.26 (`uv run --with pefile --with capstone`) for the disassembly.
  - Blender 5.2.1 + cdcEditor 0.1.1 (commit `5f2d5ab`) for DRM models and animations, and our own Python codec for
    animation sections and event lists.
  - ffmpeg 9.0.2 (gyan.dev full build, `gfxcapture` input) for recordings.

## Route and why
Native hooks. The engine is native x86 with no scripting layer for the player's weapon logic; the community loader
only swaps files. Data-only edits could replace animations and models but cannot select among reload variants, drive
new segments, or add input handling, so a small ASI with proof-checked hooks was the cheapest route that reaches
the idea. Decompiling the whole game was never needed: eight hooked functions and ~170 proof sites cover it.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Reload state machine.** `playerCheckWeaponReload` enters inventory state 10 (only caller of
  `playerInvSetState(10)`), which plays the weapon object's AnimBlend named by `invProp.iPlayerReloadAnim` on
  Lara's layer 1 through `razRequestVAnimCharacterSwitch(player, blend, host, 1, -1, 0)`. The blend index is read
  once, unchecked, so swapping that one byte around the call selects a different hosted blend; the end of the
  reload is driven by the layer's DONE alarm, not by which blend played. Anim event 51 (type-2 player event)
  refills both clips mid-animation (`playerDoWeaponReload`), and a flag bit prevents the end-of-anim refill from
  running twice. Vanilla reload blends never carry event 51; the stock reload refills at the end.
- **Hosted animations.** Weapon objects host Lara's weapon animations: `AnimBlend` entries point into the host's
  `animList`, whose ids index one global resident table (first loaded copy of an id wins, 1,024 slots). Animation
  sections are keyed at 30 keys/s (timePerKey 100, 3,000 units per second); rotations are axis-angle vectors;
  LINEAR tracks must cover the whole animation. A new hosted animation = a new section id, an `animList` entry, an
  event list in its own DTP section (ids below 0x8000, global), and an AnimBlend table copied with one more entry.
- **Layer 1 bone set.** The weapon overlay drives segments 2..99 only; pelvis (1) and legs (100..108) stay with
  locomotion. Weight shift in a reload therefore has to be faked from the spine.
- **Segment matrices are world matrices.** `G2Instance_BuildTransforms` fills a double-buffered pool of per-segment
  world matrices; the NextGen draw and shadow passes read them as-is, and visibility uses a box over all segments
  rebuilt every frame, so extra rigid segments of a model can be placed anywhere in the world by rewriting their
  matrices after the build (that is how the backpack magazine tree, belt carrier magazines and a 16-entry pool of
  dropped magazines ride on the pistol model). Shadow casters still use the model's static sphere.
- **Terrain query.** `MULTIBODY_LineProbe(flags, start, end, result, exclude)` (cdecl, caller pops 0x14) probes the
  loaded collision meshes with flags = 3 and returns hit position and normal; start/end must be 16-byte aligned, it
  must not run with a NULL exclude while no player exists, and the multibody system global can be NULL between
  levels. Engine gravity is 3 units per frame^2 scaled by `timeMult` (1.0 per 1/30 s), about 2,700 units/s^2.
- **Mini-instances** (a 160-slot pool of lightweight engine instances, `MINIINSTANCE_BirthObjectNoParent`) are the
  engine's own host for debris and would give per-object culling and relocation; an unowned instance of a weapon
  object instead turns into a dropped rigid-body gun (family 0x27 installs the RBWEAPON behaviour), so never birth
  weapon-family instances for props.
- **Fire input.** `playerHandleWeaponsFire` reads the fire action's pressed bit (0x10) from the input mapper's
  `ActionResult` array inside the same call; a press can be consumed by clearing that bit in a pre-hook (the mapper
  re-derives the bits next frame), which is cleaner than forcing `bCanAttack`, a byte with 44 writers.
- **Outfits and copies.** Every outfit is a whole player DRM bound by name; chapters force outfits; most cutscenes
  animate the live player (so the gameplay DRM shows in them); texture ids are global and only 64 are unused, so
  new art needs fresh ids and byte-identical sections wherever an id is shared.

## Build steps
1. Back up first, then install the loader and menu hook:
   - Saves live in `<Documents>\Tomb Raider - Legend\` (`autosave.dat` and `Saved Games\`):
     `um backup create "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\Tomb Raider - Legend" --name trl-saves` (PowerShell).
   - Settings live in `HKCU\Software\Crystal Dynamics\Tomb Raider: Legend` (subkeys `Graphics`, which holds
     `FullscreenModeID` and the resolution, and `Input`):
     `reg export "HKCU\Software\Crystal Dynamics\Tomb Raider: Legend" trl-registry.reg /y`
     (restore with `reg import trl-registry.reg`).
   - Keep the original `binkw32.dll` before the loader replaces it.
2. Build the ASI (`cmake` + ninja via `build.bat clean check`): the self-check must print all sites holding the
   vanilla bytes before anything is deployed.
3. Build models and animations into copies of the vanilla DRMs (cdcEditor exports, our splice/add tools), verify by
   re-parsing (only the intended sections change, byte for byte), re-import with cdcEditor.
4. Deploy: the ASI and ini next to trl.exe, DRMs into `mods\`; keep a pre-deploy copy of everything replaced.
5. QA: ini `[Test] Windowed=1 Bridge=1`, launch, then drive the bridge (`ping`, `boot`, `state`, `cam orbit`,
   `hold lock`, `outfit <name>` to reload a player DRM live) and screenshot with `um win shot`.

## Verification
- Static: every hooked prologue and proof site compared with the exe on disk; MinHook trampolines decoded; detours
  exercised in a self-check that maps the exe at its real base and fakes the engine globals (446 checks at the last
  count); a fake-host exe runs the startup path and the bridge end to end.
- In game (0.3.0): the bridge's 13 protocol checks, boot to gameplay, camera orbit and turntable screenshots, HUD
  and timescale overrides, `outfit` re-switch in gameplay, held actions and axes; the reload selector's log lines
  matched the animations seen in the user's recording; a 24k-vertex player model (vanilla is 15k) rendered.
- In game (0.5.0): the six reload variants (forced through the bridge) each entered the reload state with their own
  animation id; `MULTIBODY_LineProbe(3, ...)` returned real floor hits for every dropped magazine (12 asleep on the
  ground after 45 s, none on the fallback plane); the tree, carriers and pool segments drew from the pistol model's
  extra segments; `STREAM_RelocateUnit` fired five times while the level loaded; the slide lock engaged after every
  reload from empty and the release key cleared it; a 44k-vertex, 15-batch player model (vanilla 15k / 13) loaded
  and played. Not measured: frame time, a long soak, level changes with magazines on the ground.

## Gotchas
1. **"Failed to open BIGFILE.000" right after launch.** The exe was started with another working directory
   (older `um win launch` did that). **Fix:** start it from its own folder. `um win launch` now does this
   itself (`start /D <exe folder>`); with an older toolkit, use `Start-Process -WorkingDirectory <game>`.
2. **The level-start cutscene looks like gameplay.** `playerControl` is true but the player state is PuppetShow;
   fire/jump/teleport do nothing and `PLAYER_DebugSwitchPlayerCharacter` raised an access violation there and the
   game exited. **Fix:** skip the cutscene (Esc, Up, Enter) and require a non-PuppetShow state before switching
   outfits.
3. **Lara's position becomes NaN and the screen goes grey.** The bridge's animation `freeze` (speed 0) leaves
   section times NaN. **Fix:** never freeze; shoot turntables with the orbit camera only.
4. **Injected one-frame presses never fire.** The engine needs the press edge its own mapper derives from device
   state; injected pressed bits are wiped before it reads them, and SendInput mouse clicks only produce the held
   bit. **Fix:** test firing with real input, or add a test command that writes the magazine count.
5. **The idle counter reads 0 while the game runs**, so an "only when the user is idle" gate must be checked before
   launching, not after.
6. **The game stops at its own "Tomb Raider: Legend - Setup" dialog on every launch.** Its saved display mode no
   longer passed the game's validation (`0xEC6180`, called from WinMain through `0x405AD0`; the dialog is
   `DialogBoxParam` at `0xEC4FA0`), even though D3D9 listed every mode. It was not the display, the driver, the
   registry key or the mod (reproduced with the ASI removed). **Fix:** run `trl.exe -setup`, pick the real resolution
   and refresh rate (the refresh list repopulates after the resolution change, so select it second), press Ok; the
   game rewrites `FullscreenModeID` and starts normally. A black screen from an OLED-protection overlay looks the
   same in a GDI capture but is unrelated.
7. **Turntable yaw 0 shows the back of the head** for this model (its front is opposite to `rotation.z`): use the
   front offset of 180 degrees.
8. **Animation seats drift when accessory anchors move.** Hand targets that seat a gun on a magazine read the
   accessory's anchor file; rebuilding the accessory after the animations were authored moved the seats several
   units. **Fix:** regenerate the segment table/header and re-author from the current anchors; keep the anchor file
   versioned.
9. **A second `anim_add` on its own output silently lost the first added blend** (the blend count was not re-read).
   **Fix:** read the appended table back; a self-test now adds six blends in a row.
10. **The 8-frame blend-in performs your first move for you.** A hosted reload that starts far from the aim pose
    looks like it teleports into the first key; start and end every variant on the centre aim pose so the blend
    overlaps an authored rise.

## Assets
Pistol models rebuilt from our own mesh (no game geometry shipped); magazines and the backpack tree are our meshes;
textures baked in Blender (CPU). No generated images were used for the character likeness, by decision.

## Cost and time
Two long sessions (one evening, one night) with up to six agents under a machine-wide heavy-job limiter after a
freeze from running three workflows at once.

## Open questions
- The slide lock drops when the engine auto-holsters right after a reload (no enemy, no fire input); keeping it
  through a holster/draw needs the draw-state interception the recon described.
- Whether far pool segments lose their shadow (static shadow sphere) and how often `STREAM_RelocateUnit` fires.
- A runtime head-look controller may override authored head and eye keys during a reload.
- Mini-instances as the host for dropped magazines (per-object culling, engine relocation) remain the upgrade path.

# TrackMania 2 custom content: where it lives, and how a skin/model pack is assembled

A map of the ManiaPlanet install: which folder holds which media, how the client imports
your own content, and what a community skin/model zip had to contain to be accepted by the
old Maniapark uploader. Everything here is client-facing asset packaging — no anti-cheat or
ownership checks are involved. I did **not** run the game against these paths; the layout
comes from a 2011 Mania-Creative tutorial and from Maniapark's own PHP upload validator. For the
older TrackMania Forever `.3ds` model pipeline (TMF uses older GBX classes than ManiaPlanet), see
`techniques/trackmania-forever-3ds-model-export-in-blender.md`.

## Setup
- Game: TrackMania 2 Canyon (and the whole ManiaPlanet family — Stadium, ShootMania share the client).
- OS the paths describe: Windows. The ManiaPlanet installer lets you split two roots:
  a **common** folder (`CommonFiles`, shared, large) and a **personal** folder (`PersonalFiles`,
  your own content). Choose both explicitly rather than accepting the default buried under `C:\`.
- Both root locations can be changed later from the launcher: **Help → move game data** /
  **move personal data**. The same Help menu has **custom data** for importing content.

## Route and why
Route: **data** (asset and container layout). There is no engine hook here and none is needed —
ManiaPlanet reads its content from fixed directories and from `.Gbx` pack files, so a mod is
files dropped in the right place. The point of this note is to make that "right place" findable
without digging through a 2011 forum thread.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Two roots.** `[CommonFiles]` holds shipped content; `[Personalfiles]` holds yours. The client
  searches both, so your content is not a patch over the game files — it lives beside them.
- **`.Gbx` is the Nadeo container** for meshes, maps, replays and many other resources.
  A `.Pack.Gbx` is a distributable bundle of a model plus its skins; it is a `NadeoPak` archive,
  not a `.Gbx` object graph (`techniques/trackmania-gbx-containers-and-mesh-extraction.md`).
- **`.dds`** textures are DDS; a skin is a set of DDS maps, a model is `.Gbx` meshes plus DDS maps.
- **Locators (`.loc`).** A small text file whose entire body is one URL; renamed `<content>.loc`
  it tells the game "fetch/download this content". They exist so other players can see your skin
  without the game transferring the actual asset peer-to-peer. The URL must start with `http://`.
- **Common content layout** (`[CommonFiles]/PacksCache/*.zip`):
  - `ManiaPlanet_extras.zip`, `ManiaPlanet_Painter.zip` (Painter stencils/stickers),
    `ManiaPlanet_Skins.zip` (advertisement signs, avatar flags, horn sounds).
  - `Titles.zip` — title definitions and menu media (e.g. Canyon icon, `Menu/TitlesMedia/TMCanyon`).
  - `TMCanyon_HD.zip` — the Canyon HD texture/audio pack: `Canyon/Media/Texture/...`,
    `Canyon/Media/Moods/{Day,Night,Sunrise,Sunset}`, `Canyon/Media/Texture Decal/...`,
    `Vehicles/Media/Audio/Sound/WavData/CanyonEngine/`, and the default car skin
    (`Canyon/GameCtnObjectInfo/Vehicles/CanyonCarDefaultSkin.zip`).
  - `TMCanyon_skins.zip` — race music (`Media/Musics/Canyon/Race/*.ogg`) and painter layers
    (`Media/Painter/Vehicles/Canyoncar/Layers/Dirt`, `.../Layers/PreLight`, `.../SubObjects/Body`, `.../SubObjects/Rims`).
- **Personal content layout** (`[Personalfiles]/`):
  - `Blocks/` and `Blocks/Solid/` — custom 3D blocks; `Maps/`, `Maps/Downloaded/`, `Maps/My Maps/`.
  - `Media/{Images,Musics,Painter,Sounds}/` — Mediatracker images/sounds, challenge music, custom
    painter stencils and stickers.
  - `Packs/` — your own `.Gbx` packs; `Replays/{Autosaves,CreatedGhosts,Downloaded,Mediatrackerghosts,Replays}/`.
  - `Scripts/Editorplugins/` — custom track-editor scripts.
  - `Skins/` — `Any/Advertisement/` (track signs), `Avatars/` (user avatars), `Canyon/Mod/` (Canyon mods),
    `Horns/` (user horns), `Vehicles/CanyonCar/` (car skins).

## Build steps
To install a downloaded skin or mod, or to build your own pack:
1. Put a **Canyon car skin** in `[Personalfiles]/Skins/Vehicles/CanyonCar/`.
2. Put a **Canyon mod** in `[Personalfiles]/Skins/Canyon/Mod/`.
3. Put a **track sign** in `[Personalfiles]/Skins/Any/Advertisement/`.
4. Put an **editor script** in `[Personalfiles]/Scripts/Editorplugins/`.
5. Or use the in-client path: launcher → **Help → custom data** (import).
6. To make a distributable pack, build a zip/`.Pack.Gbx` whose entries follow the naming rules in
   the Gotchas below (a model plus its skin together), and optionally a `.loc` file containing the
   download URL.

## Verification
- The folder names, common/personal split, and launcher "move"/"custom data" menu items are from the
  Mania-Creative tutorial *Trackmania 2 – File locations* (author TStarGermany, last updated 2011-09-15).
- The upload acceptance rules (required zip entries) and the `.loc` behaviour are from Maniapark's own
  PHP validator, `Class/Ressource.php` (`analyse()` and `makeLocator()`), which is the code that decided
  whether a community upload was valid — a real, if historical, oracle.
- **Not verified:** I did not open the game, did not confirm later ManiaPlanet builds kept every path
  unchanged, and did not test a pack in-client.

## Gotchas
1. **Skin shows up but the car looks untextured/wrong.** **Cause:** a "skin" is a paintjob
   (`SkinDiffuse.dds` + `DetailsDiffuse.dds`), while the 3D shape comes from a *model* (`.Gbx` meshes).
   **Fix:** ship both together — a model and its skin belong in the same zip, in the same directory.
2. **"Wrong media type" / pack rejected.** **Cause:** the zip does not contain the minimum pieces.
   **Fix:** a valid model pack needs `Model.Pack.Gbx` **or** `MainBodyHigh.Solid.Gbx` (the 3D mesh)
   *plus* `Icon.dds` *plus* `Diffuse.dds`/`SkinDiffuse.dds`. Allowed file extensions are only
   `jpg`, `jpeg`, `zip`, `gbx`, `txt`; entry names must be lowercase.
3. **Others never see your skin.** **Cause:** without a locator, the asset stays local/peer-to-peer and
   may not propagate. **Fix:** add a `<content>.loc` text file whose whole body is one URL starting
   `http://` (name it e.g. `MyAwesomeSkin.zip.loc`, or `MyAwesomeMod.Skin.Pack.Gbx.loc` for a pack).
4. **`.loc` file does nothing.** **Cause:** the URL scheme is checked, and relative or `https://` URLs
   are/were rejected. **Fix:** use a full `http://…` URL, and name the file after the content it locates.
5. **Content works for you, not for the person who receives your pack.** **Cause:** a pack can carry a
   Planets price and a moderator/"free key" (`pak_key`) in the community site metadata. **Fix:** when
   handing a pack to someone, ship the `.Pack.Gbx`; a priced or keyed pack must be obtained by the
   recipient themselves, so do not pass a `pak_key` on.
6. **Thumbnail rejected by the uploader.** **Cause:** the site enforced a 4:3-ish aspect (±0.1) and a
   minimum of 200×150. **Fix:** export the preview at close to 4:3 and at least 200×150.

## Assets
Skins are DDS paintjobs (`SkinDiffuse.dds`, `DetailsDiffuse.dds`, plus `Icon.dds`); models are `.Gbx`
meshes plus DDS maps; signs use the same DDS packing under `Skins/Any/Advertisement/`. Audio (horn
sounds, challenge music `.ogg`) is optional extra content in the same tree.

## Cost and time
Small: one source tutorial plus one PHP validator read, plus a Docusaurus/site survey. No in-game session.

## Open questions
- Which of these paths still hold in the final ManiaPlanet/Nations Forever builds, and how they map on
  Linux via Proton.
- Whether `.Pack.Gbx` has a documented binary grammar beyond its `NadeoPak` header.
- The exact `.loc` fetch/verification flow between clients (who serves the asset, and how conflicts resolve).
- Later title (Stadium/ShootMania) skin directories beyond the Canyon ones listed here.

# Custom 3D car skins in Trackmania (2020)

> This is a write-up of a third-party route, not of work done here: nothing below was executed by us.
> Trackmania (2020) accepts custom car meshes as **GBX** assets plus DDS textures, authored in Blender
> with the Blendermania add-on, exported by **NadeoImporter**, then repaired/converted for the live
> build by **gbx-py**'s `skinfix`. The write-up follows bmx22c's June 2024 tutorial and its pinned
> corrections; every step is second-hand until someone runs it on a real install.

## Setup
- **Blender** (the tutorial era is Blender 3.2–4.x) with the **Blendermania** add-on, which bundles
  **NadeoImporter** and **NICE** — install them from inside Blendermania, not separately, so the
  add-on's own copies are not overridden.
- **gbx-py** (schadocalex) with **drunub's `skinfix` script** next to it. Newer builds merge gbx-py
  and the script into one `skinfix.exe` (Openplanet file 119): drag the produced `.gbx` onto it.
  gbx-py needs `python-lzo`; drunub's tm-pf-converter README says it has to be compiled from source on
  Python 3.14 and that build fails, so use Python 3.11 or `skinfix.exe`.
- **Openplanet** if you want to pull apart an existing skin.
- Folders that matter, under the Trackmania user folder (`Documents\Trackmania\`, or
  `Documents\Trackmania2020\` on some installs; drunub's example config shows both): the FBX and its
  `.MeshParams.xml` go in `Work\Skins\Models\<SkinName>\`, and the finished ZIP goes in
  `Skins\Models\CarSport\`.
- An existing skin to start from, or a template. `.Solid.Gbx` opens directly in Blender through NICE;
  `.Pack.Gbx` does not (see gotcha 11). Someone else's skin is for learning from: don't upload it, or a
  conversion of it, without its author's permission (drunub's converter README asks the same).

## Route and why
`route: asset-only`. The game loads a **GBX model** and **DDS textures** from a ZIP in the user's
`CarSport` folder; nothing in the executable is patched and no DLL is injected, so this stays inside
the "own assets, own client" line. The two alternatives the tutorial mentions and does not use are a
converter for existing TM2 skins (drunub's tm-pf-converter in `links`; its README says it only takes skins
built with TM2's NadeoImporter, not TMNF meshes) and a map-to-Blender ripper — both aimed at *porting
existing* content, not at authoring a new skin.

The container half of this route is already covered in this base by
[*Reading TrackMania GBX containers and getting meshes out without Nadeo tooling*](../../techniques/trackmania-gbx-containers-and-mesh-extraction.md),
and the ManiaPlanet folder layout that gotcha 11 relies on by
[*TrackMania 2 custom content*](../trackmania-2/maniaplanet-content-locations-and-custom-pack-layout.md);
this note is the TM2020 authoring half.

## How the game works (what the tutorial explains)
- **Two container shapes.** `.Solid.Gbx` is the simple mesh and converts straight to Blender. `.Pack.Gbx`
  is a package whose members (`.Solid.Gbx` and textures) have to be extracted first.
- **Materials are named by convention, not by path.** The four the tutorial creates, as transcribed:
  `SkinDmg_Skin` → `Skin_D.DDS`, `DetailsDmgNormal_<name>` → `Details_B.DDS`,
  `DetailsDmgNormal_Details` → `Details_D.DDS`, `GlassDmgCrack_<name>` → `GlassO_T.DDS`. Extra
  materials are allowed as long as the prefix matches. drunub's converter template uses the same models
  as `SkinDmg_Skin`, `DetailsDmgNormal_Details`, `DetailsDmgNormal_Wheels` and `GlassDmgCrack_Glass`
  (plus `...Decal` variants), with textures named after the part after the underscore (`Skin_*`,
  `Details_*`, `Wheels_*`).
- **`SkinDmg_Skin` carries no normal map.** If a part needs normal detail, put it in
  `DetailsDmgNormal_*`. TM2020 skin textures take the same `_R` (roughness) and `_N` (normal)
  suffixes as other TM2020 textures. drunub's README adds that the TM2-style `_D` texture only works on
  the skin material (details and wheels take `_B` plus an optional `_R`) and that `Skin_B` needs a
  `Skin_R`, so check the `Details_D` mapping above on a real build.
- **Textures do not tile.** A model whose UVs run outside the texture limits loses the texture, so
  fitting the UVs to the image is part of modelling, not an afterthought.
- **LODs are duplicated meshes with a bone/skeleton binding.** The usual count is three, up to five
  for complex cars; the exported name carries `_lod0`, `_lod1`, … and the skeleton stops being usable
  from LOD 4 upward.
- **A `.MeshParams.xml` sits next to the FBX** (`MeshType="Vehicle"`, `SkelSocketPrefix="_"`,
  `Collection="Stadium"`, plus the material list). NadeoImporter needs it and reports a collection
  error when it is missing or wrong.
- **Visibility online is not the same as visibility in your own garage.** Other players see the skin
  only when it is uploaded to your Club, and only if it respects the vertex budget.

## Build steps
Second-hand, in the tutorial's order:

1. Build the four textures, or reuse the template's, and keep every one inside the model's UVs.
2. Start from the template `.blend`; delete the **FakeShad** plane if you are not using a custom fake
   shadow.
3. For each part, select the part, go into edit mode, select all, return to object mode, Ctrl+click the
   matching LOD object, then Ctrl+J to join.
4. Assign each part to its body vertex group, then move the group's bone to the part's origin. Wheels:
   `Reactor` and `Guard` share the same position, and the bone's rotation must match the mesh's.
   Bones can be added or removed as long as the matching vertex groups come and go with them.
5. Exhaust flames: use the `TwoCorExhaust` bones (one bone if you only want one flame).
6. Keep the model inside the template's bounding box; otherwise other players do not see it.
7. Extra LODs: duplicate the previous LOD, unparent it with Alt+P → *Clear and Keep Transformation*,
   rename to `_lod2` (then `_lod3`…), reselect the correct **skeleton modifier** and the correct
   materials. A name Blender has suffixed with `.001` will not work.
8. Trigram / player-position meshes: copy them from the supplied Blender file, place them, and **do not
   modify their UVs**. Their material is `SkinDmgTrigram_Skin` → `SkinD.DDS`, and each decal material
   needs a second UV layer named `Decal`, identical to the `BaseMaterial` layer.
9. Export FBX with **Add Leaf Bones unchecked**, as
   `Documents\Trackmania\Work\Skins\Models\<SkinName>\<SkinName>.fbx`, and copy
   `<SkinName>.MeshParams.xml` beside it.
10. Run `NadeoImporter.exe Mesh Skins\Models\<SkinName>\<SkinName>.fbx` from the Trackmania install
    folder (a PowerShell window opened there).
11. Repair/convert with `python skinfix.py <path>\<SkinName>.gbx`, or `--fakeshad` when you supply a
    FakeShad DDS. The script writes `MainBody.Mesh.Gbx` next to `<SkinName>.Mesh.Gbx`.
12. ZIP the textures together with `MainBody.Mesh.Gbx` into
    `Documents\Trackmania\Skins\Models\CarSport\<SkinName>.zip`.
13. In game: plugins → classic menu → editors → **paint a car** → pick the skin. Refresh the garage
    with M (stops the car spinning) then Ctrl+R. Check bone rotations in Cam 7 with the camera locked
    to the car. Upload to your Club to let other players see it.

## Verification
**Nothing here was run by us.** The route above is transcribed from bmx22c's tutorial (19 June 2024)
and the four corrections pinned in its description, plus the comments' workarounds. The oracle the
tutorial itself uses: the skin appears in *paint a car*, the car stops spinning on M, Ctrl+R reloads
it, and Cam 7 shows whether the bones are rotated correctly. The vertex budget message is the other
oracle — the top-left corner says only "build …" unless you open the detailed overlay.

## Gotchas
1. **NadeoImporter prints only its banner and produces no `.gbx`.** **Cause:** the `.MeshParams.xml`
   is missing or misnamed next to the FBX. **Fix:** copy `<SkinName>.MeshParams.xml` beside the FBX,
   in the same `Work\Skins\Models\<SkinName>\` folder.
2. **`collection Common not found`.** **Cause:** the collection in `.MeshParams.xml` does not match
   what the importer expects (the template uses `Collection="Stadium"`). **Fix:** use the template's
   file rather than hand-rolling the XML.
3. **`Mesh : not enough UvLayers for material (1 < 2)` on the trigram or player-position mesh.**
   **Cause:** the decal material needs two UV layers. **Fix:** add a second UV layer named `Decal`,
   identical to `BaseMaterial`.
4. **The skin is invisible to other players.** **Cause:** a LOD exceeds the vertex budget (the game
   silently keeps the default skin), or the skin was never uploaded to the Club. **Fix:** open
   system → scene explorer → viewport overlays index 4 → *frame* → *vehicle* → *profile menu* →
   *frame instance* → *frame content*, uncheck *frame Vehicles* to read the real message, cut the LODs'
   vertex counts, re-export, and upload the skin to your Club.
5. **A duplicated LOD loses its materials or skeleton.** **Cause:** Blender renamed the copies to
   `.001`, which the game does not match. **Fix:** in the duplicated LOD, reselect the correct
   skeleton modifier and the exact materials.
6. **Skeleton binding stops working on the highest LODs.** **Cause:** the tutorial's own warning that
   skeletons do not work from LOD 4 up. **Fix:** for those LODs bind everything to the body bone and
   reduce the vertex count until the budget complains no more.
7. **A part is invisible or misplaced for other players.** **Cause:** it sits outside the bounding box
   the game checks, or its bone was never moved to the mesh origin (wheels: `Reactor`/`Guard` share a
   position and the bone rotation must match the mesh). **Fix:** re-check the box and the bone
   transforms.
8. **Parts end up in the wrong LOD.** **Cause:** the join was done without selecting the target LOD
   object first. **Fix:** Ctrl+click the LOD object, then Ctrl+J.
9. **Trigram or player position renders as a smear.** **Cause:** their UVs were modified. **Fix:**
   paste the supplied meshes and leave their UVs alone.
10. **A custom normal map changes nothing on the main body.** **Cause:** `SkinDmg_Skin` has no normal
    slot. **Fix:** put normal detail on `DetailsDmgNormal_*` instead.
11. **`.Pack.Gbx` will not open in Blender.** **Cause:** it is a package, not a mesh. **Fix:** pull
    the `.Solid.Gbx` and textures out first — either with Ninja Ripper, or, from ManiaPlanet, by
    unpacking the skin ZIP into `ManiaPlanet\Skins\Models\StadiumCar\<SkinName>\` and using Openplanet
    (developer mode) in the garage: F3 → System → Folders → MemoryTemp → PackDescContents →
    `_user__Skins_Models_StadiumCar_<SkinName>` → `Model.Pack.Gbx` → *Preload Nod* each member →
    *Extract*.
12. **Console players crash.** **Cause:** custom 3D skins, per the tutorial's own warning. **Fix:**
    treat this as a reason to keep custom skins private or limited, not as a bug to solve.

## Open questions
- Does the live build still accept the same `.MeshParams.xml` schema and material prefixes? Nothing
  here was validated against a current build.
- Which vertex budget actually applies per LOD today, and is it per-LOD or per-model?
- The Windows-only NadeoImporter is the one hard dependency; NICE and gbx-py are the parts that might
  run natively on Linux under Blender's own Python. Worth testing before assuming the route is
  Windows-only.

# Seamless co-op for TUNIC (BepInEx 6 IL2CPP, native hooks, autonomous 2-PC testing)

> A 2–8 player co-op mod for TUNIC as a BepInEx 6 IL2CPP plugin: player puppets with smooth animation, shared
> world flags, shared inventory/money, synced pots/coins/chests, per-enemy ownership with hit forwarding,
> scene transitions and death/respawn. It runs in the real game: the features were verified on two physical
> PCs plus a third game instance by an in-mod test autopilot driven over files/SSH, checked via state
> files, logs and screenshots the agent looked at. Verification lists what wasn't.

## Setup
- TUNIC (Steam 553420), Unity 2020.3.17f1, IL2CPP, product folder `AppData\LocalLow\Andrew Shouldice\Secret Legend`.
- BepInEx **6.0.0-pre.1 UnityIL2CPP x64** (same as the TUNIC Randomizer). Runtime is Mono → target `net472`.
  First launch generates interop assemblies in `BepInEx/unhollowed` (UnhollowerBaseLib, not Il2CppInterop).
- .NET 8 SDK; `ilspycmd` latest fails on .NET 8 → `dotnet tool install -g ilspycmd --version 8.2.0.7535`.
- LiteNetLib 1.2.0 (UDP, MIT) shipped next to the plugin.
- **Co-op scope.** Every player runs their own copy of TUNIC. LiteNetLib connects straight to the host's IP and
  port, and the host relays to the others. No game traffic goes through Steam networking or any other online
  service. Since v0.2.0 the mod also does a few things online, each behind a config switch: it asks the host's
  router to forward the port (UPnP), looks up the host's public address with one STUN request
  (`stun.l.google.com`), can use a self-hosted introducer that only exchanges addresses, checks GitHub once per
  launch for a newer release, and in a Steam copy sets Steam rich presence, so friends get "Join Game" with the
  join code in its `connect` string.

## Route and why
BepInEx plugin + **native code hooks**. The mod's hooks are MonoMod `NativeDetour`s on the IL2CPP methods'
native code, because an early Harmony attempt seemed not to fire. A later re-test showed Harmony **does** work
on this build (Gotcha 1), so either is fine for new work. World state is mostly **polled**, not hooked, because
hooks on the `SaveFile.SetInt`/`SetFloat`/`SetString` setters never saw the game's own writes (Gotcha 1).

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
- **Player**: `PlayerCharacter.instance` (static); `PlayerCharacter : Creature`; `Creature.cachedAnimator`;
  god mode for tests: static `PlayerCharacter.DebugInvincible`.
- **World state** is a flat KV store: `SaveFile.intStore/floatStore/stringStore` with `SetInt/SetFloat/SetString`;
  `StateVariable` wraps it (`NotifyAllSubscribers` wakes listeners). Opened chests = `"chest open <chestID>"`;
  inventory mirrors to `"inventory quantity <Item>"`; money item is `MoneySmall`. Per-player keys include
  `playtime`, `last spawn *`, `last campfire *`, `bloodstain *`, `hp_lost`, `Has Ever Died`.
- **Inventory**: `Inventory.itemList` (116 items), `Item.Quantity` get/set, `Inventory.GetItemByName`.
- **Coins**: pooled `ItemPickup`s: `CoinSpawner.poolList[].pool[]` (one `PooledFX` per denomination, value =
  `quantityToGive`), `CoinSpawner.SpawnCoins(value, pos)`, `PooledFX.GetNext(pos)`.
- **Breakables**: `SmashableObject` (`smashed`, `smash(force)`, `minCoinDrop/maxCoinDrop`), a
  `PermanentStateByPosition` → identify by position.
- **Chests**: `Chest` (`chestID`, `IInteractionReceiver_Interact`, coroutine class `_openSequence_d__35`);
  the opened key is written at open time. `BloodstainChest` is your dropped money after death.
- **Monsters**: `MonsterManager.instance.monsters`; `Monster.runtimeStableID.ID` is **identical across
  machines** (verified, 60/60). `Creature.hp` (setter clamps to maxhp), `IsDead`,
  `IDamageable_ReceiveDamage(dmg, poise, force, freeze, poison)`; `MonsterManager.checkMonster` deactivates
  monsters far from the *local* player.
- **Scenes**: `ScenePortal` (`destinationSceneName`, `id`, trigger collider); `ScenePortal.DepartToScene(runner,
  whiteout, duration, scene, id, pauseTime, delay)` is the clean programmatic transition to a connected area
  (for warps, see "Bosses, runtime spawns and sleepers").
- **Input**: InControl. `PlayerInput.Actions` (PlayerCharacterActionSet); gamepad bindings read at runtime:
  InteractDodge=Action1, Item1=Action3, Item2=Action4, Item3=Action2, Flask=RB, Shield=RT.
- **Title**: `TitleScreen.__Continue()/__NewGame()`; `FileManagementGUI.LoadFileAndStart(file)`.

## Build steps
1. Install BepInEx pre.1 into the game, run once.
2. `dotnet build src/TunicCoop -c Release -p:TunicDir=<game> -p:Deploy=true` (references `BepInEx/core` and
   `BepInEx/unhollowed`; copies `TunicCoop.dll` + `LiteNetLib.dll` to `BepInEx/plugins/TunicCoop`).
3. Architecture: `Net` (LiteNetLib star, host relays), `Puppet`+`Visibility` (player mirrors),
   `WorldSync` (poll + deltas), `CoinSync`, `SmashSync`, `ChestSync`, `MonsterSync`, `NativeHook`, `Autopilot`.

## Verification
An **in-mod autopilot** (`Debug.EnableAutopilot`): reads `BepInEx/coop_test/cmd.txt`, writes
`results.txt`/`state.json`, takes screenshots, drives a virtual InControl gamepad (`new InputDevice`,
`InputManager.AttachDevice`, values pushed in `InputManager.add_OnUpdateDevices`). Second PC driven over SSH
(file append + scp). Suite of ~40 checks, each from a fresh session (save reload): presence (puppet error
0.00 m both ways), coins (3 race scenarios, exact money), chests, pots, enemy ownership/positions/kills both
ways, enemies attacking the remote player (real hp loss), scene transitions, death + bloodstain recovery,
3 players. v0.2.0 grew it to ~106 checks: five bosses and the Cathedral gauntlet (players warped in, see
below), host rules, revive and bleed-out, pings/chat, shared camera, go-to-teammate, join codes, rejoin after a
simulated crash and a NAT punch-through relay. The last full run: 101/106; the 5 failures were boss-test setup
(fixed and re-run per boss). **Not verified**: The Heir (needs an endgame save), >3 players, UPnP on a router
that supports it, Steam "Join Game" (tests start the exe outside Steam).

The autopilot's input is a virtual device inside the game, so it never moves the OS mouse or keyboard. The
second PC was set up with the human (they authorized the SSH key); gotcha 5 says what a remote launch does
there. The same command-file pattern is written up in
`knowledge/techniques/driving-a-game-from-a-mod-side-command-file-lab-profile-wake.md`.

## Gotchas
1. **"Harmony never fires" was wrong; hooks on `SaveFile.SetInt` miss the game's writes.** The first attempt
   saw 0 calls on `Chest.Interact`, a coroutine `MoveNext` and `SaveFile.SetInt`. **Re-test**, patched exactly
   like the TUNIC Randomizer (`harmony.Patch(AccessTools.Method(...), postfix: new HarmonyMethod(...))`,
   counting postfixes, no native detour on the same methods): `PlayerCharacter.Update` 57,941 calls,
   `Chest.IInteractionReceiver_Interact` 1 per chest opened by the player, `Chest._openSequence_d__35.MoveNext`
   221, `SaveFile.SetInt` **0** while the chest wrote `chest open 15 = 1`. So pre.1's `FastNativeDetour` on the
   `MethodPointer` catches native and vtable callers. The first result was most likely a test that never really
   opened a chest: in the re-test the fox first stood *behind* the chest and Interact never ran. For the
   setters, our explanation is that `SetInt` and friends are tiny statics inlined into their callers, where no
   hook on them sees the write (not checked in the disassembly); either way, poll the stores instead. Don't put
   Harmony and a `NativeDetour` on the same method. **Native alternative (what the mod uses):** `NativeDetour`
   on `*(IntPtr*)NativeMethodInfoPtr_<method>` (first field of Il2CppMethodInfo = methodPointer); delegate
   `ret fn(IntPtr self, args…, IntPtr methodInfo)`; Win x64: Vector3 *args* by pointer, Vector3 *return* via a
   hidden first-arg buffer. Keep delegates alive. Verified with a counter on `PlayerCharacter.Update`
   (15k calls).
2. **Injected MonoBehaviour crashes the game at load** (native, nothing logged) after adding an iterator method
   and a `Nullable<Vector3>` return to the class. **Fix:** keep `ClassInjector` types to simple signatures;
   helpers in plain static classes.
3. **Exclusive fullscreen freezes unfocused** (even `Application.Quit` never completes; process stuck).
   **Fix:** test launches `-screen-fullscreen 0 -screen-width 1280 -screen-height 720`; set
   `Application.runInBackground` every frame; `InputManager.SuspendInBackground=false`.
4. **Relaunched game ran without BepInEx.** Child processes inherit `DOORSTOP_*` env vars and Doorstop skips.
   **Fix:** clear them before `Process.Start` (self-restart). Use `UseShellExecute=true` or the child's
   inherited handles hang Unity's quit.
5. **SSH can't start a windowed game.** Session 0. **Fix:** one-shot `schtasks /create … /it` → `/run` →
   `/delete` (date format may be yyyy/mm/dd); afterwards the game restarts itself from inside the session.
   Ask the human first: `/it` starts the game on the desktop of whoever is logged in on that PC.
6. **`ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshot` is stripped** ("Method unstripping failed") and **`Camera.allCameras`
   throws** `ObjectCollectedException`. **Fix:** `FindObjectsOfType<Camera>`, render main + overlay
   (Depth/Nothing clear) cameras into a RenderTexture, `ReadPixels`, `ImageConversion.EncodeToPNG`.
7. **Inputs ignored right after loading.** Loading a save plays an island camera flyover. **Fix:** wait until
   `Camera.main` is < 70 m from the fox (gameplay camera sits ~50 m away). `SceneLoader.Progress` parks at 0.9.
8. **Puppet shows every weapon/effect at once.** Prefab children are toggled by scripts the puppet doesn't
   have. **Fix:** sync per-child-path (FNV hash) active/renderer/emitting flags; send as a separate reliable
   delta message (the full 303-node table blew the ~1.4 KB unreliable MTU).
9. **Roll lags/offsets on puppets.** Roll is root motion + an Animator *trigger*. **Fix:** a component with an
   empty `OnAnimatorMove` (consumes root motion) + 100 ms snapshot interpolation + immediate send on animator
   state change + crossfade at the right offset.
10. **Money double-paid / diverged.** Polling item deltas raced with remote applies; game-paid coin pickups
    couldn't be deduplicated. **Fix:** shift the baseline by the applied delta; while connected set every coin's
    `quantityToGive=0` and credit once via an owner-arbitrated claim (first claim wins).
11. **Mirrored enemies all died instantly.** `hp = 9999` sentinel clamped to maxhp (10) → read as 9989 damage.
    **Fix:** pin mirror hp to the owner's streamed hp; damage = drop below the pin.
12. **Enemies won't attack the non-host.** Redirecting `get_playerOrBaitWorldPosition`, NavigatingMonster
    destination/facing, `ReceiveBroadcastAggro` all failed; `checkMonster` deactivates monsters far from the
    local fox. **Fix:** per-monster ownership by proximity with owner-driven handoff (≥4 m hysteresis): the
    unmodified AI then chases its local fox = the nearest player.
13. **Blue fox in Sword Cave on one PC only** = a TUNIC ghost-fox NPC tied to that save's progress, not a mod
    bug (prove by entering alone). Separately, tether-wand windup tentacles (own Animators) render as blue
    wisps on puppets and the real fox's hiding mechanism wasn't found → hidden on puppets.
14. **Test harness traps:** a steering command must stop on scene change (it walked the fox back out of the
    door it entered); multi-word scene names; dead monsters leave `MonsterManager.monsters`;
    `BloodstainChest` steals the interaction near your death spot; PowerShell `@(f) + @(g)` vs string concat.

## Bosses, runtime spawns and sleepers (v0.2.0)
- **Warp anywhere:** static `Cheats.CheatWarpToPortal(scene, fullId)` arrives at the portal whose
  `ScenePortal.FullID` (`<destinationScene>_<id>`) matches. `DepartToScene` from an unrelated area has no arrival
  portal and drops the fox into the void. List FullIDs by warping with an empty id and reading the scene's
  `ScenePortal`s before the fall.
- **Bosses are ordinary `Monster`s** (`Spidertank`, `Librarian`, `ScavengerBoss`, `Knightbot`, `Foxgod`); the
  Guard Captain is a 50 hp `Skuladin` named by a `BossAnnounceOnAggro`. Never hand an engaged boss (hp < max or
  aggroed) to another player: its phase state only exists in the owner's game. Defeat flags are plain SaveFile
  ints (`SV_Fortress Arena_Spidertank Is Dead`, `Librarian Dead Forever`, `SV_ScavengerBossesDead`,
  `SV_Archipelagos Redux TUNIC Knight is Dead`, `SV_Forest Boss Room_Skuladot redux Big`).
- **Mirrors replay attacks.** A mirrored boss's own explosions damage it on the mirror machine. Mirrors must
  never decide their own damage or death: forward the local player's hit from the damage hook, keep the mirror
  at ≥1 hp, and die only when the owner says so. If that message lands in post-hit invulnerability, call
  `Monster.Die()` directly.
- **Runtime spawns** (boss adds, `(Clone)`s) have no `RuntimeStableID`: the spawning machine names them; others
  pair by name + distance or instantiate a copy from a same-named monster/prefab.
- **Sleepers** (Cathedral wave altars, ambushes) are pre-placed and inactive until a trigger in one game. An
  object that never ran Awake has `Monster.runtimeStableID == null`: read the component and derive
  `buildIndex * 1e6 + intraSceneID`, wake your copy, mirror the claimer's.
- **Defaults aren't progress:** a scene writes new SaveFile keys = 0 on load; syncing them reset a teammate's
  altars. `Creature.ModifyDefensePower` doesn't affect direct `IDamageable_ReceiveDamage`: scale damage in
  your own hook. `DownloadHandlerBuffer` is stripped (use `HttpWebRequest` + TLS 1.2); `steam_api64.dll`
  (needed for rich presence) sits in `Tunic_Data/Plugins/x86_64`, where Mono's DllImport misses it
  (`GetModuleHandle` + `GetProcAddress`).
- **Test rig traps:** saves autosave in boss arenas, so the next session loads there; fast chasers close any
  distance you set up (freeze the boss's AI on its owner first); config changes made by one test persist.

## Assets
None (no new art).

## Cost and time
One long agent session over ~2 days, plus two short human interventions (authorizing an SSH key, ending one
hung process the sandbox couldn't kill).

## Open questions
- The Heir (`Foxgod`) fight and its cutscenes under the boss rules (needs an endgame save).
- Internet play without port forwarding now uses UPnP when the router allows it, or a self-hosted relay
  (LiteNetLib `NatPunchModule` introducer) that only exchanges addresses; game traffic stays a direct
  connection. Neither has been tried across two real NATs yet.
- Why the tether-wand windup tentacles are invisible on the real fox (renderer flags, forceRenderingOff,
  bones, bounds, animator state, property blocks and materials were all identical).

# BG3-style controller support for Underrail: stick movement, context interaction, menus, bars and combat via a Cecil-patched input layer

> A full gamepad layer for Underrail (XNA 4, .NET 4, x86, Dotfuscator-renamed) aimed at the Steam Deck:
> left-stick direct movement outside combat, nearest-object highlight + one-button interaction, a stick/D-pad
> cursor for every menu, L2/R2 bar navigation, console-style window switching, a stick cursor in turn-based
> combat, and an Options > Controller tab with a drawn DualSense schema. A Cecil installer injects one call
> into the game loop and redirects all mouse/keyboard polls into the mod. Play-tested in the real game on
> macOS through CrossOver with a DualSense; the Steam Deck run is not yet verified.

## Setup
- Game: Underrail **1.3.1.2**, Steam, build 21973456. `underrail.exe` is a 32-bit IL-only .NET Framework 4
  assembly (8.5 MB); XNA 4.0 comes from the GAC (installed by Steam's redist), SFML is only used for audio.
- Dev box: macOS, game in a CrossOver bottle. No Homebrew: .NET 8 SDK via `dotnet-install.sh` into
  `~/.dotnet`. `ilspycmd` latest needs a newer runtime: `dotnet tool install -g ilspycmd --version 8.2.0.7535`
  and run with `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major`.
- Mod: C# `net40`, x86, references `underrail.exe` (always the clean `underrail.orig.exe`) plus
  `Microsoft.Xna.Framework{,.Game,.Graphics}.dll` from the bottle's `windows/Microsoft.NET/assembly/GAC_32`.
  `Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies` makes `net40` build on macOS.
- Controller: XNA `GamePad.GetState` (XInput). Wine/CrossOver presents a DualSense as XInput; on the Deck use a
  Steam Input "Gamepad" layout (not "Keyboard (WASD) and Mouse").

## Route and why
`managed-patch`: decompile with ILSpy, write a separate mod DLL compiled against the game exe, and patch the
exe with Mono.Cecil. No loader exists for Underrail; BepInEx has no supported path for plain .NET Framework XNA
games; Harmony would still need a bootstrap. Two patches cover everything:
1. `call PadMod.Tick(this)` at the top of `tb.Update` (the `Game` subclass's Update).
2. Every parameterless `Mouse.GetState()` / `Keyboard.GetState()` call in the exe (7 + 23 sites) retargeted to
   the mod's `VirtualInput.GetMouse()/GetKeyboard()`, which return the real state merged with controller-made
   buttons/keys. The GUI then sees ordinary clicks, drags, double-clicks and key presses everywhere.
The patched exe is never distributed: the release ships an installer that verifies the exe hash, keeps
`underrail.orig.exe`, and patches the player's own copy.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
Names are Dotfuscator-renamed but stable per build; string literals are plain (no string encryption), no
tamper checks, exe not strong-named.
- **Loop/input:** `tb : Game`; `tb.Update` polls Mouse/Keyboard into a per-frame context `e6d`; Draw polls
  separately (latch virtual state per frame). GUI manager `bso` (service `d1a`/`bcm`): `aau()` root screen,
  `aa7()` focus, `aa8()` control under mouse, `aam()` text capture. Controls derive from `euz`
  (`Controls`, `Visible`, `Enabled`, `Ghost`, `IsShadow`, `at()` absolute pos, `Size` (`esj`)); clickables
  from `cao`. Clicks fire on release if the press started on the same control; double-click = 350 ms.
- **Player and movement:** player data `bpo.GetService<cnk>().aqu().v()` (don't use `ces.c()`, it throws
  at the main menu); entity `c5x`, `Location` in tile units. Move = trekker aspect `ale.a(tile, stopDist,
  retries, delayMs)` → action queue → path request in a time-sliced path processor. Tile lookup
  `aud.b(x,y)` (null outside). Vanilla click walkability: `tile.a(player.a().d)` (tile flags vs movement
  mask). Isometric 2:1 diamond tiles: screen right = tile (+1,-1), screen down = (+1,+1).
- **Modes:** turn-based combat `dz6.e()`; dialog/busy via the `ps` service (`dka`): `alc()`, `alg()`.
  In-game windows are `LocaleSubInterfaceController<,>` fields on `dka`: `j()` open, plus open/close
  methods the hotkey handler calls (`alv/alw` inventory, `al3/z` character, `al8/al9` map, ...).
  Pending ability target: `bpo.GetService<bi3>().aij() != null`.
- **Interaction:** `ps.aln(entity)` returns the command a left-click would issue (talk, use, disarm, attack);
  `cmd.io() && cmd.a(ent)` then `cmd.f1(cnk.aqw())` runs it exactly like a click. Right-click options:
  usable aspect `bim.jz()`; menu via `bc.a(screen, screen.n(), bim, point)`.
- **Picking:** per-pixel over last frame's sprite list (`a7m` private `List<cy5>`); the private
  `a7m.a(int x, int y, out bool)` is the real hover pick and stops at fade-able walls in front.
- **HUD:** bottom bar `ci3.n()` (`ek7`): action slots `cqn`, weapons `tt`, shield `efq/dvx`, belt `boq/dho`.
  Window buttons `ci3.m()` (`e60`, `cep` buttons). Speed/zoom are `doz` buttons on `ci3` (first four
  `doz` fields: speed up, slow down, zoom out, zoom in); clicking them via `euz.a(eoo.b)` runs the game's
  own handlers. Camera `an9()` (`c5m`) has 8 scroll methods used by edge scrolling; playfield settings
  `dnx` toggle mouse edge scrolling.
- **UI building:** options screen `t1` uses a tab control `dpg` (`n()` tab list of `cvh` pages,
  `b(esj)` tab size); `bg1` draws a `Func<Texture2D>`; `bnr.a(...)` is a one-call message box.

## Build steps
1. Decompile outside the repo: `ilspycmd -p -o ~/underrail-decomp underrail.exe`.
2. Build the mod DLL (`net40`, x86) against `underrail.orig.exe` + XNA GAC assemblies.
3. Patcher/installer (net8, Mono.Cecil): back up to `underrail.orig.exe`, verify sha256, insert
   `ldarg.0; call PadMod.Tick` before the first instruction of `tb.Update`, retarget the GetState calls,
   write `underrail.exe`. Always patch from the backup so reruns are idempotent; detect a Steam update by
   "current exe has no AssemblyRef to the mod but differs from the backup" and drop the stale backup.
4. Release: `dotnet publish -r win-x64|linux-x64 --self-contained -p:PublishSingleFile=true
   -p:PublishTrimmed=true -p:TrimMode=partial` (11 MB; full trimming isn't needed, partial keeps Cecil
   working) zipped with the DLL and assets; `um publish check` passes.

## Verification
- Oracles: a mod log (`UnderrailPad.log`) with mode transitions, each move order (`moved`, `offLine`,
  probed tiles ok/x), each selection (entity type + command), bar slot lists, and errors; a mouse-click
  calibration logger proved `Location` == tile index; a dry-run patch on a copied folder diffed with Cecil
  (types/methods/resources identical) and PE `.rsrc` intact; the installer was exercised end-to-end
  (install, rerun, simulated game update, uninstall) and its output is byte-identical to the dev patch.
- Real-game playtests on macOS/CrossOver with a DualSense across ~15 iterations: walking, interaction,
  menus, dialogue, loot, save/load, bars, windows, combat cursor.
- NOT verified: the Steam Deck/Proton run, native Windows, the Linux installer binary on Linux (the same
  code was run as an osx-arm64 build), vehicles, very long sessions, GOG (different exe; refused).

## Gotchas
1. **Mod dies at the main menu.** `ces.c()` throws when no game is loaded and the error budget ran out in a
   second. **Fix:** walk `bpo.GetService<cnk>()?.aqu()?.v()` with null checks; isolate optional features.
2. **Reflection by field name finds nothing.** ILSpy shows `m_h` etc. when a field collides with a method
   name; the IL name is `h`. **Fix:** look fields up by type (each window controller type is unique).
3. **C# can't bind obfuscated members.** A field and a method share a name (`c5x.k`, `esj.c/d`, `dnn.d`),
   so the compiler picks the method group. **Fix:** use helpers (`esj.b()` returns size as Vector2),
   `GetAspect<T>()`, or reflection by type.
4. **Stick walking stutters.** Each re-issued move cancels the path and the time-sliced path processor answers
   a frame or more later; the character idles meanwhile. **Fix:** after `ale.a(...)` call
   `Playfield.PathProcessor.a()` (drains the queue synchronously; the game does this before saving).
5. **Most directions "blocked".** `ale.a(ak1)` is not the click walkability test. **Fix:** use
   `tile.a(player.a().d)` (what the move cursor uses).
6. **Character drifts to neighbouring lines / wrong angle.** Re-aiming from the current position accumulates
   grid-path error. **Fix:** lock a line per stick direction (anchor + direction, keep under ~12° wobble),
   aim 3 tiles ahead along it, re-steer every ~250 ms.
7. **Releasing the stick walks back a tile.** Stopping at round(position) can be behind. **Fix:** stop on the
   nearest walkable tile not behind the walking direction.
8. **Doors only highlight with the Highlight key.** The hover picker walks sprites front-to-back and a
   fade-able wall sprite in front ends the pick with nothing. **Fix:** choose cursor pixels with the game's
   own pick method (`a7m.a(int,int,out bool)` via reflection) so the door really is hovered; run the
   interaction command directly so even fully hidden doors work.
9. **Square moves the camera.** Right-click on an object without options selects it (camera focus).
   **Fix:** only open `bim.jz()` options when there are any.
10. **Context menus not detected as menus.** They are plain controls added to the root (`exj`/`bys`), not
    modals. **Fix:** search the root for visible `exj`/`bys`.
11. **"Real mouse moved" false positives under Wine.** `Mouse.SetPosition` reads back a pixel off.
    **Fix:** 3 px tolerance.
12. **Stick cursor scrolls the map at screen edges.** **Fix:** turn off `dnx` mouse edge scrolling while a pad
    is connected; restore on disconnect.
13. **D-pad up/left re-snaps to the same button.** Snap points are nudged down-right of centre, so the current
    button counts as "up-left". **Fix:** skip the control under the cursor.
14. **Speed/zoom mapping.** `ci3` has 5 `doz` fields; the first four (declaration order) are speed up, slow
    down, zoom out, zoom in.
15. **Single-press loot/save-load.** Items and save rows act on double-click. **Fix:** a scripted
    down/up/down/up over four Update frames (well inside 350 ms) when the hovered control is a `cqy` inside
    the loot window `c15` or a save row `afg`.
16. **A custom overlay caused graphical artifacts** during gameplay (an `ec9` frame + ghost label added to the
    game screen root). Cause not isolated; removed the overlay. Help lives in an Options tab instead.
17. **Loaded PNG has dark fringes.** XNA blends premultiplied alpha; `Texture2D.FromStream` doesn't
    premultiply. **Fix:** premultiply the pixel data once after loading.
18. **Patched exe is ~390 KB smaller.** Cecil compacts heaps; type/method counts, resources and `.rsrc`
    are identical. Not a problem.
19. **Repo tooling on macOS system Python 3.9.** `um kb new/index` fail (`write_text(newline=)`, PEP 604
    types at runtime in places); `um publish check` works. Use Python 3.10+ (uv) for the kb commands.

## Assets
The DualSense schema is vector-drawn with Pillow (`Tools/make_schema.py` in the mod source: Bézier body
outline, glow pass, leader-line callouts laid out per column) rather than AI-generated, so every callout lands
on its button. Style: thin amber (the game's accent is `(174, 87, 0)`) on transparent, DIN/Avenir Next
Condensed.

## Cost and time
One long session (~3 hours wall clock) with ~15 play-test iterations; research delegated to a sub-agent that
read the decompile and answered targeted questions (movement, input, UI, picking, windows).

## Open questions
- Steam Deck/Proton verification (XInput through Steam Input, performance of per-frame reflection).
- Root cause of the overlay artifacts (draw order vs the game's render targets?).
- Native combat polish: snapping the combat cursor to enemies/tiles, End Turn/target cycling on the D-pad.
- A version-independent build: resolve the obfuscated names by signature/strings at install time so game
  updates don't need a mod release.
