# Frostner into Mjolnir: a returning thunder hammer for Valheim 1.0

> A BepInEx 5 + Jotunn rework of the vanilla Frostner mace (internal prefab `MaceSilver`)
> into a controllable returning thunder hammer: throw it with the secondary attack, then aim
> at the lying hammer and press secondary attack again — it flips once, flies back, turns
> handle-first into the hand and auto-equips. Verified in the real game over dozens of
> throw/recall cycles on a native-Linux (Steam Deck) install.

## Setup

- Game: Valheim **1.0** (l-1.0.16, network 40), Steam appid 892970, buildid 25527674,
  **Unity 6000.0.75f1 (Unity 6), Mono backend**. Native Linux build (`valheim.x86_64`).
- Loader: **BepInExPack_Valheim 5.4.2351** (denikson; preconfigured, ships
  `start_game_bepinex.sh` + `libdoorstop_x64.so` for Linux). Library: **Jotunn 2.30.2**.
- Plugin: C# / **net472** (Jotunn is net462), built with .NET SDK 8 +
  `Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies`. References: `assembly_valheim.dll`
  (the actual game code — `Assembly-CSharp.dll` is nearly empty in 1.0), `assembly_utils.dll`,
  the split `UnityEngine.*Module.dll` set, BepInEx core + Jotunn.
- Saves: `~/.config/unity3d/IronGate/Valheim/` on Linux (worlds + characters + `Player.log`).

## Route and why

BepInEx 5 + Jotunn + Harmony (managed patch). No new item is created — the vanilla Frostner
prefab itself is mutated on `PrefabManager.OnVanillaPrefabsAvailable` (Jotunn), so every
Frostner the player owns or crafts gains the powers. This keeps saves and multiplayer
consistency simple, and matches the "rework the existing item" request.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

- **Spear throw = secondary attack.** `ItemDrop.ItemData.SharedData.m_attack` (primary) and
  `m_secondaryAttack` are separate `Attack` objects; spears throw via the secondary
  (`AttackType.Projectile` + `m_attackProjectile`). Frostner's own secondary is a melee slam —
  we replace it with `SpearSplitner_Lightning.m_shared.m_secondaryAttack.Clone()`.
- **The throw consumes the item.** `Attack.m_consumeItem` → `ConsumeItem()` removes the weapon
  from the inventory at throw time (`UnequipItem` + `Inventory.RemoveItem`). The thrown
  `ItemData` instance arrives in `Projectile.Setup(owner, velocity, hitNoise, hitData, item, ammo)`.
- **Item drop on hit.** Inside its own body, `Projectile.Setup` reads `m_respawnItemOnHit` and
  stores `m_spawnItem = item`; `OnHit` → `SpawnOnHit` → `ItemDrop.DropItem(...)` **clones**
  the ItemData and drops it. A Harmony **postfix** is too late to prevent this — patch `Setup`
  with a **Prefix** and set `m_respawnItemOnHit = false` + `m_spawnItem = null` before the body
  runs. Also set `m_stayAfterHitStatic/Dynamic = true`, `m_attachToRigidBody/Bone = false`,
  `m_ttl = 0` so the projectile survives and waits.
- **Unarmed is a weapon.** `Humanoid.GetCurrentWeapon()` returns `m_unarmedWeapon.m_itemData`
  when hands are empty — the unarmed secondary is the kick. To intercept "press while unarmed",
  patch `Humanoid.StartAttack(Character target, bool secondaryAttack)` with a **Prefix**
  (before the busy checks) and only consume the press when `GetCurrentWeapon()` is null or the
  unarmed weapon.
- **EquipItem refuses while attacking.** `Humanoid.EquipItem` returns false during
  `InAttack()/InDodge()`. Playing an attack animation for the "catch" gesture put the character
  in that state and silently broke auto-equip. Use the one-shot `interact` trigger
  (`Character.GetZAnim().SetTrigger("interact")`) for the reach, check `EquipItem`'s bool, and
  retry for ~2.5 s if it fails.
- **Hand position.** `VisEquipment.m_rightHand` (public Transform); get the component via
  `owner.GetComponent<VisEquipment>()` (`Humanoid.m_visEquipment` is protected).
- **Console gating.** F5 works only when the game was started with `-console`
  (`FejdStartup.ParseArguments` → `Console.SetConsoleEnabledForThisSession()`); there is no
  runtime toggle. On Linux, launch via `./start_game_bepinex.sh -console`.

## Key facts

- **Frostner's internal name is `MaceSilver`** (not "Frostner" — that string does not exist
  anywhere in 1.0's assets). The RU name is Ледомор.
- Lightning assets (exact names, from `valheim_Data/StreamingAssets/SoftRef/manifest_extended`,
  which is a readable text catalog — grep it instead of the hashed bundles):
  `SpearSplitner_Lightning`, `projectile_splitner_lightning`, `fx_lightningweapon_hit`,
  `sfx_mistlands_thunder`, `sfx_staffthunderblood_thunder`.
- Weapon model in hand: child `attach` → `attachobj` (`ItemStand.GetAttachPrefab`).
- Damage lives in `SharedData.m_damages` (plural!).
- `Inventory.AddItem(ItemData)` / `ContainsItem` / `RemoveItem`; `ItemDrop.DropItem(item, amount, pos, rot)`.
- Valheim 1.0 stores content in Addressables-style `SoftRef/Bundles/<hash>` bundles; prefab
  names are in `SoftRef/manifest_extended`.

## Build steps

1. `um backup` the saves.
2. BepInExPack_Valheim into the game folder (keep `start_game_bepinex.sh`), Jotunn into
   `BepInEx/plugins/Jotunn/`.
3. `dotnet build -c Release` (net472) → `BepInEx/plugins/Mjolnir/Mjolnir.dll`.
4. Launch on Linux: `./start_game_bepinex.sh -console` (Steam launch option:
   `./start_game_bepinex.sh %command%`).
5. Drive the mod without synthetic input: the plugin polls
   `<persistentDataPath>/mjolnir-cmd.txt` (commands `give`, `restyle <prefab> [scale]`) and
   writes `mjolnir.log` next to it. Console commands: `mjolnir give | restyle ...`.

## Verification

Oracle: the mod's own log during hand-played sessions (native Linux, Steam Deck), dozens of
cycles. The full chain logs as `projectile setup: Mjolnir thrown by ...` →
`mjolnir deployed at (x,y,z)` → `return start (summon)` → `reach animation: interact` →
`catch: returned to inventory` → `catch: equipped to hand`. Edge cases verified: recall while
walking, early grab by pressing the wheel when the hammer is close (< 4.5 m), kick preserved
when aiming away from the hammer, full inventory → item drops at feet, projectile timeout
(6 s) drops the item safely so it can never be lost.

## Gotchas

1. **`pgrep -f valheim.x86_64` false-positives on your own shell command** (the pattern is in
   the script's own cmdline). Use `pgrep -x valheim.x86_64`.
2. **Duplicated item on the ground:** `Projectile.Setup` must be patched with a Prefix; a
   postfix runs after `m_spawnItem` was stored and the clone is dropped on hit.
3. **The kick eats the recall:** `GetCurrentWeapon()` returns `m_unarmedWeapon` when unarmed —
   check it, not null.
4. **Auto-equip silently fails** when the catch gesture leaves the player `InAttack()` —
   check the bool and retry; use `interact`, not an attack animation.
5. **Thunderstore zips use backslashes** — extract with 7z/bsdtar/python.
6. **`ilspycmd` needs** `DOTNET_ROOT` and `DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor` on a newer SDK.
7. **`um publish check` flags your own deployed plugin** as a copied game file — check the
   release staging folder with the deployed DLL temporarily moved out.
8. The 1.0 Splitner throw fires a big launch wave (`Attack.m_burstEffect`/`m_triggerEffect`/
   `m_startEffect`) — clear those lists on the cloned attack and put the drama on impact
   (`fx_lightningweapon_hit` in the projectile's `m_hitEffects`).

## Cost and time

A few sessions of iterative play-testing; no API spend (all assets are the game's own, "bring
your own game files").

# South Central 1985: a Victoria 2 total conversion into an LA gang-territory game

> A data-only total conversion. The world map is replaced with South LA, generated from real neighbourhood
> boundaries: 265 land provinces, 98 states and 54 playable gang sets plus LAPD, the Sheriff and La Eme as a
> sphere-leading great power. The changes include:
> - the 48 goods re-skinned as a criminal economy (crack, pistols, stolen cars, counterfeit money);
> - populations scaled to real neighbourhood sizes (~3.7M in total);
> - 1985–1992 events;
> - procedurally drawn goods icons and event pictures.
>
> It loads, plays and survived a 19-year soak at max speed (1985 → 2004) with no crash. This was checked with
> in-game screenshots, logs and a scripted soak test.

## Setup
- **Game:** Victoria II with Heart of Darkness 3.04 (Steam), on Windows 11.
  - `victoria2.exe` is only the .NET launcher. The real game is `v2game.exe`: 32-bit, ASLR, no anti-cheat.
  - That is why `um scan` reports ".NET".
- **Mod layout:** `<game>\mod\SouthCentral\` plus `<game>\mod\SouthCentral.mod`. Mods go in the game folder,
  not Documents.
- **User data and logs:** with `user_dir = "SouthCentral"` they go to
  `Documents\Paradox Interactive\Victoria II\SouthCentral\` (`logs\`, `map\cache\`).
- **Launch:**
  `Start-Process v2game.exe -ArgumentList "-mod=mod/SouthCentral.mod" -WorkingDirectory <game>`.
- **Windowed mode:** set `fullScreen=no` in `<game>\settings.txt`. Back it up first.
- **Map source:** click_that_hood `los-angeles-county.geojson` (LA Times "Mapping L.A.", 272 neighbourhoods).
- **Build:** everything is generated by Python scripts.
  - The scripts are `mapgen` → `histgen` → `econgen` → `themegen` → `eventgen` → `texgen` → `icongen` →
    `install`.
  - Nothing is hand-edited in the mod folder, so every change is a rebuild.

## Route and why
- **Chosen route:** data/script only, with `replace_path` in the `.mod` descriptor. Paradox games expose
  nearly everything as text, BMP, CSV and DDS, and that was enough for a full conversion.
- **Native work was only for diagnosis.** No exe patching: the Python ctypes debugger and capstone were used
  only to *understand* crashes. Every fix stayed in data.
- **Considered and rejected:**
  - Adapting an existing big mod (e.g. CWE). It would drag in a whole world.
  - Extending the vanilla map. You can't shrink the world without replacing `map/` wholesale.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Map files (`map/`)
- **`provinces.bmp`:** 24-bit, one colour per province.
- **`terrain.bmp` and `rivers.bmp`:** 8-bit palettised. In terrain, index 254 = water. In rivers, 255 = no
  river.
- **`definition.csv`:** `id;r;g;b;name;x`.
- **`default.map`:** contains `max_provinces` and `sea_starts`.
- **`positions.txt`:** y is flipped relative to the BMP (`H - y`).
- **Also needed:** `region.txt`, `region_sea.txt`, `continent.txt`, `climate.txt`, `adjacencies.csv`.
- **No wasteland:** V2 has no real impassable wasteland, so the map edge is ringed with sea provinces.
  - We used two kinds: "outside the area" and "ocean".
  - Each is a coarse grid, so no province gets too big.
- **Province colours:** the engine expects province ids to keep the vanilla `definition.csv` colour for that
  id (see Gotcha 4). We generate the map so that province `n` uses vanilla province `n`'s RGB.

### History loading
- **`replace_path` is not recursive.** Each vanilla subfolder needs its own line.
- **`history/*` paths must use the engine's capitalisation:** `history/Provinces/<sub>`, `history/Wars`,
  `history/Countries`. Lowercase alone did not take effect.
- **The *presence* of some files creates objects:**
  - a war file with no participants creates an empty war;
  - a province file with no data resets that province.

### Economy
- **Keep the vanilla goods keys.** Techs, inventions, pop needs, the icon strip order and some hard-coded
  references assume the 48 vanilla keys. So we re-skinned them through localisation instead of adding new
  ones. Examples:
  - `furniture` = Crack, `paper` = Counterfeit money, `radio` = Motorbikes, `luxury_furniture` = Lowriders;
  - `small_arms` = Pistols, `artillery` = Assault rifles, `timber` = Stolen cars, `silk` = Cocaine kilos.
- **New buildings work:** we added two (PCP lab, meth lab) with their own production types plus artisan
  versions. They are unlocked with `activate_building` inside an existing invention.
- **Factory inputs were rescaled** so each chain's input value ≈ output value / 1.35 at the new target prices.
  Otherwise re-pricing goods makes every factory lose money.
- **Building factories depends on the ruling party.** A country can build factories only if its ruling
  party's `economic_policy` allows it (`state_capitalism` / `planned_economy`). Gangs got an "OG" party with
  `state_capitalism`.
- **Starting tech goes in `history/countries/<TAG>.txt`** (`<tech> = 1`, `<invention> = yes`). We gave every
  gang a starter kit that unlocks the basic factory types. Don't use `default_enabled` (Gotcha 8).

### Events
- **`fire_only_once = yes` is global.** The event fires for one country in the whole world, not once per
  country.
- **The `month` trigger did not fire reliably** in our tests.
- **What worked:** a year window plus `mean_time_to_happen`, with a per-country flag set in the option.
  - Trigger: `NOT = { has_country_flag = X }`.
  - Option: `set_country_flag = X`.
- **Event pictures:** 521x203 TGA, referenced as `picture = "name"` and looked up in `gfx/pictures/events/`.

### Graphics
- **Goods icon strips** live in `gfx/interface/` and hold 49 frames: frame 0 empty, then the goods in
  `goods.txt` order.

  | File | Frame size |
  |---|---|
  | `resources_big.dds` | 35x29 |
  | `resources.dds` | 28x23 |
  | `resources_small.dds` | 20x16 |

- **Uncompressed DDS works everywhere:** A8R8G8B8 with a 128-byte header, `DDPF_RGB|ALPHAPIXELS`, masks
  `00FF0000/0000FF00/000000FF/FF000000`. We never needed DXT compression.
- **Colormaps:**
  - `map/terrain/colormap*.dds` are top-down, the same orientation as `provinces.bmp`.
  - Sizes: `colormap_water.dds` 936x360 with 10 mips; the others ~1880x720 with no mips.
  - `gfx/interface/minimap.dds` is an interface texture; we fill it with political colours.
- **Flags:** `gfx/flags/<TAG>[_<gov>].tga` at 93x64. 32-bit RLE TGA is safe.

### Pops and scale
- **Shrink the regiment defines** so pops of a few hundred can raise units: in `defines.lua` we used
  `POP_MIN_SIZE_FOR_REGIMENT 30` and `POP_SIZE_PER_REGIMENT 100`.
- **Population sizes:** we set each neighbourhood's density from real-world figures (people/km²), then split
  it by an ethnic mix. That gives a realistic ~10–100k per province instead of millions.

## Build steps
1. Rasterise the neighbourhood polygons onto a canvas (LA ~46 px/km, 5616x2160 like vanilla).
   - Assign owner seeds per neighbourhood and split it among gangs.
   - k-means each owner's area into provinces of ≤ ~32 km², capped well under 70k px.
   - Fix contiguity, then wrap the land in sea grid cells.
2. Write all map files.
   - Use vanilla colours per id.
   - Keep all vanilla continent names defined. Put every land province in `north_america` and leave the
     others empty.
   - Write `region_sea.txt` as one empty region.
3. Generate the remaining data:
   - countries, parties, cultures, religions;
   - country history (techs and starter kit);
   - province history (owner, core, `trade_goods`), pops, OOBs;
   - defines, bookmarks, economy, localisation (cp1252, `;`-separated, CRLF), events, textures, icons.
4. `install.py`:
   - Write the `.mod` with `replace_path` for every vanilla folder and subfolder, in both spellings.
   - Add a placeholder file to otherwise empty folders.
   - Shadow vanilla files with empty stubs, **except** `history/provinces`, `history/wars` and
     `history/diplomacy`.
   - Copy the mod over.
   - Delete `Documents\...\SouthCentral\map\cache`.
5. Launch with `-mod=mod/SouthCentral.mod`.

## Verification
- **Oracles:**
  - Screenshots of the nation picker, political map, production screen, tech tree, build-factory dialog and
    events, read back each time.
  - `Documents\...\SouthCentral\logs\*.log`.
  - A scripted **soak test** (PowerShell + WinDrive). It launches, clicks Single Player → a nation → Play,
    sets max speed, waits N seconds, then reports the last in-game date and whether the process is alive.
- **Crash diagnosis:**
  - A ~200-line Python ctypes debugger: Wow64 thread context, EBP chain walk, module map.
  - An int3 breakpoint probe.
  - capstone disassembly around the faulting VA, plus string references to name the subsystem.
  - With ASLR, `static VA = runtime − base + 0x400000`. WER offsets are RVAs.
- **Results:**
  - The 19-year soak ran with no crash.
  - Events fired as intended: the crack event 51× (once per gang), Operation Hammer 1×, raids 51×, 1992 riots
    49×, Watts truce 2×, Eme tax 115×.
  - The AI builds factories (labs).
- **Not verified:**
  - Multiplayer.
  - Game balance beyond "AI survives 19 years".
  - Close-zoom terrain textures, which still look vanilla.
  - Unit sprites and tech pictures (vanilla).

## Gotchas
1. **Vanilla countries and provinces still loaded under the new map.** **Cause:** `replace_path` is not
   recursive, and empty mod folders replace nothing. **Fix:** one `replace_path` per vanilla subfolder, plus a
   placeholder file in each otherwise empty folder.
2. **`replace_path = "history/provinces/usa"` had no effect.** **Cause:** the engine matches its own spelling,
   `history/Provinces/usa`. **Fix:** emit both spellings for every `history/*` path.
3. **Crash in trade-goods code right after loading.** **Cause:** empty stub files for vanilla province
   histories load *after* ours (same ids, different subfolders) and wipe owner and `trade_goods`. **Fix:**
   never stub `history/provinces`. Replacing the paths is enough.
4. **Heap corruption at startup, at random places.** Several causes together:
   - Sea provinces of ~185k px: vanilla's largest is ~69.5k. Keep provinces under ~70k px.
   - A stale map cache in `Documents\...\<user_dir>\map\cache`: the engine reuses it even after the map
     changed. Delete it on every install.
   - Province colours that differed from vanilla `definition.csv` for the same id: under the debugger, our sea
     province 266 carried Aberdeen's colour. Use vanilla colours per id.
   - Missing vanilla continent names: other files reference them. Keep `north_america`, `europe`, `asia`,
     `africa`, `south_america` and `oceania` defined, even when empty.
   - `region_sea.txt` listing our sea provinces: write it vanilla-style, as an empty region.
5. **Crash when pressing Play, inside war-name formatting.** **Cause:** a stub file in `history/wars` creates
   a war with no participants. **Fix:** no stubs for `history/wars` or `history/diplomacy`.
6. **"Build factories: No" for every gang.** **Cause:** the ruling party's `economic_policy` was
   `laissez_faire` / `interventionism`. **Fix:** use a `state_capitalism` party as the starting ruling party.
7. **Only one country in the world got the "crack arrives" event, and month-based events never fired.**
   **Cause:** `fire_only_once` is global, and the `month` trigger was unreliable. **Fix:** per-country flags
   plus a year window plus MTTH.
8. **Crash about 3 weeks in.** It was at static VA 0x857559, in AI building choice: it dereferenced a
   building with no production type. **Cause:** `default_enabled = yes` on every factory building. **Fix:**
   remove it, and give starting techs and inventions in country history instead.
9. **Goods icons showed vanilla meat and fabric.** **Cause:** the icon strips are by index, not by key.
   **Fix:** regenerate the three `resources*.dds` strips in `goods.txt` order, with frame 0 empty.
10. **The harbour appeared in the north of the map.** **Cause:** we flipped the colormap vertically, assuming
    DDS was bottom-up. **Fix:** no flip; colormaps are top-down like `provinces.bmp`.
11. **"Artillery" was renamed in a confusing way.** **Cause:** the unit and the good share the localisation
    key `artillery`. **Fix:** localise it once, with a name that fits both, or drop the unit.
12. **Windows/agent environment:**
    - The Store `python` alias virtualises writes under `AppData`, so the game never saw the generated files.
      Use the real interpreter path.
    - Files written from the Bash sandbox were not always visible to Windows processes. Do file operations
      from PowerShell or the real Python.

## Assets
- **No AI image generation in the final build.** The fal account ran out of balance, so everything is drawn
  in code with Pillow.
- **48 goods icons:** drawn at 140x116, 4× supersampled, with outline and drop shadow, then downscaled into the
  three strips.
- **5 event pictures:** flat illustrations at 521x203.
- **Other generated art:** flags (5 government variants per tag, generated from gang colours), colormaps (an
  urban palette per neighbourhood type, a mile street grid, freeways, the LA River, beaches) and the minimap.

## Cost and time
- About one long agent session (~6 h wall clock), including about 1.5 h chasing startup heap corruption.
- No paid assets.

## Open questions
- Close-zoom terrain textures (`map/terrain/*.dds` atlas) and the water normal maps are still vanilla.
- No new unit sprites or tech pictures.
- Balance is untuned: police AI aggression, gang growth, and RGO output per km².
- It is unknown whether `month` triggers can work. Their failure may be specific to how we combined them with
  MTTH.

# Space Marine 2 missions: scenario faction swaps, level files, the ESD spawn director and rebaking a navmesh with spawn points

> Mission-level modding in Space Marine 2: swapping a mission stage's enemies from Chaos to Tyranids (working in
> game), turning the campaign prologue into a PvE operation with the stock enemy spawn director (in progress: the map
> plays, the navmesh was rebuilt with 388 spawn points, enemies from the director not yet seen),
> per-level vehicle swaps, and why the 12-player flag splits the hub barge. Builds on
> [the foundations note](sm2-modding-foundations-paks-tools-and-crash-triage.md) (scenario manifest rules, blueprint
> pin and value rules, crash triage); level collision and models are in
> [the models note](sm2-models-tpl-format-modelconverter-and-textures.md).

## Setup
- Steam build 25799387 (Patch 15.1). Scenario text in `default_other.pak` (`xscenes/<level>/<level>_scenario_server.sso`
  and `_client.sso`); level binaries in per-level scene paks (`paks/client/default/scenes/<level>.pak` and the server
  equivalent) under `scenes/<level>.scn/`.
- Saber Mod Tools with the documented toolchain layout (the package extracted into the game's `client_pc/root`, or
  a mirror of that layout elsewhere with junctions to the game paks) for AIConverter / Furnace / MapBuilder.
- `meta_desc_ssl.ps` for every node's pins and the on-screen debug node `BlueprintNodeDrawModUiLog`: see the
  foundations note.
- Saber's own Map Converter / Furnace pages (spacemarine2-modding.prismray.io) cover building NEW levels from glTF;
  this note works on existing levels.

## Route and why
Data route: scenario graphs are plain text and can be edited freely as long as every node type is declared and every
link targets a real pin. Level data (entities, classes, navmesh, static geometry) is binary, but Saber ships the C#
source of its scene readers/writers, so cd_list / class_list can be rewritten byte-exactly. A level's scenario logic is
a compiled module, so a cloned level cannot get its own scenario; modded levels branch inside the original level's
scenario.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Scenario waves and faction swaps
- Waves are `GetCustomEnemyPackComposition` blocks: `archetypeN` (`AiArchetypeRefParam`) + `amountN`. Valid archetype
  names live in `ssl/spawn_system/archetypes/archetypes_library.sso`, grouped `NPC_TYRANIDS` / `NPC_CHAOS` /
  `NPC_LOYALIST`, each with `threatClass`, `powerRating`, `combatType`: match those when swapping to keep pacing.
  Omitting `amountN` while keeping `archetypeN` is a normal retail idiom (~43 % of compositions).
- **The pool table is the must-do.** Each `*_scenario_server.sso` ends with `useDefaultArchetypesPoolsLibrary = False`
  and an `archetypes = { ... }` table of `LevelArchetype` entries (`amount = N` concurrent pool, or `takeDefault =
  True`, plus the `npc_*_server` class). A level can only spawn archetypes listed there, and each needs its class in
  the scenario manifest's `linksDescWeak`. Size `amount` for peak simultaneous demand, not one wave.
- `spawnVisTypeRef` (`CHAOS_PORTAL` / `TYRANID_SPOROCYST` / `VR_PORTAL`) is cosmetic; it does not gate archetypes.
  Portals, swarms (`BlueprintNodeStartSwarm` `spawnerTagRef`) and flocks are LEVEL actors: you can change what walks
  out of a portal, not the portal.
- `BlueprintNodeGetCharactersByArchetypeUid` finds spawned enemies BY ARCHETYPE NAME for scripted beats; retarget those
  lookups when you swap, or the array is empty and the beat silently dies. `Chs*Dummy` / `Tyr*Dummy` are invisible AI
  targets; leave them.
- Mixed factions in one level are supported (several retail levels do it), but assets stream per level: prefer
  archetypes that already appear in some campaign mission.
- Worked example (one stage of a Chaos mission -> Tyranids, 61 references): Cultist -> Termagant, Tzaangor ->
  Hormagaunt Sergeant, shieldless Tzaangor -> Hormagaunt, Rubric Marine -> Warrior (assault), flamer Rubric -> Warrior
  (whip), Occult Terminator ranged -> Zoanthrope, melee -> Ravener, lesser Sorcerer -> Zoanthrope; gaunt counts doubled
  to offset their much lower power rating; seven pool entries appended. Played fine; Tyranids walking out of warp
  portals is the accepted cosmetic cost.

### Level files
- Per level: `.cd_list` (entities: name, row-major 4x4 matrix with translation at elements 12-14, affixes, a
  descriptor text, parent index/object, flags), `.class_list` (64-byte header, u32 count, u32, u8, the names, u8, then
  each descriptor as u32 length + text; nothing after it, so it can be resized), `.dom_list`, `.lg` + `.lg_data`
  (static geometry, GeomManager-style chunks), `.cdt` (static collision, see the models note), `.nav` (navmesh; the
  same file is in the client and server scene paks), `lwi_container` (instanced props), terrain. Client and server
  have their own cd_list and class_list (spawn points and `server_driven` physics parts are server-side).
- Invisible walls come from two places: static-collision objects in the `.lg` named `scripting|constrains|...`,
  `*_playable_zone` and camera constraints (removing one: see the models note's level collision), and scripted 1x1 m
  `invisible_player_blocker` entities in the cd_list scaled by their matrix. The navmesh stops at those walls too.
- Saber ships `SaberTools/Scene/CDList.cs`, `ClassList.cs`, `DOMList.cs`, `SaberScene.cs`, `MapConverter.cs` and
  MapBuilder in `ModelConverter/ToolsSource`; a straight port round-trips retail files byte-exactly, and entities can
  be APPENDED.
- Entity descriptors are plain text (`matr`, `__type`, ColorCtrl light colours as A,R,G,B); same-length edits keep a
  file valid without any re-layout. Scene post-FX presets live in `default_presets.pak`
  (`presets/data/<scene>/*.s3dprs`).
- Some binary lists (e.g. `loading_scene.cd_list` records: marker, u32 next-field offset, u32 flag, u32 end offset, u32
  length, text) use ABSOLUTE offsets: resizing one record shifts every later one.
- Per-level class swaps: a vehicle that appears in many levels is baked into each level's class_list as its own
  classes. Swap a model by changing `nameTpl` of the right class in every level's class_list and adding the tpl to
  `linksTpl` of `<level>.scn.resource`. Cutscene copies and interplay ships are separate: `.xseq` files spawn their own
  actors in `spawnableActors` (give them `desc.properties.geom.nameTpl` overrides + a `linksTpl` in the xseq's
  resource). Interplay ships sit at the origin and their clips carry world-space root motion. Class-level
  `objectsOverrides = { <runtime object name> = { isHidden = true } }` (or `transform`) hides or moves parts.
- Do not "clone" a level to get new logic: a cloned level re-homed under a new name still runs the original level's
  compiled scenario. Branch inside the original scenario on `CompareGameModeName "Pve"` and add "Pve" to its
  `startingParameters`.
- New mission-select entries extend the `MissionUid` enum (Saber's enum extension) and the shared missions files;
  several map mods do this, so ship a merged copy of the current winner and sort first.

### The ESD spawn director
- ESD = the enemy spawn director of operations. Pressure presets are in `esd_manager.sso` `basePressureSettings`
  (NORMAL 140 in retail), waves/breathers and swarm cooldowns there too; `ai_spawn_manager` `maxAiCount` (100 by
  default, 150 in story). Influencers: progress spline, players count, difficulty.
- **Spawn points are navmesh inputs.** `ai_dynamic_spawn_point` entities (`__type = "ai_dynamic_spawn_point";`,
  flags 1, aggro / idle / miniboss variants) sit in the SERVER cd_list and are baked into the `.nav`
  (`AiDynamicSpawnPointCreator` only enables points that match targets baked into the level). A campaign level has
  none, so adding points means rebuilding its navmesh (next section).
- **The server scene manifest must link the spawn-point classes**:
  `scenes/<level>.scn/server/<level>_server.scn.resource` (server `resources.pak`) needs
  `ssl/spawn_system/dynamic_spawn/ai_dynamic_spawn_point{,_idle}.{cls,ssc}.resource` and
  `ssl/spawn_system/archetypes/ai_archetype_classes.ssl.resource`, or the server never creates the entities. We then
  added every server-scene link that ALL reference PvE levels share and the target lacks (34 links, e.g.
  `hidden_spawn_table/hidden_spawn_target.ssc`, `float_range`, `dom_players_and_bots_check`,
  `dom_dynamic_spawn_area`), computed as a set intersection at build time.
- **The director starts ON HOLD.** Every retail operation releases it with `BlueprintNodeEsdSetScenarioHoldStage`
  (`stateRef` False). Retail starts only set faction/pack settings (`EsdUpdateFactionAndPackSettings`) and never force
  a stage; forcing a stage left desired pressure at 0. Readouts: `GetEsdWavesBreathersInfo.IsOnHold`,
  `GetEsdPressure` (Desired / Current / Available, server).
- Domain-based packs: `Spawn Npc Pack` (Domain preset) into the level's `enemy_spawn_domains`. On a converted campaign
  level in PvE mode these never produced enemies. Decompiled reasons it can fail silently: the node always fires
  `OnExit`; each spawn request times out after 5 s and then reports "finished" even with zero actors (so `OnSpawned`
  means "requests finished", not "enemies exist"); a domain without a random navmesh tracker yields nothing; the NPC
  limit or an empty pool returns null.
- `ESD: Select Aggro Pack` does not scale with ESD pressure and clamps to pool availability.
- **What always worked:** direct `SpawnActorByArchetype` at a random navmesh point near a squad member
  (`GetRndNavmeshPointInRadius`), with `isIdle True` for idle groups; loop with `ForEachInt` over
  `CreateRandomizedIntArray` (output pin `Get`).

### Rebaking a level's navmesh with spawn points (Saber's offline toolchain)
- `ModEditor/tools/bin/ResourceManager/AIConverterExe.exe` builds a navmesh from the EXISTING scene binaries
  (`--cd-list --class-list --dom-list --geom-dbg --lg --lg-data --lwi-container -o -p <project>`), adds terrain, and
  bakes spawn points. Furnace calls it with an extra `--xgine-link intermediate/.xgine_link` (one line:
  `xgine-scene-path: <map>\<map>.scn`, relative to `mods_source/xscenes`); without a text SCN providing the
  `navmesh_project` object it prints "Skipping navmesh generation". Run from the standalone tools folder it silently
  does nothing: it needs Saber's documented layout (`.project`, prjenv, tools, preload, mods_source, paks).
- **Spawn generation is switched by the SERVER cd_list:** AIConverter reads navmesh settings from the
  `navmesh_project` entity's descriptor. Campaign levels have a bare `__type = "navmesh_project";`; PvE levels have
  `settings = {advanced = {spawnPointsGeneration = {isEnabled = true;};};};` in front of it. With that string the
  rebuild reported our 388 points and ~3,600 total spawn points.
- `-o` must be the scene folder under `<root>/local/scenes/<map>.scn`; copy the level's `terrain/` there (else
  "Invalid terrain version 0 instead of 1"); provide `intermediate/.lwi_container_conv_output` (and `_unresolved`)
  listing the lwi containers and the unique tpl names they use; extract the level's scene paks into `mods_source/`
  (scene-local collision lives there: "there are no collision file").
- Patch-15 tpls with a newer refs sub-chunk are rejected by the tools ("Unknown chunk id: 4"); rewriting it to the
  old form (same size) only took effect in a COPY of the default tpl paks, because a second loader opens the original
  pak entry directly.
- The tools print their real error only through OutputDebugString and then hang on an assert; a small debugger that
  logs debug strings and kills the process after an error report made them usable.
- Cost: ~45 min per rebuild (~25-35 min loading every prop's descriptors in tiny reads, then the navmesh), peak ~23 GB
  commit. Don't rebuild a whole existing level through the Map Converter (scenes can't be decompiled; hundreds of
  thousands of instances and heavy terrain).

### Turning a campaign level into an operation (what else we hit)
- A story "get up" interplay registered in `interplay_controller_default` can be played by any player via
  `EnterSmart`; teleport first, wait ~0.5 s, then EnterSmart (both in one frame fails). Strip camera-cut, game-camera
  and letterbox tracks from the xseq for gameplay use; `SequenceHolsterWeaponTrack` hides weapons (link its module).
- Use `PLAYERS_AND_BOTS` when collecting the squad, or bots miss scripted steps.
- `Delay` nodes stop on node reset; `OnStartedOrReset` fires on start, reset and reload. Chain long sequences from
  independent timers while debugging, with numbered on-screen checkpoints.
- Objective gates: `InteractWithObjectStage`; the default highlight preset's marker has no distance cull (a cloned
  preset with `isCullByDistance` fixes far markers - prepared, not tested).
- Client graph crashes at level load, beyond the foundations note's pin, shipped-node and bare-value rules: a debug
  readout using a node with zero retail client uses (`Vector3dToString`). Prefer nodes retail uses on that side.

### Hub barge and the 12-player flag
- `ssl/main/user/mod_support_consts.sso` `isTwelvePlayerPveLobbyEnabled` is read in five places (decompiled): on the
  client it makes PvE sessions ignore the match's hub data, so each player loads their OWN barge; on the server it
  allows duplicate classes in private sessions and disables class-conflict tracking. The host only publishes its barge
  address when its own flag is off, so "host on, joiners off" can't work, and the flag must be the same on client and
  server. A one-byte edit of the compiled server module to allow duplicates crashed the server at startup (sslbins
  can't be replaced). Data-only fix for a shared barge: flag False.
- The loading-screen Thunderhawk roster is client-side (session members this client knows, duplicate classes dropped
  in compiled code, bots fill to 3); seats are `interplayTracks` in `scenes/loading_scene.pak` `loading_scene.cd_list`
  plus 3 tracks per loading cinematic. The 3-member squad cap is compiled.

## Build steps
Faction swap: rewrite `archetypeN` in the stage's compositions (role/threat matched), fix
`GetCharactersByArchetypeUid` lookups, append `LevelArchetype` pool entries + `linksDescWeak` classes, adjust counts,
ship the scenario `.sso` (+ `.sso.resource`) in a ZIP_STORED pak.

Spawn points on a level without them:
1. Port Saber's CDList code; append `ai_dynamic_spawn_point` entities (per area: aggro / idle / miniboss, anchored on
   the level's own enemy domains and spawn markers) to the SERVER cd_list.
2. Replace the `navmesh_project` descriptor with the PvE one that enables spawn-point generation.
3. Rebuild the `.nav` with AIConverter in Saber's toolchain layout (inputs above), ship the `.nav` + server cd_list.
4. Link the spawn-point classes (and the PvE-shared links) in the server scene manifest.
5. In the scenario: set faction/pack settings, release the hold stage, set pressure; keep direct spawns as a fallback.

## Verification
- In game: the Chaos -> Tyranid stage swap (played through); direct `SpawnActorByArchetype` spawns; the modded
  prologue loads, plays its objectives and the get-up; the rebuilt navmesh (with 388 baked points) loads; the server-side
  pressure / hold readouts work (they showed desired pressure 0 and "ON HOLD", which led to the hold-stage finding);
  the `IntRefParam` and missing-pin crashes.
- Offline: cd_list / class_list byte-exact round trips; the rebuilt `.nav` contains all 388 point names.
- NOT yet seen in game: enemies spawned by the director on the converted level (the hold release was the last fix and
  is untested), the shared-barge fix pak, near objective markers.

## Gotchas
1. **Swapped enemies never appear.** Cause: archetypes not in the level's `LevelArchetype` pool (and `linksDescWeak`).
   Fix: append pool entries; size them for peak concurrency.
2. **A scripted beat silently stops after a swap.** Cause: `GetCharactersByArchetypeUid` still looks for the old
   archetype names. Fix: retarget those lookups.
3. **New enemies still come out of Chaos portals.** Cause: portals are level actors; `spawnVisTypeRef` is cosmetic.
   Fix: none from the scenario; accept or edit the level.
4. **Cloned level runs the original mission's logic.** Cause: the scenario is a compiled per-level module. Fix: branch
   inside the original scenario on game mode.
5. **"Spawned" fired but no enemies.** Cause: spawn requests report finished after a 5 s timeout with zero actors.
   Fix: verify with a direct spawn and on-screen counts; don't trust `OnSpawned`.
6. **Domain packs never spawn on a converted level.** Cause: no usable domain trackers / navmesh match in PvE mode.
   Fix: direct `SpawnActorByArchetype` near the squad, or rebake with ESD points.
7. **Rebuilt navmesh has no spawn points ("Skipping...").** Cause: the server cd_list's `navmesh_project` has no
   spawn-generation settings, or no xgine link/text SCN. Fix: the PvE descriptor string + Furnace's inputs.
8. **Spawn points baked but never created.** Cause: the server scene manifest lacks the spawn-point class links. Fix:
   add them (and the PvE-shared links).
9. **Director stuck: desired pressure 0, "ON HOLD".** Cause: the scenario never released the hold stage (and/or a
   forced stage). Fix: `EsdSetScenarioHoldStage` False; don't force stages.
10. **Stage readout printed every tick.** Cause: `GetEsdStage` feeds an enum into `If`, which is true for any non-OFF
    stage. Fix: compare against a specific value.
11. **Saber's AIConverter exits 0 with no output, or -1 after "Loading resources...".** Cause: wrong layout, `-o`
    outside `local/scenes`, missing terrain / lwi conversion output / scene collision. Fix: mirror Saber's layout and
    capture its debug output with a debugger.
12. **Tools reject a retail tpl ("Unknown chunk id: 4").** Cause: Patch-15 refs sub-chunk newer than the tools. Fix:
    downgrade it in a copy of the pak the tools read.
13. **Client crash at level load after adding a debug readout.** Cause: a client node with no retail use, or a link to
    a missing pin. Fix: validate pins, use retail-proven nodes.
14. **Teleport + get-up in one step: camera cuts, Marine just stands.** Cause: same-frame teleport and EnterSmart. Fix:
    wait ~0.5 s between them.
15. **With the 12-player flag every player loads their own barge.** Cause: the flag makes clients ignore the match's
    hub data. Fix: flag False (shared barge); a host-only setting cannot work.

## Assets
None. A short intro voice line for the converted level was produced separately (see the voices note for the media
bundle route).

## Open questions
- Whether the director spawns on the rebaked level now that the hold stage is released.
- Why domain-based packs fail on a converted campaign level (an unknown domain flag is skipped by native code).
- A data path to more than 3 seats in the loading Thunderhawk.

# Space Marine 2 modding foundations: paks, load order, Saber's tools, manifests and crash triage

> Two months of SM2 (Saber Swarm engine) modding through Saber's official mod support: weapon skins, new NPCs,
> custom animations, voices, mission edits. This note is the base layer every other SM2 note assumes: how mod paks
> are read, which files are text and which are compiled, the manifest rules that cause most crashes, and how to read
> a crash when the game gives you nothing. Everything below was verified in the real game unless marked otherwise.

The other SM2 notes build on this one, and each fact lives in one of them:
[models and textures](sm2-models-tpl-format-modelconverter-and-textures.md),
[weapons](sm2-weapons-skins-reloads-perks-vfx-and-sounds.md),
[new enemies and Morpheme animation](sm2-new-enemies-npc-classes-and-morpheme-animation.md),
[a new playable class](sm2-new-playable-class-on-character-mod-slot.md),
[missions and the spawn director](sm2-missions-scenarios-faction-swaps-and-esd-spawning.md) and
[voices and Wwise audio](sm2-voices-talkers-and-wwise-audio.md).

## Setup
- Steam build 25799387 (Patch 15.1). Patch 14 -> 15 moved many files, so date your findings.
- Saber's official modding docs: <https://spacemarine2-modding.prismray.io/> (installing the Mod Editor, Model
  Converter and Map Converter references, uploading, playing with mods).
- **Saber's mod rules (the docs' Legal Notice):** mods must not contain AI-generated or AI-assisted content, must
  not be sold, and may only use Warhammer 40,000 IP; uploading to Steam Workshop or saber.games means accepting the
  EULA's Mods section. Several of these notes used AI-generated meshes, textures and TTS voices, so keep builds
  that contain them private, and use hand-made art and recorded voices for anything you release.
- Saber's Mod Tools (Steam app "Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 - Mod Tools"). Prefer the standalone tool folder
  over the older copy inside the game. Docs ship in `ModEditor/documentation/` (`CLS_File_Guide.pdf`,
  `Enum_Extension_Tutorial.pdf`, `whitelisted_enums.txt`, `Map_Converter_Guide.pdf`, samples) and a modding how-to
  PDF in ModEditor.
- After EVERY game update or file verification, run `client_pc/root/tools/MetaDescPatcher.exe` and press Patch.
  The meta descs now ship with the game, so Mod Editor keeps working after patches, but link fields stay locked
  until you patch.
- **The best single reference:** `client_pc/root/tools/meta_descs/meta_desc_ssl.ps`. It lists every blueprint node
  and field: input/output pin names (`__diagram.__input/__output`), param types, `__defaultValue`, captions and
  hints. Read it before guessing a pin name.
- Saber also ships tool SOURCE: `ModelConverter/ToolsSource` (GltfConverter.cs, Tpl.cs, USF code, scene
  CDList/ClassList/DOMList/MapBuilder). Reading it answered many format questions faster than reversing binaries.

## Route and why
Data route: mod paks are zip files dropped in `client_pc/root/mods/`, and a file in a mod pak overrides the retail
file at the same path. Gameplay logic is mostly plain-text `.sso` / `.cls` / `.prop` (Saber's SSL data format);
code is compiled `.sslbin`, which you cannot replace (see Gotchas). No loader or injection exists or is needed.
EasyAntiCheat blocks RenderDoc and live-memory tools, so all inspection is offline.

Modded play stays inside Saber's mod support. Its "Playing with Mods" page says that when mods are detected the
game leaves public matchmaking, plays in private lobbies only (invite or code), shows a watermark, and keeps a
progression separate from the official one. For quick iteration the docs also allow loose files in
`client_pc/root/local/` (same relative paths; the game warns about corrupt files and loads slower, because loose
files don't stream). Paks are what you ship.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

### Pak layout
- Retail data: `client_pc/root/paks/client/default/*.pak` and `server_pc/root/paks/server/...`. The game runs a
  local SERVER even in solo play; server crashes go to a separate report folder (below).
- `default_other.pak` = plain-text SSL data (`ssl/**/*.sso`, `.cls`, `xscenes/`), shipped on BOTH client and server.
  Editing the text is enough for gameplay data; no recompile.
- `default_ssl.pak` = compiled `*_release.sslbin` / `_profile.sslbin` modules. Many are ~400-byte class stubs; the
  real data lives in the text.
- `resources.pak` (client and server) = the `.resource` manifests (YAML-ish, CRLF, 3-space indent). Every asset
  is resolved through its manifest, not by path alone.
- Textures: `default_pct_*.pak` hold mips as `pct/<name>_N.pct_mip`; models in `default_tpl_*.pak`
  (`.tpl`, `.tpl_data`, `.lods_base`, `.geom_dbg`, `.cdt`, `.tpl_markup`); animations in `default_animation.pak`.
- `texts/strings_english.str`: UTF-16LE with BOM, `KEY<tabs>"value"`. Retail values are obfuscated (`6d3s9<hex>`),
  but plaintext values also render. Some values span lines with real newlines; edit single-line keys only.

### Load order and conflicts
- **When two mod paks contain the same file, the pak that sorts FIRST alphabetically wins.** Saber's "Using Mod
  Packs" page says so: mod paks override the default paks and are sorted alphabetically, and if modA and modB change
  the same file the virtual file system takes modA's. This is the reverse of the usual "z_ loads last" convention.
  Name an override `00000_0_...` to beat a pak named `00000_t...`; `0000_x` sorts AFTER `00000` because `'0' < '_'`.
  The same page says editing the default paks directly crashes the game at start: mod paks are the only route.
- Shared files (`strings_english.str`, `mml_cfg/all_levels.mml_cfg`, `sounds/localization/english.sound_localization.resource`,
  big libraries like `melee_actor_factory.sso`) are winner-takes-all. Two mods that both ship one silently erase each
  other's entries. Build your copy as a MERGE: current retail + every installed mod's changed keys + yours, and
  rebuild whenever those mods change.
- **Write mod paks with `zipfile.ZIP_STORED` for every file** (Saber's page: a pak is a ZIP with compression set to
  Store). The engine streams `tpl_data` and texture mips by byte range straight out of the pak. A DEFLATED pak loads
  but renders black textures and invisible near LODs.

### Manifests (`.resource`) and the crash rules they cause
- `.sso.resource` has several link sections (`linksDesc`, `linksDescWeak`, `linksSsl`, `parents`, `dynamicLinks`).
  Scan all of them before deciding something is undeclared.
- **Node-type declarations in scenario manifests are all-or-nothing per type.** Measured over every retail
  scenario: some blueprint node types are declared in `linksDesc` every time they're used
  (`EsdUpdatePressureAndDurationSettings`, `EsdSetScenarioHoldStage`, `OnBlueprintStartedOrReset`,
  `EsdUpdateFactionAndPackSettings`, `SwitchByInt`, `GetDifficultyLevel`, `AddResourcesToPlayers`), others never are.
  Map a `__type` to its module by snake_casing the class name. Library nodes (`BlueprintStringLibraryAppend` etc.)
  live in `.ssolib.resource`, not `.sso.resource`.
- **Archetype pool <-> `linksDescWeak` is 1:1.** Every `LevelArchetype` entry in a scenario has a matching
  `<npc>.cls.resource` in `linksDescWeak`. Add one without the other and the class never loads.
- Symptom of breaking either rule: ACCESS_VIOLATION reading `0x8` (null class pointer) during scene load.
- `.tpl.resource`: always start from RETAIL's and only add `linksPct` / `linksTd` entries (alphabetical, CRLF).
  The exporter's own `.tpl.resource` leaves `linkTplMarkup` / `tplMarkup` empty, which crashes on a shader-cache
  miss (see the [models note](sm2-models-tpl-format-modelconverter-and-textures.md)).
- New animation clips need a `.sani.resource` and a link in `<set>.mr.resource`, or the game crashes at boot (see
  the [NPC/animation note](sm2-new-enemies-npc-classes-and-morpheme-animation.md)).
- A node type that exists in `meta_desc_ssl.ps` is not necessarily shipped. Assert that every node type you use
  has a resource in that side's `resources.pak` (example: `BlueprintNodeEsdClientGetStage` is described but not shipped).

### SSL: what you can and cannot change
- Text `.sso` / `.cls` overrides work. Keep every `__type` line when overriding a node; keep indentation exact
  (a node nested inside a field instead of beside it passes brace checks but breaks).
- **A mod pak that replaces an existing retail `.sslbin` crashes the server at startup**, even a same-length
  one-byte edit. Hand-built new sslbins are ignored. Change behaviour through data only.
- **A new data "brand" (new compiled class referenced by `__type`) crashes at boot.** Use existing types, inline
  objects, or Saber's modder slots / the official CLS route (below).
- **Official way to add classes (Oct 2026 Mod Tools, `CLS_File_Guide.pdf`):** copy a retail `.cls`, write its
  `.ssc.resource` with `noSsl: true` (no ssl/sslbin fields), `className`, `clientClassName` / `authorityClassName`
  for replicated pairs, `isServerReplicaModule` / `isClientReplicaModule`, links = own `.cls.resource` + the
  parent's `.ssc.resource`, `parentClassName`. Append net-replicated ones to
  `initial/replicas/initial_replicas_all_{server,client}.resource`. The guide states this gives unlimited custom
  NPCs, actors and outfits. (We built NPCs on Saber's older `npc_modded_1..5` slots before this existed.)
- **Custom enum values** (same update): set `extension: <file>.ext` on the enum's `.ssl.resource` (retail
  `ability_consts_library.ssl.resource` already has an empty `extension:` field); the `.ext` is YAML
  (`enumExtend: / - enumName: AbilityUid / enumValues: [...]`). Only enums in `whitelisted_enums.txt` (AbilityUid,
  FirearmUid, MeleeStrikeWeaponType, ...). Verified in game: a cloned ability on a new AbilityUid works.
- Saber also pre-registers modder slots: `melee_mod_1..5`, `ultimate_mod_1..5`, `equipment_mod_1..5`
  ability uids, `for_modders/melee_mod_desc_1..5`, `ssl/characters/modded/npc_modded_1..5_{server,client}`,
  `CHARACTER_MOD_N` classes.
- Reading compiled logic: the sslbin is a protobuf-like container (field 6 string table, type table, class defs,
  functions with a simple stack bytecode: word op = `w & 0xff`, arg = `(w >> 8) - 0x800000`). A rough
  disassembler is a day's work and was worth it: it settled equipment, lobby and HUD questions that data alone
  couldn't. Client and server global-function indices differ.

### Other game-wide levers found
- `mml_cfg/all_levels.mml_cfg` (JSON, default_other.pak) caps texture mips per quality slot by texture NAME
  (`topmip` = mips kept, counted from the smallest). **Unlisted textures lose their top mip on High** (the exe skips
  1 mip on High, 2 on Medium, 3 on Low unless a side is small). Every custom texture shows at half resolution on
  High unless you add entries. Insert yours at the top of the CURRENT retail file and ship it. Only one pak wins it.
- Quality-setting data (`ssl/main/user/quality_settings/`, `animation_quality_settings.sso`): ragdoll / gib caps,
  ragdoll freeze timers, cloth/physics quality presets. Console "SPEED" presets show Saber's own perf cuts.
- Key codes in keymaps / `InputActionHold` are DirectInput scan codes (Esc 1, Enter 28, P 25, Numpad2 80), not ASCII.
- Cosmetic challenge locks are data: `challengeLock = { challengeUid, tier, __type "ChallengeLockReason" }` blocks on
  regions in `character_customization_library.sso` and on decals.
- Lobby/session: `ssl/main/user/mod_support_consts.sso` holds mod-support switches (e.g.
  `isTwelvePlayerPveLobbyEnabled`, which also splits the hub barge: see the
  [missions note](sm2-missions-scenarios-faction-swaps-and-esd-spawning.md)).
- The retail game writes no log files. Your only runtime readouts are crash reports, `.ssldmp` script dumps and
  on-screen debug (`BlueprintNodeDrawModUiLog` = "Draw UI Mod Message", client side; its input pin is `Draw`).

### Crash triage when the game shows nothing
- Reports: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Saber\Space Marine 2\{client,server}\reports\report_<ts>_pid<N>\` (error.yaml, a
  `.ssldmp`, `CrashDump.dmp`). Script errors without a crash also land in `...\client\ssl_crash_dump\`.
- **An empty `report_*` folder is created at EVERY launch.** A crash = `CrashDump.dmp` present. The folder is
  deleted when the dialog closes, so copy it while the dialog is open.
- `error.yaml` says client vs server and the active scene. Its callstack is often empty: go to the minidump.
  Parse it with Python `struct` (stream 6 = exception, 4 = module list) to get module+offset. Reading `0x8` / `0x48` =
  a lookup returned null (usually a class or resource that never loaded).
- Since Patch 15.1 the `.ssldmp` is JSON `{callstack, objects}`. The `objects` heap is gold: count `$type`s to see
  which libraries were built, and inspect objects (e.g. which anim lookups resolved) right before the crash.
- Since 15.1, server code lives in `...Retail.dll` (thread DLL_SERVER_MAIN), not the exe.
- Compare module+offset only within one build.
- Saber's "Install Extra Tools" page also describes an advanced crash reporter: copy the toolset's `CrashReporter`
  files into `client_pc/root/bin/pc` for more detail on each crash. This note doesn't cover it.

## Build steps
1. Extract the retail files you change from the CURRENT paks (an extraction from an older patch silently differs;
   we lost a day to a stale animation clip).
2. Edit text files; keep CRLF and indentation; add `.resource` links for anything new.
3. Write a ZIP_STORED pak named so it sorts before anything it must beat; put it in `client_pc/root/mods/`.
4. Never swap paks while the game runs: it caused an out-of-memory server crash mid-load. Check for the process
   `Warhammer 40000 Space Marine 2 - Retail` first (note: `tasklist` truncates names to 25 chars).
5. After a game patch: 3-way merge your text edits (old retail -> new retail onto yours). Line-based merges misplace
   SSL blocks; a tree merge keyed by unique fields (`firearmUid`, `type`, `packUid`) leaves only real decisions.
   Treat numeric lists (splines) as atomic values. Scan for types the patch removed.

## Verification
- Oracle = the real game: the testing arena `test_scene_mod`, taken from a community testing-menu mod, with buttons
  wired to `SpawnActorByArchetype`, plus screenshots and crash dumps. The level itself is Saber's sample: the Map
  Converter docs build it with `tools/MapBuilder.exe`. Saber's autostart flag
  `--startup --set /Config/WhiteListedVariables/enableModdersAutostartFlow true` jumps straight into the mod test scene.
- Every rule above came from a crash or a visible failure that went away when the rule was applied.
- Not verified: whether `mml_cfg` defaults differ on consoles.

## Gotchas
1. **Two mods override the same file and one "stops working".** Cause: first-alphabetical pak wins the whole file.
   Fix: merge and ship a superset in the first-sorting pak.
2. **Black textures, invisible LOD0/LOD1, far LODs fine.** Cause: pak written with DEFLATE. Fix: ZIP_STORED.
   Cost us ~6 test rounds chasing geometry first.
3. **Server crashes at startup after shipping a "harmless" patched sslbin.** Cause: retail sslbins can't be
   replaced. Fix: data-only changes.
4. **Boot crash reading 0x48, stack mentions the new type** (e.g. `AnimTableActor` for a new anim-table type).
   Cause: a new compiled brand / hand-built sslbin. Fix: inline objects, existing types, modder slots or the `noSsl`
   CLS route.
5. **Scene-load crash reading 0x8.** Cause: undeclared always-declared node type, or a `LevelArchetype` without its
   `linksDescWeak` class. Fix: follow the two manifest rules.
6. **Client crash at scenario load with a garbage type index.** Cause: a blueprint link to a pin that doesn't exist
   (e.g. `Input` instead of `Draw`). Fix: validate every link against `meta_desc_ssl.ps` (inputs AND outputs, following
   `__type` inheritance).
7. **Server crash on a scenario int field.** Cause: `IntRefParam` written as a quoted string `"2"`. Fix: write
   Int/Float/Bool values bare.
8. **Custom textures look soft on High but fine on Ultra.** Cause: not listed in `all_levels.mml_cfg`. Fix: add entries.
9. **"Mods Detected" even for a tiny performance tweak.** Any mod pak does it, and with it come private lobbies only
   and the separate progression; there is no "vanilla-safe" pak.
10. **Saber's tools crash and fill the disk.** Running them with a cwd on a small drive, one tool wrote a 270 MB
    dump per model into `<cwd>\sandbox\crash_dumps` (12 GB in one run). Run them from a roomy drive and watch that folder.
11. **ModelConverter exits with code 82 and a "Press any key" exception.** Harmless; it happens after the work is done
    when stdin isn't a console. Don't treat exit codes as failure signals for these tools.
12. **A patch silently changes text you merged.** Strings, cloth colours, presets and class names moved in Patch 15
    (`PVP_*` presets -> `PVE_PVP_*`, new `PVE_MEDIC`). Fix: the 3-way merge in Build steps; for armour presets see
    the models note (gotcha "not available for the selected Class").

## Assets
None in this note.

## Open questions
- Whether `.ssldmp`-style heap dumps can be triggered on demand (they'd make an oracle without crashing).
- Exact rules behind `mml_cfg` size budgets for the `*Base` quality slots.
