# Worms W.M.D: Script-based weapon modding and lockstep multiplayer synchronization

> Worms W.M.D's weapon stats (W1 Rocket damage, blast radius, crater size, knockback, fire clusters) are
> plain-text scripts inside `CommonData/scripts.rpg`, an AES-256-encrypted ZIP that the game mounts over
> `scripts:/`. This note records the archive's cipher, the weapon properties, a first set of edits, and why
> lockstep multiplayer desyncs when two players' scripts differ. **Not yet verified in game:** no run with a
> repacked `scripts.rpg` is recorded, so the edits are untested (see Verification).

## Setup
- **Game:** Worms W.M.D (Steam app 327030, build 24946469). It also ships for Windows and macOS. These facts come from
  the Linux build.
- **OS:** Linux (native x64 binary `Worms W.M.Dx64`).
- **Anti-cheat:** none found (no EAC, BattlEye or VAC). The game has online quick and ranked matches and Steam
  leaderboards. Use modded scripts only in local games and in private matches with friends who agreed and run the
  same files (gotchas 2-3).
- **Paths:**
  - Game root: `~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/WormsWMD`
  - Script archive: `CommonData/scripts.rpg`
  - Saves: `~/.local/share/Steam/userdata/<SteamID>/327030`
- **Loose scripts:** this Linux install also had loose `CommonData/Scripts/Equip/*.txt` files. A recon of the Windows
  install ([Elliot95/worms-wmd-weapon-mods](https://github.com/Elliot95/worms-wmd-weapon-mods),
  `docs/game-data-layout.md`) found only `scripts.rpg` and `Scripts/SceneScript.xss` in `CommonData`. Check whether
  yours are shipped files or the output of an earlier extraction (see Open questions). Either way, the game doesn't
  read them (gotcha 1).

## Route and why
- **Route:** data. Edit the scripts inside the encrypted archive `CommonData/scripts.rpg`.
- **Why:** the retail executable mounts `scripts.rpg` over `scripts:/` and `bootScripts:/` in
  `GameApp::OpenScriptsZip()`, so editing loose `.txt` files has no effect in game. To change weapon stats, decrypt
  `scripts.rpg`, patch it and re-encrypt it.
- **Not the bundles:** `DataPC/Bundles/In-Game.bdl` holds weapon art and animation (Team17 XOM containers), not stats,
  per the Windows recon above.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)
1. **Script archive and encryption:**
   - `CommonData/scripts.rpg` is an encrypted ZIP holding all 436 game script files.
   - In the binary, `GameApp::OpenScriptsZip()` calls `XCryptSymKeyFile::Open()` and `XCryptSymKey::Decrypt()`.
   - **Cipher:** AES-256 with a counter-mode keystream.
   - **Key:** a 32-byte ASCII constant in the executable (it begins `WormsWMD`), which `OpenScriptsZip()` passes to
     `XCryptSymKeyFile::Open()`. Read it from your own binary. This note doesn't reproduce it.
   - **Counter:** each 16-byte counter block is `struct.pack("<QQ", offset, 0)`, a little-endian byte offset. The
     starting offset passed to `Decrypt` is the archive's total size, so block *i* uses `file_size + 16*i`. A stock
     CTR implementation (a 128-bit big-endian counter that steps by 1) won't produce this keystream. Encrypt each
     counter block with AES-ECB and XOR it with the data yourself.
   - Decrypting gives a standard ZIP (`PK\x03\x04`). The binary opens weapons as `scripts:/Scripts/Equip/%s.txt`.
   - **Re-encrypting:** the starting counter is the file's length, so if the repacked archive's size changes, use the
     new length. This follows from the reader's side and hasn't been tested in game.
2. **Key properties in Equip configs:**
   - `ShockDamageMin` / `ShockDamageMax`: direct explosion damage range.
   - `ShockRangeMax`: blast wave radius.
   - `LandGougeRadius`: size of the terrain crater carved out on impact.
   - `PushForceMax`: impulse applied to push worms.
   - `ChainedPayloadID` / `ChainedPayloads`: sub-munitions spawned (e.g. `kPayload_W1RocketFire`).
   - `FlameLifetimeSecs_Min/Max` and `FlameDmgDelaySecs_Min/Max`: fire particle lifetime and damage tick interval.
   - `FlameBurnRadius1/2`: scorch crater size carved into the landscape by burning flame clusters.
3. **Multiplayer lockstep architecture:**
   - The game uses deterministic lockstep, peer to peer. Clients share inputs and a seed, and each engine runs the same
     physics and destruction.
   - The engine checks frame-by-frame consistency with internal checksums (`WS_DestructionManager::GetCheckSum`,
     `WS_CollisionManager::__DebugColManCheckSum`, `CalcLogicalCrc`).
   - If one player has modified weapon stats and the other has vanilla files, destruction bitmaps and worm health
     diverge once the weapon detonates. `NetGame::UpdateDesyncChecker` then raises `kResult_SocketDesync` and the match
     ends. This is read from the binary's symbols; Verification records no multiplayer test.

## Build steps
No in-game run of these steps is recorded yet (see Verification).
1. Back up first: `um backup create` on the save folder, and copy `CommonData/scripts.rpg` to `scripts.rpg.vanilla`.
2. Decrypt `scripts.rpg` as described above and unzip it.
3. Edit `Scripts/Equip/W1Rocket.txt`:
   - `ShockDamageMax = 75;` (vanilla: 20)
   - `LandGougeRadius = 110;` (vanilla: 50)
   - `ShockRangeMax = 240;` (vanilla: 150)
   - `PushForceMax = 38;` (vanilla: 20)
   - `ChainedPayloads = 48;` (vanilla: 32)
4. Edit `Scripts/Equip/W1RocketFire.txt`:
   - `ShockDamageMin = 2; ShockDamageMax = 3;` (vanilla: 1)
   - `FlameLifetimeSecs_Min = 4.5; FlameLifetimeSecs_Max = 5.5;` (vanilla: 3)
   - `FlameDmgDelaySecs_Min = 0.35; FlameDmgDelaySecs_Max = 0.35;` (vanilla: 0.5)
   - `FlameBurnRadius1 = 6; FlameBurnRadius2 = 4;` (vanilla: 0)
5. Re-zip, re-encrypt with the new file length as the starting counter, and replace `CommonData/scripts.rpg`.
6. Test in a local (offline) match: fire the W1 Rocket and compare the crater and damage with vanilla.
7. Before any online quick or ranked match, restore `scripts.rpg.vanilla` (Steam's "Verify integrity of game files"
   restores it too).

## Verification
- **Done:**
  - checked that the edited files match the format of the game's own scripts;
  - confirmed the path the binary resolves (`scripts:/Scripts/Equip/%s.txt`);
  - diffed the edits against vanilla, so no other property changed;
  - tested the ZIP packaging.
- **Not verified:**
  - that the game loads a repacked, re-encrypted `scripts.rpg` (whether it checks a hash or signature is unknown);
  - any of the new values in a match;
  - multiplayer: the desync behaviour (gotcha 2) is read from the binary's checksum and desync-checker symbols.

## Gotchas
1. **Loose text file edits have no effect in game.**
   - **Symptom:** editing files in `CommonData/Scripts/Equip/` doesn't change damage, blast radius or weapon
     behaviour.
   - **Cause:** the retail binary mounts the encrypted ZIP `CommonData/scripts.rpg` over `scripts:/` and
     `bootScripts:/` in `GameApp::OpenScriptsZip()`. Loose files there aren't read.
   - **Fix:** decrypt `CommonData/scripts.rpg` (AES-256 keystream, key and counter above), put the modded files into
     the ZIP, and re-encrypt it to `scripts.rpg`.
2. **Multiplayer desync when a modded weapon hits.**
   - **Symptom (implied by the desync checker; no multiplayer run is recorded):** a match ends with a sync error
     when a modded W1 Rocket lands.
   - **Cause:** one client runs modified damage or gouge radius while the other runs vanilla files, so
     `WS_DestructionManager::GetCheckSum` no longer matches.
   - **Fix:** in a private match, every player installs the byte-identical `scripts.rpg`. Or use Steam Remote Play
     Together, where only the host runs the game and the simulation and the friends stream it.
3. **Never take modded scripts into quick or ranked matches.**
   - **Cause:** strangers in matchmaking haven't agreed to modded weapons, and a mismatch desyncs the match anyway
     (gotcha 2).
   - **Fix:** restore `scripts.rpg.vanilla` (or verify the game files) before going online. Use the mod only in local
     games and private matches with friends who run the same files.

## Open questions
- Does the game load a repacked `scripts.rpg` at all, and do the new values show up in a match?
- Does the Linux depot really ship `CommonData/Scripts/Equip/*.txt`, or did those come from an earlier extraction?
- Can weapon crafting recipes be changed from custom schemes without editing `Scripts/Equip/*.txt`?

# Changing a vanilla food's hunger with a replace-mode .zedmod

> ZED ZONE ships a first-party, data-driven mod system: `.zedmod` files are ZIPs holding a `mod.json`, and
> `publishMode: 1` replaces a vanilla item's definition. A locally-built mod was loaded from the game
> install's `Mods\` folder and the game's own MOD manager reported it as `Food / 替换211 / 激活`. No DLL
> injection, no IL2CPP reverse engineering and no BepInEx were needed — the whole mod is 2.3 KB of JSON and
> one self-drawn PNG. Registration and the replacement target are confirmed in game; the player-visible
> numeric effect was **not** read back (see Verification).

## Setup

- Game: **ZED ZONE**, Steam appid **1211600**, version shown on the loading screen as
  `ZED ZONE OS vBETA 0.9.9.8.18`.
- Engine: **Unity 2023.1.18f1, IL2CPP, x64** — `GameAssembly.dll` (66 MB) plus
  `ZEDZONE_Data/il2cpp_data/Metadata/global-metadata.dat`; there is no `Managed/` folder.
- Platform: Windows. No anti-cheat; single-player test.
- Tooling: `um` 0.2.0, Python 3.14 with `Pillow` (sprite), and `UnityPy` (asset probing, via
  `uv run --with UnityPy`) — UnityPy found nothing useful for this game, see *How the game works*.
- Nothing was installed into the game folder except the game's own `Mods\` directory.
- `um scan "ZED ZONE"` suggests **BepInEx 6 (IL2CPP)** as route 1. **That is the wrong route for this
  game** — ignore it and use the built-in system.

## Route and why

`route: data`. The idea (change a number on an existing item) fits the game's own data format exactly.

Considered and rejected:

- **BepInEx 6 (IL2CPP) / MelonLoader** — what `um scan` recommends. Works, but it means shipping a managed
  plugin, running `ClassInjector`, and fighting IL2CPP stripping, to change one float. The game's own
  loader does it with a JSON field.
- **Native hooks** — no need; there is no loader gap to fill.
- **Asset editing (UABEA/AssetRipper)** — item values weren't found in any asset UnityPy could read (see
  below), and the game's own loader already replaces an item.

## How the game works (what we had to learn)

**The loader is first-party.** `Player.log` names the game's own classes:
`ModLoader:LoadAll()` → `EnsureHandlersRegistered()` → `LoadLocalMods()` → `TryLoadZedmod(String, IModHandler)`,
and the per-type handlers `ModHandler_<Type>` register into an item manager. There is no community loader
and none is needed.

**Mod types.** Handlers registered at startup, from the log:
`Ammo`, `Arrow`, `Container`, `FaceMask`, `Food`, `GunPart`, `Magazine`, `MeleeWeapon`, `RangedWeapon`.
The Steam Workshop additionally carries pack kinds `locale` (translation, a `<lang>.json` key/value file)
and `audio` — the most-subscribed Workshop items for this game were `locale` packs.

**File format.** A `.zedmod` is an ordinary **ZIP** with three entries: `mod.json`, `preview.jpg`,
`sprite.png`. A Workshop *pack* is a folder with `modpack.json` (pack name, author, and a `mods[]` list of
`{modGuid, modType, itemName, relativePath}`) plus one sub-folder per mod type holding `<guid>.zedmod`.

**`publishMode` is the whole trick.**

| `publishMode` | `targetNativeItemId` | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `0` | adds a new item |
| `1` | the vanilla item's id | replaces that vanilla item's definition |

For replacements the Workshop samples also set `runtimeId` to the *same* number as
`targetNativeItemId`.

**`mod.json` shape.** Common identity fields are `modType`, `modGuid` (a UUID), `runtimeId`,
`publishMode`, `targetNativeItemId`, `spritePath`, `ppu`, `spriteRegions[]`
(`{slotName, region{x,y,w,h}}`), `itemName` / `itemName_EN`, `itemDescription` / `itemDescription_EN`,
`itemRarity`, `hiddenItem`, `itemInventorySizeX/Y`, and spawn weights
(`generateItemInRoom`, `generateItemInField`, `generateItemInCoastFloat`). Each type then adds its own:

- `Food`: `hp hunger thirst fatigue sanity energy bodyTemperture perishTime addiction badStomach soundClip
  recoverBuffRealTime buffConfigs[] returnItemData{...}`, plus a fishing group (`isFish fishQuality
  fishSize minimumCastingRange fishRarity fishBaitTypes[]`).
- `GunPart`: `gunPartType worldOffset_x/y ammoIds[] damageFloat fireIntervalFloat speedFloat accuracyFloat
  recoilIntensityFloat noiseFloat sightRangeFloat sightAngleFloat laserEffect laserColor_r/g/b/a
  firingDurability airPressure* thermalVision sniperScope*`.
- `Ammo` / `Arrow`: `weight itemPrice stackNumber craftRecipeItems[{itemId,itemNumber}] craftPlatform
  craftAudioType craftOutputNumber repairRecipeItems[]`; `Ammo` adds `ammoNumber ammoBaseDamage`, `Arrow`
  adds `damageFloat speedFloat`.

**Where local mods go.** `<install>\Mods\<ModType>\<guid>.zedmod`. The per-type sub-folder is mandatory —
see Gotcha 1.

**Vanilla item ids are readable, item values are not.** The shipped localization CSVs
(`ZEDZONE_Data\StreamingAssets\Localization\Localization_en_to_<lang>.csv`, rows `id,english,translation`)
encode the item id: `100<4-digit id>` is the item **name**, `110<4-digit id>` is its **description**. So
`1000232,Canned Stew` is item **232**, `1000211,Canned Fruit` is item **211**. Ammo occupies 100–121 and
arrows 150–152.

Vanilla *values* (how much hunger item 211 restores) could not be read from anything on disk:
the 22 `TextAsset`s in `resources.assets` are dialogue, quests and rig data only; the player build ships
without type trees, and for an IL2CPP game UnityPy has no managed DLLs to rebuild them from, so reading a
`MonoBehaviour` fails (it raises a short-read byte-count error); `env.container` is empty; and the saves
under `GameData\*.game` are binary. Next steps, untried: generate type trees from Il2CppDumper's or Cpp2IL's
dummy assemblies (or open the game in AssetRipper, which reads IL2CPP builds through Cpp2IL) to read
`MonoBehaviour`/`ScriptableObject` data; if the values turn out to be hard-coded, read them from Cpp2IL's
output for `GameAssembly.dll`.

**Other useful facts.** The mod manager's own config is
`%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\LevenLiu\ZEDZONE\mod_manager_config.json`, `{"disabledGuids": []}`.
The game keeps a mod *workspace* in that same folder, under `Mods\Workspace\<guid>\` — an unpacked copy of
each loaded mod, which is a handy confirmation that a mod was processed. The game has its own safety nets:
missing mod items are shown as grey blocks, and obviously wrong mod values trigger an "abnormal MOD item
values" warning. Co-op reportedly syncs mods from the host automatically; that wasn't tested here, and the
Steam page lists the game as single-player.

## Build steps

```text
# 1. Back up saves first (the save folder holds everything: worlds, characters, mod workspace)
um backup create "%USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\LevenLiu\ZEDZONE" --name zedzone-saves

# 2. Find the vanilla item id you want to replace, from the localization CSV
#    rows look like:  1000232,Canned Stew,Fleischeintopf in Dose
#    -> item id 232

# 3. Zip a mod.json + a 32x32 sprite.png (+ optional preview.jpg) into <uuid>.zedmod
#    mod.json: modType "Food", publishMode 1, targetNativeItemId <id>, runtimeId <id>, hunger 200
#    (the tested mod used item 211, Canned Fruit)

# 4. Install it — the per-type folder is required
#    copy <uuid>.zedmod to  "<install>\Mods\Food\<uuid>.zedmod"

# 5. Launch, then verify in two places
#    %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\LevenLiu\ZEDZONE\Player.log
#    in game: pause menu -> MOD管理器 (MOD manager)
```

## Verification

Two oracles were used.

**The game log** (`AppData\LocalLow\LevenLiu\ZEDZONE\Player.log`) is the primary one:

```
[ModLoader] 已加载：Canned Fruit  (type=Food, runtimeId=211, source=.zedmod)
[ModLoader] 本地加载完成，1 个 Mod 加载成功。
[ModLoader] Workshop 订阅加载完成，117 个 Mod 加载成功。
```

The lines read "loaded: Canned Fruit", "local loading done, 1 mod loaded" and "Workshop subscriptions loaded,
117 mods loaded". No `异常` (abnormal) / `配置问题` (config problem) / `无法加载` (can't load) warnings. The game
also unpacked the mod into `Mods\Workspace\<guid>\`, confirming it was processed rather than merely scanned.

**The game's own MOD manager** (pause menu → `MOD管理器`) is the visual one. Its columns are name, type,
mode (`模式`) and state. The mode column prints the publish mode directly (`新物品` new item, `替换211`
replaces 211; `激活` is active), and local mods are distinguishable because they carry **no** `(创意工坊)`
(Workshop) suffix:

```
名称             类型    模式      状态
Alyonka巧克力棒 (创意工坊)   Food   新物品    激活
Canned Fruit                Food   替换211   激活     <-- the local mod
DevilDog蛋黄酱 (创意工坊)    Food   新物品    激活
```

**Not verified:** that a player actually sees hunger **200** on the item. The game accepted and activated
the replacement, and the replacement target 211 is confirmed by the game's own UI, but the numeric effect
was not read back in game, and the vanilla value it replaced is unknown (see above). The item's sprite was
deliberately replaced with a self-drawn icon, so an icon change in game is a reliable tell that the
replacement — and therefore the value — is live.

## Gotchas

1. **A `.zedmod` flat in `Mods\` is silently ignored.** Symptom: the game logs
   `本地加载完成，N 个 Mod 加载成功` and your mod is not in that N, with no error anywhere. **Cause:** the
   loader scans per-`ModType` sub-folders, not the `Mods\` root. **Fix:** `Mods\<ModType>\<guid>.zedmod`
   (the folder name must match `modType`). Diagnosed by installing two probes with different target items
   in one launch — flat vs. sub-folder — and seeing which one the log named.
2. **`um win shot` times out on a Unity game that is not focused.** Symptom:
   `subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... gfxcapture=window_exe=...` and no PNG. **Cause:** the game stops
   redrawing while unfocused (most likely Unity's Run In Background is off), and gfxcapture only delivers a
   frame when the window redraws — this is *not* a crash.
   **Fix:** `um win drive --proc ZEDZONE "focus"` first, then capture.
3. **The driver's client rect disagrees with the screenshot's size.** Symptom: `um win drive ... "rect"`
   reports `1536x864` while `um win shot` writes `1920x1080`. **Cause:** display scaling of 125%; the
   driver addresses logical pixels, capture is physical. **Fix:** divide screenshot coordinates by 1.25
   before clicking (or scale small-image coordinates by `1536/width_of_small_image`).
4. **`wheel 120` scrolls the wrong way.** **Cause:** in `um win drive`, a *positive* wheel delta is one
   notch **up**. **Fix:** `wheel -120` to scroll down. Symptom of getting it wrong: two screenshots with
   identical hashes.
5. **`um scan` recommends a loader this game does not need.** Symptom: route 1 is
   `BepInEx 6 (IL2CPP) or MelonLoader`. **Cause:** it fingerprints the engine, not first-party mod support.
   **Fix:** before installing any loader, grep the game folder for a `Mods` directory and the log for
   `[ModLoader]` / handler registration. ZED ZONE has both.
6. **The MOD manager list is not sorted the way you expect.** It sorts by `ModType` first and then by name
   as **Unicode code points**, so any Latin-named mod sorts before every CJK-named one (and `TP-200` after
   `MRE`). Symptom: a long hunt for your own row. **Fix:** compute where your name sorts, and remember
   local mods have no `(创意工坊)` suffix.
7. **Clicking a row in the MOD manager does nothing.** No detail panel opens; the list just redraws. Don't
   rely on it to inspect a mod's values.
8. **Replace-mode mods in the wild carry a *complete* item definition, not a patch.**
   Every `publishMode: 1` mod inspected (GunPart, Ammo, Arrow) lists every field of its type. The mod here
   follows that: an unknown or stripped field would be applied as its default. Whether a *minimal*
   `mod.json` (only the changed field) is accepted is **untested** — if you try it, the log will say.

## Assets

The item sprite is drawn in code with Pillow — a 32x32 PNG matching the `spriteRegions` seen in Workshop
Food mods (`region 0,0,32,32` at `ppu: 96`). **No game art was copied, extracted or shipped**; replacing
the icon is also what makes the mod visible at a glance in game. `preview.jpg` is the same sprite scaled up
on a flat background. fal was not used (the account had no credit balance), so nothing here depends on it.

## Cost and time

One session. Two game launches to resolve unknowns (one to settle the `Mods\` layout, one to verify the
final artifact). The delivered mod is 2.3 KB. No paid API calls.

## Open questions

- Is a minimal `mod.json` enough for `publishMode: 1`, or is a full definition required? (Untested.)
- The custom 3D model format and the limit behind the `Model too large: {0:F2}m x {1:F2}m (single axis
  limit {2}m)` string, which implies items can carry models.
- The exact `locale` and `audio` pack formats.
- How `runtimeId` is allocated for *new* items — observed 6-digit ids (e.g. `633939`, `704059`) against
  vanilla's small ids (2xx, 1xxx).
- The vanilla item value table (type trees from Il2CppDumper/Cpp2IL dummy assemblies, AssetRipper, or
  Cpp2IL output for `GameAssembly.dll`; see How the game works). That would turn
  "hunger → 200" into a real before/after.

# A force-quit PC game relaunch wedges as an unkillable zombie (Steam/Ubisoft)

> A practical hazard for agents that launch a game many times in one session: after a forced kill
> or a quick relaunch, the new process can freeze during early init as a windowless, **unkillable**
> one-thread zombie — and only a reboot clears it. This note is about recognising it fast and
> structuring test sessions so a wedge costs you as little as possible.

## When to use it
Any time you are launching a native Windows game repeatedly to test a mod, especially a
Steam + Ubisoft Connect title. Applies to agents on Windows and (via the same OS) WSL. If you plan
more than a handful of launches, read this first so you don't lose time rediscovering it.

## How
- **Symptom.** The game process starts but never gets a window; the mod's own log freezes partway
  through init (here: during address/pattern resolution, *before any hook installed* — which is the
  tell that it is not your mod). Task Manager shows **one thread** and no window.
- **Confirm it's a zombie.** Try to kill it by exact PID. `Stop-Process -Id <pid>`, `taskkill /F /PID <pid>`,
  and `um win kill <pid>` all fail with a variant of "There is no running instance of the task." A
  child launcher process *may* die, but the game PID persists.
- **Recover.** A reboot clears it: ask the human to reboot. There is no in-session fix once it is wedged.
- **Prevent (the useful part).**
  - **Quit the game cleanly to the desktop** (in-game Quit / Exit), never Alt+F4 or a task kill.
  - **Wait for the process to disappear completely**, and for the launcher (Steam / Ubisoft Connect)
    to settle, before launching again. A quick quit→relaunch is the usual trigger.
  - **Assume one launch per boot.** Batch your tests: make a single launch answer as many questions
    as possible, and log the discovery data *before* any risky action so a crash still leaves you
    with the reading.
  - **Ask the human before removing D3D overlay hooks** (ReShade `dxgi.dll`, Bandicam, Fraps): they can wedge the game
    at `D3D11CreateDeviceAndSwapChain` independently.
  - **Clear stale crash reporters** (BugSplat and friends) by PID — a stuck reporter makes Steam
    refuse to relaunch.
- **Make the test itself resilient.** Isolate risky calls in their own hook so a fault disables only
  that hook, not the whole plugin; and log the read-only discovery before attempting the risky call.

## Gotchas
1. **"It crashed."** It usually didn't — it wedged. **Cause:** early-init block (launcher handshake
   or D3D device creation). **Fix:** check for the one-thread windowless process; if present and
   unkillable, ask the human to reboot. Don't chase it in the mod code.
2. **`taskkill /F /PID <pid>` kills the launcher child, not the game.** **Cause:** the zombie has no killable thread.
   **Fix:** don't keep hammering it; ask the human to reboot.
3. **The mod's log stops mid-init.** **Cause:** the plugin init runs on a game thread; if the game is
   blocked before the window exists, the plugin can't finish. **Fix:** recognise the freeze *point*
   (before any hook installs) as the signature of an environment wedge, not a mod bug.
4. **The first launch after boot works; the next one doesn't.** **Cause:** repeated fast relaunches.
   **Fix:** space launches out; one per boot; quit cleanly.
5. **The zombie "holds" the mod DLL.** **Cause:** a wedged process keeps the file mapped. **Fix:**
   you cannot overwrite the deployed DLL until it is gone (reboot).

## Seen in
- games/assassin-s-creed-rogue/anvilnext-internals-for-ac-rogue-co-op-player-transform-the-.md

# A scenario harness in a Minecraft Fabric dev client: real clicks, natural worlds, two clients

> GameTests run on a headless server and call mod code directly, so they miss what only a real client and real
> packets show: the click path, screens, rendering, natural world generation, a second player. A small client
> entrypoint that plays a scripted scenario, logs checks and saves screenshots closes that gap with one command.

## When to use it
- After GameTests pass, to check the same feature the way a player reaches it (a right click goes through
  `ClientPlayerInteractionManager`, a packet and the server's use path; a GameTest calling the item method does not).
- For anything visual (models, item display transforms, screens, particles) and for naturally generated content.
- For a cheap multiplayer smoke test with two real clients.
- On Minecraft 1.21.4 and later, look at Fabric API's own client game tests first: `fabric-client-gametest-api-v1`
  (entrypoint `fabric-client-gametest`) has simulated input, singleplayer and dedicated-server contexts and
  screenshot comparison. Fabric API 0.92 for 1.20.1 has only the server-side `fabric-gametest-api-v1`, hence this
  hand-made harness.
Verified on Minecraft 1.20.1, Fabric Loader 0.16.14, Loom 1.7.4, Windows 10 and Linux (Xvfb).

## How
- **Where it lives:** a `ClientModInitializer` in the test source set (never shipped), active only with a system
  property (`-D<mod>.screenshots=true`) set by its own Loom run config with `--quickPlaySingleplayer <world>`
  (or `--quickPlayMultiplayer host:port`). An environment variable picks the scenario.
- **The script:** a queue of steps `(waitTicks, action, screenshotName)` run from `END_CLIENT_TICK`, starting about
  100 ticks after joining. Server-side setup runs on the integrated server with
  `client.getServer().execute(...)`. Screenshots wait until `worldRenderer.isTerrainRenderComplete()` (bounded).
- **Cheats for setup, not for the thing under test:** give items, place blocks, set time, grant research by
  command; then switch to survival and click for real:
  `interactionManager.interactBlock(player, MAIN_HAND, new BlockHitResult(center, UP, pos, false))` or
  `interactItem(player, MAIN_HAND)`. Check results server-side and `client.currentScreen` client-side; log
  `[harness] <scenario> <check>: OK|FAIL` and a final count.
- **Prove the requirement, not only the effect:** do the action once without its requirement (expect refusal),
  grant it, do it again (expect success). Same tool, same spot, so the refusal cannot come from anything else.
- **Natural generation:** create the world once with the dedicated server (`level-type=minecraft:normal`, fixed
  seed, structures on), then copy it fresh for every run. Find jigsaw pieces by walking the structure set's
  `RandomSpreadStructurePlacement.getStartChunk(seed, rx * spacing, rz * spacing)` cells and loading chunks only to
  `ChunkStatus.STRUCTURE_STARTS`; find biomes with `ServerWorld.locateBiome`; find features by generating chunks
  outwards and scanning sections with `ChunkSection.hasAny(predicate)`. Log the seed, the generator class and every
  position used, and fail loudly when nothing is found instead of placing it by hand.
  - Scan `getStructureStarts()` children for `PoolStructurePiece`s and match a piece by its template id
    (`getPoolElement().toString()` contains it). Element identity maps break for starts read back from a saved
    chunk, where the elements are new instances. 81 placement cells took about 12 s.
- **Two clients:** a second Loom client run config with its own `runDir` and `--username`, started some seconds
  after the first, against a dedicated server run config whose stdin gets `op @a` every few seconds.
- **The wrapper script** fails when no new screenshot was written, so a crashed or never-compiled client is not
  mistaken for success. (A failed harness compile once still exited 0 and left the previous PNG on disk.) Compare
  each PNG's hash with the last run's before looking at it.
- **Load probe:** the same queue can spawn N entities / block entities and log `MinecraftServer.getTickTime()`
  before and after.

## Gotchas
1. **A check ran before the thing it checks.**
   - **Cause:** in a `(wait, action, shot)` step the action runs first and the wait comes after it. A log in the
     same step as a teleport saw `void_air` (the chunk was not there yet).
   - **Fix:** put the wait in its own step before the check, or let a check step re-queue itself until a flag
     set by the server action is true.
2. **The camera fell into the ocean.**
   - **Cause:** a creative player teleported into chunks the client has not loaded counts as on the ground, and the
     client switches flight off.
   - **Fix:** spectator mode for camera-only scenarios, set before long teleports (flight is locked, and no hand
     shows in the shot).
3. **Commands silently did nothing in the multiplayer run.**
   - **Cause:** the clients sent commands before the server's op loop had opped them ("Unknown or incomplete
     command" in the client log).
   - **Fix:** op from the first seconds and give the scenario a 10 s idle step before its first command.
4. **Gradle `--args` replaced the run config's program args** (the quick-play address was lost).
   - **Fix:** put per-client arguments such as `--username` in separate run configs.
5. **No `xvfb-run` on Windows.**
   - **Fix:** use it only when present; elsewhere the client opens a normal window.
6. **A hostile test mob disappeared mid-scenario or merged with a stranger.**
   - **Cause:** `checkDespawn`, or entities left over from other scenarios or tests nearby.
   - **Fix:** `setPersistent()` and clear same-type entities in range at the start.

7. **A short-lived effect is missing from its screenshot.**
   - **Cause:** the capture waits for the terrain to finish building; a beam or bolt has expired by then.
   - **Fix:** let the terrain build first (about 100 ticks after a teleport), then trigger the effect right before
     the capture.
8. **A scripted "throw the item in" step failed.**
   - **Cause:** the selected-slot change had not reached the server before the drop key was pressed, and a throw
     from the ground landed short.
   - **Fix:** change slots at least a tick before dropping, and throw from a block beside the target.
9. **A real-click scenario failed in one run of two.**
   - **Cause:** the original's own random failure path (infusion instability scattering the items).
   - **Fix:** build the original's stabilising setup in the scenario so the chance is 0, rather than changing the
     code under test.
10. **The dev runtime hid release-only problems.**
    - **Fix:** a production-style launch. Build the classpath as a launcher does: Mojang's client jar and libraries
      from the version JSON, Fabric Loader's production `KnotClient` from its loader profile, Loom's cached assets
      and the real dependency jars. Run it 80-90 s and fail on ERROR lines or missing models and textures.
    - Filter the expected offline profile-key 401. The server-side twin is the official Fabric server launcher
      with the remapped jar in `mods/`.
    - It found the atlas mip-level cap ("limits mip level from 4 to 1") that no dev run reported.
11. **Error dialogs on the user's screen.** Harness clients open real windows, so loader or Sodium error dialogs
    appear on the user's desktop. Run under `xvfb-run` where available. A Linux container with Xvfb and Mesa
    (software OpenGL) needs no physical display.
12. **Synthetic clicks on a screen did nothing, or hit the wrong element.**
    - **Cause:** screens that pick their hover target while rendering, from the real mouse position, ignore the
      coordinates passed to `mouseClicked`.
    - **Fix:** set `Mouse.x` / `Mouse.y` by reflection (window pixels = scaled point x window width / scaled width),
      let a frame render, then call `mouseClicked` / `mouseReleased` at the same scaled point. Small read-only hooks
      on the mod's screens that report element centres keep layout copies out of the harness.
    - To hold an item use, `useKey.setPressed(true)` plus `interactItem`: the client then re-uses every 4 ticks
      while the key is held, as a player's would.

## Seen in
- `games/minecraft/porting-thaumcraft-4-1-7-10-forge-to-minecraft-1-20-1-fabric.md`: natural villages, biomes and
  features on a seed-12345 world; 9 of 9 real-click checks and a 28 / 28 progression scenario; two clients; a
  100-node / 40-golem load probe.
  Its gotchas 28 and 29 are two more finds of this harness (aiming the camera at RNG-predicted positions, a refusal
  that was silent only in the port).
- `techniques/fabric-1-20-1-gametests-as-the-oracle-of-a-large-mod-port.md`: the server-side suite this harness
  complements.
- Other scripted dev-client autotests in this KB:
  - `games/halo-3-mcc/halo-3-weapons-covenant-vehicles-and-maps-ported-into-minecr.md`;
  - `games/fpv-logic/fpv-logic-drones-flight-model-rc-radio-and-3d-models-in-minecraft.md`;
  - `games/minecraft/bloons-td-6-in-minecraft.md`.

  - "https://github.com/liquidctl/liquidctl/blob/main/docs/asus-aura-led-guide.md"
---

# ASUS AURA USB protocol: opcodes, zone table and the unresolved TUF X570 4-pin header

> The ASUS AURA USB controller is a simple 65-byte HID device driven by four opcode groups
> (SetEffect / SetEffectColor / Commit / Direct). Reverse-engineering the mainboard HAL
> (`Aac3572MbHal_x86.exe`) yields the full opcode set and zone table. Our own attempt to
> drive the TUF X570's two **4-pin 12V RGB headers** with these packets was **unresolved** —
> the packets executed but the header LEDs stayed white — while OpenRGB documents X570 boards
> driving the 12V headers *from this same controller*, so it is not a hardware limit.

## When to use it

Writing or debugging an AURA USB driver (e.g. an OpenRGB fork), or deciding whether a board's RGB
header is reachable over the AURA HID interface.

Game relevance: many games drive motherboard/case RGB through vendor SDKs, so this protocol is the
low layer under in-game lighting effects. AURA's per-zone effect/colour/commit opcodes are the same
shape as MSI Mystic Light (MSI's `MysticLight_SDK`) and Razer Chroma — a game or mod that reacts to
in-game events (health, engine RPM, alerts) ends up issuing exactly these SetEffect / SetEffectColor
/ Commit writes. If a mod needs to reproduce or intercept such effects, this is the transport to
understand.

## How

### Raw materials and extraction

The AURA installers are self-extracting bundles with embedded CABs. The useful binaries:

- **Mainboard HAL:** `Aac3572MbHal_x86.exe` (796 KB) — the COM server that actually writes to the
  HID device via `UsbHidControl::DoWrite`.
- **Type library:** `Aac3572MbHal.tlb` — COM interface signatures.
- **SDK:** `AuraSdk_x86.dll` — a pure COM wrapper over the HAL.

SFX bundles carry CABs at fixed offsets (`0x70E00` small, `0x8D040` mainboard / `0x8CF70` service);
`dd` the CAB out, `7z x` it, then `7z x` the MSI inside to get the PE/TLB.

### COM API surface

Library `Aac3572MbHalLib`. Base interface `IAsusAacLedDeviceHal`, plus `...Hal2`, `IAacMotherboard`
(+`2`), `IAacLedDeviceOpt`, `...VariedLedCount`, `...Temperature`, `...Reset`, `IAacLedDevice2`,
`IAacLedDeviceOpt2`, `IAacMotherboardFunction`.

Key methods: `GetCapability`, **`SetEffect(effectId, colors[], numberOfColors)`**,
`GetEffect`, `Enumerate`, `SetStandbyEffect`, `SetSpeed`, `SetDirection`, `SetEnabled`,
`GetBiosOnOff`, `GetManualLedCount`, `GetTemperature` (1/10 °C), `Reset`, `SetFunction`,
`Synchronize(milliseconds)`. **Parameter order varies** between `(in,in,out)` and `(out,in,in)` —
always read the TLB.

### AURA opcodes (all 65-byte HID packets)

| Opcode | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `EC 35` | SetEffect "open" (device context) |
| `EC 36` | SetEffectColor (LED mask + 52 B colour data) |
| `EC 3F 55` | Commit (apply pending) |
| `EC 40` | Direct mode (per-LED write) |
| `EC 82` | GetFirmwareVersion |
| `EC B0` | GetConfigTable |
| `EC 32` | Read paths |
| `EC 52 53 00 01` | SetGen1 (brief flash on detection) |

### SetEffectColor packet (`EC 36`)

| Offset | Size | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1 | `0xEC` |
| 1 | 1 | `0x36` |
| 2 | 1 | mask_hi |
| 3 | 1 | mask_lo |
| 4 | 1 | channel (0 or 1) |
| 5–56 | 52 | RGB colour data |
| 57–64 | 8 | zero padding |

### SetEffect + Commit flow

1. Build a 16-bit LED mask: for each LED, `mask |= (1 << channel_id) & 0xffff`.
2. Send `EC 36` SetEffectColor with the mask and colours.
3. Send `EC 35` SetEffect open: `EC 35 00 00 10 02 00 00 ...`.
4. Send `EC 3F 55` Commit.

All I/O is serialized under the global mutex `Global\asusaurausb`.

### Zone table (HAL `FUN_0042bd50`)

Maps a case id to a zone name, returning `(name_ptr, length)`: `0x06` RGB strip-1, `0x07` RGB strip-2,
`0x11` RGB HEADER, **`0x13` `RGB_HEADER_1_2`** (the TUF X570 pair), `0x14` `RGB_HEADER_3_4`,
`0x1E` IO+BACK LED ZONE, `0x1F` NB+BACK LED ZONE, `0x20`+ per-board zones.

### HID write primitive

`UsbHidControl::DoWrite` (`FUN_00450560`) is a thin `WriteFile` wrapper — 65-byte buffer straight to
`kernel32!WriteFile`, handle at `this[0x1c]`. `DoRead` (`FUN_00450ba0`) is the `ReadFile` companion.
No per-zone logic lives here.

### TUF X570 channel mapping (hypothesis)

Within the mainboard device: channels 0–2 are the three onboard LEDs (`IO+BACK LED ZONE`), channels
3–4 are the two 4-pin headers (`RGB_HEADER_1_2`); the 12 ARGB LEDs are a separate device/zone.
Masks: onboard-only `0x07`, headers-only `0x18`, all mainboard `0x1F`.

### Ghidra workflow

```
/opt/ghidra/support/analyzeHeadless /tmp/ghidra_proj aura_hal \
  -process Aac3572MbHal_x86.exe -noanalysis \
  -scriptPath .../ghidra_scripts -postScript find_aura_strings
```

Do not re-analyze; run postScripts against the existing project.

## Gotchas

1. **The 4-pin headers did not respond to AURA HID — unresolved, not a hardware limit.**
   **Symptom:** every packet format (Direct `EC 40`, SetEffect `EC 35`, SetEffectColor `EC 36`,
   Commit `EC 3F 55`) writes successfully but the header LEDs stay white; the same packets drive
   onboard and ARGB zones fine. **Cause:** not established here. OpenRGB documents X570 boards
   driving the 12V headers *from this controller*, so the headers are reachable over AURA HID in
   general; our TUF X570 result is an unresolved per-board/address-mapping problem. A different
   bus (the **ENE eIO chip on `/dev/i2c-8`**, same SMBus as DRAM at `0x70–0x73`) remains a
   candidate. **Fix:** check `i2cdetect -l` / `i2cdetect -y 8` and re-check the channel/zone
   mapping; do not conclude the headers are off-limits on all boards.
2. **`UsbHidControlWithPatch` is dead code.** **Symptom:** a promising "patched HID path" class.
   **Cause:** it has RTTI but zero code references — empty vtable, no constructor. **Fix:** ignore it;
   there is no hidden patched path.
3. **Generic ASUS DLLs carry no AURA strings.** **Symptom:** you chase `AsIO.dll`, `ASUS_WMI.dll`,
   `ATKEX.dll`. **Cause:** they are generic platform libraries. **Fix:** the protocol lives in the
   mainboard HAL, not these.
4. **Parameter order is inconsistent in the COM API.** **Symptom:** a call succeeds but returns
   garbage. **Cause:** some methods are `(in,in,out)`, others `(out,in,in)`. **Fix:** read the TLB per
   method.
5. **A locked mutex serializes everything.** **Symptom:** writes appear to hang. **Cause:** all I/O is
   under `Global\asusaurausb`. **Fix:** don't hold it across UI waits; keep transactions short.

## Seen in

- An ASUS AURA reverse-engineering workbench (unpublished), target TUF X570, device `0B05:18F3`
- The OpenRGB AURA driver fork (a local OpenRGB checkout) — implements Direct-mode emulation and the LED-mask fix
  from this protocol knowledge

# Combat in Bannerlord mods: damage models, scripted blows, AI combat properties and guns on the crossbow class

> How damage flows in Bannerlord, how to deal your own damage safely, which AI properties decide blocking and aim, and how to
> build working guns when the game's Pistol and Musket classes are dead: everything on the crossbow class. From a Borderlands 2
> total conversion ([`../games/mount-and-blade-ii-bannerlord/bannerlord-borderlands-2-total-conversion.md`](../games/mount-and-blade-ii-bannerlord/bannerlord-borderlands-2-total-conversion.md)).

Evidence tags: **[V]** seen in the running game or by a byte-exact round trip, **[M]** measured, **[S]** static analysis only,
**[H]** hypothesis. "TN n" = gotcha n of [`editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md`](editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md).

## When to use it
- You change how much damage anything does, deal damage from script, or need deaths, knockouts and morale to behave.
- Your AI troops never block, never fire or deal zero damage.
- You want firearms in Bannerlord (the Pistol and Musket classes do not work), explosions, pellets or range caps.

## How
**Agents, combat and damage**
- **Models are the extension point.** Game models (`AgentApplyDamageModel`, `AgentStatCalculateModel`, `BattleMoraleModel`,
  `PartySizeLimitModel`, `BattleRewardModel`, `SettlementEconomyModel`, `AgentDecideKilledOrUnconsciousModel`,
  `StrikeMagnitudeCalculationModel`...) are looked up so the LAST registered one wins. Wrapper pattern: in `OnGameStart` find the
  registered model with `gameStarter.Models.OfType<X>().LastOrDefault()`, `gameStarter.AddModel(new Wrapper(inner))`, where
  `Wrapper : X` forwards every abstract member (33 for the damage model) and overrides the one you change. Never subclass a SandBox
  type from the always-loaded assembly or the module fails to load in custom battles. Mission models: `MissionGameModels.Current`.
  A wrapper around `AgentStatCalculateModel` misses calls the inner model makes to its own virtuals, so rescale after.
- **Damage pipeline.** `AgentApplyDamageModel` is the one damage step for melee, missiles, area, charge and falls;
  `ApplyGeneralDamageModifiers` is the last step before `InflictedDamage`; `ApplyDamageAmplifications` multiplies after armour.
  `Agent.HandleBlow` kills only when health is below 1 and drops a 0-damage hit (no flinch, blood or hit event; the swing bounces):
  let 1 through. Not covered: drowning, burning (`RegisterBurnBlow` calls Die), `Mission.KillAgentsOnEntity`. Armour: damage x
  50/(50+armour), then a type-dependent subtraction.
- **Own damage.** Build a `Blow` (`DamageCalculated=true`, `InflictedDamage`, `DamageType`, `BoneIndex`, `VictimBodyPart`,
  `WeaponRecord.FillAsMeleeBlow(null,null,-1,0)`, `BlowFlags`) plus an `AttackCollisionData` from `GetAttackCollisionDataForDebugPurpose`
  and call `victim.RegisterBlow(blow, in cd)`. The engine never filters this path (no friendly-fire cancel, no armour). Registering
  blows or spawning from inside an engine callback (missile hit, removal) is unsafe: queue to the next tick or `OnPreMissionTick`. Kill
  credit comes from the `_lastHitInfo` a blow in another agent's name sets.
- **Kill or knock out** is decided late: `Agent.HandleBlow` -> `Mission.OnAgentHit` -> `Agent.Die` -> native -> `Mission.GetAgentState` ->
  `AgentDecideKilledOrUnconsciousModel`. In a campaign mission a hero or boss death may come out Unconscious, so check Killed OR Unconscious.
  A missile's damage type and flags come from the AMMO item and `AttackCollisionData.DamageType` is get-only.
- **Morale.** Each nearby death moves a human AI agent's morale (0 to 100) through `BattleMoraleModel.CalculateMoraleChangeToCharacter`; at 0 it
  asks `CanPanicDueToMorale`, so a wrapper lets robots never rout.
- **AI skill properties** are written at the end of the stat model's `UpdateAgentStats` (at spawn and on every equipment/wield change).
  Block and parry: `AIBlockOnDecideAbility`, `AIParryOnDecideAbility`, `AIParryOnAttackAbility`, `AIParryOnAttackingContinueAbility`,
  `AiParryDecisionChangeValue`, `AiDefendWithShieldDecisionChanceValue`, `AiUseShieldAgainstEnemyMissileProbability`,
  `AiAttackingShieldDefenseChance`; aim: `AiRangerLeadErrorMin/Max`, `VerticalErrorMultiplier`, `HorizontalErrorMultiplier`,
  `WeaponInaccuracy`. Zero the first eight and the AI never blocks. Re-apply anything you pin on a short timer.
- **Spawning an agent mid-battle.** `new AgentBuildData(troop).Team(team).Formation(team.GetFormation(FormationClass.Infantry))
  .TroopOrigin(new BasicBattleAgentOrigin(troop)).InitialPosition(in pos).InitialDirection(in dir).Controller(AgentControllerType.AI)
  .IsReinforcement(true)`, then `Mission.SpawnAgent(data)`, then `agent.WieldInitialWeapons()` and
  `agent.SetWatchState(Agent.WatchState.Alarmed)` (what `Mission.SpawnTroop` does); without the last two the AI never wields or picks a
  target. A custom battle loads troops as `BasicCharacterObject`, the campaign as `CharacterObject`. Spawn after deployment, never from a callback.
- **Pinning an agent** (stationary bosses): `Controller = None`, `MaxSpeedMultiplier = 0` + `UpdateCustomDrivenProperties`, re-applied on a timer.
- **Friendly fire.** In single-player field battles `Mission.MissileHitCallback` cancels a non-physics missile meeting a friend (AI always;
  the player because both `FriendlyFireDamageRanged*Percent` options are 0), and melee against a friend is cancelled. A bouncing physics
  missile does hurt friends; splash through your own `RegisterBlow` is never filtered.
- **Items.** A hand-written `<Item>` melee weapon gets inertia = weight x 0.05, centre of mass = length/2 and damage factor 0.4; Native
  weapons are `CraftedItem`s with piece physics, so the same sword hits for about 7 instead of about 47: keep Native ids and re-skin.
  Weapon reskin takes THREE hooks: `MissionWeapon.OnGetWeaponDataHandler` (Native's `ViewSubModule` RESETS it at every game start: install in
  `OnGameStart` after Native's and again at `OnMissionBehaviorInitialize`), `CraftedDataView.OnWeaponMeshBuilt` and `ItemObject.MultiMeshName`
  set by reflection. Item value: shield tier = (hit_points^1.22 + 3 x body armour + thrust speed) / (6 + weight^1.11) x 0.04 minus 2; value =
  100 x 2.75^tier x (1 + 0.2 x (appearance minus 1)); loot rolls 7.25 x level^2 per casualty, so a looter can drop any item it carries.

**Guns on the crossbow class**
- **`Pistol` and `Musket` classes are dead in 1.4.8** (no skill, ammo type, item usage or animations). EVERY gun is `Type="Crossbow"`,
  `ammo_class="Bolt"`, with crossbow item usages (heavy `crossbow` with `CantReloadOnHorseback`, or `crossbow_light`), the Crossbow skill
  relabelled "Guns". The Old Realms and Shokuho do the same with own item usages.
- **Missile physics.** Damage = gun `thrust_damage` + ammo damage, scaled by (impact speed / launch speed)^2 (`SandboxStrikeMagnitudeModel`),
  so faster bullets are NOT harder. Vanilla bolts at 55 to 97 m/s drop about 3 m at 50 m; `missile_speed` 180 to 420 gives about 4 cm. The AI
  aims with the gun's own speed, but `Agent.GetMissileRange` grows with speed and `Mission.SetMissileRangeModifier` is ONE number for the
  whole mission (the weather model may overwrite it).
- **Ammo and reload.** `ammo_limit` becomes the magazine size; a crossbow is preloaded with min(ammo_limit, stack) at spawn;
  `reload_phase_count` is read (max 10; native crossbows use 2). Aim spread = (100 minus accuracy) x (1 minus 0.002 x skill) x 0.001.
- **Muzzle and eye.** The item XML `AmmoOffset` (weapon-local vec3 on the main-hand item bone) sets the muzzle; the missile start point
  measured as the EYE position. AI fires when a ray from the eye to the target is clear; an eye inside the model's own mesh blocks it.
- **Pellets.** Extra missiles come from `Mission.AddCustomMissile` (no gun damage bonus: scale strike magnitude in a wrapper). Every shot
  reaches `MissionBehavior.OnAgentShootMissile` with the `Missile` already in `Mission.MissilesList`; `Mission.OnMissileRemovedEvent` works
  while `OnMissileRemoved` is never called. The list mutates during hit hooks: snapshot it.
- **AI range control.** No managed hook can veto a native release. What works: per-agent `Agent.SetFiringOrder(HoldYourFire)` on a 4 Hz
  sweep for gunners whose `GetTargetAgent()` is beyond range; blocking releases beyond 1.1x range in `OnAgentShootMissile`.
  `Formation.SetFiringOrder` copies onto units only when the order changes or a unit joins.
- **Auto-resolve ignores guns.** `MapEvent.SimulateBattleRound` -> `DefaultCombatSimulationModel.SimulateHit` ->
  `MilitaryPowerModel.GetTroopPower` -> `GetDefaultTroopPower` = (2 + tier) x (10 + tier) x 0.02 (hero x1.5), tier = clamp(ceil((level
  minus 5)/5), 0, 6). Party strength, army power and garrison use the same function; wrapping it changes them all at once.

## Gotchas
1. **Symptom.** A fully soaked hit leaves the target immortal in melee and the swing bounces. **Cause:** `Agent.HandleBlow` drops 0-damage hits.
   **Fix:** let 1 damage through at the end of the damage model. [V]
2. **Symptom.** AI troops spawned after deployment (reinforcements, scripted swarms) deal zero damage. **Cause:** `Mission.SpawnAgent` alone does not do
   what `Mission.SpawnTroop` does: no `WieldInitialWeapons`, no `Alarmed` watch state. **Fix:** call both after spawning; make test spawns mimic the game. [V]
3. **Symptom.** `Agent.Die` from script throws or the death never registers. **Cause:** `CalculateMaxMoraleChangeDueToAgentIncapacitated` throws when a
   death has no affector, and native models read the killer's formation. **Fix:** always give a killer; have the morale wrapper catch and return (0,0). [V]
4. **Symptom.** `thrust_damage_type="Blunt"` or `CanKillEvenIfBlunt` on a gun does nothing for knock-outs. **Cause:** a missile's damage type comes from the
   AMMO item and `AttackCollisionData.DamageType` is get-only. **Fix:** mark the victim in `OnAgentHit` and answer Blunt from a wrapper
   `AgentDecideKilledOrUnconsciousModel`; in custom battle the default model always kills. [S]
5. **Symptom.** Guns have too much bullet drop; after raising speed they snipe across the whole map. **Cause:** vanilla bolt speed 55 to 97 m/s; raising it
   inflates `Agent.GetMissileRange` (AI engagement range) while the range modifier is global; damage does not inflate (magnitude is relative to the weapon's
   own launch speed). **Fix:** bullet speed 180 to 420 m/s by class, hold-fire sweeps and release blocks beyond a per-class range cap, reduced AI aim error. [engine check V, behaviour partly unverified]
6. **Symptom.** Mass battles with scatter guns flood the engine with live missiles. **Cause:** every pellet is an engine missile. **Fix:** for AI shooters one
   real missile plus "group" missiles standing for several pellets; above 700 live missiles groups of 6 and merged bursts, above 1,300 every volley collapses to one. [V]
7. **Symptom.** Splash does not hurt allies; bullets disappear on a friend. **Cause:** a non-physics missile meeting a friend is cancelled and melee against a
   friend is cancelled; your own `RegisterBlow` is never filtered. **Fix:** explosions through your own blows (friendly fire by design); a direct rocket hit on a
   friend is cancelled but the rocket still bursts. [V]
8. **Symptom.** Robots and creatures still block and parry. **Cause:** block and parry are AI properties set by the stat model, not by the roster. **Fix:** zero
   the eight AI properties for the agents concerned at the end of `UpdateAgentStats` (the engine reruns it on equipment change). [unverified until tallied]
9. **Symptom.** A pinned boss or a property you set drifts back. **Cause:** the stat model rewrites driven properties on every weapon or formation change and
    controller changes reset speed limits. **Fix:** re-apply on a 0.25 s timer, comparing to the last value you wrote (an unexpected value is the new base). [V]
10. **Symptom.** Damage hooks run on hits that never hurt; damage applied twice, native callback state corrupted. **Cause:** wooden-shield-blocked and
    weapon-blocked missiles also run the calculation; blows registered or behaviours removed inside engine callbacks. **Fix:** skip blocked hits; queue work for
    the next tick, a few blows per tick, re-validated. [V]
11. **Symptom.** Auto-resolve says "gun troops 3x too strong" or a huge beast pack looks harmless. **Cause:** auto-resolve, party strength and fight-or-flee read
    the TROOP TIER only. **Fix:** do not add scale constants; wrap `MilitaryPowerModel.GetDefaultTroopPower`. [V by reading]

- [Editor-free assets for Bannerlord](editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md) for the binary formats behind the races and clips.

# Custom races and creatures in Bannerlord at runtime: the humanoid path, quadruped mounts and hidden-rider creatures

> What it takes to make Bannerlord accept non-human bodies that move, fight and ride: races on their own skeletons (the
> humanoid path), creatures as mounts (the quadruped path), why a creature cannot be a soldier on its own and the hidden-rider
> workaround, flying creatures, and the animation rules that decide whether any of it moves. Learned while porting Borderlands 2
> ([`../games/mount-and-blade-ii-bannerlord/bannerlord-borderlands-2-total-conversion.md`](../games/mount-and-blade-ii-bannerlord/bannerlord-borderlands-2-total-conversion.md));
> binary formats are in [`editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md`](editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md).

Evidence tags: **[V]** seen in the running game or by a byte-exact round trip, **[M]** measured, **[S]** static analysis only,
**[H]** hypothesis. "TN n" = gotcha n of the asset note. Offsets are search handles for the client build above.

## When to use it
- You want a non-human body in Bannerlord that walks, fights or can be ridden: a monster, a robot, an animal, a boss.
- Your custom race spawns but slides, T-poses, never hits, or crashes seconds after it appears.
- You want a creature as a mount or as a fighter on its own, or something that flies (agents cannot).

## How
**Races and animation**
- A **race** is a skin entry (skeleton, body/face/hair meshes, deform keys) mapped to a `Monster` (bone fields, capsules, flags)
  whose action set, found by the name `as_<monster>[_female]<suffix>`, names the skeleton and the clip for every action. The agent's
  VISUAL skeleton comes from the ACTION SET's `skeleton=`, not the skin's; UI paths that pass no action set (character-creation
  preview, `BasicCharacterTableau`) use set 0, the human set, which twists a custom body and reads past the human bone array.
- **Humanoid path** (everything that fights as a troop): a copy of the human race with `skeleton=<own>`, `body_meta_mesh=<own mesh>`,
  every other body slot a one-triangle "none" mesh, `uses_stitching="false"`; hair/beard entries nameless but the ENTRY COUNTS kept;
  empty `<deform_keys />`; a placeholder face mesh with a submesh; non-empty colour lists. A monster with ALL ~55 bone fields named
  (omitted ones inherit the BASE monster's INDEX), plus `<id>_settlement`, `_settlement_slow`, `_settlement_fast`, `_child` variants;
  keep `IsHumanoid` (AI, morale, deployment read it). An action set per suffix the code asks for (`_warrior`, `_facegen`, `_map`,
  `_poses`, `_villager`, `_lord`, tavern and carry sets: **88 `as_human_*` sets, 7,649 actions**); `MBGlobals.GetActionSet` THROWS when
  one is missing (about 35 call sites of `FaceGen.GetMonsterWithSuffix`). A clip must exist for EVERY action type of the human set
  or the engine plays nothing; races copy all human sets and re-point only actions that have a clip.
- **28 biped bone order:** see "What the engine assumes about a human" in the asset note (first 28 bones in human biped order,
  extras after 27). Hero rigs of 90 to 122 bones are 27 body + face + finger bones; dropping face and fingers leaves 28 to 36.
- **Movement.** `movement_sets.xml` has 18 slot actions (idle, forward, backward, strafes, rotate, adders); the engine caches
  per-direction speed = distance per cycle / duration. Native locomotion clips are authored IN PLACE; speed comes from the agent and the
  clip's `bip_mov_ik` distance block, not the root channel. Recipe: one FBX per movement sequence, cycles in place, `bip_mov_ik` =
  metres per cycle measured from the planted foot.
- **Key units:** see "Clip record" in the asset note. Measure the key rate per rig, or hit windows land on the wind-up instead of the
  contact frame (gotcha 3).
- **Layers.** Channel 0 is movement, channel 1 the upper body (ready, aim, release, reload, defend); the skeleton's per-bone
  `lowerbody` flag decides which bones channel 0 keeps. Never set `enforce_*` flags on ready, release, reload or defend clips.
- **Combat clips** are written in copy mode from the Native clip of the same action. The hit window is `combat_parameters.xml`
  `collision_check_starting_percent` .. `ending_percent` of clip progress (parser default start 1.0 = empty window, so a plain clip never
  hits; e.g. 1h overswing 0.38 to 0.50). Ranged releases need step points (launch: bow 0.0, javelin 0.25); equip/unequip use the 4th
  step point as the switch progress and `agent_wield_update` needs channel 1 to play an equip/unequip action (type 33) until then or
  it logs "Weapon wield interrupted". Ready clips keep the `keep` flag. Keep Native durations to keep AI timing.
- **Hit geometry.** A chain of segments from shoulder to weapon bone, then along the weapon. A hit by an arm segment is
  `HitWithAnotherBone` (bounced, damage multiplied by `SwingHitWithArmDamageMultiplier`). Blow magnitude uses `AttackProgress`
  through `SpeedGraphFunction` (`managed_core_parameters.xml`) times weapon speed; bone velocity is not used.
- **Prebaked animations:** custom clips have none and off-screen agents' skeletons are not ticked, so
  `AgentVisuals.GetBoneEntitialFrame` returns stale or NaN frames: call `Skeleton.ForceUpdateBoneFrames` first.
- **Loop flags.** Conversation, inventory and pose "start" clips run once and rely on `continue_with` and the loop clip's `cyclic`
  flag; battles hide a missing one because movement re-issues idle.
- **Face builder:** see "Skin and face" in the asset note and TN 13. In addition, hair and beard lists are bound-checked (face,
  mouth, eyebrow and tattoo lists are not); put the fixed head in `body_meta_mesh`. `FaceGenVM` throws in randomise for a female skin
  with 0 beards.
- Tracks carry rotations per bone plus root translation only: non-root bone translations never animate; design rigs around rotations.
- **Retargeting a foreign body onto Bannerlord joints:** fit each bone with an affine, move vertices by linear blend skinning. BL2 is
  right-handed, forward +X, up +Z; Bannerlord agents face +Y, left at -X. Native clips cannot drive a foreign skeleton (bind rotations
  differ by a median 7 to 28 degrees).

**Creatures**
- A **quadruped path** exists and is safe only for mounts: an action set with `movement_system="quadrupedal"` and its own `skeleton=`.
  Rider and mount poses come from `monster_usage_sets.xml` (Native: human, horse, camel, animals). All monsters on one action set must
  share `num_paces` and `monster_usage`; the pace table is built once PER ACTION SET by the first agent using it.
- **Recipe (own-skeleton mounts):** canonical ids; an action set with the Native horse's action types; your own usage set (a copy of
  the horse's rows with a new id) as a new file under `soln_monster_usage_sets`; rider rows (`mount_id=<new usage id>`) appended to
  Native's `human` set by a same-named `.xslt`; gait clips with `quad_movement` as the FIRST of at most two parameter entries. Base the
  creature on the HORSE when its back is at horse height: rider clips are absolute from the mount origin and `rider_sit_bone` does not
  lift or lower the rider.
- **Mount monster fields:** `rider_sit_bone` a real back bone; `front_/back_bone_to_detect_ground_slope_index` are raw bone NUMBERS
  (signed byte), not names; `body_rotation_reference_bone` must not be the root; `fall_blow_damage_bone` below 28; a unique `family_type`
  keeps horse harnesses off. `Mission.SpawnAgent` mounts any agent with a rideable horse in slot 10.
- **Riderless creature troops are unsafe.** Native builds a non-humanoid agent only from a horse item; a character agent on a quadruped
  monster runs character-only steps (weapon component, facial controller, voices, formation, the AI target scorer reading the TARGET's
  weapon component). Guards held for most sites but the AI target-scorer site still crashed, so creatures are **jockey pairs**: a human
  cavalry NPC (no `race=`) rides an invisible-rider mount whose item carries the creature's monster and skin metamesh.
- **Jockey pair details.** Hide the rider with `AgentVisuals.SetVisible(false)` at build and EVERY tick; health 100000, healed inside
  `OnAgentHit`; blows on the rider are redirected to the mount one tick later in the attacker's name; the rider's own swings are dropped
  (`IsDamageIgnored`); no dismount by blow; mount and rider die together; scale, health and speed live on the MOUNT. The creature attacks
  with a scripted blow in the rider's name shortly after the mount plays a kick clip. The mount agent has no team (use the rider's).
- **Creature AI.** Native AI gives non-humanoid agents no attacks and native cavalry AI charges through and wheels away, so a boss mount is
  in reach a fraction of the time. A hold-and-bite driver (`Agent.SetScriptedPosition` with `AIScriptedFrameFlags`) fixes it.
- **Humanoid-path creatures** (fight as team members or never walk): `monster_usage="human"`, bipedal sets, at most 64 bones with the first
  28 in biped order; bosses that never walk play attacks through spare action slots and are pinned.
- **Flight.** An agent cannot be held in the air: `TeleportToPosition` every tick is pulled back down. Fly a separate `GameEntity`.

## Gotchas
1. **Soldiers slide with frozen feet, later drift and snap each cycle.** See TN 6.
2. **Every animation plays the same death pose.** See TN 5.
3. **Symptom.** Swings land on the wrong part of the arc. **Cause:** clip ranges are in stored keys and rigs store different rates (12.548 keys/s
   for one bake, one per frame for others). **Fix:** measure the key rate per rig and fit ranges in keys. [V]
4. **Symptom.** Conversation, inventory and party-screen figures fall to the reference pose after 2 to 3 s. **Cause:** start clips run once; loop
   clips lacked `cyclic` and the start clip lacked `continue_with`. **Fix:** looping copies with Native's stock flags and follow-ups. [V]
5. **AI troops with new combat clips deal no damage; troops swap weapons back ("Weapon wield interrupted").** See TN 21.
6. **Managed throw in the campaign UI, map or town code for a custom race.** See TN 19 (88 suffix sets and four monster variants).
7. **Holstered items on the wrong bone, UI code reading past the bone array, hit chain misaligned.** See TN 16.
8. **A Native clip on a custom skeleton plays garbage or crashes.** See TN 22.
9. **Symptom.** Melee does about 1 damage per swing; blows register at attack progress 0.00 to 0.04 or with the back of the weapon. **Cause:** the
   race builder gave every race the CROSSBOW AIM frame on the weapon bone, so the blade swung sideways (blade reach 0.59 of Native). **Fix:** a per-rig
   grip rotation on the weapon bone searched over the melee release clips (reach 0.99); recompute landed blows with the engine's `ComputeRawDamage` if
   the swings move the weapon slower in the damage window. Cover every monster that shares the skeleton. [V]
10. **Symptom.** AI never fires although it has line of sight; barely shoots. **Cause:** the AI shoot check traces from the eye (head-look bone frame +
    eye offset, moved back 0.45 x scale) and the eye sat inside the model's own mesh; the aim pose held the gun beside the body. **Fix:** eye at standing
    height, 5 cm in front of the front surface; a torso-only aim layer with the gun in front at chest height. [V]
11. **Riders float 0.45 m above a custom mount's back with straight legs.** See TN 24.
12. **Gait crash at creature spawn in an own quadruped set.** See TN 9, and TN 8 for the canonical-id cause.
13. **Symptom.** A player cannot switch from a heavy gun to melee on a creature mount; a mounted player cannot reload. **Cause:** native refuses the
    animated switch AWAY from a crossbow-class gun on a mount with `FamilyType` of 10 or more (182 of 210 refused; on foot 0), cause unknown; the
    generator wrote `CantReloadOnHorseback` on guns copied from the heavy crossbow usage. **Fix:** Harmony prefixes on `Agent.TryToWieldWeaponInSlot` and
    `WieldNextWeapon` force Instant for those riders (210 of 210); stop writing the flag where a mounted reload clip exists. [V]
14. **Symptom.** Boss rider redirect does nothing; hidden agents reappear. **Cause:** an Invulnerable victim drops every blow before any hit event
    exists; the engine re-shows agent visuals every tick. **Fix:** make the rider mortal with 100000 health and heal inside `OnAgentHit` (runs before the
    death check), redirect to the mount next tick; call `SetVisible(false)` every tick. [V]
15. **Symptom.** Map figure, encounter conversation and loot screen of a creature party show the hidden human jockey; a bandit-talk surrender is offered.
    **Cause:** the party leader is the human rider troop. **Fix:** a Harmony prefix on `PlayerEncounter.DoMeetingInternal` taking the engine's own army path
    (an "Attack / Leave" menu) and a postfix on `CharacterImageIdentifierVM` showing the mount item picture. [V]
16. **Symptom.** A flying boss made by teleporting the real agent every tick falls back to the ground. **Cause:** the engine pulls agents down. **Fix:**
    park the real agent (hidden every tick, AI off, engine blows ignored, following the flyer's ground shadow so enemy AI gathers under it) and fly a
    `GameEntity` built from the creature's skinned metamesh and skeleton along a precomputed arc to a navmesh landing spot; swap back in the same tick;
    far entities `DoNotTick` with hand ticks; fail-safe to a ground boss on any exception. Enemy AI aims at the parked agent's shadow, so count bullets at
    an airborne flyer as aimed. [V]
17. **Symptom.** Small troops are missed by the AI and barely hit. **Cause:** scale 0.45 to 0.5 gives tiny hit capsules. **Fix:** never scale
    below 0.65; for the capsule refit see TN 29. [offline measurement]

# Native crashes and hangs in Bannerlord: finding them in dumps and guarding them from managed code

> Bannerlord's release client reads bone indices, clip data, action indices, weapon components and usage-set slots without
> checking them, so bad mod data crashes or freezes it natively, often seconds after the cause. This note is the method used
> to find each one (WER and watchdog minidumps, Ghidra on a copy of the client DLL), the catalogue of crash sites and hangs
> solved with their causes, and how to guard a native fault from managed code. From a Borderlands 2 total conversion
> ([`../games/mount-and-blade-ii-bannerlord/bannerlord-borderlands-2-total-conversion.md`](../games/mount-and-blade-ii-bannerlord/bannerlord-borderlands-2-total-conversion.md)).

Evidence tags: **[V]** seen in the running game or by a byte-exact round trip, **[M]** measured, **[S]** static analysis only,
**[H]** hypothesis. "TN n" = gotcha n of [`editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md`](editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md). Offsets are search
handles for the client build above and go stale on any update.

## When to use it
- Bannerlord crashes or freezes with your mod and the log shows no managed exception ("faulting module TaleWorlds.Native.dll" or nothing).
- A crash happens seconds after a spawn, at deployment end, on the first melee contact, at a death, or only in sieges.
- You need to turn a native fault into a rule your pipeline checks, or guard it with a Harmony patch on the managed call leading to it.

## How
**Method.** Strings (assert and error text) -> referencing functions; crash RVA -> function; minidump registers -> object layout. A WER
dump has no heap: scan the stack for return addresses and decode the 256 code bytes WER keeps at the fault address by hand. Compare the
editor build (more strings and asserts) with the client for the same function. Run Ghidra headless with a Java batch script on a COPY of
the DLL and keep the analysed project on disk, so each later crash costs one script run.
**Guards.** The release client has almost no range checks: bone indices and counts, clip data pointers (`bip_mov_ik`, `quad_movement`,
`blends_with`), action index -1, face morph buffers, weapon components and usage-set slots are read unchecked, while the editor build
asserts. Validate in your pipeline instead, and at every mission start log `MBActionSet.GetActionSet(code).IsValid` and
`Agent.GetMonsterUsageIndex(usage) >= 0` for each custom monster; refuse to spawn agents that fail them.
**Interop.** Managed methods call native entry points by id from the `AutoGenerated` enum order; a managed null or exception where native
expects a pointer shows up as an access violation with module "unknown". Function names below are OUR labels (the DLL has no symbols).

| RVA | analyst's label | what it does | what faulted | details |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| +0x759c47 | `movement_set_calc_direction_speeds` | reads each movement slot clip's `bip_mov_ik` distance | clip without it | TN 7 |
| +0x760967 | `horse_movement_select_pace` | picks the gait from `quad_movement` | unloaded quadruped sets (canonical ids) | TN 8 |
| +0x636b6e | usage-set lookup | buckets of the monster usage set | usage set that never loaded | TN 8 |
| +0x584fec | `facegen_apply_static_morph` | applies skin deform keys | morph-less face + human deform keys | TN 13 |
| +0x6feb3f | `IMBAnimation.GetAnimationName` path | clip lookup for (action set, action) | action index -1 | TN 23 |
| +0x66d5a9 | `clip_balance_table_lookup` | weapon-balance child clip table | unregistered melee clip | TN 10 |
| +0x669cc5 | `anim_system_set_action` | blends with `blends_with` partner for shields | partner -1 | TN 12 |
| +0x730550 | `xml_load_file` | raw XML read | missing file: write at address -1 | TN 26 |
| +0x6a1004 | `agent_ai_score_target` | scores a target | target's weapon component null | TN 25 |
| +0x6fcc23 | `get_bone_type_data` | body type of a bone | bone index from another skeleton | gotcha 10 |
| +0x616dab | ragdoll stationary check | `ragdoll_*` monster bones | bone without a ragdoll body | gotcha 11, TN 15 |
| 0x180768b60 | `ik_solve_type5_hit_chain` | hit-reaction IK | no ik joint: endless loop on a worker | TN 30 |

The start-up fast-fail (ucrtbase `0xc0000409` in "Initializing items", clip names of 64+ characters) is TN 11.

Agent layout (client): weapon component at agent +0xad8 (allocated only if monster flag 0x4000); skeleton model bone records 0x1b0 bytes
each (+0xf0 parent, +0x104 body part, +0x110 ik-joint index), bone count a signed byte at +0x148; the agent grid is 208 x 529 cells of 1.5 m.

## Gotchas
1. **Access violation 3 to 4 s after a custom-race agent spawns, when it starts to move (+0x759c47).** See TN 7.
2. **Crash about 7 s after a non-human race spawns (+0x584fec).** See TN 13.
3. **About 1 in 3 battles crash at deployment end (+0x6feb3f).** See TN 23.
4. **Crash at the first melee contact or on a blocked reaction (+0x66d5a9).** See TN 10.
5. **Process dies at start-up in "Initializing items" with fast-fail 0xc0000409, even after rolling back.** See TN 11.
6. **Crash when an agent on a custom skeleton raises a shield (+0x669cc5).** See TN 12 (fix not run in game).
7. **Crash at game start (+0x730550) after adding a sound-event line to `project.mbproj`.** See TN 26.
8. **Hard freeze (no crash report, CPU busy) on the first hit on a jaw, toe, heel, cape, claw or robot arm.** See TN 30.
9. **Symptom.** Freeze about 3 s after deployment with riders on a custom mount, intermittent. **Cause:** the mount's `body_rotation_reference_bone` was the
   skeleton ROOT: the banking code rotates it in its PARENT's frame, parent -1 is memory before the animation result, the quaternion explodes, and the melee hit
   search then walks the agent grid for about 2^62 cells. **Fix:** no monster bone field the editor validates with "has parent" (body rotation reference, head
   and thorax look, neck root, hand and item bones, foot IK, slope bones) may be a root; a runtime guard sets the monster's body-rotation
   reference bone index to -1 at mission start when `MBActionSet.GetBoneHasParentBone` is false. `Monster.BodyRotationReferenceBoneIndex`
   is get-only in the public API, so the guard calls its private setter by reflection (`GetProperty(...).GetSetMethod(true)`, invoked
   with `(sbyte)-1`) for each monster whose reference bone has no parent, at every mission start; no Harmony patch. [dump analysis V;
   the guard runs in game (its log line in 187 test runs, no failure lines); that it cures the freeze is not shown, since no control run
   with it switched off was recorded]
10. **Symptom.** Siege with creature riders crashes seconds after spawn (+0x6fcc23); field battles never do. **Cause:** native fall damage builds a blow on the
    mount's `fall_blow_damage_bone` and `Mission.FallDamageCallback` repeats it for the RIDER, whose 28-bone skeleton has no such bone. **Fix:** keep a mount's
    fall bone below 28 and add a Harmony prefix on `Mission.FallDamageCallback` that remaps or skips. Any blow whose bone index belongs to another skeleton
    ends here: fix the class. [V]
11. **Symptom.** Crash about 3 s after a custom boss dies (+0x616dab), or a stuck agent when a custom skeleton dies. **Cause:** `ragdoll_*` monster bones name
    bones with no ragdoll body (index -1 read unchecked). The boss's `ragdoll_stationary_check_bone_*` and `ragdoll_fall_sound_bone_*` fields named arm and
    leg bones while only the spine, neck and head had bodies. The death path also dereferences bone 0's ragdoll body unchecked. **Fix:** point those fields
    at the nearest ancestor with a ragdoll body (or give every such bone a body); always a capsule on the root bone; joints are optional. [crash at +0x616dab
    V from the Windows crash event, not a dump; the next three runs that reached the boss's death did not crash, but the fix was not re-tested on its own or
    reverted; the root half is read from the code only, TN 15]
12. **NaN bone frames, NaN eye position, damage `int.MinValue` and an AI that never fires, only on AI-driven agents.** See TN 14.
13. **A riderless creature fighter crashes in five places (+0x6f45a6, +0x6fca17, voice, formation, +0x6a1004).** See TN 25; the working
    fix is the hidden-rider jockey pair in the [races note](bannerlord-custom-races-and-creatures.md).
14. **"Faulting module unknown, 0xc0000005" with no native frame of ours.** See "Crash triage" under Verification in the asset note.
15. **Hangs are reported as "undecided fights" or time caps and leave nothing to analyse.** See "Hangs are not crashes" under
    Verification in the asset note.
16. **Reading a crash dump gives the wrong frame.** See "Crash triage" under Verification in the asset note.

- [Editor-free assets for Bannerlord](editor-free-bannerlord-assets.md) for the binary formats behind the races and clips.
